Problem statement
-----------------
When filters applied to the work items pane return no visible open items the pane shows an unhelpful blank list or generic text. Users need a clear, contextual empty-state message that explains why the list is empty and offers an action when closed items exist.

Users
-----
- Primary: Developers and producers using the TUI to find or triage work items.
- Secondary: Automation users and CI authors who scan the TUI output during debugging.

User stories
-----------
- As a developer, when my filters match no open items I want the pane to tell me whether closed items exist and how to view them so I don't assume there is nothing in the project.
- As an accessibility-minded user, I want the empty-state message to be announced by screen readers so I immediately understand the state without extra navigation.

Success criteria
----------------
- When openCount == 0 and closedCount == 0 the pane shows a prominent, centered message: "No items are available." and no list rows are rendered.
- When openCount == 0 and closedCount > 0 the pane shows: "Only closed items are available — click \"Closed\" (bottom right) to view them." and provides an inline CTA or visible pointer to the Closed control that toggles the closed view.
- Messages are localised and announced to screen readers (use ARIA live region or role="status").
- Provide a thin metrics hook or telemetry event (optional) so product can measure how often the empty-state appears (add TODO comment if metrics system is not obvious).
- Unit tests cover message selection logic and an integration test verifies the CTA toggles the closed view.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

Constraints
-----------
- Keep changes small and local to the TUI code (src/tui/*). Avoid wide refactors.
- Follow existing empty-state component patterns and i18n conventions in the repo.
- Keyboard accessible and screen-reader compatible (no visual-only affordances).

Existing state
--------------
- There is already an EmptyStateComponent (src/tui/components/empty-state.ts) and multiple early-return paths in controller.ts that show the empty state when no items are visible.
- Tests exist that exercise the empty-state behaviour (tests/tui/controller.test.ts) and integration tests mention startup paths that avoid early-return.

Desired change
--------------
- Centralise the empty-state copy selection logic where the list rendering determines openCount and closedCount and passes the correct message/call-to-action to EmptyStateComponent. Keep public API surface of EmptyStateComponent unchanged unless necessary.
- Add i18n keys for the two messages and wire them into the existing i18n system.
- Add unit tests for the selection logic and an integration test for the CTA toggling closed items.

Related work
------------
 - src/tui/components/empty-state.ts — existing UI component used to render empty states.
 - src/tui/controller.ts — places where empty-state early-return occurs and the list rendering logic. Relevant comments at controller.ts around early-return and showToast('No work items found').
 - src/tui/components/index.ts — re-export of EmptyStateComponent.
 - tests/tui/controller.test.ts and tests/tui/dialog-integration.test.ts — tests that exercise empty-state behaviour and startup paths.
- WL-0MM04G2EH1V7ISWR "Add Intake and Plan filters to TUI" — related filtering work; may affect filter UI options.
- WL-0MNAGHQ33005BVY6 "Slow down investigation" — related TUI performance and behavior work.

Risks & assumptions
-------------------
- Risk: Scope creep if additional empty-state variants are requested (filters, search, user role). Mitigation: record follow-up feature requests as separate work items and keep this item focused on the two core messages.
- Risk: Changing EmptyStateComponent API may break other callers. Mitigation: avoid API changes; add a compatibility shim if needed.
- Assumption: i18n infrastructure already in place and adding two keys is straightforward (repo contains localization patterns used elsewhere).

Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers
---------------------------------------
- Q: "May I ask follow-up questions during the intake interview?" — Answer (agent inference): "do not ask questions". Source: seed argument provided to the intake run. Final: yes (preserve instruction; no interactive questions asked).

Headline: Show a contextual empty-state message in the work items pane when filters return no visible open items, with guidance and CTA when closed items exist.

5) Tests: unit tests for selection logic and integration test for CTA.

- Implement where work items list decides empty-state copy. Use i18n strings and ARIA live region.
- Expose derived props: openCount, closedCount, currentFiltersDescription.

Summary

Pressing the Escape (ESC) key causes the application to exit entirely. ESC should not terminate the program; at most it should close a modal, cancel an in-progress action, or be ignored when no cancellable UI is open.

User stories

- As a user, I want pressing ESC to cancel or close the current dialog instead of quitting the app so I don't lose work unexpectedly.
- As a user, I expect explicit quit actions (menu > Quit, Ctrl+C in terminal, or a dedicated shortcut) to be required to terminate the program.

Expected behaviour

- Pressing ESC will close the topmost transient UI element (modal, dropdown, inline editor) or do nothing if there is no such element.
- Pressing ESC must not cause the application process to exit.

Steps to reproduce

1. Start the application.
2. Ensure there is no explicit quit confirmation shown.
3. Press the ESC key.
4. Observe that the application exits (current behaviour).

Suggested implementation

- Add a global key handler that intercepts ESC key events and routes them to UI components/menus rather than allowing process-level exit.
- Ensure terminal-level handlers (if any) do not translate ESC into SIGINT or process termination.
- Add unit/integration tests covering key handling and a manual QA checklist for desktop and terminal environments.

Acceptance criteria

1. Reproduction: before the fix, ESC exits the app on the reported platform(s).
2. After the fix, pressing ESC does not terminate the process in any tested environment.
3. Pressing ESC closes modals or cancels in-progress operations when appropriate.
4. Automated tests for ESC handling are added and pass in CI.
5. A comment or short note is added to the relevant input/key handling code explaining the change.

Notes / Implementation hints

- If the app uses a UI framework that already maps ESC to window close, override that mapping only in places where the behaviour is undesirable.
- Investigate whether terminal/TTY libraries (if applicable) are translating ESC sequences into control sequences that lead to exit.
- Add `discovered-from: none` in description if creating additional follow-ups is necessary.

Summary:
Under certain circumstances the update dialog's keyboard handling registers every keypress three times (e.g. typing 'a' results in 'aaa'). This is reproducible and breaks text input in the dialog.

Why it's critical:
- Blocks users from reliably entering text into the update dialog
- Can cause data corruption or repeated commands

Reproduction steps:
1. Open the application and navigate to the Update dialog (Settings → Update).
2. Click into the text input field (or focus it via keyboard).
3. Perform the steps that trigger the bug: observed when the dialog is opened while a background input listener is active — preconditions: open Update dialog while global keyboard shortcut handler is enabled and the devtools console shows no errors.
4. Type any character; each keypress is inserted three times.

Clarification (2026-02-09):
- Triple registrations start after exiting the comment box; reproduce by focusing the comment box, then leaving it, then typing into the Update dialog input.

Observed behavior:
- Each single keypress is registered and inserted three times into the input field.

Expected behavior:
- Each keypress should be registered once.

Suggested root causes to investigate:
- Duplicate event listeners attached to the input or window (listener attached on each dialog open without removal).
- Global keyboard shortcut handler forwarding events to the dialog as well as the input.
- Race condition causing event handler to be bound multiple times.

Acceptance criteria:
- Fix prevents triple key registration for all input fields in the Update dialog under all app states where it previously occurred.
- Add unit or integration tests to cover single keypress behavior in the dialog.
- Add a small manual test checklist in the issue to verify behavior across platforms (Linux/macOS/Windows if supported).
- Add a short note to the changelog or release notes if behaviour change is user visible.

Suggested implementation approach:
1. Audit the update dialog lifecycle to find where keydown/keypress/keyup listeners are registered and ensure they are only added once and removed on dialog close.
2. Prefer attaching listeners to the input element rather than the global window if appropriate.
3. If global listeners must remain, guard handlers with a check to ignore events originated from input elements or ensure event.stopPropagation/stopImmediatePropagation is used properly.
4. Add automated tests that mount the dialog, simulate a single key event, and assert a single insertion.

Manual verification checklist:
- Open Update dialog, focus input, type text -> each key appears once.
- Reopen dialog multiple times -> typing still registers single keypress.
- Toggle global shortcuts on/off and verify behavior.

References and context:
- Observed during QA session 2026-02-08; no existing work item found in repo referencing this exact failure.

data.description:
Introduce a file-based (flock) process-level mutex to serialize access to the JSONL data file so concurrent processes don't cause merge races or data corruption.

## Problem
Multiple CLI processes or the API server can simultaneously read/modify the shared worklog-data.jsonl file. The exportToJsonl() method in database.ts performs a read-merge-write cycle that is susceptible to TOCTOU races. refreshFromJsonlIfNewer() can interleave with exports from other processes. The sync command performs fetch-merge-import-export-push without any lock.

## User Story
As a developer using Worklog in a team environment, I want concurrent wl commands to safely serialize their access to the shared JSONL data file so that no data is lost or corrupted due to race conditions.

## Implementation Approach
- Create a new src/file-lock.ts module that implements file-based locking using Node.js fs.open with O_EXCL (advisory lock file)
- The lock file will be placed alongside the JSONL data file (e.g., worklog-data.jsonl.lock)
- Provide withFileLock(lockPath, fn) helper that acquires the lock, runs the callback, and releases it (with proper cleanup on error)
- Include retry logic with configurable timeout and backoff for waiting on a held lock
- Include stale lock detection (process ID recorded in lock file, checked on acquisition failure)
- Integrate locking into WorklogDatabase.exportToJsonl() and WorklogDatabase.refreshFromJsonlIfNewer()
- Integrate locking into the sync, import, and export command handlers
- Write tests that simulate concurrent processes to validate serialization

## Acceptance Criteria
- A new src/file-lock.ts module exists with withFileLock() and related helpers
- Import/export/sync operations acquire the lock before running and release after
- Stale locks (from crashed processes) are detected and cleaned up
- Tests simulate concurrent processes to validate serialization
- All existing tests continue to pass
- The lock does not introduce noticeable latency for single-process usage
data.title: Process-level mutex for import/export/sync

data.description:
# Audit comment improvements

Replace noisy, full-dump audit comments with structured, delimiter-bounded reports that include deep code-review verdicts for acceptance criteria on both parent and child work items.

## Problem statement

The AMPA triage scheduler's audit comments currently contain the entire raw output of `opencode run "/audit <id>"`, which includes tool call logs, intermediate reasoning, and other noise alongside the actual audit summary. Additionally, the audit skill's acceptance criteria validation is shallow -- it relies primarily on work item descriptions and comments rather than performing a thorough code review. This makes audit comments both noisy and insufficiently rigorous for verifying whether work is actually complete.

## Users

- **Producers reviewing work items:** As a producer, I want audit comments on work items to contain only a clear, structured status report with code-validated acceptance criteria verdicts so I can quickly and confidently understand the true state of each item without sifting through tool call noise.
- **Agents consuming audit comments:** As an automated agent, I want audit comments to follow a predictable structure with per-criterion verdicts so I can reliably extract status information for downstream processing (e.g. cooldown detection, delegation decisions, auto-close evaluation).
- **Discord notification consumers:** As a team member receiving Discord notifications, I want the triage audit summary to be extracted from a well-structured report so the notification is concise and accurate.

## Success criteria

1. The audit skill (`skill/audit/SKILL.md`) produces output with clearly defined delimiter markers (`--- AUDIT REPORT START ---` / `--- AUDIT REPORT END ---`) around the final structured report.
2. The structured report between the markers contains these sections in markdown: **Summary**, **Acceptance Criteria Status**, **Children Status**, and **Recommendation** (where applicable).
3. For the parent work item, the audit skill performs a deep code review for each acceptance criterion: reading the actual implementation code, assessing correctness, completeness, and edge cases. Each criterion receives a verdict (met/unmet/partial) with a one-line evidence note referencing the relevant file and line number.
4. For each child work item, the audit skill performs the same deep code review of acceptance criteria as for the parent. Each child's acceptance criteria are individually validated against the codebase with per-criterion verdicts and file references.
5. The triage audit runner (`ampa/triage_audit.py`) extracts only the content between the delimiter markers and posts that as the WL comment (under the existing `# AMPA Audit Result` heading).
6. The Discord notification is updated to extract the Summary section from the structured report (between delimiters) rather than applying regex heuristics to the full raw output.
7. When a work item or child has no acceptance criteria defined, the audit report notes this explicitly (e.g. "No acceptance criteria defined") rather than silently skipping the item.
8. Unit tests cover the marker extraction logic (including edge cases: missing markers, malformed output, empty report). A lightweight integration test verifies end-to-end format from the audit skill through to the posted comment structure.

## Constraints

- **Short-term fix:** This is an incremental improvement to comment quality and audit rigor. The broader initiative to replace comment-based audits with a structured `audit` field on work items (WL-0MLDJ34RQ1ODWRY0) remains a separate, future effort.
- **Breaking change acceptable:** The triage runner does not need to handle the old unstructured format. Once the audit skill is updated, old-format output can be dropped.
- **Truncation default unchanged:** The existing `truncate_chars` default (65536) is retained. Structured reports are expected to be much shorter in practice but the safety limit remains.
- **Audit skill is an OpenCode skill:** Changes to the audit skill output format are made in `~/.config/opencode/skill/audit/SKILL.md`, which is an instruction file for the AI agent -- not executable code. The skill instructions must be updated to mandate the structured output format with delimiters and the deep code review approach.
- **Triage runner is AMPA Python code:** The extraction and comment-posting logic lives in `~/.config/opencode/ampa/triage_audit.py` (and the legacy path in `~/.config/opencode/ampa/scheduler.py`).
- **Code review depth is instruction-driven:** The depth of code review depends on the AI agent following the skill instructions. The instructions should be explicit about reading implementation files, checking function signatures, verifying test coverage, and assessing edge cases -- not just checking that files exist.

## Existing state

- The audit skill (`skill/audit/SKILL.md`) produces freeform markdown output with a `# Summary` section. It does not use delimiter markers and does not enforce a consistent structure for all sections.
- The current skill mentions validating acceptance criteria "where appropriate, code in the repository" but this is vague. In practice the agent often relies on descriptions and comments rather than performing actual code review.
- The skill does not instruct the agent to review children's acceptance criteria against code -- it only lists child items by title, id, status, and stage.
- The triage audit runner (`triage_audit.py`) posts the entire stdout+stderr of `opencode run "/audit <id>"` as a WL comment under `# AMPA Audit Result`. It uses a regex-based `_extract_summary()` function to find a `Summary` section for Discord, but this is fragile and operates on the full raw output.
- Discord notifications currently receive the regex-extracted summary or a fallback of `<work-id> -- <title> | exit=<code>`.

## Desired change

1. **Audit skill update:** Modify `skill/audit/SKILL.md` to instruct the AI agent to:
   - Wrap the final report in `--- AUDIT REPORT START ---` and `--- AUDIT REPORT END ---` delimiters.
   - Structure the report with markdown headings: `## Summary`, `## Acceptance Criteria Status`, `## Children Status`, `## Recommendation`.
   - For the parent work item's acceptance criteria: perform a deep code review by reading the actual implementation code, assessing correctness and completeness against each criterion. Report each criterion as met/unmet/partial with a one-line evidence note including `file_path:line_number`.
   - For each child work item: extract the child's acceptance criteria and perform the same deep code review. Report per-criterion verdicts with file references. Present children as subsections under `## Children Status` with their own acceptance criteria tables.
   - Keep the report concise and actionable despite the deeper analysis.

2. **Triage runner update:** Modify `triage_audit.py` to:
   - Extract content between the `--- AUDIT REPORT START ---` and `--- AUDIT REPORT END ---` markers from the raw `opencode run` output.
   - Post only the extracted report as the WL comment (still under the `# AMPA Audit Result` heading).
   - If markers are not found, fall back to posting the full output (defensive behavior) but log a warning.

3. **Discord extraction update:** Update the Discord summary extraction to:
   - Parse the structured report (between markers) and extract the `## Summary` section.
   - Use this instead of the current regex heuristic on raw output.

4. **Tests:**
   - Unit tests for the marker extraction function covering: happy path, missing start marker, missing end marker, empty content between markers, multiple marker pairs (take first).
   - Unit tests for the updated Discord summary extraction.
   - Lightweight integration test verifying the audit skill output format contains the expected markers and sections.

## Risks & assumptions

- **AI compliance:** The deep code review behavior is instruction-driven. The AI agent may not consistently follow the skill instructions, producing varying output quality or omitting markers. Mitigation: the triage runner falls back to posting the full output and logs a warning when markers are missing.
- **Token/context budget:** Deep code review of parent + all children may exceed the AI agent's context window for work items with many children or large codebases. Mitigation: the skill instructions should cap the review to a reasonable depth (e.g. direct children only, not recursive grandchildren) and note when truncation occurs.
- **Runtime increase:** Deep code review will increase the duration of each audit run compared to the current shallow approach. Mitigation: the existing `_audit_timeout` / `AMPA_AUDIT_OPENCODE_TIMEOUT` configuration bounds execution time.
- **Scope creep:** This work item covers structured output format + deep code review of acceptance criteria. Additional ideas (e.g. structured audit field, delegation recommendations, auto-close improvements) should be tracked as separate work items (WL-0MLDJ34RQ1ODWRY0, WL-0MLI9B5T20UJXCG9) rather than expanding scope here.
- **Assumption: acceptance criteria format.** The skill assumes acceptance criteria are in a markdown section starting with `## Acceptance Criteria` formatted as a list. Work items that use a different format may have criteria missed or misidentified.

## Related work

- **Replace comment-based audits with structured audit field** (WL-0MLDJ34RQ1ODWRY0) - open, medium priority. Future effort to move audits out of comments entirely. This work item is a short-term improvement that does not conflict with that direction.
- **Scheduler: output recommendation when delegation audit_only=true** (WL-0MLI9B5T20UJXCG9) - open, medium priority. Discovered from this work item. Enhances audit output with delegation recommendations.
- **Only send in_progress report to Discord if content changed** (WL-0MLX37DT70815QXS) - open, medium priority. Involves Discord notification from the scheduler/triage system. The Discord summary extraction changes in success criterion 6 intersect with this item's shared notification logic.
- **Audit: SA-0MLHUQNHO13DMVXB** (WL-0MLOWKLZ90PVCP5M) - open, medium priority. An active audit task that will produce output in the new structured format once the skill is updated. Serves as a downstream consumer of these changes.

## Related work (automated report)

The following related items and files were discovered by automated search. Each entry describes its relevance to WL-0MLG60MK60WDEEGE.

### Related work items

| ID | Title | Status | Relevance |
|---|---|---|---|
| WL-0MLDJ34RQ1ODWRY0 | Replace comment-based audits with structured audit field | open | Future effort to move audits from comments to a structured field. This work item is the short-term incremental fix; that item is the long-term replacement. Both improve audit data quality but are independently scoped. |
| WL-0MLI9B5T20UJXCG9 | Scheduler: output recommendation when delegation audit_only=true | open | Discovered from this item. Adds a Recommendation section to audit output. The `## Recommendation` heading in the structured report format directly supports this item's goals. |
| WL-0MLX37DT70815QXS | Only send in_progress report to Discord if content changed | open | Involves Discord notification and shared helper code (`_summarize_for_discord`). Success criterion 6 changes how Discord summaries are extracted, which may interact with this item's deduplication logic. |
| WL-0MLOWKLZ90PVCP5M | Audit: SA-0MLHUQNHO13DMVXB | open | Active audit task that will consume the new structured output format. Once the audit skill is updated, this and all future audit runs produce delimiter-bounded reports. |

### Related files

| Path | Relevance |
|---|---|
| `~/.config/opencode/skill/audit/SKILL.md` | Primary target. Audit skill instructions to be updated with structured output format, delimiters, and deep code review mandates. |
| `~/.config/opencode/ampa/triage_audit.py` | Primary target. Contains `_extract_summary()` regex and comment-posting logic that must be updated for delimiter-based extraction. |
| `~/.config/opencode/ampa/scheduler.py` | Legacy triage-audit path with duplicate `_extract_summary()` and comment-posting code. Must be updated in parallel or confirmed as dead code. |
| `~/.config/opencode/tests/test_triage_audit.py` | Existing test file for the triage audit runner. Must be extended with marker extraction and Discord summary extraction tests. |
| `~/.config/opencode/ampa/delegation.py` | Contains `_summarize_for_discord()` used by `triage_audit.py`. Discord extraction update may change how this function's input is prepared. |
| `~/.config/opencode/docs/triage-audit.md` | Documentation for the AMPA triage-audit flow. Currently describes posting full audit output; must be updated to reflect delimiter-based extraction. |
| `~/.config/opencode/docs/workflow/examples/02-audit-failure.md` | Workflow example with sample `# AMPA Audit Result` comment format. Should be reviewed for consistency with the new structured report format. |

## Key files

- `~/.config/opencode/skill/audit/SKILL.md` - audit skill instructions (primary target)
- `~/.config/opencode/ampa/triage_audit.py` - triage audit runner, comment posting, Discord extraction (primary target)

# Intake Brief: Migrate GitHub Sync Helpers to Async Pattern

## Problem Statement

The codebase contains both synchronous and asynchronous GitHub integration functions. The synchronous versions (`ensureGithubLabels`, `listGithubIssues`) block the event loop and can cause performance issues when called from async contexts. The goal is to migrate all callers to use the async versions and deprecate the synchronous functions.

## Users

- **Developers** working with GitHub integration code will benefit from non-blocking async operations
- **TUI and CLI components** that currently use synchronous functions will see improved responsiveness
- **Plugin authors** who interact with GitHub will have consistent async APIs to work with

### Example User Stories

- As a developer, I want to fetch GitHub issues without blocking the event loop so the TUI remains responsive
- As a plugin author, I want to use async helpers for label management to avoid blocking other operations
- As a maintainer, I want a single consistent async API surface for GitHub operations

## Success Criteria

- [ ] All label management functions have async versions available (already exist)
- [ ] All issue listing functions have async versions available (already exist)
- [ ] All callers in the codebase use async versions
- [ ] Synchronous versions marked deprecated with JSDoc `@deprecated`
- [ ] All existing tests pass with the async migration
- [ ] Unit tests added or updated for async migration paths (verify no coverage regression)
- [ ] Integration tests verify async behavior works correctly

## Constraints

- **Backward compatibility**: Must maintain sync versions until all callers are migrated
- **GitHub API rate limits**: Async operations should respect rate limiting (already handled by throttler)
- **Error handling**: Async versions must maintain same error handling as sync versions
- **Test coverage**: Must not reduce existing test coverage during migration

## Risks & Assumptions

### Risks

- **Scope creep**: Adding new features during migration could delay completion
  - *Mitigation*: Record opportunities for additional features/refactorings as work items linked to the main item, rather than expanding the scope of the current item

- **Breaking changes**: Converting sync to async could break existing callers if not properly awaited
  - *Mitigation*: Add comprehensive error handling tests and verify all callers properly await async functions

- **Performance regressions**: Async operations might introduce unexpected overhead
  - *Mitigation*: Profile before and after migration to ensure no performance degradation

- **Incomplete migration**: Some callers might be missed during migration
  - *Mitigation*: Run grep search after migration to verify all callers use async versions

### Assumptions

- Async versions already exist and are fully functional (already implemented in `src/github.ts`)
- All callers can be migrated without API changes
- No external consumers depend on the synchronous API
- Error handling behavior is identical between sync and async versions

## Existing State

### Current Synchronous Functions

- `ensureGithubLabels(config, labels)` - Synchronous label creation helper
- `listGithubIssues(config, since?)` - Synchronous issue listing with pagination
- `ensureGithubLabelsOnce(config, labels)` - Internal sync cache helper (used by `updateGithubIssue`)

### Current Asynchronous Functions (Already Exist)

- `ensureGithubLabelsAsync(config, labels)` - Async label creation with cache
- `listGithubIssuesAsync(config, since?)` - Async issue listing with pagination
- `ensureGithubLabelsOnceAsync(config, labels)` - Internal async cache helper

### Callers (Based on Code Search - grep results)

- `src/github-sync.ts:726` - Uses `listGithubIssues` (sync)
- `src/github.ts:1172` - Uses `ensureGithubLabelsOnce` in `createGithubIssueAsync`
- `src/github.ts:1249, 1264` - Uses `ensureGithubLabelsOnceAsync` internally
- `src/github.ts:1410` - Uses `ensureGithubLabelsOnce` in `updateGithubIssue`

## Desired Change

1. **Migrate callers** to use async versions:
   - Update `github-sync.ts` to use `listGithubIssuesAsync`
   - Update `updateGithubIssue` to use `ensureGithubLabelsOnceAsync` where appropriate

2. **Deprecate synchronous versions**:
   - Add `@deprecated` JSDoc comments to sync functions
   - Add migration notes in function comments

3. **Verify async behavior**:
   - Ensure async functions are properly awaited in all callers
   - Test error handling paths
   - Verify rate limiting works correctly

## Related Work

- **Parent epic**: WL-0MLGAYUH614TDKC5 - Wire CLI to async GitHub sync
- **GitHub integration**: `src/github.ts` (lines 467-1425) - Core GitHub API helpers
- **GitHub sync**: `src/github-sync.ts` (line 726) - Sync operations between Worklog and GitHub
- **Existing async functions**: Already implemented but not fully adopted (see `src/github.ts` lines 1188-1379)
- **Related work item**: WL-0MNAGHQ33005BVY6 - Slow down investigation (contains async rendering context)

### Related work (automated report)

- **WL-0MLGAYUH614TDKC5** (Parent): Wire CLI to async GitHub sync - This work item is part of a larger effort to migrate all GitHub sync operations to async. The parent epic covers the CLI command handlers, while this item focuses on the underlying helper functions.

- **WL-0MNAGHQ33005BVY6** (Related): Slow down investigation - This critical issue identified performance problems with TUI rendering that may be related to synchronous GitHub API calls. While focused on rendering, it highlights the need for async patterns throughout the codebase.

- **src/github-sync.ts:726** (File): Current usage of `listGithubIssues` (sync) - This is the primary caller that needs to be migrated to `listGithubIssuesAsync`.

- **src/github.ts:1410** (File): Current usage of `ensureGithubLabelsOnce` (sync) in `updateGithubIssue` - This internal function needs to be updated to use `ensureGithubLabelsOnceAsync`.

## Appendix

### Clarifying Questions and Answers

- Q: "What is the primary purpose of this work item - adding new async functions, migrating existing code to use them, or both?" — Answer: "Both add and migrate". Source: User interview. The goal is to both ensure async versions exist AND migrate all callers to use them.

- Q: "Which specific functions need async versions? Based on the work item description, are you referring to label management helpers and issue listing helpers?" — Answer: "All labels and All lists". Source: User interview. The scope covers all label management functions and all issue listing functions.

- Q: "What is the expected impact on callers? Should all synchronous versions be deprecated, or should both sync and async versions coexist?" — Answer: "Deprecate sync versions". Source: User interview. After migration, sync versions should be marked as deprecated with JSDoc `@deprecated` tags.

### Open Questions

- **External callers**: Are there external callers (plugins, external tools) that use the synchronous versions that we need to consider? **[Directed to: User]**

### Failure Modes

- **Partial migration**: If some callers remain on sync version, performance benefits are reduced
  - *Detection*: Run grep search after migration to verify all callers use async versions
  - *Recovery*: Create follow-up work item for remaining callers

- **Rate limit exhaustion**: Async operations might hit GitHub API rate limits faster
  - *Detection*: Monitor GitHub API response headers for rate limit warnings
  - *Recovery*: Throttler already handles rate limiting, verify configuration

# Async list issues and repo helpers / central throttler — WL-0MLGBAPEO1QGMTGM

Problem statement
- GitHub-related async helpers are in place, but requests are coordinated only via per-function bounded concurrency (e.g., `WL_GITHUB_CONCURRENCY` in `src/github-sync.ts`). There is no central throttler/token-bucket to enforce global request rates and bursts across all async GitHub calls, which makes it harder to reason about and control overall API usage and to simulate rate-limit behavior in tests.

Users
- Engineers and automation that run `wl github push`, `wl github sync`, and other GitHub-backed sync flows; CI or agent-run automation performing bulk syncs; maintainers who need predictable, testable API usage.

Example user stories
- As an engineer running `wl github push`, I want requests to GitHub to be globally rate-limited so I avoid secondary-rate-limit/abuse responses during large syncs.
- As a maintainer, I want a central throttler utility with clear config (env or config.yaml) so I can tune behavior per-environment.

Success criteria
1) Implement a reusable token-bucket throttler utility and export a single shared instance for GitHub calls; default behaviour uses token-bucket refill.
2) Migrate all async GitHub call sites (github helpers and callers, including `src/github-sync.ts`) to use the throttler so concurrency/rate is enforced globally.
3) Add unit tests for the throttler (token-bucket semantics) and integration tests exercising `github-sync` under simulated load and rate-limit conditions.
4) Update repository docs to explain throttler behaviour and how to tune the env vars.

Constraints
- Must avoid changing GitHub API semantics; throttler only changes client-side scheduling.
- Keep implementation small, dependency-free (vanilla TS/JS), and testable offline (use injectable clocks/mocks for timing in unit tests).
- Backwards-compatible: keep honoring `WL_GITHUB_CONCURRENCY` where used, but prefer centralized throttler when available.

Existing state
- `src/github-sync.ts` already uses `Number(process.env.WL_GITHUB_CONCURRENCY || '6')` in two places to bound concurrency for upserts and hierarchy checks. Many async helpers exist in `src/github.ts` (async variants, create/update/get/list helpers). No central throttler file or tests for a throttler were found.

Desired change
- Add `src/github-throttler.ts` (or similar) implementing a token-bucket with optional concurrency cap; export a default/shared instance wired by `config` helpers or env vars. Replace local concurrency pools in `src/github-sync.ts` and update other async GH callers to use the centralized throttler API (e.g., `throttler.schedule(() => helperAsync(...))`). Add unit and integration tests and documentation updates.

Related work
- `src/github-sync.ts` — existing sync logic and current per-function concurrency usage (see `upsertConcurrency` & `concurrency`).
- `src/github.ts` — async GH helpers to be wrapped or called via throttler.
- WL-0MLGBABBK0OJETRU — "Async comment helpers and comment upsert migration" (completed) — shows async migration pattern and tests for comments; may be useful for migration examples.

Please review this draft and confirm or provide edits for scope, defaults, and test expectations.

Problem statement
Run a safe, idempotent schema migration to add the `needsProducerReview` INTEGER column to the `workitems` table and provide a repeatable, documented, and automatable upgrade path via `wl doctor` so the application can run migrations manually or automatically after an upgrade.

Users
- Maintainers and Producers: need the DB to be up-to-date so CLI commands (`wl create`, `wl update`, `wl list`) work without errors and new fields are queryable.
- Developers and automation agents: need an automated, auditable migration path that can run on first command after upgrading the application or be run manually in CI or by operators.

Success criteria
- `wl doctor upgrade --dry-run` lists pending migrations including the `needsProducerReview` ADD COLUMN migration; `wl doctor upgrade --confirm` applies them.
- After applying the migration, `PRAGMA table_info('workitems')` shows the `needsProducerReview` column and existing rows report 0 (false) by default.
- The migration process creates a timestamped backup of `.worklog/worklog.db` (retain last 5 backups) before applying changes and fails if backup cannot be created.
- Automatic run behavior: on first command after an upgrade, non-safe migrations are notified and applied only after acknowledgement; safe non-destructive migrations may be auto-applied per policy; CI environments do not auto-apply migrations.
- Operations are idempotent: re-running the same migration does not fail or create duplicate schema changes.

Constraints
- Migration tooling must respect environment and flags: WL_AUTO_MIGRATE (opt-out), CI=true disables automatic application, and `wl doctor upgrade --dry-run` must be available.
- Backups must be automatic and pruned to the last 5; a failed backup prevents migration.
- By default the system will notify and then apply destructive migrations only after explicit confirmation (interactive or `--confirm`); non-destructive migrations may be applied automatically per the chosen policy.
- Application version is read from `package.json` and schemaVersion is stored in DB metadata.

Existing state
- The codebase references the new `needsProducerReview` field in several places (CLI flags, persistence, JSONL) but some installations lack the DB column and see SQLite errors referencing a missing column.
- There is an existing `wl doctor` command and a set of doctor checks and a `doctor --fix` pipeline that handles safe fixes (see `src/commands/doctor.ts`, `src/doctor/*.ts`).
- Current manual migration guidance exists in work item WL-0MLGVVMR70IC1S8F (this item) and the immediate problem has an acceptance test suggested (run `ALTER TABLE` and verify PRAGMA).

Desired change
- Implement a migration runner and integrate it into `wl doctor` with:
  - `wl doctor upgrade --dry-run` to preview migrations (JSON output and human summary).
  - `wl doctor upgrade --confirm` to apply migrations non-interactively (for automation) and interactive flow otherwise.
  - Automatic timestamped DB backup creation (retain last 5) before applying migrations.
  - SchemaVersion stored in DB metadata and compared to application `package.json` version; migrations keyed by id and target schemaVersion.
  - Migration policies: notify-then-apply for destructive migrations, allow operator to opt-in, auto-apply non-destructive migrations depending on WL_AUTO_MIGRATE and CI.

Related work
- Work items:
  - WL-0MLGTKW490NJTOAB — Add Needs Producer Review flag to work items (parent feature)
  - WL-0MLGW90490U5Q5Z0 — Implement migration runner module (planning task created)
  - WL-0MLGW91WT0P3XS5T — Wire migration runner into SqlitePersistentStore (planning task created)
  - WL-0MLGW93H91HMMUOT — Add 'wl migrate' / 'wl doctor upgrade' CLI commands (planning task created)
  - WL-0MKRPG64S04PL1A6 — Worklog doctor intake brief and doctor command (related doctor work)

- Potentially related docs / files:
  - `src/commands/doctor.ts` — doctor CLI wiring
  - `src/doctor/fix.ts`, `src/doctor/status-stage-check.ts`, `src/doctor/dependency-check.ts` — existing doctor checks/fix pipeline
  - `src/persistent-store.ts` — current SQLite schema creation and initializeSchema logic
  - `.worklog/worklog-data.jsonl` and `.worklog/worklog.db` — canonical datastore and examples
  - `CLI.md` — CLI docs to update with `wl doctor upgrade` usage

Notes / decisions captured from interview
- Default behavior: Automatic migration defaults to notifying the user then applying migrations for which the user provided consent; destructive migrations require explicit confirmation (interactive or `--confirm`). User chose: allow destructive with confirmation.
- Storage: use DB metadata for schemaVersion and read application version from `package.json`.
- Backup policy: always create an automatic timestamped backup before applying migrations and retain the last 5 backups; fail if backup cannot be made.
- CI: automatic migrations are disabled when CI=true; CI runs should require `wl doctor upgrade --confirm` to proceed.

Suggested next step (implementation)
1) Implement the migration runner module (`src/migrations/index.ts`) that exposes `listPendingMigrations` and `runMigrations({dryRun, confirm, logger})` and includes the `ADD COLUMN needsProducerReview` migration as idempotent.

Present for review
Please review this draft for completeness and correctness. If you approve, I will:
 - Update work item WL-0MLGVVMR70IC1S8F description with this intake brief and move it to `intake_complete`.
 - Create the migration runner implementation and tests (referencing WL-0MLGW90490U5Q5Z0) and add the CLI `wl doctor upgrade` wiring.

Problem statement

Provide a single‑key TUI shortcut to toggle a "do-not-delegate" marker on the currently selected work item so users can prevent the item from being auto-assigned by automation or agents. The toggle should be discoverable in the help overlay, testable, and also exposable from the CLI.

Users
- Producers and Team Leads: want to mark items that should not be automatically assigned by agents or automation (for special handling or manual assignment).
- Keyboard-first TUI users: want a fast, single-key toggle accessible from the item list or detail view.
- Automation scripts / tooling: should be able to set/clear the marker from the CLI for non-interactive flows.

User stories
- As a Producer, I want to mark an item so agents do not auto-assign it, using the keyboard without opening a full edit UI.
- As a keyboard-first user, I want to press a single key to toggle the setting and receive immediate feedback (toast + list marker).
- As an automation operator, I want to set the same marker non-interactively via `wl update <id> --do-not-delegate true` in CI or scripts.

Success criteria
- Pressing `D` while an item is focused toggles the `do-not-delegate` tag on that item and shows a toast: "Do-not-delegate: ON" / "Do-not-delegate: OFF".
- The item's list row and detail pane display a visible marker/icon when the tag is present.
- A CLI convenience flag `--do-not-delegate true|false` can add/remove the tag and is documented in `CLI.md`.
- Unit tests cover TUI key handling, toast feedback, tag add/remove, and the new CLI flag; automated tests pass locally.
- The change is implemented as idempotent tag add/remove and does not require a DB schema migration.

Constraints
- Persist the setting as a tag named `do-not-delegate` on the work item (no DB schema changes).
- Follow existing TUI keybinding patterns and use centralized constants in `src/tui/constants.ts` when present.
- Avoid breaking existing hotkeys and respect help overlay conventions.
- Keep behavior idempotent: toggling an already-present tag is a no-op except for feedback.

Existing state
- There is an existing work item: WL-0MLHNPSGP0N397NX titled "Do not auto-assign shortcut" with a short description; it is at stage `idea` and assigned to Map.
- The TUI already supports many shortcuts (R, N, U, /, etc.); examples and tests exist showing how to add keybindings, update help, and test behavior.
- `src/tui/constants.ts`, `src/tui/controller.ts`, and `src/tui/components/help-menu.ts` are the primary places to add the new binding and help entry.
- The CLI already supports tag add/remove patterns; the proposed `--do-not-delegate` convenience flag will call the existing tag update path.

Desired change
- Add a TUI keyboard shortcut `D` that toggles the `do-not-delegate` tag on the currently selected item.
  - Show a toast message indicating new state and update the row/detail marker immediately.
  - Update the help overlay to include the `D` shortcut entry.
- Add a CLI convenience option: `wl update <id> --do-not-delegate true|false` which maps to tag add/remove.
- Add unit tests for the TUI handler, toast/marker behavior, and the CLI flag.
- Update `CLI.md` and any in-TUI help text to document the flag and tag name.

Related work
- Work items:
  - WL-0MKX5ZV9M0IZ8074 — Centralize commands and constants (in_progress) — affects where to register/document the shortcut.
  - WL-0MLK58NHL1G8EQZP — Extract TUI keyboard shortcuts to constants (in_progress) — relevant for implementation location.
  - WL-0MLGW96KF1YLIVQ3 — Add 'wl reviewed' CLI helper and TUI support (idea) — example pattern for CLI+TUI toggle helpers.
  - WL-0MKVZ5TN71L3YPD1 — TUI UX improvements (epic) — umbrella for TUI shortcuts and help updates.

Potentially related files
- `src/tui/constants.ts` — add/update named constant for `D` key and help text.
- `src/tui/controller.ts` — attach handler to toggle tag and update UI.
- `src/tui/components/help-menu.ts` — add the `D` entry to help overlay.
- `src/commands/tui.ts` — TUI registration entrypoint (for context).
- `CLI.md` — document `--do-not-delegate` flag.

Notes / decisions captured from interview
- Persist as a tag: `do-not-delegate` (no DB migration required).
- CLI flag: `--do-not-delegate true|false` to add/remove tag via existing update code path.
- GitHub label sync: handled automatically by existing code when tags map to labels; if not, surface an implementation note — but no explicit GitHub label sync is required as part of this work.

Suggested next step (implementation)
1) Implement the TUI and CLI changes on a feature branch:
   - Add `D` key binding to `src/tui/constants.ts` and hook into `src/tui/controller.ts` to toggle the tag using existing tag update helpers.
   - Add help overlay entry in `src/tui/components/help-menu.ts`.
   - Add a CLI convenience flag handler in the update command path to accept `--do-not-delegate true|false` and translate to tag add/remove.
   - Add unit tests for the TUI handler, toast feedback, marker rendering, and the CLI flag.
   - Update `CLI.md` and in-TUI help copy.

Please review this draft for completeness and clarity. If you approve I will run the five conservative reviews and then update the work item WL-0MLHNPSGP0N397NX description and stage to `intake_complete` per the process.

Headline
Display clickable dependency links ("Blocking" and "Blocked by") in the TUI Details pane so users can transiently inspect related work without leaving the TUI.

Problem statement
When displaying issue metadata in the TUI Details pane, dependency relationships are not shown as actionable links. Users need clear, clickable dependency output so they can quickly inspect related work from the Details pane (e.g. "Blocking" and "Blocked by").

Users
- Developers and triage engineers who read work item metadata in the TUI.
- Example user stories:
  - As a developer, I want to click a dependency shown in the Details pane and open that work item's details so I can quickly review blockers and follow-ups.
  - As a release coordinator, I want to see whether an item is "Blocking" or "Blocked by" at a glance so I can prioritise actions.

Success criteria
- Details pane shows dependency sections for both "Blocking" and "Blocked by" when applicable.
- Each dependency is rendered as a link labelled "WL-<id> — <short title>" and activating it opens the referenced item using the TUI's existing transient details behaviour.
- When there are more than 5 dependencies in a section, the pane shows the first 5 and a "+N more" indicator that can be expanded to reveal the rest.
- If no dependencies exist, the Details pane shows "Dependencies: None" (or equivalent messaging).
- Changes are implemented in the TUI codebase and covered by at least one unit or integration test that verifies rendering and activation behaviour.

Constraints
- Respect existing TUI navigation patterns: activation should use the same transient modal/inspection behaviour already used for clicking IDs in the Details pane.
- Do not open external browsers from the TUI for dependency navigation.
- Keep the Details pane layout responsive to terminal sizes (avoid unbounded growth—use +N more or collapse).

Existing state
- Current work item: WL-0MLLGKZ7A1HUL8HU (this intake). Title: "Add links to dependencies in the metadata output of the details pane in the TUI." Description currently says: "When displaying issue metadata in the TUI Details pane include dependencies if there are any. Show \"Dependencies: None\" if there are none and \"Blocking: <ID>, <ID>\" and \"Blocked by: <ID>, <ID>\" if there are some".
- Relevant code locations:
  - src/tui/components/detail.ts — Details pane component (rendering area, copy-id button)
  - src/tui/components/index.ts — components entry (wiring)
  - src/tui/controller.ts — selection/interaction controller
  - src/tui/state.ts — work item selection/state handling

Desired change
- Render "Blocking" and "Blocked by" sections in the Details pane when dependencies exist.
- For each dependency, render an interactive label: "WL-<id> — <short title>". Activation should open the referenced item using the same transient details/modal behaviour that existing ID clicks use.
- When a section has more than 5 entries, show first 5 and a "+N more" control to expand the rest.
- If a dependency has an associated GitHub issue number, do not expose an external link in the default UI.
- Add tests verifying rendering, truncation (+N more), and activation behaviour.

Related work
- Files (potentially relevant):
  - src/tui/components/detail.ts — detail pane implementation used to render content and host interactive widgets.
  - src/tui/controller.ts — input handling and navigation (may require wiring to support link activation).
  - src/tui/state.ts — work item selection and lookup utilities.
- Worklog items:
  - Add wl dep command (WL-0ML2VPUOT1IMU5US) — related feature for dependency tracking; may inform data shapes.
  - Enable description to be a file (WL-0MKXAUQYM1GEJUAN) — shows prior work on description handling and intake file conventions.

Related work (automated report)

- WL-0ML2VPUOT1IMU5US — Add wl dep command
  The completed 'Add wl dep command' feature implements CLI commands to record, remove, and list dependency edges. This is directly relevant as it defines the CLI-side shape and human/JSON output for dependency edges that the TUI Details pane should display and link to.

- WL-0ML4TFSGF1SLN4DT — Persist dependency edges
  This work item implements persistent storage for dependency edges (data layer and JSONL embedding). It is relevant because the Details pane must read and render dependency relationships that are persisted by these storage changes.

- WL-0ML4TFT1V1Z0SHGF — wl dep list
  This item implements the 'dep list' human output with inbound/outbound sections. It documents expected presentation of dependency lists (sectioning and fields) which can inform the Details pane layout and truncation behaviour (+N more).

- src/tui/components/detail.ts
  The Details pane component hosts the detail content and interactive widgets. This is the primary location to render dependency sections and attach activation handlers for clickable dependency entries.

- src/tui/controller.ts
  The TUI controller wires selection, input handling, and activation behaviour; it contains utilities for ID decoration and click/activation handling. Activation of a dependency link should reuse the controller's transient details/modal behaviour described here.

- src/tui/state.ts
  State handling (itemsById, childrenMap, lookup utilities) is used by the TUI to resolve work item titles and lookup referenced IDs. Ensure any rendering of "WL-<id> — <short title>" uses the same lookup/data shapes provided by this module.

Notes and conservative decisions:
- I only included completed/explicit dependency work items and the small set of TUI files that clearly host the Details pane and interaction logic. I avoided more distant docs or tests even if they mention "dependency" to reduce false positives.
- Suggested next step: append this report under a clearly labelled "Related work (automated report)" section in WL-0MLLGKZ7A1HUL8HU, then (optionally) link these work items in the intake description using their WL-IDs.

Risks & assumptions

- Risk: scope creep — adding UI affordances can lead to requests for richer dependency management (edit, add, remove) during implementation. Mitigation: record any additional feature requests as separate work items and keep this work focused on read-only rendering and navigation.
- Risk: performance/latency when resolving many referenced items for titles. Mitigation: use cached lookups where available and limit initial render to first 5 entries per section.

- Activation behaviour: Open in the TUI details pane using the existing transient modal/inspection behaviour (consistent with current ID click behaviour).

Problem statement

Add tooling to collect per-test timing information when running the test suite (Vitest) so maintainers can identify slow tests and decide which tests should be converted to integration-only or optimized.

Users

- Primary: Core maintainers running the test suite locally and in CI to diagnose slow tests and improve test-suite reliability and speed.
- Secondary: Contributors who need to understand test run durations to limit PR size and avoid long-running tests.

Success criteria

- A script/command exists (e.g. `npm run test:timings`) that runs the test suite and emits a machine-readable timings report (JSON and CSV) in the project root (CSV optional but recommended).
- The timings report includes per-test duration (ms), test file path, full test title, and a timestamp; report generation should be reproducible and documented.
- A README section documents how to run the timings, interpret the output, and a suggested threshold for "slow" tests (e.g. top 5% or >500ms).
- The report is produced without changing existing test behaviour (tests still pass the same) and the full project test suite passes when the timings run is executed.
- Tests and CI are not modified in a way that breaks current pipelines; any changes must be opt-in (separate script) and not alter default `npm test` behavior.

Finished Completeness review: ensured explicit JSON+CSV output, clarified field names.

Constraints

- Use Vitest's existing reporter/plugin API or a small wrapper script; avoid forking the test runner.
- Keep the change minimally invasive: provide a separate command (`test:timings`) rather than modifying default `test` scripts used by CI.
- Output must not include secrets or environment-specific data. Respect `.gitignore` for any generated files.

Risks & assumptions

- Risk: Report may be noisy if tests are parallelized; mitigation: document that timings reflect wall-clock durations and include worker/process info when available.
- Risk: Adding reporters could change timing behaviour slightly; mitigation: keep this as an opt-in script and avoid modifying test code paths.
- Assumption: Vitest version in package.json supports reporter/plugin API required. If not, a minimal wrapper that parses `--reporter` or `--outputFile` will be used.
- Mitigation for scope creep: any additional features (aggregated dashboards, CI integration) will be captured as separate, linked work items instead of expanding this item.

Finished Risks & assumptions review: added concise risks, mitigations, and scope-scope mitigation note.

Existing state

- The repository uses Vitest for tests and already has an npm script `test:timings` that references `./scripts/test-timings.cjs` in package.json. There is an existing work item WL-0MLLHF9GX1VYY0H0 tracking a task with this title (status in-progress, low priority).

Desired change

- Implement or update the `scripts/test-timings.cjs` script (or a new script) to run Vitest with a reporter that collects per-test durations and writes JSON and CSV reports to the repo root (e.g. `test-timings.json`, `test-timings.csv`).
- Add README/tests.md documentation explaining how to run the script, interpret fields, and suggested actions for slow tests.

Polish & handoff

- Final headline: "Collect per-test timings with a dedicated Vitest reporter and produce JSON/CSV reports for slow-test analysis."
- Ensure copy-paste command example is included in README: `npm run test:timings` and location of outputs (project root: `test-timings.json`, `test-timings.csv`).
- Keep the implementation in a single small script (`scripts/test-timings.cjs`) and document expected output file names.

Finished Polish & handoff review: tightened headline and added command example and output locations.

Related work

- WL-0MLLG2HTE1CJ71LZ — parent epic (if present) or related item. (WorkItem summary: parent for testing infra changes.)
- package.json — contains `test:timings` script (path: ./package.json)
- scripts/test-timings.cjs — existing script referenced by package.json (path: ./scripts/test-timings.cjs)

Related work (automated report)

- Parent: WL-0MLLG2HTE1CJ71LZ — Reduce test-suite runtime and prevent CI timeouts (completed)
  - Relevance: This timing-collector task is a direct child of that parent. The parent defines the goal of identifying slow tests and moving expensive tests to integration-only runs; include the parent to preserve traceability.

  - Relevance: This task already ran the CLI tests with per-test timings and documented slow tests and root causes. Use it as the canonical example for:
    - command lines to run (how they invoked vitest),
    - output format examples,
    - thresholds used to pick slow tests (>5s),
    - remediation suggestions (mock/stub git, split integration-only tests).
  - Suggested action: Link this item in the README/tests.md section and copy the example command and sample JSON/CSV output format as a template.

- Harness / bench examples:
  - WL-0MLBWGPIG013LQNQ — Add headless TUI test runner (completed)
    - Relevance: Demonstrates a headless harness pattern and CI-friendly run which may be reused to run vitest in a reproducible, instrumented environment.
  - WL-0MNAL6OXK0072IGQ — Create benchmark harness (completed)

Headline: Permanently prune soft-deleted work items older than a configurable age while avoiding orphaning GitHub issues.

Problem statement
Implement a conservative, auditable `wl doctor prune` command that permanently removes soft-deleted work items older than a configurable threshold while ensuring dependent data (dependency edges, comments) are cleaned and GitHub-linked items are not orphaned.

Users
- Maintainers and operators who need to reclaim storage and remove stale DB rows/edges.
- Automation agents or CI that run periodic maintenance (dry-run reports useful for automation).

User stories
- As a maintainer, I want to preview which soft-deleted items would be pruned before actually removing them so I can verify safety (`--dry-run`).
- As an operator, I want the prune operation to skip items that have an unsynced GitHub issue so I don't orphan external issues.
- As an automation engineer, I want the command to emit JSON output for programmatic consumption.

Success criteria
- `wl doctor prune --dry-run --days 90` lists candidate ids and count with no DB changes (JSON and human-readable output supported).
- `wl doctor prune --days 30` (default) permanently removes candidates older than 30 days and returns pruned ids and count; dependency edges and comments are removed from the DB.
- Items with a `githubIssueNumber` where `updatedAt > githubIssueUpdatedAt` are skipped from pruning (avoids orphaning GitHub issues).
- Command supports `--prefix`, `--days`, `--dry-run`, and `--json` flags and has unit tests for dry-run and actual prune behaviour.

Constraints
- Default retention window is 30 days (per operator confirmation).
- Prune must not remove items that appear unsynced with GitHub (skip when updatedAt > githubIssueUpdatedAt).
- Backups are handled via the repository/git workflow (operator indicates backups via git) so prune will not create automatic DB backups by default.
- Implementation must be reversible in the sense that dry-run is available and outputs candidate ids; actual prune permanently deletes rows when persistent store delete is available.

Existing state
- A `prune` subcommand has already been implemented in `src/commands/doctor.ts` with flags `--days`, `--dry-run`, and JSON output. (See `src/commands/doctor.ts`, `CLI.md`, `DOCTOR_AND_MIGRATIONS.md`.)
- There is an existing work item (this item) tracking the feature: WL-0MLORM1A00HKUJ23 — "Doctor: prune soft-deleted work items" (status: in-progress, stage: idea).
- There is a note in the worklog that prune should avoid removing items that may leave GitHub issues orphaned (ordering note by Map).

Desired change
- Stabilize behaviour: ensure prune skips unsynced GitHub-linked items, document default `--days`=30, ensure JSON and human output are consistent, add unit tests for dry-run and actual prune, and update CLI docs.
- Optionally, add an explicit `--backup` flag in future if operators want automatic DB backups; not in scope unless requested.

Related work
- src/commands/doctor.ts — current prune implementation and CLI wiring (`prune` command and flags).
- CLI.md — documents `wl doctor prune` usage and examples.
- DOCTOR_AND_MIGRATIONS.md — describes pruning policy and examples for `wl doctor prune`.
- WL-0MLWTZBZN1BMM5BN — "Sync locally-deleted items" — ensures deleted items are pushed to GitHub; coordinate ordering with prune to avoid orphaning (see comment by Map).

Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "How should 'wl doctor prune' treat soft-deleted items that have a linked GitHub issue which has not been synced (updatedAt > githubIssueUpdatedAt)?" — Answer (user): "Skip unsynced items (Recommended)". Source: interactive reply. Final: yes. Evidence: WL comment note and repo discussion recommending coordination (see work item WL-0MLWTZBZN1BMM5BN and comment by Map).

- Q: "Is the current default age threshold of 30 days acceptable for pruning, or prefer a different default?" — Answer (user): "Keep 30 days (Recommended)". Source: interactive reply. Final: yes.

- Q: "Should the prune command create an automatic timestamped DB backup before deleting, or rely on dry-run and operator backups?" — Answer (user): "We have backups already via git". Source: interactive reply. Final: yes. Note: As a result, prune will not create automatic backups by default; consider `--backup` opt-in flag in a follow-up.

Appendix: Research & related artifacts (short summaries)
- `src/commands/doctor.ts` — Current implementation: registers `prune` with `--days`, `--dry-run`, collects candidates where status === 'deleted' and older than cutoff, attempts persistent-store delete when available; outputs JSON for dry-run and actual runs. (See lint blocks around `command('prune')`.)
- `CLI.md` — CLI docs include `prune` examples and flags; update recommended to mention skipping unsynced GitHub items and default `--days=30` semantics.
- `DOCTOR_AND_MIGRATIONS.md` — Documentation describing pruning behavior and examples; ensure edits reflect skip-unsynced behaviour.
- Related work item: WL-0MLWTZBZN1BMM5BN — "Sync locally-deleted items"; contains ordering note advising prune skip or coordinate with github push. Consider adding dependency or comment linking these items.

Problem statement
The Item Details dialog does not close when the user presses Escape; it currently only supports the top-right X button. Add standard keyboard close behaviour so keyboard-first users can dismiss the dialog with Esc.

Users
- Primary: TUI users who open item details (keyboard-first users and power users). Example user story: "As a power user, I want to close the Item Details dialog with Esc so I can keep my hands on the keyboard and work faster."

Success criteria
- Pressing Esc while the Item Details dialog is open closes the dialog reliably across platforms and contexts.
- No regressions in existing dialog behavior: other dialog controls and focus management remain unchanged.
- Unit or integration tests cover the ESC close behaviour and run green in the suite.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

Constraints
- Preserve existing accessibility/focus behavior: focus must be managed so keyboard users and screen readers continue to work correctly.
- Minimise scope: prefer a small, well-tested change to add ESC handling rather than a large refactor, unless refactoring is necessary to implement the behavior cleanly.

Risks & assumptions
- Risk: Adding global key handlers can interfere with other keyboard shortcuts or nested components. Mitigation: register/unregister the handler when the dialog is shown/hidden and scope it to the dialog's focused elements.
- Risk: Focus may not be restored correctly after the dialog closes, impacting keyboard navigation. Mitigation: record and restore focus to the originating component after close; add tests for focus behaviour.
- Assumption: There exists shared dialog helper code or patterns for ESC handling in the codebase (agent inference based on other dialogs). If not, a small helper should be introduced rather than adding ad-hoc handlers.
- Scope-scope creep risk: Additional desired improvements (e.g., refactoring the dialog system) should be captured as separate work items rather than expanded here. Mitigation: record additional opportunities as linked work items.

Existing state
- Current description (from WL-0MLPRA0VC185TUVZ): "The Item Details Dialog can only be dismissed by clicking the X in the top right. Remove the X and its handler, replace it with the standardized ESC handler to close the dialog. If this means the dialog should be refactored go ahead and do that."
- Code references of likely interest: UI dialog component implementations and the Item Details dialog file in src/tui/components or similar. There is existing dialog helper code elsewhere in the codebase that standardises ESC handlers for other dialogs.

Desired change
- Add a keyboard handler so Esc closes the Item Details dialog. If the dialog currently implements a custom close handler tied to the X button, update it to use the shared dialog close API or wire the ESC key to the same handler.
- Remove or repurpose the X button if team decides the visual affordance should change; otherwise, keep the X while also supporting Esc.

Related work
- WL-0MLLGKZ7A1HUL8HU — Add links to dependencies in the metadata output of the details pane in the TUI. (related to the Item Details pane)
- WL-0MLOXOHAI1J833YJ — Render responses from opencode in TUI as markdown content. (TUI rendering concerns)
- WL-0MLSDDACP1KWNS50 — TUI does not start when there are no items. (general TUI stability work)
- Code: src/tui/components/dialogs.ts — contains the Item Details dialog implementation and the detailClose close control that should be updated to wire ESC handling.

Related work (automated report)
- WL-0MMNB77CF15497ZK — "dialogs don't dismiss" — Epic addressing dialog lifecycle issues where dialogs remain open after their workflows complete; likely shares root causes and tests. (worklog)
- WL-0MLLGKZ7A1HUL8HU — "Add links to dependencies in the metadata output of the details pane in the TUI." — Related to the Item Details pane and recent changes to the details display which may affect layout or focus. (worklog)
- WL-0MLOXOHAI1J833YJ — "Render responses from opencode in TUI as markdown content." — Related to detail pane rendering; changes here could affect how the detail modal manages content and focus. (worklog)
- src/tui/components/dialogs.ts — Implementation file for dialogs including the Item Details modal and the detailClose control. Update here to attach/detach Esc handling and restore focus on close. (repo)
- tests/tui-integration.test.ts — contains tests that reference the 'Item Details' label, useful for integration test updates after the change. (repo)

Note: This report is conservative — included items have clear, documented relevance to dialog lifecycle, detail-pane rendering, or tests that reference the Item Details modal.

Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers
- Q: "May I ask follow-up questions during the intake interview?" — Answer (seed instruction): "do not ask questions". Source: seed argument provided to the intake run. Final: yes (agent followed instruction and did not ask additional clarifying questions).

Headline
Enable Esc to close the Item Details dialog so keyboard-first users can dismiss it without using the mouse.

- False positives in "wl next" due to scanning comments for blocker phrases.

Acceptance criteria
- Any logic that infers blockers from comment text is removed.
- Blocking determination uses only work item children and formal dependencies.
- "wl next" no longer flags items as blocked based solely on comments.

## Summary

Add move mode state tracking to TuiState and a utility to compute all descendants of a given item, preventing circular reparenting.

## User Story

As a TUI developer implementing move mode, I need a state model and descendant detection utility so that the move mode UI can track which item is being moved and which items are invalid targets (descendants of the source).

## Acceptance Criteria

- `TuiState` (or a companion type) includes a `moveMode` field with `sourceId`, `active` flag, and `descendantIds` set
- `getDescendants(state, itemId)` returns the complete set of descendant IDs for any item
- Descendant detection correctly identifies all descendants at any nesting depth; tested with a hierarchy of at least 5 levels
- Unit tests verify descendant computation for flat, nested, and edge cases (no children, item not found)

## Minimal Implementation

- Add `MoveMode` type to `src/tui/types.ts`
- Add `getDescendants()` function to `src/tui/state.ts`
- Add `enterMoveMode()` / `exitMoveMode()` state helpers
- Unit tests in `tests/tui/` for state transitions and descendant detection

## Dependencies

None (foundational feature)

## Deliverables

- Types (`MoveMode` in `src/tui/types.ts`)
- State helpers (`src/tui/state.ts`)
- Unit tests

## Related Files

- `src/tui/types.ts` — Type definitions
- `src/tui/state.ts` — Tree state module with `buildVisibleNodes`, `childrenMap`, parent/child mapping

## Summary

Render visual indicators during move mode: highlight the source item (color + marker), dim/grey-out descendants, and display contextual footer instructions.

## User Story

As a TUI user in move mode, I want clear visual feedback showing which item I am moving, which targets are invalid (descendants), and instructions for how to complete or cancel the operation.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Source item is rendered with a distinct background/foreground color AND a prefix marker (e.g. `[M]` or `▶`)
- Descendant items of the source are visually dimmed/greyed; pressing `m`/Enter on a greyed-out descendant produces no action (no-op)
- Footer displays: `Moving: <title> (<ID>) — select target, press m/Enter; Esc to cancel`
- When move mode exits (cancel or success), all visual indicators are removed and the tree renders normally
- Valid target items retain their normal styling

## Minimal Implementation

- Modify tree line rendering logic in controller (the list line building path) to check move mode state
- Apply color styling for source item and dim styling for descendants during rendering
- Add prefix marker to source item line
- Update footer content during move mode
- Restore default rendering on exit
- Integration tests verifying visual output lines contain expected markers/styles

## Dependencies

- Move mode state and descendant detection (WL-0MLQXVUI91SIY9KM)
- Move mode keybinding and activation (WL-0MLQXW5MX1YKW5H1)

## Deliverables

- Rendering changes in controller/list rendering
- Footer update logic
- Integration tests

- `src/tui/controller.ts` — Tree rendering and footer management

## Summary

Handle target selection during move mode: pressing `m`/Enter on a valid target executes `wl update <source-id> --parent <target-id>`, refreshes the tree, and follows the moved item.

## User Story

As a TUI user in move mode, I want to select a target parent by navigating to it and pressing `m` or Enter, so the selected item is reparented under the target without me typing any IDs.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Pressing `m` or Enter on a valid (non-descendant, non-source) target executes reparent via `wl update`
- Tree refreshes after successful reparent
- New parent is auto-expanded and cursor follows the moved item (scroll to moved item, select it)
- Success toast is displayed: `Moved <title> under <target-title>`
- Error toast is displayed if `wl update` fails, and the tree remains unchanged
- Move mode exits after execution regardless of success or failure, returning to normal navigation state

## Minimal Implementation

- Add target confirmation handler in controller's move mode key handler
- Execute `wl update <source-id> --parent <target-id>` via the existing CLI/API integration
- Call tree refresh, expand the target parent, and scroll to moved item
- Show toast via existing toast/notification mechanism
- Integration tests for success and error paths with mocked wl update

## Dependencies

- Move mode keybinding and activation (WL-0MLQXW5MX1YKW5H1)
- Move mode visual feedback (WL-0MLQXWHZD107999R)

## Deliverables

- Reparent execution logic
- Tree refresh + auto-expand + cursor follow
- Toast messages (success and error)
- Integration tests

## Related Files

- `src/tui/controller.ts` — Controller with existing tree refresh, toast, and CLI execution patterns
- `src/tui/state.ts` — Tree state rebuild after reparent
- `src/commands/update.ts` — CLI update command that handles `--parent`

## Summary

When the source item is selected as its own target in move mode, detach it from its parent and promote it to root level.

## User Story

As a TUI user, I want to detach an item from its parent by selecting the item itself as the target during move mode, so I can promote items to top-level when they no longer belong under a specific parent.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Selecting the source item itself as the target during move mode clears its parent (moves to root)
- The operation calls `wl update <source-id> --parent ""` (or equivalent to clear parentId)
- Success toast: `Moved <title> to root level`
- Tree refreshes and cursor follows the item at its new root position
- If the item is already at root level and self-selected, show toast: `<title> is already at root level` and exit move mode
- Attempting to unparent an item that has children does not orphan the children — they remain attached to the moved item

## Minimal Implementation

- Add self-select detection in the target confirmation handler
- Execute parent-clearing update via `wl update`
- Handle already-at-root edge case
- Unit test for self-select detection
- Integration test for full unparent flow including children preservation

## Dependencies

- Target selection and reparent execution (WL-0MLQXWUCY08EREBY)

## Deliverables

- Self-select handler logic
- Edge case handling (already at root, children preservation)
- Unit and integration tests

## Related Files

- `src/tui/controller.ts` — Controller with move mode handler
- `src/commands/update.ts` — CLI update; passing empty parent clears parentId
