# Non-/wl command dispatch in Herdr plugin (WL-0MS4GHV30000HXL0)

## Problem Statement

The Herdr worklist plugin's chord dispatch mechanism (`dispatchChordCommand`) currently only handles `/wl <stage>` filter commands. Any other command type — text-insertion templates (`!!wl`), agent workflow invocations (`/skill:`, `/intake`, `/plan`), and audit/review compounds — is silently dropped when a chord resolves, because `dispatchChordCommand` returns `false` and the chord completion handler falls through to normal key handling instead of outputting the resolved command. In contrast, the Pi TUI extension handles ALL command types uniformly: when a chord or shortcut resolves, the command string is output via `ctx.ui.setEditorText()` and inserted into the chat editor for execution. The Herdr plugin needs an equivalent mechanism.

## Users

- **Herdr users** who rely on keyboard shortcuts for daily work item management and expect consistent behaviour with the Pi TUI
- **Agent operators** who invoke skill commands (`/skill:implement`, `/skill:audit`) and workflow commands (`/intake`, `/plan`) via chord shortcuts
- **Plugin developers** who need a clean extensible dispatch architecture

### Example User Stories

- As a **Herdr power user**, I want to press `u p h` to set a work item to high priority, and have the `!!wl update <id> --priority high` command output to the editor for execution — rather than it being silently swallowed.
- As an **agent operator**, I want to press `i` (or a chord) to invoke `/skill:implement <id>` and have the command appear in the editor ready for execution.
- As a **producer**, I want to press `r` to insert the `!!wl reviewed <id> && wl comment add ...` template for a producer review comment.
- As a **developer**, I want the dispatch infrastructure to support new command types without modifying core TUI logic.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `runWorklistTui` accepts a new `onCommand` callback parameter (or equivalent stdout-output mechanism) that receives resolved non-/wl commands
- [ ] When a chord resolves to a command that is NOT a `/wl` filter command, the resolved command string is passed to the callback / output to stdout with a distinguishable mechanism
- [ ] `/wl <stage>` filter commands continue to be handled directly by `dispatchChordCommand` (internal state mutation, no stdout output) — unchanged behaviour
- [ ] Text-insertion template commands (`!!wl update`, `!!wl close`, `!!wl delete`, `!!wl search`) are recognized and routed through the output mechanism
- [ ] Agent workflow commands (`/skill:implement`, `/skill:audit`, `/intake`, `/plan`) are recognized and routed through the output mechanism
- [ ] Audit/review compound commands (`!!wl reviewed`, `!!wl reviewed ... && wl audit-set ...`) are recognized and routed through the output mechanism
- [ ] When a resolved command contains `<id>` placeholders, they are replaced with the currently selected work item's ID before output
- [ ] When no item is selected and the command requires `<id>`, the command is NOT dispatched (graceful no-op)
- [ ] The Herdr main entry point (`index.ts`) passes the appropriate callback / handles the new output mechanism
- [ ] All child work items (WL-0MS4GICML0015GW5, WL-0MS4GIMBD008GWVM, WL-0MS4GIMB80084PC5) are completed
- [ ] Full project test suite passes with the new changes
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments and README

> **Note:** CHANGELOG.md is excluded from this list. It is managed automatically by the ship skill's release pipeline.

## Constraints

- **No breaking changes to existing behaviour:** `/wl` filter commands must continue working unchanged (internal dispatch, no stdout output)
- **Backward compatible API:** Adding `onCommand` callback must not break existing callers (optional parameter with default no-op)
- **No Pi TUI coupling:** The dispatch mechanism is Herdr-specific — no changes to Pi TUI code
- **Consistent with Herdr's output model:** Follow the same stdout-based pattern as existing item ID output (`console.log`)
- **Children remain unchanged:** The child work items already have their own detailed ACs — this epic does not redefine them

## Existing State

Currently, the chord completion handler in `runWorklistTui`'s `onData` callback at `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` checks if `dispatchChordCommand` returns `true`. If it returns `false` (command not handled), the code falls through to normal key handling and the resolved command is lost.

```typescript
if (command && dispatchChordCommand(command, state)) {
  render();
  return;
}
// Unknown command — fall through to normal handling
```

The `dispatchChordCommand` function only handles `/wl <stage>` patterns:

```typescript
function dispatchChordCommand(command: string, state: WorkItemListState): boolean {
  const wlStageMatch = command.match(/^\/wl\s+(\S+)$/);
  if (wlStageMatch) {
    // ... apply filter ...
    return true;
  }
  return false; // Everything else is dropped
}
```

The current `shortcuts.json` at `packages/herdr/src/shortcuts.json` contains 8 entries: `c` (create), `n` (intake), `p` (plan), `s` (search), and 4 stage-filter chords (`f-i`, `f-n`, `f-p`, `f-r`).

The shortcut infrastructure (`ShortcutRegistry`, chord state management, help-line hints) is already fully implemented and functional.

## Desired Change

1. **Output mechanism** — Modify the chord completion path in `runWorklistTui` to accept an `onCommand` callback (or equivalent mechanism) for non-filter commands. When `dispatchChordCommand` returns `false`, pass the resolved command to the callback instead of dropping it.
2. **Command routing** — Enhance or replace `dispatchChordCommand` to recognize all command families:
   - `/wl <stage>` — handled internally (existing behaviour)
   - `!!wl update`, `!!wl close`, `!!wl delete`, `!!wl search` — routed to output
   - `/skill:implement`, `/skill:audit` — routed to output
   - `/intake`, `/plan` — routed to output
   - `!!wl reviewed`, compound audit commands — routed to output
3. **ID substitution** — Replace `<id>` tokens in resolved commands with the selected item's ID before output (or gracefully no-op if no selection and `<id>` is required)
4. **Main entry point** — Update `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` to pass the `onCommand` callback to `runWorklistTui` (outputting the command string via `console.log` with a distinguishable prefix or the raw command)

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — `dispatchChordCommand`, chord completion handler in `runWorklistTui`, `onCommand` callback plumbing
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — Pass `onCommand` callback to `runWorklistTui`
- `tests/herdr/shortcuts.test.ts` — Tests for non-/wl command dispatch, callback invocation, ID substitution, graceful no-op for missing selection

## Related Work

### Related work items

- **WL-0MS4GICML0015GW5** (Stdout output infrastructure for resolved commands) — Child task: implements the output mechanism this epic orchestrates
- **WL-0MS4GIMBD008GWVM** (Wire text-insertion template commands) — Child task: routes `!!wl` commands through the output mechanism
- **WL-0MS4GIMB80084PC5** (Wire agent workflow and audit commands) — Child task: routes `/skill:`, `/intake`, `/plan`, audit compounds through the output mechanism
- **WL-0MS4FHW290053SH4** (Missing text-insertion shortcuts) — Dependents on this epic for the dispatch mechanism before shortcuts can produce usable output
- **WL-0MS39YPR5005MJ81** (Feature gap analysis: Pi TUI Worklog extension vs Herdr plugin) — Parent epic cataloguing all gaps; this item addresses the dispatch infrastructure gap

### Related files

- `packages/herdr/src/shortcuts.json` — Currently has 8 entries; will be extended by WL-0MS4FHW290053SH4 once dispatch is working
- `packages/herdr/src/shortcut-config.ts` — ShortcutRegistry implementation (assumed complete, no changes expected)
- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/shortcuts.json` — Reference implementation showing all 21 Pi TUI shortcuts

### Related work (automated report)

#### Related work items
- **WL-0MRMCO4VB009HIJL** — Tests: getChordByPrefix and arbitrary-depth dispatch (completed) — Tests for chord infrastructure in Pi TUI that this epic's dispatch mechanism builds on
- **WL-0MQEBM6OM004Q1Q7** — Chord dispatch and help text in browse views (completed) — Original Pi TUI chord dispatch implementation; this epic ports equivalent behaviour to Herdr
- **WL-0MQEBLZIK002JTXI** — Tests: Chord schema, registry, and dispatch (completed) — Tests for the chord schema and ShortcutRegistry that Herdr's registry is based on

#### Repository file matches
- `packages/herdr/src/shortcuts.json` — Matches on: chord, command, dispatch, filter, herdr, idea, intake, key, label, plan, review, search, shortcuts, stage, view, wl — The config file that this epic's expanded dispatch will support
- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/shortcuts.json` — Matches on: audit, chord, close, command, delete, dispatch, filter, herdr, implement, intake, key, label, plan, priority, search, shortcuts, stage, update, view, wl — Reference implementation with 21 shortcut entries; the dispatch model this epic mirrors

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions and Answers

- Q: "When a chord resolves to a non-/wl command, should the output be printed to stdout with a prefix (like `CMD:`), or should `runWorklistTui` return the command, or should there be a callback?"
  - Answer (Map, via existing context): The child work item WL-0MS4GICML0015GW5 proposes an `onCommand` callback parameter. The preferred approach is an `onCommand` callback passed to `runWorklistTui`, which the caller (`index.ts`) can wire to `console.log` or other output. Source: child work item WL-0MS4GICML0015GW5 problem statement.

- Q: "Should the dispatch recognize commands by prefix matching, full matching, or both?"
  - Answer (inferred from existing code): The existing `/wl` dispatch uses regex matching (`^\/wl\s+(\S+)$`). For text-insertion templates, prefix matching (e.g., `!!wl update` pattern for any `!!wl update ...` variant) is more appropriate since template commands vary. Source: inspection of `dispatchChordCommand` in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`.

- Q: "Is the `dispatchChordCommand` function the right place for command routing, or should there be a separate dispatch module?"
  - Answer (inferred): Keeping routing in `dispatchChordCommand` is simplest and minimizes diff. The function is small (12 lines) and can be extended with additional branches. A separate module is overengineering at this stage. Source: simplicity principle / existing architecture review.

## Risks and Assumptions

- **Scope-creep risk:** If the `onCommand` callback proves insufficient (e.g., the Herdr pane needs more than raw stdout), a larger architectural change may be needed. This is tracked as a discovery task; any such change would create a new work item rather than expanding this epic.
- **Assumption:** The `onCommand` callback is the right abstraction. If the Herdr editor integration layer needs a different interface, this epic's child items can adapt without changing the callback contract.
- **Assumption:** Child work items capture the full implementation detail — this epic drives architectural alignment and completion verification only.
- **Risk:** Command routing in `dispatchChordCommand` may become unwieldy as more command families are added; the function should remain focused on routing logic with command output delegated to the callback.
- **Mitigation:** Adding targeted tests for each command family to ensure the dispatch mechanism correctly routes all command types.
- **Mitigation:** Use prefix-matching constants or a simple route table rather than nested conditionals to keep `dispatchChordCommand` maintainable.

# Wire text-insertion template commands (WL-0MS4GIMBD008GWVM)

## Problem Statement

When the Herdr worklist plugin's chord system resolves a text-insertion template command (e.g., `!!wl update <id> --priority high`), the command must be output for the Herdr pane to insert into the editor. The `executeResolvedCommand` infrastructure (implemented by sibling child WL-0MS4GICML0015GW5) now routes non-`/wl` commands through an `onCommand` callback, performing `<id>` placeholder substitution. Remaining work includes: (a) verifying `dispatchChordCommand` pattern matching doesn't inadvertently intercept `!!wl` commands, (b) adding targeted tests for `!!wl` command families flowing through the full dispatch path, and (c) verifying the integration between `dispatchChordCommand`, `executeResolvedCommand`, and the chord completion handler.

## Users

- **Herdr power users** who press chord shortcuts to update work item priority, status, title, close, delete, or search — expecting the `!!wl` template to appear in the editor ready for execution.
- **Plugin developers** who need a clear test suite confirming that text-insertion commands flow correctly through the dispatch chain.

### Example User Stories

- As a **Herdr power user**, I want to press `u p h` to set priority to high and see `!!wl update WL-001 --priority high` inserted into the editor, so I can execute it with one more keystroke.
- As a **developer**, I want test coverage confirming that `!!wl update`, `!!wl close`, `!!wl delete`, and `!!wl search` all resolve through `executeResolvedCommand` → `onCommand` with correct `<id>` substitution.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `dispatchChordCommand` is verified to return `false` for `!!wl update`, `!!wl close`, `!!wl delete`, and `!!wl search` command prefixes (so they fall through to `executeResolvedCommand` for `onCommand` routing)
- [ ] `executeResolvedCommand` routes `!!wl update`, `!!wl close`, `!!wl delete`, and `!!wl search` commands through the `onCommand` callback
- [ ] `<id>` placeholders are replaced with the selected item's ID for all four command families
- [ ] When no item is selected and the command requires `<id>`, dispatch returns `'noop'` (graceful no-op — not dispatched)
- [ ] Tests verify the full dispatch chain for each command family: chord resolution → `executeResolvedCommand` → `onCommand` invocation with correct arguments
- [ ] All existing tests continue to pass
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments and relevant README entries

> **Note:** CHANGELOG.md is **excluded** from this list. It is managed automatically by the ship skill's release pipeline.

## Constraints

- **No breaking changes:** Existing `/wl` filter commands must continue to dispatch internally (return `'dispatched'`). Existing keyboard navigation must remain unchanged.
- **Consistent return types:** `executeResolvedCommand` must continue returning `'dispatched' | 'callback' | 'noop'` per the established contract.
- **No new dependencies:** All routing is implemented via existing infrastructure (`dispatchChordCommand` → `executeResolvedCommand` → `onCommand`).
- **Backward compatible:** The `onCommand` callback is optional; callers that don't provide it must continue to work (commands without `<id>` silently output, commands with `<id>` silently no-op).

## Existing State

The stdout output infrastructure (WL-0MS4GICML0015GW5) is **completed and in review**. It provides:

1. `executeResolvedCommand(command, state, onCommand?)` — routes non-`/wl` commands through `onCommand` callback with `<id>` substitution. Returns `'dispatched' | 'callback' | 'noop'`.
2. `runWorklistTui` accepts an `onCommand` callback via the `options` parameter.
3. The chord completion handler calls `executeResolvedCommand` for every resolved chord command.

Existing tests in `tests/herdr/shortcuts.test.ts` cover:
- `!!wl search test` routed to callback ✓
- `!!wl update <id> --priority high` with `<id>` substitution ✓
- No-op when no item selected ✓
- Multiple `<id>` occurrences ✓
- Commands without `<id>` passed to callback when no items ✓

Remaining work:
- Verify `dispatchChordCommand` does NOT intercept `!!wl` commands (it should return `false` for non-`/wl` patterns)
- Add targeted tests for `!!wl close`, `!!wl delete`, `!!wl search`, and `!!wl update` patterns flowing through the full dispatch chain
- Integration test: chord resolution → `executeResolvedCommand` → `onCommand`

## Desired Change

1. **Verify `dispatchChordCommand` pattern matching** — Ensure the function's regex (`/^\/wl\s+(\S+)$/`) does not match `!!wl` prefixes (it currently doesn't, but verify with explicit tests)
2. **Add `dispatchChordCommand` tests** — Test that the function returns `false` for `!!wl update`, `!!wl close`, `!!wl delete`, `!!wl search`, and `true` for `/wl idea|intake|plan|review`
3. **Add integration tests** — Add test cases verifying the full chord dispatch path for each `!!wl` command family
4. **No code changes expected in `worklist.ts`** — The routing infrastructure (`executeResolvedCommand`, `onCommand`) is already complete. Any necessary changes will be discovered during testing.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — `dispatchChordCommand` and `executeResolvedCommand` (verify no changes needed)
- `tests/herdr/shortcuts.test.ts` — Add tests for `dispatchChordCommand` return values and `!!wl` command families

## Related work

### Related work items

- **WL-0MS4GHV30000HXL0** — Non-`/wl` command dispatch in Herdr plugin (parent epic, intake_complete)
- **WL-0MS4GICML0015GW5** — Stdout output infrastructure for resolved commands (sibling child, completed/in_review) — Implements the `executeResolvedCommand` and `onCommand` infrastructure this item builds on
- **WL-0MS4FHW290053SH4** — Missing text-insertion shortcuts (blocked, depends on this dispatch mechanism)
- **WL-0MS4GIMB80084PC5** — Wire agent workflow and audit commands (sibling child, plan_complete)

### Related files

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — Core dispatch functions
- `tests/herdr/shortcuts.test.ts` — Existing tests for `executeResolvedCommand`

### Automated related work report

#### Related work items
- **WL-0MLARH59Q0FY64WN** – TuiController Class (completed) — Tangential: TUI infrastructure, not directly related to dispatch routing.
- **WL-0MKX5ZV3D0OHIIX2** – Add regression tests for mouse click crash and TUI behavior (completed) — Tangential: TUI test infrastructure.
- **WL-0MP14Z8R1002WN2Z** – Add by Type to wl stats (completed) — Tangential: unrelated feature.

#### Repository file matches
- `.worklog/tmp/intake-draft-wire-text-insertion-template-commands-WL-0MS4GIMBD008GWVM.md` — This draft file (self-match, excluded from decisions).
- `packages/tui/extensions/README.md` — Extension documentation referencing shortcut infrastructure.
- `CLI.md` — Root CLI documentation with wl command reference.

## Risks and Assumptions

- **Assumption:** `dispatchChordCommand` returning `false` for `!!wl` commands is the correct behavior (let `executeResolvedCommand` route to `onCommand`). If the design intent was different, a scope-creep risk exists for reworking the dispatch chain.
- **Assumption:** No code changes are needed in `worklist.ts` — only tests. If testing reveals bugs in `dispatchChordCommand` or `executeResolvedCommand`, minor fixes may be needed (scope-limited).
- **Risk:** The `dispatchChordCommand` function's current regex may unexpectedly match `!!wl` commands in edge cases (e.g., `!!wl search something`). Verification tests mitigate this.
- **Scope-creep risk:** If integration with the Herdr editor pane requires changes beyond what `executeResolvedCommand` provides, the scope may expand. Any such changes should be a new work item rather than expanding this task.

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions & Answers

- Q: "Should `dispatchChordCommand` explicitly recognize and handle `!!wl` commands, or should they continue to fall through to `executeResolvedCommand` for routing?"
  - Answer (inferred from code inspection): `dispatchChordCommand` returns `boolean` — `true` = handled internally, `false` = not recognized. For `!!wl` commands, returning `false` is correct because `executeResolvedCommand` catches them and routes to `onCommand`. If `dispatchChordCommand` returned `true` for `!!wl` commands, they would be marked as "dispatched" and NOT routed to the callback. Source: `executeResolvedCommand` code at worklist.ts:1145.

- Q: "What is the minimum testing scope for this work item?"
  - Answer (inferred from ACs and existing state): The existing tests cover `executeResolvedCommand` with `!!wl` commands. What's missing are: (1) tests for `dispatchChordCommand` verifying it returns `false` for `!!wl` prefixes, (2) tests for each `!!wl` command family (`update`, `close`, `delete`, `search`) flowing through the full chain, (3) integration verification that chord resolution → `executeResolvedCommand` → `onCommand` works end-to-end. Source: test file analysis at `tests/herdr/shortcuts.test.ts`.

- Q: "Are there any specific `!!wl` command variants that should not be supported?"
  - Answer (inferred from shortcuts in WL-0MS4FHW290053SH4): The supported `!!wl` variants are:
    - `!!wl update <id> --priority low|medium|high|critical`
    - `!!wl update <id> --status <status> --stage <stage>`
    - `!!wl update <id> --title`
    - `!!wl close <id>`
    - `!!wl delete <id>`
    - `!!wl search [query]`
    These match the shortcuts defined in the "Missing text-insertion shortcuts" work item. Source: WL-0MS4FHW290053SH4 Desired Change section.

# Tab key to expand/collapse children in selection browser

## Problem statement

The Herdr `worklog-selection-list` plugin's selection browser (list view) has no dedicated keyboard shortcut for expanding or collapsing child work items inline. The Enter key selects an item and opens its detail view. The Tab key should handle hierarchical expansion/collapse, providing a clear separation: Enter = select/open detail, Tab = toggle hierarchy.

## Users

- **Herdr users** who navigate hierarchical work items (epics → features → tasks) and want keyboard-driven expand/collapse without entering detail view
- **Power users** who rely on keyboard workflows and expect Tab for hierarchy navigation (consistent with common UX patterns like file trees)

### Example User Stories

- As a **Herdr user**, I want to press Tab on a parent work item to expand its children inline, so I can browse the hierarchy without leaving the list.
- As a **Herdr user**, I want to press Tab again on an expanded parent to collapse its children, so I keep my view uncluttered.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Tab key (`	`) in list mode toggles expand/collapse for the currently selected item when it has loaded children data
- [ ] Tab on an item without children (childCount undefined or 0) is a noop
- [ ] Tab on an item with childCount > 0 but no pre-loaded children data is a noop (children must be pre-fetched for expand to work)
- [ ] Enter continues to work as before — its behavior is unchanged
- [ ] Tab does NOT open detail view — strictly hierarchy expansion only
- [ ] Tab does not trigger chord mode — it is a direct action key
- [ ] All existing tests continue to pass
- [ ] Full project test suite passes with the new changes

## Constraints

- No breaking changes to Enter, Escape, or other existing keybindings
- Tab should not interfere with chord mode (it's a direct action)
- Follows the same expand/collapse logic that `toggleExpand()` already implements

## Existing state

Currently, Tab is unhandled in the selection browser. The `keyToAction()` function in `worklist.ts` does not recognize `	` and returns null. The `handleKeypress()` function does not process Tab. The expand/collapse infrastructure (`expandedItems` set, `toggleExpand()`, `getFlattenedItems()`, ▶/▼ icon rendering) is already fully implemented and triggered only by Enter when the item has pre-loaded children.

Enter currently toggles expand/collapse for items with children data AND opens detail view for items without children. Tab should handle ONLY the expand/collapse aspect, leaving Enter's behavior unchanged.

## Desired change

Add Tab (`	`) handling in `keyToAction()` and `handleKeypress()`:

1. `keyToAction` — Map `	` to a new action like `'toggle-expand'`
2. `handleKeypress` — Handle `'toggle-expand'` action in list mode:
   - If selected item has children data → call `state.toggleExpand(id)` → return `'toggle-expand'`
   - Otherwise → noop (return null)
3. Tab should be identified as a direct key (not starting chord mode) — add `	` to the keys that skip chord leader check

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — Add Tab handling in `keyToAction()` and `handleKeypress()`
- `tests/herdr/hierarchy.test.ts` — Add tests for Tab expand/collapse behavior

## Related work

- **Child-fetching on demand from detail view in Herdr plugin (WL-0MS3AM1UG00036NL)** — Open: Tab in detail view fetches children; this item is about Tab in list view
- **Child-fetching on demand in detail view (WL-0MS4FHZLS003BS4R)** — Completed: implemented the detail view child-fetching
- **Navigation stack for hierarchical browsing (WL-0MS4FI763006105Y)** — Open: hierarchical back-navigation
- **Hierarchical navigation & selection widget (WL-0MS31XU8V005HOAL)** — Completed: base expand/collapse and flattened item display
- **Feature gap analysis (WL-0MS39YPR5005MJ81)** — Parent epic for all feature gaps

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions & Answers

- Q: "Should Tab be a toggle (expand if collapsed, collapse if expanded) matching Enter's existing behavior, or should it only expand children?" — Answer (user@rgardler): "No Enter selects the item and displays the detail view. Add the tab behaviour." Interpretation: Enter's job is select/detail. Tab should be used for expand/collapse. A toggle approach (expand if collapsed, collapse if expanded) is implied for natural UX.

- Q: "For items with childCount > 0 but no pre-loaded children data, should Tab be a noop or trigger on-demand fetching?" — Answer: No answer yet. Defaulting to noop since the feature is about inline expand/collapse of pre-fetched data. On-demand fetching is a separate concern (addressed by WL-0MS3AM1UG00036NL and WL-0MS4FHZLS003BS4R).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scope-creep risk:** Tab could potentially conflict with focus-cycling between panes in some terminal environments. If the Herdr pane intercepts Tab, it must be ensured that focus-cycling still works when no item has children or after Tab-to-expand.

data.description:
## Problem

When expanding a parent work item in the Herdr TUI using the Tab key, the children are displayed twice — each child appears exactly twice in the expanded list.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open the Herdr worklog-selection-list plugin
2. Navigate to a parent work item that has children (e.g., WL-0MS1W8Y1L0059AKP with 7 children)
3. Press Tab to expand the parent
4. Observe: 14 children are shown instead of 7, each unique child appearing twice

## Root Cause

The renderer inside `createListRenderer` (worklist.ts) has its own flattening logic that re-flattens items that are ALREADY flattened by `state.getFlattenedItems()`. 

Flow:
1. `render()` in `runWorklistTui` calls `state.getFlattenedItems()` which produces `[parent, child1, ..., child7]`
2. This already-flattened list is passed to `createListRenderer` as `items`
3. `createListRenderer` has a second flattening pass that checks each item's `children` array — for the parent item, it pushes the 7 children AGAIN
4. Result: `[parent, child1, ..., child7, child1, ..., child7]` (15 items instead of 8)

## Fix

Remove the redundant flattening logic from `createListRenderer`. The items passed to it should be treated as already-flattened. The `expandedItems` parameter is still needed for rendering the expand/collapse icon (`_expanded` flag), but the flattening pass itself should be removed.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Expanding a parent item shows each child exactly once
2. Collapsing and re-expanding works correctly without duplication
3. The expand/collapse icon (▶/▼) continues to render correctly
4. Auto-refresh does not cause duplication
5. All existing tests continue to pass
6. A regression test is added for the flatten-deduplication behavior
data.title: Fix: Children duplicated when expanding parent with Tab in Herdr TUI

data.description:
# Herdr selection list: navigation breaks when parent expanded, add wrap-around

## Problem statement

In the Herdr work item selection list, when a parent item is expanded to reveal its children, the Up/Down navigation cannot reach the last items in the displayed list. This happens because the boundary checking in `moveUp()`, `moveDown()`, `goToLast()`, `_adjustScroll()`, and `_clampSelection()` all use `this.items.length` (only top-level items) instead of the flattened list count which includes children of expanded parents.

Additionally, the list lacks wrap-around navigation — pressing Up at the first item or Down at the last item has no effect, unlike standard terminal UI conventions.

## Users

- **Herdr TUI users** who navigate the work item selection list with arrow keys.
  - As an operator, when I expand a parent item to see its children, I expect to be able to navigate to all children including the last visible item in the flattened list.
  - As an operator, when I press Up at the top of the list, I expect to wrap to the bottom item so I can quickly cycle through items.
  - As an operator, when I press Down at the bottom of the list, I expect to wrap to the top item.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. After expanding a parent item with children, pressing Down navigates all the way to the last child item (not stopping before it).
2. Pressing Up at the first visible item (index 0) wraps to the last visible item in the flattened list.
3. Pressing Down at the last visible item in the flattened list wraps to the first item (index 0).
4. Wrapping only applies when at a list boundary (standard up/down movement within the list is unchanged).
5. When the list is empty (0 items), Up/Down have no effect (no crash).
6. `goToLast()` navigates to the flattened list's last item, not just `this.items.length - 1`.
7. `_adjustScroll()` uses the flattened item count for scroll offset calculation.
8. `pageUp()`/`pageDown()` operate within the flattened list bounds.
9. All existing tests in `tests/herdr/` pass with the new changes.
10. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
11. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

> **Note:** CHANGELOG.md is **excluded** from this list. It is managed automatically by the ship skill's release pipeline.

## Constraints

- Must not break existing keyboard navigation behaviour in the Herdr selection list.
- Must handle the edge case of an empty item list gracefully (no error).
- Must not introduce new dependencies.

## Existing state

- `WorkItemListState` in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` has `items` (top-level items) and `getFlattenedItems()` which returns the display list including children of expanded parents.
- `moveUp()` uses `this.selectedIndex > 0` as its only guard (no wrap).
- `moveDown()` uses `this.selectedIndex < this.items.length - 1` (uses wrong count, no wrap).
- `goToLast()` uses `this.items.length - 1`.
- `_adjustScroll()` uses `this.items.length` for maxOffset.
- `_clampSelection()` uses `this.items.length`.
- The existing TUI browse list (`packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/browse.ts`) already has wrap-around navigation implemented (WL-0MR5KB76Q006OAXG).

## Desired change

Modify the following methods in `WorkItemListState` to use `this.flatCount` (which returns `this.getFlattenedItems().length`) instead of `this.items.length`:

1. **`moveUp()`**: Check bounds against `this.flatCount`; wrap to last when at index 0.
2. **`moveDown()`**: Check bounds against `this.flatCount`; wrap to first when at last.
3. **`goToLast()`**: Navigate to `this.flatCount - 1`.
4. **`_adjustScroll()`**: Use `this.flatCount` for max offset.
5. **`_clampSelection()`**: Consider flatCount when clamping.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — `WorkItemListState` navigation methods
- `tests/herdr/worklist.test.ts` — Tests for navigation and wrapping
- `tests/herdr/hierarchy.test.ts` — Tests for hierarchical navigation with wrapping

## Related work

- WL-0MR5KB76Q006OAXG — "Wrap arrow key navigation in browse selection list" — previously implemented wrapping for the TUI browse selection list (different component, same concept). Provides a reference pattern.

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions & Answers

No clarifying questions required. The seed intent was self-contained and well-defined.

- Q: "What priority?" — Answer (user): "high". Source: interactive request.

This is a different component: the Herdr plugin's selection list in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`. Source: code inspection.

- **Risk: Scroll offset mismatch** — If `_adjustScroll()` uses `flatCount` but `getVisibleItems()` still slices from `this.items`, the visible items could be wrong. Mitigation: verify that `getVisibleItems()` is only used for testing/legacy purposes and not in the main render path. The render callback in `runWorklistTui` calls `state.getFlattenedItems()` directly, so this is low risk.
- **Risk: Wrapping disorientation** — Users may find instant wrap-around confusing without a visual indicator. Mitigation: follow the same pattern as the existing TUI browse implementation which wraps without animation. If requested, a visual cue can be added as a follow-up.
- **Assumption: Single-item wrapping is acceptable** — Wrapping a single-item list onto itself is a no-op by design (selection doesn't change). This matches user expectation.
- **Assumption: No visual indicator of wrap** — The current design does not require a visual animation or indicator when wrapping.

# Align icon prefix in selection list and remove spaces between icons

## Problem

In the Herdr TUI selection list, items have a variable-length icon prefix showing status, stage/audit result, producer review flag, and child count. Currently these icons are joined with spaces (`join(' ')`), and different items have different numbers of visible icons. This causes the item ID and title columns to shift left/right depending on the icon count, breaking vertical alignment.

The user wants:
1. No spaces between icons
2. The columns (item ID, title) to always align regardless of how many icons are present

## Users

- **Herdr TUI users** who browse work items in a selection list. Misaligned columns make it harder to quickly scan items.

### User Stories

- As a Herdr user, I want the icon prefix area to have a consistent width so that item IDs and titles always start at the same column, making the list easier to scan.
- As a Herdr user, I want icons to be directly adjacent without spaces between them, for a cleaner look.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A consistent fixed width is allocated for the entire icon prefix, so item IDs start at the same column regardless of which icons are present.
- There are no spaces between adjacent icons within the prefix (icons are concatenated directly).
- Items with no icons (empty prefix) still appear correctly with column alignment preserved.
- All existing tests in `tests/herdr/worklist.test.ts` and `tests/herdr/icons.test.ts` still pass.
- When `noIcons` mode is active, the prefix area collapses to zero width (no extra padding).

## Constraints

- Changes limited to `packages/herdr/src/icons.ts` and `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`.
- Must be backward compatible — no changes to shortcut/chord behaviors.
- Must handle edge cases: no icons mode, no status, missing optional fields.

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Width estimation risk:** The padding width must be determined statically. If new icons are added later without updating the width, columns will misalign again. Mitigation: define the padding width as a named constant in `icons.ts` with a comment documenting how it was calculated.
- **Horizontal space risk:** A fixed-width prefix may waste horizontal space on narrow terminals. Mitigation: choose the minimum width that accommodates all current icon combinations.
- **noIcons mode risk:** Must collapse to zero width to avoid breaking `--no-icons` Terminal output. Covered by ACs.

## Existing state

Current code in `packages/herdr/src/icons.ts` `getIconPrefix()`:
- Joins core icons with spaces: `[sIcon, secondIcon, prIcon].filter(Boolean).join(' ')`
- Then joins with childSuffix: `[coreIcons, childSuffix].filter(Boolean).join(' ')`

Current code in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` `formatItemLine()`:
- `const iconStr = iconPrefix.length > 0 ? \`\${iconPrefix} \` : '';` — adds a trailing space after icons
- The line format is: `\`\${depthIndent}\${prefix}\${expandIcon}\${iconStr}\${item.id} \${colouredTitle}...\``

Since different items have different combinations of icons (some have child count, some have producer review flag, some don't), the total prefix width varies and columns don't align.

## Desired change

1. **Remove spaces between icons:** Change `join(' ')` to `join('')` in `getIconPrefix()`.
2. **Add fixed-width padding:** After building the icon prefix, pad it to a consistent width so that the item ID that follows always starts at the same column.
   - Determine the maximum possible prefix width (e.g., by looking at all icon strings and child count formats).
   - Pad shorter prefixes with spaces on the right (between the last icon and the item ID).
3. **Remove the trailing space** added in `formatItemLine()` at line 518, since padding will handle spacing.
4. **Update tests** to expect the new format (no spaces between icons, consistent width).

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/icons.ts` — `getIconPrefix()` function: remove spaces between icons, add padding logic.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — `formatItemLine()` at line 517-518, 533: adjust iconStr usage.
- `tests/herdr/icons.test.ts` — tests for getIconPrefix, if any.
- `tests/herdr/worklist.test.ts` — tests for formatItemLine render output.

## Related work

- `WL-0MS4GHV30000HXL0` (discovered-from) — Original work item that introduced icon system in Herdr
- `WL-0MS4FIEN40037GB9` — Total actionable count display in header (also touches formatItemLine)
- `WL-0MS31PYPP0006M8P` — Icon system, stage colouring & group separators (foundational icon work)

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions & Answers

- Q: "Do you want spaces between icons at all?" — Answer (user): "Do not put spaces between icons."
- Q: "Should the icon prefix be padded to a fixed width or should we left-align item IDs?" — Inferred from "Columns should always align no matter how many icons are present": fixed-width padding to ensure alignment.
data.title: Align icon prefix in selection list and remove spaces between icons

# Problem

When users type shortcut commands in the Herdr plugin (e.g., `u-p-h` which maps to `!!wl update <id> --priority high`), the command is sent to Herdr with the `!!` prefix intact. Herdr then tries to execute `!!wl` as a shell command, which fails silently because `!!` is bash history expansion.

## Root Cause

The `shortcuts.json` file contains commands with `!!` prefixes:

```json
{
  "chord": ["u", "p", "h"],
  "command": "!!wl update <id> --priority high",
  ...
}
```

These commands flow through:
1. `shortcuts.json` → `ShortcutRegistry.lookupChord()` → returns command with `!!` prefix
2. `executeResolvedCommand()` → calls `onCommand(resolvedCommand)` with `!!` still present
3. `index.ts` `onCommand` callback → writes `CMD:!!wl update <id> --priority high
` to stdout
4. Herdr receives and tries to execute `!!wl` — fails silently

## Required Changes

In `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` or `packages/herdr/src/index.ts`, strip `!!` or `!` prefix from commands before they are sent to Herdr via stdout.

The stripping should handle:
- Commands starting with `!!` → strip both `!` characters
- Commands starting with `!` → strip single `!`
- Other commands → leave unchanged

This can be done as a simple transformation before the `CMD:` prefix is added:

```typescript
function stripCommandPrefix(command: string): string {
  if (command.startsWith('!!')) {
    return command.substring(2);
  }
  if (command.startsWith('!')) {
    return command.substring(1);
  }
  return command;
}
```

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Commands with `!!` prefix have the prefix stripped before being sent to Herdr
- [ ] Commands with `!` prefix (single) have the prefix stripped before being sent to Herdr
- [ ] Commands without prefix are unchanged
- [ ] All existing shortcuts work correctly (u-p-h, u-p-m, u-p-l, u-p-c, u-s, u-t, x-c, x-d, r, etc.)
- [ ] Agent commands (`/skill:*`, `/intake`, `/plan`) are NOT affected (they don't use `!!` prefix)
- [ ] Tests added for the prefix stripping function

## Files to Modify

- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — where `CMD:` prefix is added
- `packages/herdr/src/shortcut-config.ts` — potentially the shortcut-config module
- `packages/herdr/src/shortcuts.json` — may need to be updated to remove `!!` from all commands

# Intake Brief: Herdr plugin - open worklist in new tab with prefix+l key

## Problem Statement

The `prefix+l` keybinding in Herdr currently opens the Worklog work item selection list as a split pane on the right side of the current workspace. This should instead open in a new tab in the current workspace, providing full-screen access to the worklist without reducing space for existing panes.

## Users

- **Herdr users** who use the worklog-selection-list plugin to browse and manage work items.
- **User story:** "As a Herdr user, when I press `prefix+l` to open the worklist, I want it to open in a new tab so I can see more items without compromising my current pane layout."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The `prefix+l` keybinding opens the worklog-selection-list plugin in a **new tab** in the current workspace (not a split pane).
2. The plugin manifest (`herdr-plugin.toml`) pane `placement` is changed from `"split"` to `"tab"`.
3. The `scripts/open.sh` script uses `--placement tab` instead of `--placement split --direction right`.
4. The existing `toggle-worklist` behavior is no longer needed for `prefix+l` — the keybinding invokes `open-worklist` (always opens, never toggles).
5. All existing plugin-manifest tests continue to pass.
6. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.
7. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.

## Constraints

- Herdr must support `--placement tab` (confirmed: the CLI accepts `tab`, `overlay`, `split`, and `zoomed` as valid placement options).
- The `open-worklist` action already exists in the manifest — no new action needed.
- The `toggle-worklist` action remains available but is no longer bound to `prefix+l`.

## Existing State

- `packages/herdr/herdr-plugin.toml` — `[[panes]]` section has `placement = "split"`
- `packages/herdr/scripts/open.sh` — uses `--placement split --direction right --focus`
- `~/.config/herdr/config.toml` — `prefix+l` invokes `worklog-selection-list.toggle-worklist`
- The plugin currently opens as a split pane on the right side of the current workspace

## Desired Change

1. **`packages/herdr/herdr-plugin.toml`**: Change `placement = "split"` to `placement = "tab"` in the `[[panes]]` section.
2. **`packages/herdr/scripts/open.sh`**: Replace `--placement split --direction right` with `--placement tab`.
3. **`~/.config/herdr/config.toml`** (outside project, user-managed): Change keybinding command from `toggle-worklist` to `open-worklist`.

**Key Files:**

- `packages/herdr/herdr-plugin.toml` — Change pane placement from `"split"` to `"tab"`
- `packages/herdr/scripts/open.sh` — Update CLI arguments to use tab placement
- `tests/herdr/plugin-manifest.test.ts` — Update tests if they assert `"split"` placement (unlikely, but verify)

## Related Work

- WL-0MS5CDIR1008VRTN — "Open pi agent pane for skill commands sent from herdr worklist" (completed, related pane management)
- WL-0MS3ANB04006ZR0H — "Auto-sync (background wl sync) for Herdr plugin" (completed, related plugin infrastructure)
- Various other herdr work items (completed, infrastructure)

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions & Answers

- Q: "Toggle behavior with tabs — Should toggle behavior be preserved?"
  - Answer (user): "now we will only open" — No toggle, always open.

- Q: "New tab creation — Manifest or script level?"
  - Answer (user): "manifest" — Change placement in herdr-plugin.toml.

- Q: "Workspace context — Current workspace or dedicated?"
  - Answer (user): "current" — Open tab in current workspace.

## Summary

Add a form input feature to the Herdr plugin that scans chord commands for `<identifier>` patterns (angle brackets with a variable name inside). Known identifiers like `<id>` are resolved automatically (already supported). Unknown identifiers trigger a dialog with labeled input fields. The dialog displays the command description, followed by the input fields and a submit/cancel option. On submit, the field values are substituted into the command and executed.

## User Stories

- As a Herdr user, I want to execute commands that require variable data (e.g., `!!wl update <id> --title <title>`, `!!wl update <id> --status <status> --stage <stage>`) without first knowing all possible values.
- As a Herdr user, when a chord command contains `<id>`, I expect it to be automatically substituted with the selected item's ID as before.
- As a Herdr user, when a chord command contains unknown identifiers like `<title>` or `<status>`, I want a form dialog to appear so I can fill in the values before the command executes.

## Current Behavior

- Identifiers like `<id>` in chord commands are resolved via `resolveAndRouteCommand` / `executeResolvedCommand` in `worklist.ts`. If the command has `<id>`, the selected item's ID is substituted. Other `<...>` patterns are passed through verbatim.
- If a command like `!!wl update <id> --title <title>` is executed, the `<title>` part is sent as-is to Herdr, which causes a syntax failure.

## Desired Behavior

1. **Scan for identifiers**: When a chord command is resolved (before execution), scan for `<identifier>` patterns.
2. **Known identifiers**: `<id>` is automatically resolved to the selected work item's ID (existing behavior).
3. **Unknown identifiers**: For any other `<identifier>`, generate a modal dialog/overlay in the TUI with:
   - The command's `description` from `shortcuts.json` (if available), or the command text itself
   - An input field for each unknown identifier, labeled with the identifier name
   - A submit option and a cancel option
4. **Substitution**: When the user submits, substitute the entered values for each identifier and execute the command via `onCommand`.
5. **Cancel**: When the user cancels, dismiss the dialog and return to the list without executing.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A new module `packages/herdr/src/form-dialog.ts` (or equivalent) extracts `<identifier>` patterns from commands using a regex
- [ ] `<id>` is recognized as a known identifier and auto-resolved to the selected item's ID (backward compatible)
- [ ] Unknown identifiers (e.g., `<title>`, `<status>`, `<query>`) trigger a form dialog overlay in the TUI
- [ ] The form dialog shows the command's `description` (from shortcuts.json) prominently
- [ ] Each unknown identifier gets a labeled input field
- [ ] Tab/arrow keys navigate between input fields
- [ ] Enter submits the form
- [ ] Escape cancels the form and returns to the list
- [ ] On submit, all auto-resolved and user-provided values are substituted into the command before execution
- [ ] The form dialog is rendered as a TUI overlay (not a separate terminal prompt)
- [ ] All existing tests in `tests/herdr/` still pass
- [ ] New tests cover identifier extraction, known/unknown classification, form rendering, and substitution
- [ ] The feature works for both single-key and multi-key chord commands

## Files to Modify

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — add form mode handling, integrate with chord execution flow
- `packages/herdr/src/shortcuts.json` — optional: update command descriptions for clarity
- `packages/herdr/src/form-dialog.ts` — new module for form dialog logic (extraction, rendering, input handling, substitution)

### Key integration points in worklist.ts

1. The `ChordState` or TUI loop state needs a new mode: `'form'`
2. The `ViewMode` union type needs a `'form'` option
3. The `onData` handler needs to detect when entering form mode and delegate to form input handling
4. The `render` function needs to render the form overlay when in form mode
5. `executeResolvedCommand` needs to check for unknown identifiers and enter form mode instead of immediately executing

## Constraints

- Must be backward compatible — all existing shortcuts continue to work
- Commands with only known identifiers (like `<id>`) should execute without showing a dialog
- The form dialog must not break terminal raw mode or cleanup
- Should handle edge cases: no unknown identifiers, single unknown identifier, multiple unknown identifiers, empty field values

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Input complexity**: Terminal-based text input handling requires care (backspace, cursor movement, text display). Can use simple line editing similar to a shell prompt.
- **Screen layout**: The form overlay needs enough terminal space. If the terminal is very small, the form may not fit. Can fall back to a compact single-line mode or show an error.
- **Known identifier set**: Currently only `<id>` is known. The set should be extensible (e.g., could later add `<status>`, `<stage>`, `<title>` pre-populated from the selected item).
- **Command description**: Not all shortcut entries have a `description` field. Fall back to the command text itself.

# Reselect item after list reorder from status change

## Problem statement

When a work item in the Herdr selection list changes status (either via manual `wl update --stage` or via auto-refresh/sync), the list re-fetches and re-renders. Items may be reordered because `wl next` returns items in a different order. Currently, the refresh resets the selected item to the clamped index position rather than preserving the originally selected item. The system should detect this re-ordering and re-select the original item by its ID.

## Users

- **AI coding agents** using the Herdr work item selection list who navigate to an item and have it displaced by a status change
- **Human users** browsing work items in Herdr who lose their selection context when the list auto-refreshes

### User stories

- As a user, when I select a work item and the list auto-refreshes after a status change on that item, I want the selection to remain on my chosen item (at its new position) rather than jumping to whatever item now occupies the old index.
- As a user, if the item I selected is removed from the list entirely (filtered out, completed), I want the selection to clamp gracefully to the nearest valid item.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Preserve selection by ID on refresh** — When `refreshItems` is called and the previously selected item still exists in the updated list, the selected index updates to match that item's new position.
2. **Fallback clamping** — If the previously selected item no longer appears in the refreshed list (e.g., removed by filter, completed, or stage change makes it invisible), fall back to the current index-clamping behavior (selection clamped to array bounds).
3. **No positional drift** — The fix applies to all code paths that call `refreshItems`: auto-refresh timer, auto-sync callback, and any manual refresh trigger.
4. **All related documentation is updated** to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
5. **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- The solution must not introduce a dependency on data that isn't available (item IDs are always available).
- The fix must be in `WorkItemListState.refreshItems` — no external refactoring of the refresh pipeline.
- If the item ID is present in the new list, selection must move to it regardless of index changes.

## Existing state

- `WorkItemListState.refreshItems()` in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` currently replaces `_allItems`, re-applies filters, and calls `_clampSelection()` which only ensures `selectedIndex` is within `[0, flatCount-1]`.
- `doRefresh()` in the TUI loop calls `refreshItems` and is triggered by both the auto-refresh timer and the auto-sync timer.
- The `WorkItem` type always carries an `id` field which can be used to track the selected item.

## Desired change

In `WorkItemListState.refreshItems()`:
1. Before replacing items, capture the currently selected item's ID from `getFlattenedItems()[selectedIndex]` (if the list is non-empty).
2. After applying filters and rebuilding `items`, search the new flattened list for an item with the saved ID.
3. If found, set `selectedIndex` to its new position.
4. If not found, run existing `_clampSelection()` fallback.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — Modify `WorkItemListState.refreshItems()` to preserve selection by ID. Add a helper method to find an item by ID in the flattened list.

## Related work

- **WL-0MNN5WVHA003O1ES** — "Search results reset the selected item to the top of the list": A similar bug in the Pi TUI (blessed-based) where search results lost selection. Marked wont-fix because blessed TUI was deprecated.
- **WL-0MS1W8Y1L0059AKP** — "Create a work item selection list in Herdr": The epic that created the Herdr selection list, including the `refreshItems` method that now needs this fix.
- **WL-0MKX63D5U10ETR4S** — "Deduplicate list selection/click handlers": Related refactoring of selection logic.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption**: Item IDs are stable across fetch cycles. This is guaranteed by the Worklog data model.
- **Assumption**: The flattened list (including expanded children) may contain items with the same ID — this is unlikely but the first match should be used.
- **Risk**: If the auto-sync and auto-refresh timers fire simultaneously, the ID-based lookup could be redundant (second refresh finds the item from the first refresh). No harm — idempotent.
- **Scope creep risk**: Adding the same fix to other components (blessed TUI, etc.). This is out of scope — the bug is specific to the Herdr plugin.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1**: "Does the reorder happen from manual `wl update --stage` commands, auto-sync/auto-refresh, or both?"  
  **Answer** (user): "both" — The fix must cover all code paths that call `refreshItems`.

- **Q2**: "If the previously selected item is no longer visible after refresh (e.g., because a filter hides it or its stage changed), what should happen?"  
  **Answer** (user): "yes" — Fall back to current index-clamping behavior.

# Problem

When the herdr plugin is invoked from a Herdr tab whose working directory differs from the ContextHub project directory, the plugin continues operating within ContextHub instead of switching to the tab's working directory. This means work items from other projects' `.worklog/` directories are not accessible from within Herdr tabs that point to different locations.

## Users

- **Developer working on multiple projects**: Opens a Herdr tab in a different project directory (e.g., `/foo/bar`) and wants to browse/manage work items from that project's `.worklog/` — but the herdr plugin defaults to ContextHub instead.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] When a Herdr tab is opened in a directory containing a valid `.worklog/` (with `worklog.db`), the herdr plugin operates in that directory
- [ ] When a Herdr tab is opened in ContextHub, the plugin continues to operate in ContextHub (no regression)
- [ ] The `CMD:` prefix commands sent to Herdr are executed from the tab's working directory
- [ ] Agent commands (`/skill:*`, `/intake`, `/plan`) are sent via `send-to-pi.sh` from the correct working directory
- [ ] All existing functionality (shortcuts, worktree detection, auto-sync, auto-refresh) continues to work from any working directory
- [ ] Unit and/or integration tests cover the working directory resolution logic
- [ ] All existing tests pass with the new changes
- [ ] When no valid `.worklog/` exists in the tab's directory, the plugin reports the uninitialized state to the user (e.g., clear error message) rather than silently falling back to ContextHub

## Constraints

- Must not break existing worktree support (the `findWorklogRoot()` logic that walks up from `cwd` to find `.worklog/`)
- Must not break ContextHub's own usage of the plugin
- The plugin is invoked by Herdr — we need to understand how Herdr communicates the tab's working directory to plugins
- Must not modify files outside the ContextHub repository (`.pi/`, `skill/`, etc.)

## Existing State

The plugin currently uses `findWorklogRoot()` in `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` which walks UP from `process.cwd()` to find a `.worklog/` directory with `worklog.db` or an `initialized` marker. If found and different from cwd, it calls `process.chdir(wlRoot)`.

The plugin is invoked by Herdr (a terminal UI framework). Herdr sets `HERDR_PANE_ID` when running in a pane. Herdr supports multiple tabs, each potentially with a different working directory.

**Key Files:**

- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — Main entry point; `findWorklogRoot()` and `process.chdir()` logic; `send-to-pi.sh` invocation
- `packages/herdr/scripts/send-to-pi.sh` — Agent command dispatch script; may need `cwd` override
- `packages/herdr/src/settings.ts` — Settings system; may need a new config option for working directory behavior

## Related Work

- **WL-0MS5ZEAQJ001KSYI** — "worklog-selection-list plugin not finding work items when opening herdr" (completed). Related issue about the herdr plugin not finding work items from the correct directory.
- **WL-0MS631PQ80024R6W** — "Strip !! and ! prefixes from Herdr plugin commands before sending to Herdr" (plan_complete). Related herdr plugin work affecting the same code paths.

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Risk**: Herdr may not currently expose the tab's working directory to plugins. We may need to discover how Herdr communicates with plugins or request a Herdr feature.
- **Risk**: Changing working directory behavior may affect existing users who rely on the current context-sensitive `.worklog/` discovery.
- **Risk (Scope Creep)**: This feature could expand into a larger "multi-project support" epic. Keep scope focused on respecting the tab's cwd; record additional enhancements as separate work items.
- **Assumption**: Herdr sets `process.cwd()` to the tab's working directory when invoking plugins. If not, we may need to rely on environment variables or other mechanisms.
- **Assumption**: The user has multiple projects each with their own `.worklog/` directory and wants to switch between them via Herdr tabs.
- **Edge Case**: The `.worklog/` directory may not exist in the tab's directory. In this case, report the uninitialized state clearly to the user (e.g., "No `.worklog/` directory found in <path>").

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions & Answers

- Q: "How does Herdr communicate the tab's working directory to plugins?" — Answer: Herdr should set `process.cwd()` to the tab's working directory. This needs investigation of how Herdr invokes plugins. Source: pending Herdr investigation.
- Q: "Should the plugin always use the tab's working directory, or only when a `.worklog/` exists there?" — Answer: Always use the tab's cwd. If a valid `.worklog/` exists, operate in that directory. If not, report the uninitialized state clearly to the user rather than silently falling back.
- Q: "What should the uninitialized state error look like?" — Answer: Clear, actionable message (e.g., "No `.worklog/` directory found in <path>"). Source: user clarification.

# Intake Draft — Metadata in work-item detail views should be presented as markdown table (WL-0MS6MOXNQ005B9IC)

## Problem statement

The metadata section at the top of work-item detail views (`wl show` CLI output and herdr plugin detail view) currently renders as key-value pair lines with colon separators. This is inconsistent with the markdown-heavy nature of the rest of the output (descriptions, comments) and makes the metadata harder to scan visually. The metadata should be rendered as a markdown table instead.

## Users

- **Primary**: Developers and operators using `wl show` CLI or the herdr TUI plugin to inspect work items
  - User story: As a user viewing a work item, I want the metadata presented in a markdown table so it's visually scannable and consistent with the rest of the markdown output.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **`wl show` full format**: The frontmatter metadata (ID, Status, Type, SortIndex, Risk, Effort, Assignee, Parent, Tags, Audit) is rendered as a markdown table instead of padded key-value lines.
2. **`wl show` normal format**: Metadata rows (ID, Title, Status, SortIndex, Risk, Effort, Audit, Parent, Tags) use a markdown table. The `Description:` line (which contains the full description content) remains as a separate section below the table.
3. **`wl show` concise format**: Metadata rows use a markdown table.
4. **Herdr plugin detail view** (`formatDetailContent`): The `pushMeta()`-based metadata section is rendered as a markdown table instead of `label:     value` lines.
5. The markdown table is used **always** — not only when `--format markdown` is active.
6. All existing tests pass after the changes.
7. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.

## Constraints

- No changes to the `raw`, `summary`, or `detail-pane` formats (they don't have the same metadata rendering).
- The `title` line (rendered separately as `# Title`) should remain separate from the metadata table.
- Color/icon/animation support (ANSI codes for terminal) must be preserved within table cells where applicable.
- The herdr plugin is a terminal-based TUI — the table must fit within terminal width constraints and be readable.

## Existing state

### `wl show` full format (default)

In `src/commands/helpers.ts`, the `humanFormatWorkItem()` function builds a `frontmatter` array of `[label, value]` tuples and renders them as:

```
ID       : WL-xxx
Status   : ✔️ Completed [DONE] · Stage: Done | Priority: ⭐ high [HIGH]
Type     : feature
SortIndex: 200
Risk     : —
Effort   : —
Parent   : WL-xxxx
```

### `wl show` normal format

Same file, different section — renders similarly as:
```
ID:    WL-xxx
Title: ...
Status: ... · Stage: ... | Priority: ...
SortIndex: 200
Risk: —
Effort: —
Audit: ...
```

### `wl show` concise format

Renders as:
```
Status: ... · Stage: ... | Priority: ...
SortIndex: 200
Risk: —
Effort: —
Audit: ...
```

### Herdr plugin detail view

In `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`, the `formatDetailContent()` function uses `pushMeta()` to render:
```
  Status:     value
  Priority:   value
  Stage:      value
  ...
```

## Desired change

Replace each metadata block with a markdown table. Example for the full format:

```markdown
| Field     | Value                                                  |
|-----------|--------------------------------------------------------|
| ID        | WL-0MQD1NJLM001Y5A4                                    |
| Status    | ✔️ Completed [DONE] · Stage: Done \| Priority: ⭐ high |
| Type      | feature                                                |
| SortIndex | 200                                                    |
| Risk      | —                                                      |
| Effort    | —                                                      |
| Parent    | WL-0MQD0YW40007RTKU                                    |
```

For the herdr plugin, similar approach but with TUI-friendly formatting that respects terminal width.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/commands/helpers.ts` — The `humanFormatWorkItem()` function for all `wl show` CLI formats (full, normal, concise). Multiple metadata-rendering sections need to be updated.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — The `formatDetailContent()` function and its `pushMeta()` helper for the herdr plugin detail view.
- `tests/herdr/detail-view.test.ts` — Tests for `formatDetailContent` metadata rendering (asserts label:value format — needs table update)
- `tests/herdr/worklist.test.ts` — Tests for `formatDetailView` detail view rendering
- `tests/cli/helpers-tree-rendering.test.ts` — Tests for tree rendering using `humanFormatWorkItem`
- `tests/integration/wl-show-formatting.test.ts` — Integration tests for `humanFormatWorkItem` output formats
- `tests/unit/human-audit-format.test.ts` — Snapshot tests for concise/normal/full formats (snapshots need update)

## Related work

- WL-0MQ9E164R0002DNF — "Replace confusing metadata lines in TUI work item detail view with clean metadata header" (completed, wontfix — Blessed TUI deprecated). Previous attempt at improving metadata display, now superseded by this work.
- WL-0MMOME4VU181A4GP — "Show risk and effort scores in the meta-data" (completed). Added risk/effort fields to metadata — this work builds on that by improving the presentation format.

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Risk**: Tables in the herdr plugin TUI may not render cleanly at narrow terminal widths. Mitigation: Ensure table columns are proportioned to fit within `maxCols` and consider wrapping or truncating long values.
- **Risk**: ANSI color codes within table cells may break alignment if not carefully handled. Mitigation: Apply colors to cell content rather than table structure.
- **Risk**: Timestamp fields (createdAt, updatedAt, auditedAt) in the herdr plugin are long ISO strings — a two-column table may overflow at narrow terminal widths. Mitigation: Consider wrapping or abbreviating timestamps in the table while keeping full values accessible.
- **Assumption**: The `normal` and `concise` formats are primarily used by humans, so the table format is appropriate for them.
- **Scope creep mitigation**: Any additional features (sortable columns, clickable fields, etc.) should be recorded as separate linked work items.

## Polish & Handoff

The metadata sections of `wl show` (full, normal, concise) and the herdr plugin detail view should render as markdown tables with two columns (Field, Value). Implementation involves modifying `src/commands/helpers.ts` and `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` to output table-formatted metadata instead of colon-separated key-value lines.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Which detail view are you referring to?" — Answer (user): Both the `wl show` CLI output and the detail view in the herdr plugin.
- Q: "Is the markdown table format correct?" — Answer (user): Yes.
- Q: "Does this apply to all formats (full, concise, normal) or just the default full format?" — Answer (user): Any format that has the meta-data in it.
- Q: "Should the table respect markdown rendering mode (i.e., only render as table when --format markdown is used), or always render as a markdown table?" — Answer (user): Always.

## Problem

When `wl list --json` returns work items, it includes `auditResult` as a boolean (`true`/`false`) but does NOT include the `auditedAt` timestamp. This causes the Herdr TUI to always show the stale audit icon (⏳) for in_review items, even when the audit was just performed, because the `isAuditFresh()` check receives `undefined` for the timestamp and immediately returns `false`.

In contrast, `wl audit-show` returns the full audit object including `auditedAt`, and `wl show` returns it at the top level. Only the list APIs (`wl list`, `wl next`) are missing it.

## Impact

All `in_review` items in the Herdr browse list show the stale-passed icon (⏳) instead of the fresh-passed icon (✅), making it look like audits are outdated across the board.

## Proposed Fix

### Approach A: Fix wl list to include auditedAt (recommended)
Modify the `wl list` command to include `auditedAt` in its JSON output for each work item. The field already exists on the audit record and is accessible via the worklog database — it just isn't surfaced in list responses.

### Approach B: Fix Herdr fetcher to fetch audit details per item
Have the Herdr fetcher make an additional `wl audit-show <id>` call for each in_review item to get the timestamp. However, this adds N+1 API calls and would slow down the browse list.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `wl list --json` returns `auditedAt` field with ISO timestamp for each work item that has an audit
- [ ] `wl next --json` similarly includes `auditedAt` in each item
- [ ] `wl list --json` items without an audit have `auditedAt: null`
- [ ] Herdr no longer has to compensate for missing auditedAt
- [ ] All existing tests continue to pass

## Discovered From

WL-0MS631PQ80024R6W — audit showed as outdated despite being fresh

The Herdr-side fix (icons.ts) handles the symptom; this work item addresses the root cause.

# Intake Brief: audit_runner: _is_exempt_child ignores status=deleted items

## Problem Statement

The `_is_exempt_child()` function in `audit_runner.py` only excludes children by checking the `deletedBy` field, but `wl delete` sets `status=deleted` instead of populating `deletedBy`. As a result, deleted children are not excluded from parent closure checks, causing parent work items to be blocked from closing by children that have been deleted.

## Users

- **Agent operators and maintainers** who delete work items (e.g., duplicates, obsolete children) and expect parent items to close cleanly.
- **Audit skill consumers** who rely on `audit_runner` to produce accurate ready-to-close verdicts for parent work items.

### User Stories

- As an agent operator, when I delete a child work item using `wl delete`, I expect the audit runner to treat it as exempt (not blocking parent closure), so that parent items can close without manual intervention.
- As a maintainer of `audit_runner.py`, I want the deleted-child check to match how `wl delete` actually marks items, so the exemption logic works correctly.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Deleted children (items with `status=deleted`) are excluded from `active_children` in the `_process_children` function (line ~1906-1908) alongside the existing `deletedBy` check.
2. The `_is_exempt_child()` function (line ~768) and `_is_exempt()` function (line ~1373) treat `status=deleted` as an exempt condition.
3. The `_has_phase1_blocking_issues()` function (line ~1309) skips children with `status=deleted` when checking for blocking stages.
4. When a parent has only deleted children, the audit runner correctly reports it as ready to close (assuming other criteria are met).
5. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.

> **Note:** CHANGELOG.md is **excluded** from this list. It is managed automatically by the ship skill's release pipeline.

## Constraints

- Changes must be backward-compatible: the `deletedBy` check should be retained as an additional guard (belt-and-suspenders approach).
- The `deletedBy` field is used for interoperability with imported data (e.g., from other issue trackers). Do not remove the existing `deletedBy` filter — augment it with a `status=deleted` check.
- Only the `audit_runner.py` file in the `skill/audit/scripts/` directory is in scope. No other skills or infrastructure should be modified.

## Existing State

- `audit_runner.py` line ~1908 filters children: `[c for c in children if not c.get("deletedBy")]`
- `audit_runner.py` line ~768 defines `_is_exempt_child()` which checks for `status=completed/stage=done` and `stage=in_review`
- `audit_runner.py` line ~1373 defines `_is_exempt()` which checks for `status=completed/stage=done` and `stage=in_review`
- `audit_runner.py` line ~1309 defines `_has_phase1_blocking_issues()` which checks children stages but doesn't consider `status=deleted`
- `wl delete` sets `status=deleted` on the work item (according to DATA_FORMAT.md: `status` can be `open`, `in-progress`, `completed`, `blocked`, or `deleted`)
- `deletedBy` is an optional interoperability field for imported data, not populated by `wl delete`

## Desired Change

1. In `_process_children` (line ~1908), augment the `deletedBy` filter to also exclude `status=deleted`:
   ```python
   active_children = [
       c for c in children
       if c.get("status") != "deleted" and not c.get("deletedBy")
   ]
   ```

2. In `_is_exempt_child()` (line ~768), add a `status=deleted` exemption:
   ```python
   def _is_exempt_child(c: dict) -> bool:
       if c.get("status") == "deleted":
           return True
       if c.get("status") == "completed" and c.get("stage") == "done":
           return True
       return c.get("stage") == "in_review"
   ```

3. In `_is_exempt()` (line ~1373), add the same `status=deleted` exemption:
   ```python
   def _is_exempt(c: dict) -> bool:
       if c.get("status") == "deleted":
           return True
       if c.get("status") == "completed" and c.get("stage") == "done":
           return True
       return c.get("stage") == "in_review"
   ```

4. In `_has_phase1_blocking_issues()` (line ~1311), skip `status=deleted` children:
   ```python
   active_children = [
       c for c in child_results
       if c.get("stage") not in ("", None) and c.get("status") != "deleted"
   ]
   ```

## Key Files

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — Contains `_is_exempt_child()`, `_is_exempt()`, `_has_phase1_blocking_issues()`, and `_process_children()` that all need modification
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_core.py` — Existing test file for audit_runner core logic; tests should be added for the new `status=deleted` handling

## Related Work

### Related docs
- `/usr/local/lib/node_modules/worklog/DATA_FORMAT.md` — Documents `status=deleted` as a valid status value
- `docs/validation/stage-in-progress-usage-inventory.md` — References `audit_runner.py` in context of stage validation

### Related work items
- **WL-0MS7M1L4L005XR2I** — This work item (current)

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Scope creep risk**: This fix is narrowly scoped to `audit_runner.py`. Any additional audit skill issues discovered during implementation should be tracked as separate work items.
- **Backward compatibility risk**: Adding `status=deleted` checks alongside existing `deletedBy` checks is conservative but could theoretically change behavior for items where both status=deleted and deletedBy are set. This is the desired behavior (exempt deleted items regardless of how they were marked).
- **Test coverage risk**: The existing test suite may not have coverage for deleted children. Tests must be added to cover the new behavior.
- **Assumption**: `wl delete` always sets `status=deleted` and never populates `deletedBy` for CLI-executed deletions. Verified via DATA_FORMAT.md and source code analysis.
- **Assumption**: The `deletedBy` field should continue to be checked as a belt-and-suspenders guard for imported data.

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions & Answers

- Q: "Does `wl delete` set `deletedBy` or `status=deleted`?" — Answer (agent research): `wl delete` sets `status=deleted`. The `deletedBy` field is an optional interoperability field for imported data from other issue trackers. Source: `DATA_FORMAT.md` at `/usr/local/lib/node_modules/worklog/DATA_FORMAT.md` and `worklog/src/commands/delete.ts` source analysis.
- Q: "Should the existing `deletedBy` check be removed or augmented?" — Answer (agent inference): Augment. The `deletedBy` check provides a belt-and-suspenders guard for data imported from other issue trackers that may use `deletedBy` instead of `status=deleted`. Removing it could break existing interop scenarios. Verified via intent analysis.
