# Herdr Plugin: Set Work-Item Status to in_progress When Instigating Agent Actions

## Problem statement

When a user triggers an agent command from the herdr plugin, the referenced work-item is not immediately marked as in_progress. The current flow requires the agent to claim the work-item after it has already been invoked, creating an unnecessary delay.

## Users

- **Herdr plugin users** — When they invoke `/intake`, `/plan`, or `/skill:*` commands from the herdr worklist, they expect the work-item to be immediately claimed and shown as in_progress.

Example user stories:
- "As a user, when I trigger `/intake WL-XXXX` from herdr, the work-item should immediately appear as in_progress."
- "As a user, I want the status transition to happen instantly so I can see the work-item is being worked on without waiting for the agent to respond."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. When an agent command (`/intake`, `/plan`, `/skill:*`) is dispatched from the herdr plugin, the plugin extracts the work-item ID and sets its status to `in_progress` before spawning the agent pane.
2. The status update must succeed silently — failures should be logged to stderr but must not block or prevent the agent pane from opening.
3. The agent receives the command unchanged and can proceed normally (it will see the item is already in_progress).
4. Only agent commands trigger this behavior — non-agent commands (stdout/pane routes) are unaffected.
5. The `--assignee` field is set to `Map` (or the current user) when setting status to in_progress, matching the existing claim pattern.

## Constraints

- Must work with the existing `send-to-pi.sh` flow — the status update happens before spawning the pane.
- The work-item ID must be reliably extracted from the command string.
- The implementation must use the `wl` CLI with the correct `--worklog-dir` to target the project's worklog database.

## Existing state

The herdr plugin routes agent commands via `isAgentCommand()` in `src/index.ts`, which detects `/skill:*`, `/intake`, and `/plan` prefixes. When detected, it spawns `send-to-pi.sh` asynchronously (detached, stdio ignored). The work-item ID is embedded in the command text but the plugin does not currently interact with the work-item's status.

The agent-side workflow (`AGENTS.md`) expects agents to claim work-items by running `wl update <id> --status in_progress`, but this only happens after the agent has already started processing the command.

## Desired change

In `src/index.ts`, when routing an agent command:
1. Extract the work-item ID from the command (it's the last argument, typically in format `WL-XXXXX` or similar).
2. Run `wl update <id> --status in_progress --assignee Map --json --worklog-dir <dir>` before spawning `send-to-pi.sh`.
3. Continue with the existing pane spawning logic.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — `routeCommand` and the `onCommand` handler need to extract the work-item ID and update its status before spawning the agent pane.
- `packages/herdr/scripts/send-to-pi.sh` — No changes needed, but the flow will now have the status already set.

## Related work

- WL-0MS5CDIR1008VRTN — Open pi agent pane for skill commands sent from herdr worklist (the item that implemented agent command routing)
- `AGENTS.md` — Workflow documentation that currently instructs agents to claim work-items (this change would shift that responsibility to the plugin)

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** The work-item ID is always the last argument in agent commands. If the command format changes, ID extraction may break.
- **Risk:** If `wl update` fails (e.g., network issues, invalid ID), the agent pane should still open. Failures must be non-blocking.
- **Risk:** If multiple agent commands reference the same work-item concurrently, the status update is idempotent (setting in_progress to in_progress is safe).
- **Risk:** Command format varies — `/intake WL-XXXX` has the ID as the last arg, but `/skill:implement WL-XXXX` also has it as the last arg. Commands without an ID (e.g., `/intake` alone) should skip the status update gracefully.
- **Assumption:** The `wl` CLI is available in the same environment where herdr runs (it already is, since herdr already uses `wl` for fetching items).
- **Scope-creep risk:** Extending this behavior to non-agent commands was considered but out of scope — only agent commands (`/skill:*`, `/intake`, `/plan`) are affected.
data.title: Herdr plugin should set work-item status to in_progress when instigating actions

# Intake Brief: auto-retry on 'Provider finish_reason: error'

## Problem statement

When a streaming model call ends with an error `finish_reason`, pi-ai's `mapStopReason` (in `pi-ai/dist/providers/openai-completions.js`) returns `{ stopReason: "error", errorMessage: "Provider finish_reason: <reason>" }`. The Worklog TUI extension's recovery module classifies the resulting assistant message and retries retryable categories — but the message `'Provider finish_reason: error'` (finish_reason === "error", e.g. proxy Tier-1 retry exhaustion on remote streaming stalls) matches **no** error pattern and falls through to `ErrorCategory.UNKNOWN`, which notifies without retrying. The user must manually retry, losing partial work.

## Users

- **Pi users whose LLM provider terminates a stream with finish_reason "error"** (transient stalls via local proxy / opencode-go / deepseek-v4-flash).
  - *As a user, I want the session to automatically retry when the provider ends the stream with finish_reason: error, so that I don't lose progress or have to manually intervene.*
  - *As a user, I want to understand why a retry happened, so I trust that the system is handling transient issues gracefully.*

## Acceptance Criteria

1. When an assistant error message contains `Provider finish_reason: error`, the recovery module classifies it as a retryable category (TIMEOUT, consistent with the 'Stream ended without finish_reason' precedent) and triggers the automatic retry loop with exponential backoff.
2. The error pattern(s) are added to `DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_PATTERNS` in `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/recovery/error-patterns.ts`, conservatively (specific to finish_reason: error; must NOT match the existing content_filter or network_error cases, which are already handled as TERMINATED / TIMEOUT).
3. A test in `error-classification.test.ts` verifies that `Provider finish_reason: error` is classified as retryable (not UNKNOWN), and that the existing `content_filter` → TERMINATED and `network_error` → TIMEOUT classifications still hold (no regression).
4. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.
5. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.

## Constraints

- Must not add new npm dependencies — pattern addition only.
- Must not modify the retry loop engine, classification dispatch, or recovery module registration — only the error patterns in `error-patterns.ts` and their tests.
- Pattern must be conservative and specific to avoid false-positive matches on unrelated errors.
- Existing behavior for `content_filter` (TERMINATED, no retry) and `network_error` (TIMEOUT, retry) must be preserved.

## Existing state

- The recovery module lives at `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/recovery/`.
- `mapStopReason` in `node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-ai/dist/providers/openai-completions.js` (lines ~930-951) produces three finish_reason error variants:
  - `content_filter` → matches `/content.filter/i` → TERMINATED (no retry, correct)
  - `network_error` → matches `/network\s*error/i` → TIMEOUT (retried, correct)
  - default catch-all `Provider finish_reason: <reason>` (e.g. "error") → matches NO pattern → UNKNOWN → no retry
- Verified by regex test against current `DEFAULT_*_PATTERNS`: `'Provider finish_reason: error'` matches none of the 7 category pattern sets.

## Desired change

1. Add a regex pattern (e.g. `/finish_reason\s*:\s*error/i` and/or a `Provider finish_reason` prefix variant) to `DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_PATTERNS` in `error-patterns.ts`, capturing `Provider finish_reason: error` and similar variants.
2. Add a test case in `error-classification.test.ts` confirming the new pattern matches and classifies as `ErrorCategory.TIMEOUT` (retryable).
3. Add regression assertions that `Provider finish_reason: content_filter` still classifies TERMINATED and `Provider finish_reason: network_error` still classifies TIMEOUT.
4. Verify no regressions in existing timeout/terminated classification tests.

## Key Files

- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/recovery/error-patterns.ts` — add pattern(s) to `DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_PATTERNS`
- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/recovery/error-classification.test.ts` — add/update classification tests
- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/recovery/register-recovery.ts` — dispatch site (reference only; no changes expected)
- `node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-ai/dist/providers/openai-completions.js` — reference only: origin of the error message (`mapStopReason`, lines ~930-951); do not modify (pi-ai is a dependency)

## Related work

- **WL-0MR4WJRGA00536X4** (completed) — 'retry Error: Stream ended without finish_reason': identical classification-gap fix; established the pattern-addition + test approach and TIMEOUT mapping. This item is the direct precedent.
- **WL-0MQZX8BTN006N4BF** — parent work item that established the recovery/retry module ('Automatically recover from appropriate server errors').
- **SA-0MS9GFH5H0033TQW** (SorraAgents worklog, deleted) — the originating client-side follow-up; this item supersedes it with a concrete, repo-specific fix.
- **LP-0MS9FR9LG002AJ4C** — RCA for occasional 'Provider finish_reason: error' from remote streaming stalls (tracked in another project's worklog).

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption:** finish_reason "error" is transient and retryable. If the provider consistently errors, retries will not help and the existing UNKNOWN diagnostic path remains the fallback.
- **Risk:** Overly broad pattern (e.g. matching any 'finish_reason: X') could reclassify errors that should be terminal. Mitigate: match only the specific 'error' value (and optionally the 'Provider finish_reason' prefix) so content_filter/network_error handling is untouched.
- **Risk:** The retry loop does not re-execute completed tool calls (existing engine behavior); no new tool-call handling is introduced in this change.
- **Scope-creep risk:** If partial-content merge semantics are later desired (retry-and-append vs. diagnostic), track as a separate follow-up work item rather than expanding this pattern-only fix.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: Should this be in the Pi client (pi-ai / pi-coding-agent) or ContextHub? — Answer (user): Create the work item in ContextHub with all available detail and the proposed fix; the recovery module (which owns retry behavior) lives there. Source: interactive reply.
- Q: Which error category should 'Provider finish_reason: error' map to? — Answer (assumption, documented): TIMEOUT, consistent with the precedent WL-0MR4WJRGA00536X4 ('Stream ended without finish_reason' → TIMEOUT) since the failure mode is a mid-stream stall. Source: precedent work item + pi-ai source inspection.
- Q: Verified classification of existing variants — `Provider finish_reason: content_filter` → TERMINATED (patterns /content.filter/i, /content_filter/i); `Provider finish_reason: network_error` → TIMEOUT (pattern /network\s*error/i); `Provider finish_reason: error` → UNKNOWN (no match). Source: regex test against current DEFAULT_*_PATTERNS.
data.title: Recovery: auto-retry on 'Provider finish_reason: error' (classification gap)

# Herdr plugin: selection list header and top lines cut off top of pane

## Problem statement

The top few lines of the Herdr worklist selection-list pane (the "Work Items — N item(s)" header, and depending on data the filter bar and first items) are cut off / scrolled off the top of the pane. The user cannot see the full list even though there is plenty of unused space at the bottom of the pane. Reported priority: **critical**.

## Users

Anyone using the Herdr `worklog-selection-list` plugin pane to browse/filter/select work items.

User story: *"As a Herdr user, when I open the Work Items pane I want to see the entire selection list (header, filter bar, and all visible items) so I don't miss items that scroll off the top."*

## Root cause (reproduced and verified)

The plugin renders a full-screen TUI to the pane's pty (`process.stdout.rows` == pane height, e.g. 53 rows). The list renderer (`createListRenderer` in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`) builds its layout budget assuming exactly `rows` lines: header(1) + blank(1) + filter bar(1) + items + fill blanks (to `rows - 1`) + footer(1). However, two additions exceed that budget:

1. **Group separator lines are not counted in the layout budget.** Each `── <Group> ──` separator line is pushed during the items loop but is not included in the `used` count, so the output is `rows + numSeparators` lines. The default list (20 items across several stage groups) renders 3+ extra lines.
2. **The notification line is appended after the `rows`-line output.** `render()` appends `output + '
' + notificationLine` (sync/refresh status) whenever a notification is active, producing `rows + 1` lines.

When the output exceeds the pane's pty height, the terminal scrolls the content up, pushing the header and the first few lines off the top of the pane — exactly the reported symptom. Reproduced live: the pane's scrollback contains ~2300 repeated header lines ("Work Items — 20 item(s) ..."), direct evidence that each auto-refresh (1.5 s interval) produced an overflowing render that pushed one line into the scrollback.

## Acceptance criteria

- When the worklist pane renders a list with any number of stage groups (including 0), the header line "Work Items — N item(s)..." is always visible at the top of the pane.
- The complete rendered output (header + filter bar + items + footer) never exceeds the pane's terminal height: for any `TermSize` and any item/group configuration, `renderer(...)` output contains at most `rows` newline-separated lines, with and without a notification line active.
- The entire list (all visible items for the current scroll/filter state) is visible without the top lines scrolling off; no content is cut off at the top when the pane is focused.
- Unit tests cover the line-count invariant (output lines ≤ `rows`) for: multiple group separators, no groups, a notification line active, and a short list; all existing tests continue to pass.
- Full project test suite passes with the new changes.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.

> **Note:** CHANGELOG.md is excluded; it is managed automatically by the ship skill's release pipeline.

## Constraints

- Keep the current pane-based TUI model (clear-screen + home + write). No API change to Herdr itself.
- The fix must not reduce the number of items shown unnecessarily — only correct the height budget (e.g. count separators, reserve a row for the notification).
- Must work in a Herdr pane pty where `process.stdout.rows` reflects the pane height.

## Existing state

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — `createListRenderer()` builds the list layout; `runWorklistTui()`'s `render()` writes `\x1b[2J` + `\x1b[H` + content, then appends the notification line.
- Pane pty size == pane viewport (verified: 53 rows x 253 cols matches `herdr pane layout`).
- The pane's scrollback accumulates stray header lines from overflowing renders (observed ~2300 lines), so scrolling up in the pane shows repeated garbage.

## Desired change

- In `createListRenderer()`: include group separator lines in the layout budget so total output is exactly ≤ `rows`.
- In `runWorklistTui()`'s `render()`: account for the notification line (e.g. reserve the last row, or pass the notification into the renderer budget) so output never exceeds `rows`.
- Optionally: clear the pane scrollback on startup (e.g. `\x1b[3J`) and/or switch to the alternate screen buffer so auto-refresh renders do not pollute scrollback; fix the stray `undefined` prefix observed in the notification line ("undefined[Sync failed: ...]").

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — list renderer layout budget (group separators, fill loop, footer) and `render()` notification append; primary fix location.
- `tests/herdr/worklist.test.ts` — existing `createListRenderer` tests; add line-count invariant tests (output lines ≤ `rows` for group/notification combinations).
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` — mirror unit tests for the same invariant.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — entry point (unlikely to change; verifies env/render flow).

## Related work

- `WL-0MQWA8ZFN008GRKM` "Improve group ordering and Other group behavior in selection list" — introduced group separator rendering; the separator layout accounting originates here.
- `WL-0MS1W8Y1L0059AKP` "Create a work item selection list in Herdr" — original worklist pane feature.
- `WL-0MS66GW0E005ZUKX` "Herdr plugin: open worklist in new tab with prefix+l key" — pane open flow.
- `docs/dev/ux/` and `docs/ux/` — pane/TUI UX notes (check for pane layout conventions).

## Risks & assumptions

- Assumption: the pane pty height equals the pane viewport height (verified live), so `output ≤ rows` is the correct invariant.
- Assumption: the desired fix keeps the current layout/formatting and only corrects the height budget; if a redesign (e.g. fewer chrome rows) is preferred, the ACs remain valid but the implementation scope changes.
- Assumption: scrollback cleanup (`\x1b[3J` / alternate screen) is in scope as it is the same root cause (overflow renders) — if the operator prefers a minimal fix, this can be deferred.
- Risk: hidden off-by-one in the fill loop could shift content in either direction; tests must assert the exact ≤ `rows` invariant, not just visual smoke tests.
- Scope-creep risk: notification styling, "undefined" prefix, and scrollback behavior are related polish; tracked here but each should be validated against the primary ACs before expanding.

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- Q: (none asked — the operator's report plus direct live reproduction and code analysis provided sufficient detail. Assumptions above are recorded; implementation plan may surface follow-ups.)
- Q: Is the fix required only for the list mode, or also detail/filter/form modes? — Answer (assumed, verified in code): detail view already renders ≤ `rows - 1` lines and filter prompt exactly `rows`; only list mode overflows. Implementation should verify all modes satisfy the ≤ `rows` invariant.
- Q: Should scrollback pollution be fixed in the same work item? — Answer (assumed): yes, same root cause; recorded as optional scope above.

# Intake Brief — wl sync lock storm: 60+ stuck sync processes spawned by worklist pane auto-sync (WL-0MSAB7ZUC004SK7E)

## Problem statement

`wl sync` cannot complete because the git sync is blocked by a pre-existing lock storm: 60+ stuck `wl sync` processes spawned by the live worklist panes' auto-sync. The worklist pane itself reports "Sync failed: wl sync timed out". The work item data is safely persisted in SQLite, but killing the stuck processes only causes the panes to respawn them, so sync remains blocked until the root cause is fixed.

## Users

- **Agents and operators relying on `wl sync`** — every sync attempt fails while the storm persists, blocking Git-backed collaboration and the TUI's auto-sync.
- **TUI users with live worklist panes** (Herdr worklist plugin) — each pane contributes its own background sync processes, amplifying the storm.

User story: "As an operator, I want `wl sync` to remain functional when multiple worklist panes are open, so that a lock storm cannot block Git sync indefinitely."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A mechanism prevents unbounded `wl sync` process accumulation from worklist-pane auto-sync (single-flight guard per pane and/or process-wide mutex), so that 60+ stuck processes cannot recur.
2. Killing/respawning behavior is fixed: terminating stuck sync processes must not cause panes to immediately respawn them into the same lock storm.
3. A stuck/stale sync cannot hold the file lock indefinitely; lock acquisition eventually times out and cleans up (existing age-based stale-lock cleanup works end to end).
4. The worklist pane auto-sync surfaces sync failure gracefully (already the case) and stops piling on more syncs while one is in-flight or the lock is contended.
5. `wl sync` succeeds with multiple worklist panes open concurrently (regression test covering N panes / concurrent syncs).
6. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.
7. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.

## Constraints

- Do not regress the existing auto-sync UX (periodic background sync, non-blocking UI, manual sync still available).
- `wl sync` semantics (rate/burst, file-lock serialization of JSONL writes) must be preserved.
- Sync must remain non-blocking for the TUI event loop.
- The fix should not rely on operators manually killing processes.

## Existing state

- Herdr worklist panes each create a `SyncTimer` (`packages/herdr/src/auto-sync.ts`) that spawns fire-and-forget `wl sync` subprocesses (`spawn('wl', ['--worklog-dir', <dir>, 'sync'])`) with no in-flight guard; the code comments claim "multiple overlapping syncs are harmless (wl sync is idempotent)".
- `SyncTimer.start()` fires an immediate tick plus an interval tick (default 30s), so each pane spawns a sync immediately on start and then periodically.
- `wl sync` acquires a file lock (`src/file-lock.ts`) with a 30s default timeout and exponential backoff (max 2s). Under contention, queued sync processes pile up; the pane's 10s safety timeout in `runSync` then reports "wl sync timed out" while the child process remains stuck waiting on the lock.
- **Double-spawn per pane:** the worklist auto-refresh timer (30s) calls `doSync()` on every refresh tick AND a separate `SyncTimer` fires `doSync()` immediately on start + every 30s — two unguarded sync sources per pane (`packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`).
- Killing stuck processes does not help because live panes respawn sync timers.
- **Pi extension path** (`~/.pi/agent/extensions/worklog/Worklog/`): `lib/browse.ts` `_triggerAutoSync` HAS an in-flight guard — but it is **per TUI process** (13 `wl pi` instances observed), so multiple TUI sessions still run concurrent auto-syncs; and `lib/tools.ts` `runWl` uses `promisify(execFile)` with **no timeout**, so a sync hung on the file lock never dies.
- **Amplifier:** `src/file-lock.ts` gives every `wl sync` a 30s lock timeout with exponential backoff (max 2s); queued processes each wait up to 30s and pi's no-timeout syncs never give up → self-sustaining storm.
- **Live evidence (2026-08-01):** 20 concurrent `wl --worklog-dir <dir> sync` processes (all herdr-style spawns) + 13 `wl pi` TUI processes observed; killing caused respawns within seconds. Also orphaned stuck `wl --json init` processes from worktrees (PPID 1, sleeping in ep_poll, alive 53min–22h) from herdr pane startup.
- The Pi TUI browse auto-sync (WL-0MQSRF0OG0025B8I) already has a per-process in-flight guard — the Herdr worklist plugin path has none, and the pi extension guard is not cross-process.

## Desired change

- Add a single-flight / in-flight guard to the Herdr worklist auto-sync so overlapping syncs are skipped (mirror the guard implemented for the Pi TUI browse path), and remove the double-spawn (drop `doSync()` from the auto-refresh timer; keep the SyncTimer).
- Consider a process-wide or lock-aware guard so multiple panes / TUI instances do not each spawn a concurrent sync; the pi extension guard must become cross-process or backed by a mutex.
- Add a timeout to the pi extension `runWl` (currently no timeout) so a sync stuck on the file lock cannot hang forever.
- Ensure the file-lock retry/cleanup path cannot be wedged indefinitely by accumulated processes (verify timeout + stale-lock cleanup under storm conditions).
- Add tests: concurrent sync spawns, timer tick while sync in-flight, multiple panes, lock storm recovery.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/auto-sync.ts` — Add in-flight guard; fix immediate-tick spawn behavior; possibly debounce.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — Auto-sync timer wiring and sync notification handling.
- `packages/herdr/src/auto-sync.test.ts` — Tests for guard, overlap, and lock-storm scenarios.
- `src/file-lock.ts` — Verify timeout/stale-lock cleanup behavior under process pile-up (may need tuning).
- `src/commands/sync.ts` — Lock integration for `wl sync`; verify no changes needed.
- `~/.pi/agent/extensions/worklog/Worklog/lib/browse.ts` — Make auto-sync guard cross-process (or back with a mutex).
- `~/.pi/agent/extensions/worklog/Worklog/lib/tools.ts` — Add a timeout to `runWl` so hung `wl sync` cannot persist.

## Related work

- `Auto-sync with thrash prevention in Pi TUI (WL-0MQRYQLQY0042UX2)` — completed; established last-sync-time tracking and thrash prevention in the Pi TUI.
- `Hook auto-sync into TUI browse refresh with in-flight guard (WL-0MQSRF0OG0025B8I)` — completed; the Pi TUI browse path already has the single-flight guard that the Herdr plugin lacks.
- `Auto-sync: periodic background wl sync (WL-0MS4FIUYS001K08K)` — completed; Herdr background sync feature (source of the respawning processes).
- `Auto-sync (background wl sync) for Herdr plugin (WL-0MS3ANB04006ZR0H)` — completed; original Herdr auto-sync.
- `Investigate file lock acquisition failure for worklog-data.jsonl.lock (WL-0MLZ0M1X81PGJLRJ)` — completed; prior lock-acquisition incident.
- `Age-Based Lock Expiry (WL-0MLZJ64X215T0FKP)` / `Corrupted Lock File Recovery (WL-0MLZJ5P7B16JIV0W)` — completed; existing lock cleanup mechanisms to verify under storm conditions.
- `wl sync in a git worktree commits the whole tree as deleted (data loss) (WL-0MS99Y6R40028Q9G)` — open; separate sync reliability issue, related-to.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk:** Process-wide guard could suppress legitimate concurrent syncs from multiple users/processes; guard must be scoped to the auto-sync path, not manual syncs.
- **Risk:** Killing processes (operator workaround) may leave stale lock files; verify stale-lock cleanup (5-min max age) recovers.
- **Risk:** Lock-storm can wedge the file lock for up to the 30s timeout per process; verify the aggregate behavior does not exceed acceptable bounds.
- **Assumption:** The storm originates from Herdr worklist panes (per the observed "live worklist panes' auto-sync" report); the Pi TUI browse path already has a guard.
- **Scope-creep risk:** any additional sync reliability issues discovered should be recorded as linked work items (e.g., `related-to:WL-0MS99Y6R40028Q9G`), not folded into this item.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Should this item be created or does an existing item cover it?" — Answer (operator rgardler): "If we do [have an item] make it critical, if we do not /intake one." Source: interactive request.
- Q: "What priority?" — Answer (operator rgardler): implied critical — sync is fully blocked and data flow is at risk. Source: interactive request ("make it critical").
- Research note: Searched worklog for "lock storm", "lock", "sync", "timed out", "stuck", "respawn", "Sync failed", "auto-sync", "60" — no open item describes the lock storm; all auto-sync/lock items are completed. Created WL-0MSAB7ZUC004SK7E.
- Research note: Inspected `packages/herdr/src/auto-sync.ts` — confirms fire-and-forget `spawn('wl', ['--worklog-dir', dir, 'sync'])` with no in-flight guard and an immediate first tick on `SyncTimer.start()`; `src/file-lock.ts` confirms 30s lock timeout with exponential backoff; the pane's 10s safety timeout produces the "wl sync timed out" report.

# Herdr plugin: use notification system (toasts) instead of bottom-line status updates

## Problem statement

The Herdr `worklog-selection-list` plugin currently renders temporary status updates (refresh results, sync outcomes, sent commands, errors) by appending a transient notification line to the **bottom of the pane output** (the `notificationLine` in `worklist.ts`). This pushes the pane content up by a line whenever a notification is active, contributes to content being cut off at the top of the pane (see related work), and the transient status text disappears after 3s via a `setTimeout`. The user wants these temporary status updates to use Herdr's native **notification system (toasts)** instead of the pane's bottom line.

## Users

Anyone using the Herdr `worklog-selection-list` plugin pane to browse/filter/select work items and run `wl` commands.

User story: *"As a Herdr user, when a refresh, sync, or command action completes in the Work Items pane, I want the status to appear as a Herdr toast notification so the pane content is not disturbed by temporary bottom-line text."*

## Acceptance Criteria

- The Herdr plugin no longer renders temporary status updates (refresh notification, sync notification, sent/skipped command feedback, errors) as a line appended to the bottom of the pane output in `worklist.ts`. With no notification active and with a notification active, the pane output must be identical (no `notificationLine` appended).
- Refresh outcomes (`[Refreshed]`, `[Refreshed: +N new]`, `[Refresh failed]`) are delivered through Herdr's notification system (`herdr notification show`) as toasts instead of the pane bottom line.
- Sync outcomes (`[Synced]`, `[Sync failed: ...]`) are delivered through Herdr's notification system as toasts instead of the pane bottom line.
- Command feedback (`Sent: <cmd>`, `Skipped: <cmd> (no item)`, `Error: <message>`) — including form-submit feedback and chord/single-key shortcut feedback — is delivered through Herdr's notification system as toasts instead of the pane bottom line.
- Toasts use position `bottom-right` (the only positions Herdr 0.7.5 supports for `notification show` are `top-left|top-right|bottom-left|bottom-right`; there is no center position — confirmed with user; `bottom-right` accepted as the fallback).
- Toast delivery is enabled via `ui.toast.delivery = "herdr"` in `~/.config/herdr/config.toml` (config updated and verified: `herdr notification show` returns `shown: true`).
- Unit tests cover the notification dispatch (including the removal of the bottom-line notification rendering); all existing tests continue to pass.
- Full project test suite passes with the new changes.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.

> **Note:** CHANGELOG.md is excluded; it is managed automatically by the ship skill's release pipeline.

## Constraints

- Keep the current pane-based TUI model (clear-screen + home + write). No API change to Herdr itself is in scope — the plugin must use the existing `herdr notification show` CLI (a subprocess spawn/exec from the plugin process).
- Herdr 0.7.5's `herdr notification show` supports **only corner positions** (`top-left | top-right | bottom-left | bottom-right`); there is **no "center" or "bottom-center" position** for `notification show` (only the clipboard toast config supports `bottom-center`). Default is `bottom-right`. User confirmed `bottom-right` is acceptable.
- Toast delivery must be enabled for toasts to appear: `ui.toast.delivery = "herdr"` in the herdr config (user originally said they would enable it; during intake the delivery setting was enabled and verified working on the user's machine).
- The plugin runs as a standalone pane process (`npx tsx src/index.ts`), so it must invoke the notification system via the `herdr` CLI subprocess — it cannot call pi's `ctx.ui.notify()` directly.
- Herdr rate-limits API notifications to 1 per second and reports `busy` if a toast is already showing; a single toast replaces any previous toast. The plugin should tolerate `shown: false` responses (no crash, no retry loop).
- Do not invent requirements — any deviation (e.g., a specific new toast position) must be flagged for user confirmation.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** the `herdr` binary is on `PATH` inside the pane process environment (the pane runs `npx tsx src/index.ts` under the Herdr TUI, so this should hold). If not, toasts silently fail — the wrapper must not crash the pane.
- **Risk:** coordination with WL-0MSAAON63003N6LO (cut-off top lines) — this work item removes the bottom-line notification append, which is root cause #2 of that item; implementers should coordinate so the two fixes don't conflict or double-fix the same lines.
- **Risk:** rapid consecutive actions (e.g., multiple chords) hit Herdr's 1/s rate limit and `busy` state; toasts may be dropped. Accepted: a single toast replaces the previous one; the plugin will not queue.
- **Scope-creep guard:** adding a "center" toast position to Herdr itself (a Herdr-side feature) is explicitly out of scope; only `bottom-right` (existing position) is used. If the user later wants centered toasts, that is a separate work item against the Herdr project.
- **Scope-creep guard:** no sound (`--sound none` default) unless the user requests it.

## Existing state

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` holds two state strings, `refreshNotification` and `syncNotification` (line ~1555), which are set at multiple call sites:
  - Refresh: `[Refreshed: +N new]` / `[Refreshed]` / `[Refresh failed]` (lines ~1619–1624)
  - Sync: `[Synced]` / `[Sync failed: <err>]` (lines ~1645–1647)
  - Form submit: `Sent: <resolved>` (line ~1668)
  - Chord feedback: `Skipped: <cmd> (no item)` / `Sent: <cmd>` / `Error: <msg>` (lines ~1753–1759)
  - Single-key shortcut: `Sent: <cmd>` / `Error: <msg>` (lines ~1837–1841)
- These are cleared via `setTimeout(..., 3000)` and rendered at lines ~1986–1991 by appending `output + '
' + notificationLine` to the pane output.
- Herdr notification system: `herdr notification show <title> [--body TEXT] [--position top-left|top-right|bottom-left|bottom-right] [--sound none|done|request]` — shows an in-app toast (delivery `herdr`), auto-dismisses after ~3s, replaces any current toast, rate-limited to 1/s, returns JSON `{"result":{"shown":bool,"reason":...}}`.

## Desired change

- Add a small notification helper (e.g., `notify.ts`) that invokes `herdr notification show <title> [--body <text>] --position bottom-right` as a fire-and-forget subprocess (spawn/exec), tolerating failures silently (non-zero exit, `shown: false`, missing binary).
- Replace every `refreshNotification = ...` / `syncNotification = ...` assignment in `worklist.ts` with a call to the notification helper (title + body), removing the 3s `setTimeout` clearing and the `notificationLine` append in `render()`.
- Keep the pane output stable: with or without a notification active, `render()` output is identical (no extra bottom line).

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — remove `refreshNotification`/`syncNotification` state and bottom-line append (lines ~1555, 1619–1624, 1645–1647, 1668, 1753–1759, 1837–1841, 1986–1991); call the notification helper instead.
- `packages/herdr/src/notify.ts` (new) — fire-and-forget `herdr notification show` wrapper (spawn, `bottom-right`, tolerant of failures).
- `packages/herdr/src/notify.test.ts` (new) — unit tests for the wrapper (arg construction, failure tolerance).
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` — update/add tests for notification dispatch and the stable render output.
- `~/.config/herdr/config.toml` — `[ui.toast] delivery = "herdr"` (done during intake; verified working).

## Related work

- **WL-0MSAAON63003N6LO — Herdr plugin: selection list header and top lines cut off top of pane** (open, critical, plan_complete): root cause #2 is exactly the notification line appended after the `rows`-line output (`rows + 1` lines). Removing the bottom-line notification rendering (this work item) resolves that root cause; the two items should be coordinated (this item may reduce/obsolete part of that fix).
- **WL-0MS7TQVK2001X4EG — Standardize worklog root resolution** (open): touches the same plugin (`worklist.ts`/fetcher) — coordinate to avoid merge conflicts.
- **WL-0MS6SWL1P006XUZE — Colour coding in herdr selection list improvements** (open): also touches the plugin's renderer; coordinate changes to `worklist.ts`.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1 (Map → user): "Centered toasts — herdr 0.7.5's `notification.show` only supports corner positions. Do you mean (a) use herdr's toast notification system as-is (default bottom-right, or configured position), or (b) toasts must appear centered (which would need a herdr-side feature, since no center position exists yet)?" — Answer (user): "I feel certain that there is a 'bottom-center' or similar. If not then bottom-right will have to do." — Research: checked herdr 0.7.5 `herdr notification show --help` (positions: `top-left|top-right|bottom-left|bottom-right`) and herdr master `ToastHerdrPosition` enum (TopLeft/TopRight/BottomLeft/BottomRight only; `bottom-center` exists only for the clipboard toast config). Conclusion: no center position exists for `notification show`; `bottom-right` (the default) is the accepted position.
- Q2 (Map → user): "Which status updates should move to toasts — just the refresh/sync notifications, or also transient feedback like `Sent: ...`, `Skipped: ...`, and `Error: ...` from chord shortcuts?" — Answer (user): "all transient feedback".
- Q3 (Map → user): "`ui.toast.delivery` is currently `off` in your herdr config, which makes `herdr notification show` a no-op. Should this work item also ensure delivery is enabled (e.g., document/update config), or is that a separate concern?" — Answer (user): "I'll enable it." — Follow-up (user, during intake): "I can't find how to enable notifications, please do it for me." — Action: enabled `[ui.toast] delivery = "herdr"` in `~/.config/herdr/config.toml`, reloaded config (`herdr server reload-config` → `status: applied`), and verified `herdr notification show "Toast test"` returns `{"reason":"shown","shown":true}`.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MS631PQ80024R6W** – Strip !! and ! prefixes from Herdr plugin commands before sending to Herdr (completed)
- **WL-0MPYOXEWK009VWWA** – [test-failure] tests/audit_results_table.test.ts — failing test (completed)
- **WL-0MP0Y4C8M0065JRW** – wl CLI Integration Layer (safe command runner) (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `.worklog/worktrees/wl-SA-0MS1T7A5W003UJUH-remove-skill-ralph-directory-tree/docs/ralph.md` — matched: action, actions, active, add, already, also, api, app, appear, append, applied, arg, auto, automatically, avoid, based, binary, bool, call, cannot, cause, change, changes, checked, clear, cli, cmd, code, coding, command, commands, comments, complete, config, configured, confirmation, content, continue, criteria, critical, current, cut, default, directly, dispatch, docs, document, documentation, don, enable, enabled, ensure, environment, err, error, errors, every, exactly, exec, existing, exists, exit, explicitly, extra, fail, failed, failure, failures, fallback, false, feature, files, filter, find, fix, fixes, follow, form, full, header, help, helper, hold, holds, home, how, identical, including, inside, instead, intake, invoke, invokes, item, items, json, keep, key, like, limit, limited, line, lines, longer, loop, machine, map, may, mean, merge, message, model, move, multiple, must, native, need, new, non, none, note, notification, notifications, off, one, open, output, part, pass, passes, path, plan, plugin, position, previous, problem, process, rate, reason, related, release, remove, render, rendered, reports, request, requests, resolution, resolves, result, results, retry, returns, risk, root, run, runs, scope, second, see, select, sent, separate, server, set, setting, show, shown, shows, side, since, single, skill, skipped, small, specific, state, status, story, subprocess, supports, system, temporary, test, tests, text, there, they, tolerate, top, transient, two, under, unit, unless, update, use, used, user, using, via, want, when, work, working, worklog, would, wrapper, write, you, your

## Summary

`wl sync` can merge one project's worklog data into another project's database and push it to the wrong project's remote `refs/worklog/data`. This occurs when `wl sync` is invoked with `--worklog-dir` from a working directory inside a *different* git repository.

## Evidence

Investigation found this exact mechanism in production:

- `Tableau-Card-Engine/.worklog/logs/sync.log` at `2026-08-01T12:15:14Z` shows a sync with:
  - `file=/home/rgardler/projects/ContextHub/.worklog/worklog-data.jsonl` (cwd-based data path)
  - Local state: 2014 work items (TCE's clean DB, via `--worklog-dir`)
  - Remote state: 2109 work items (ContextHub's remote worklog ref)
- The merge wrote `2014 + 2109 = 4123` items into the TCE DB and pushed the polluted data to `origin refs/worklog/data` (commit `7dd8a920`, +11131 lines).
- SorraAgents was polluted the same way (`2026-08-01T14:25Z`).
- Every project DB now contains a full copy of the core ContextHub worklog (2117 WL- items incl. 523 deleted) — see the cleanup work item `related-to:WL-0MSAH2A71000MUA3`.

## Root cause

Two defects combine:

1. **`cli.ts` resolves the `-f/--file` default before the `--worklog-dir` override is applied.** `createPluginContext(program)` calls `getDefaultDataPath()` → `resolveWorklogDir()` at CLI startup based on the inherited process cwd. The `--worklog-dir` override is only applied later in the `preAction` hook (`cli.ts:203-205`). So `--worklog-dir <proj>/.worklog` redirects the DB, log file, and push target to the project — but the `-f` default (used by `sync.ts` `getRemoteDataFileContent(options.file, gitTarget)` for the remote fetch) still points at the cwd's repo.

2. **herdr's auto-sync spawns `wl sync` without a `cwd`** (`packages/herdr/src/auto-sync.ts` `runSync` → `spawn('wl', ['--worklog-dir', worklogDir, 'sync', ...])`). The child inherits the herdr pane's cwd, which can be inside a different repo than the tab's resolved worklog dir (`HERDR_RESOLVED_CWD`).

Net effect of `wl sync --worklog-dir <TCE>/.worklog` run from a ContextHub-repo cwd:
- DB / log / push target → TCE (override) — correct
- remote fetch → `git show <ContextHub's refs/worklog/data>:.worklog/worklog-data.jsonl` (cwd's repo) — WRONG project's data
- merged result (union, no prefix filter) is written to TCE's DB and pushed to TCE's remote

## User stories

- As a user running `wl sync` in any project, I expect sync to only ever read from and write to my own project's worklog data.
- As a maintainer, I expect `--worklog-dir`, `-f/--file`, and the git repo context to always refer to the same project.

## Suggested implementation approach

- Apply the `--worklog-dir` override before computing `ctx.dataPath` (move `createPluginContext` after the override is applied, or compute the `-f` default inside the action after the override is set).
- Add a safety guard: when `--worklog-dir` is set and the resolved remote data path belongs to a different git repo than cwd, fail loudly instead of merging.
- Make herdr's `runSync` pass `cwd` rooted at the tab's worklog project (and/or pass `-f` explicitly) so spawned `wl sync` always operates on the tab project.
- Optionally, filter merged items by the configured project prefix as a defense-in-depth guard.

## Related work items

- `discovered-from:WL-0MSAH26DD001XXST` (self)
- `related-to:WL-0MSAB7ZUC004SK7E` (wl sync lock storm: 60+ stuck sync processes spawned by worklist pane auto-sync)
- `related-to:WL-0MSAH2A71000MUA3` (cleanup of already-polluted project DBs)

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `wl sync --worklog-dir <proj>/.worklog` run from inside a different git repo either syncs only the target project's data or fails with a clear error; it never merges foreign-prefix items.
- [ ] Unit tests cover: dataPath resolution order with `--worklog-dir`; herdr auto-sync spawning with correct `cwd`; a guard test proving no cross-project merge is possible.
- [ ] All existing tests pass; no regressions in normal `wl sync` flows (no flags, `--worklog-dir` only, `-f` only).
- [ ] The original failing scenario is reproduced in a test and fixed.
**Key Files:**

- `src/cli.ts` — `createPluginContext` runs at module load (line ~236) before the `preAction` hook applies the `--worklog-dir` override (lines ~200-205); fix the resolution order here.
- `src/cli-utils.ts` — `createPluginContext` computes `ctx.dataPath` via `getDefaultDataPath()`; must reflect the override.
- `src/worklog-paths.ts` — `setWorklogDirOverride` / `resolveWorklogDir` (override bypasses cwd/git resolution).
- `src/jsonl.ts` — `getDefaultDataPath()` (`path.join(resolveWorklogDir(), 'worklog-data.jsonl')`).
- `src/commands/sync.ts` — `-f/--file` defaults to `dataPath` (line ~336); `getRemoteDataFileContent(options.file, ...)` fetches the remote from the cwd repo's ref.
- `src/sync.ts` — `getRemoteDataFileContent` resolves the relative path against the cwd repo root (`getRepoRoot()`).
- `packages/herdr/src/auto-sync.ts` — `runSync` spawns `wl sync` with `--worklog-dir` but no `cwd`; must pass the tab project's cwd.
- `tests/sync.test.ts` — reproduction + guard tests for dataPath resolution order and cross-project merge prevention.
- `packages/herdr/src/auto-sync.test.ts` — spawn `cwd` coverage.

## Summary

Every non-ContextHub project's worklog database contains a full copy of the core ContextHub worklog (thousands of WL- items), and the same data has been pushed into each project's `origin refs/worklog/data` ref. This pollutes project DBs, breaks `wl doctor prune` (it deletes ContextHub's deleted WL- items alongside the project's own), inflates sync payloads, and leaks ContextHub's internal work items into unrelated projects.

## Evidence

Original investigation (2026-08-01): `Tableau-Card-Engine/.worklog/logs/sync.log` shows the TCE DB jumping from 2014 → 4123 items at `2026-08-01T12:15:14Z` when a sync fetched ContextHub's remote worklog ref (2109 items) while writing to TCE's DB; the polluted data was then pushed to TCE's `refs/worklog/data` (commit `7dd8a920`). SorraAgents was polluted at `2026-08-01T14:25Z`. Confirmed live at investigation time: `wl doctor prune --days 0 --dry-run` in SorraAgents listed 836 candidates: 343 SA- + 493 WL-. Once in each project's git ref, routine `wl sync` re-pulls the WL- items, making the pollution self-sustaining.

Live verification at intake (2026-08-01, direct SQLite inspection of each project's `.worklog/worklog.db`):

| DB | Configured prefix | WL- (foreign) | Other foreign prefixes | Deleted items |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ContextHub (core) | WL | — | OB: 1 | 524 |
| SorraAgents | SA | 2129 | OB: 1 | 1168 |
| Tableau-Card-Engine | CG | 2131 | SA: 2, OB: 1 | 1154 |
| open_source_llm | OSL | 2108 | OB: 1 | 1432 |

Note: the same `OB-0MN9CZ48N0053L9Q` item ("Create a full PRD for OpenBrain", deleted) exists in **every** project including ContextHub core — likely a leaked test fixture. Tableau-Card-Engine also carries 2 foreign `SA-` items. So the foreign scope is broader than `WL-`: cleanup must remove any item whose prefix is not the project's configured prefix (`WL` / `SA` / `CG` / `OSL`, from each project's `config.yaml`).

## User stories

- As a project owner, I want my worklog to contain only my project's work items, so that prune, sync, search, and reporting operate on my data alone.
- As a ContextHub owner, I do not want core ContextHub work items (including deleted ones and test fixtures) to appear in unrelated projects' worklogs or remotes.

## Suggested implementation approach

1. **Fix first** (blocker `WL-0MSAH26DD001XXST`) — otherwise new pollution re-enters on the next sync.
2. **Clean each project's local SQLite DB**: remove items whose ID prefix is not the project's configured prefix (and their comments / dependency edges / audit results / FTS rows). Verify counts before/after.
3. **Clean each project's remote ref**: rewrite `origin refs/worklog/data` (and the local `refs/worklog/remotes/origin/...` tracking ref) with a JSONL containing only the project's own items; force-push. Coordinate to avoid clobbering concurrent project activity.
4. **Sweep other pollution sources**: check `~/.pi` skills scripts and herdr panes for any workflow that may re-import ContextHub data; also remove the leaked `OB-`/foreign rows found during verification.
5. Consider a `wl doctor` subcommand (e.g. `wl doctor foreign-items`) that reports/removes items whose prefix does not match the configured project prefix, with `--dry-run` and `--apply`, so this can be run safely on any project.

## Related work items

- `blocked-by:WL-0MSAH26DD001XXST` (root-cause fix — must land first; recorded as a dependency edge)
- `related-to:WL-0MSAB7ZUC004SK7E` (wl sync lock storm: 60+ stuck sync processes spawned by worklist pane auto-sync)

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] No project worklog DB (SorraAgents, Tableau-Card-Engine, open_source_llm, and any others found) contains WL- or other foreign-prefix items (including the shared OB- fixture and the SA- items in Tableau-Card-Engine) after cleanup.
- [ ] Each project's `origin refs/worklog/data` contains only that project's own items.
- [ ] `wl doctor prune --dry-run` in a cleaned project lists only the project's own deleted items.
- [ ] Cleanup is repeatable via a documented/automated mechanism (e.g. a `wl doctor` subcommand) so any future contamination can be removed safely.
- [ ] All tests pass; counts and item sets verified before and after cleanup (recorded in comments).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No interview was required: the work item was already fully specified at intake (headline, evidence, user stories, implementation approach, 5 measurable acceptance criteria) and was auto-completed per the intake skill heuristics. The evidence was re-verified live via direct SQLite inspection of all four project databases (`/home/rgardler/projects/{SorraAgents,Tableau-Card-Engine,open_source_llm,ContextHub}/.worklog/worklog.db`) and each project's `config.yaml` prefix. No open questions.

# Herdr plugin: fix work item list grouping (duplicate In Review sections, wrong group order)

## Problem statement

The grouping of items in the Herdr plugin's work item list is broken: for example, the list can show **two "In Review" sections**. The current grouping (`assignItemGroups` in `src/commands/grouping.ts`) also differs from the desired order — it lumps all critical items into one "Critical" group, groups plan_complete items by file-path conflicts but excludes intake_complete items from those groups, and emits sections in the wrong order (Critical, Other, Plan Complete Group N, In Review, Intake Complete, Idea).

Root cause of the duplicate sections (reproduced): Herdr merges `wl next` results (which carry `group`/`groupLabel` assignments) with mandatory subsets fetched via `wl list` (critical + completed/in_review items, which have **no** group assignment). `selectWorkItems` then reorders the merged list into `[criticals, reviews, others]`, which breaks group adjacency: ungrouped mandatory items blend into the preceding section without a separator, and an `in_review` item whose status is not `completed` falls into the "others" bucket while still carrying its "In Review" group label — producing a **second** "In Review" section later in the list.

## Users

- **Herdr users** (and Pi TUI Worklog extension users — the two selection lists are intentionally duplicated and exhibit the same bug) need a stable, predictable grouping so they can quickly scan actionable work.
- **Producers** rely on the list to review completed/in_review items; duplicate/confusing sections hide the review queue.

User story: *As a Herdr user, I want the work item list grouped in a predictable order (critical groups, then plan/intake groups, then idea, then other, then in review) so I can find and act on work without scanning duplicated section headings.*

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `wl next -n N --include-in-progress` (and the Herdr + Pi TUI selection lists) displays sections in exactly this order: **Critical Group 1..x**, **Group 1..x** (plan_complete + intake_complete), **Idea**, **Other**, **In Review** (last).
- [ ] Critical items are partitioned into file-path conflict groups labeled `Critical Group 1`, `Critical Group 2`, ... using the same greedy first-fit algorithm as non-critical items (items sharing a file path land in different groups; items with unknown paths get singleton groups). No single all-inclusive "Critical" group.
- [ ] Non-critical items with stage `plan_complete` or `intake_complete` are partitioned into file-path conflict groups labeled `Group 1`, `Group 2`, ... (no stage prefix in the label). Within each group, `plan_complete` items appear first, then `intake_complete` items, **without headings** between the two sub-groups; each sub-group is sorted by priority (high → medium → low).
- [ ] Within each `Critical Group N`, the same stage sub-sort applies: `plan_complete` items first, then `intake_complete` items, then remaining stages; each sub-group sorted by priority (all critical items share priority, so ordering within a stage sub-group is stable/deterministic).
- [ ] `idea` items appear in a single "Idea" section, sorted by priority (high → medium → low).
- [ ] All remaining items (unknown/other stages, `in_progress`, etc.) appear in a single "Other" section.
- [ ] All `in_review` items appear in a single "In Review" section that follows **all other groups** (i.e., after Other). The Herdr/TUI merged list must never render more than one "In Review" section.
- [ ] Herdr and Pi TUI merged lists (top-N `wl next` results + mandatory `wl list` subsets) show **no duplicate section headings** and every displayed item receives a correct group assignment (mandatory items included).
- [ ] Regression test reproduces the original bug: a merged list containing completed/in_review items from `wl list` plus an `in_review`/non-completed item from `wl next` renders exactly one "In Review" section, positioned after "Other".
- [ ] Unit tests updated/added in `tests/grouping-utility.test.ts`, Herdr (`packages/herdr/src/...`), and Pi TUI (`packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/...`) covering the new group order, Critical Group N splitting, within-group stage sub-sort + priority sort, and duplicate-section prevention.
- [ ] Full project test suite passes with the new changes; no regressions in existing grouping/smart-selection tests.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant docs site entries.

## Constraints

- Herdr plugin has **zero npm dependencies** — the grouping algorithm cannot be imported into the plugin from `src/commands/`. The smart-selection functions are *intentionally duplicated per TUI* (decision Q2c in WL-0MS8W5LTW006YZ4B); any client-side grouping added to the plugins must follow the same duplication pattern.
- `wl next -n N` hard-caps results at 32 items, so the mandatory subsets (critical + completed/in_review) are fetched separately via `wl list` — the fix must handle items arriving without group metadata from that path.
- CHANGELOG.md is managed automatically by the ship skill's release pipeline and must not be edited manually.
- Do not change `selectWorkItems`'s core guarantee: all critical and completed/in_review items are always shown regardless of `browseItemCount`; the count limit applies only to other items.

## Existing state

- `src/commands/grouping.ts` — `assignItemGroups()` currently produces, in order: `Critical` (single group), `Other`, `Plan Complete Group N` (file-path groups, plan_complete only), `In Review`, `Intake Complete` (single group), `Idea`. `groupItemsByFilePaths()` is the greedy first-fit algorithm.
- `src/commands/next.ts` — calls `assignItemGroups` when `count > 1`, sorts results by group, emits `group`/`groupLabel` on each JSON result entry.
- Herdr (`packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts`) and Pi TUI (`packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/tools.ts`) fetch `wl next -n N --include-in-progress`, merge with mandatory `wl list` subsets (`fetchMandatorySubsets`), then `selectWorkItems(merged, count)` returns `[criticals, reviews, others]` — reordering that breaks group adjacency and leaves mandatory items ungrouped.
- Renderers (`packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`, `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/browse.ts`) insert `── <groupLabel> ──` separators when `item.group` changes between consecutive items; items with `group === undefined` render without separators.

## Desired change

1. Rewrite `assignItemGroups()` in `src/commands/grouping.ts` to the new spec:
   - **Critical Group N** — critical items partitioned by file-path conflicts (reuse `groupItemsByFilePaths`), labels `Critical Group 1..x`, placed first.
   - **Group N** — non-critical `plan_complete` + `intake_complete` items partitioned by file-path conflicts, labels `Group 1..x`.
   - **Idea** — single group, all `idea` items.
   - **Other** — single group, everything else (unknown/other stages).
   - **In Review** — single group, all `in_review` items, placed last.
2. Apply within-group ordering: stage sub-sort (`plan_complete` → `intake_complete` → remaining stages) with priority sort (high → medium → low) inside each stage sub-group; no headings between stage sub-groups. Update `src/commands/next.ts` to emit the sorted order.
3. Fix the plugin merge path so the final displayed list is regrouped after selection (critical groups preserved, no duplicate sections). Given the zero-dependency constraint, duplicate the (pure, dependency-free) grouping logic into the Herdr plugin and Pi TUI extension following the existing smart-selection duplication pattern — OR apply the grouping in a way that keeps `wl next` as the single grouping authority (to be decided by the implementing agent; the ACs above are behavior-level).
4. Update/add unit and regression tests in both TUIs and `tests/grouping-utility.test.ts`.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/commands/grouping.ts` — `assignItemGroups()` rewrite: new group order (Critical Group N, Group N plan+intake, Idea, Other, In Review), Critical Group N splitting, within-group stage sub-sort + priority sort. May need a priority-order helper.
- `src/commands/next.ts` — apply within-group sorting when emitting JSON/text results (`group`, `groupLabel`, sort by group then stage-sub-group then priority).
- `src/commands/helpers.ts` — `extractFilePaths` / `GroupableItem` / `GroupAssignment` reused as-is; possibly add a priority-order helper.
- `tests/grouping-utility.test.ts` — rewrite/extend `assignItemGroups` tests for the new spec.
- `packages/herdr/src/smart-selection.ts` — regroup/order the final selected list (duplicated grouping logic, following the existing duplication pattern); do not break the always-show-mandatory guarantee.
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — ensure merged mandatory items receive group assignments (or the regrouping happens in `selectWorkItems`); verify `fetchMandatorySubsets` path.
- `packages/herdr/src/smart-selection.test.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` — new/updated tests: duplicate-section regression, group order in rendered output.
- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/smart-selection.ts` — same regrouping fix (duplicated per TUI).
- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/tools.ts` — merged-list handling if grouping is applied at fetch time.
- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/smart-selection.test.ts` — mirrored test updates.

## Related work

- **Herdr plugin: selection list header and top lines cut off top of pane (WL-0MSAAON63003N6LO)** — prior Herdr rendering fix; the renderer's separator/row-budget logic in `worklist.ts` is the code path that displays groups.
- **Selection list must always show all completed/in_review and critical items regardless of browseItemCount setting (WL-0MS8W5LTW006YZ4B)** — introduced `smart-selection.ts` (duplicated per TUI) and the mandatory-subset merge that causes the duplicate-section bug.
- **Create a work item selection list in Herdr (WL-0MS1W8Y1L0059AKP)** — introduced the Herdr selection list.
- **Unit tests for smart selection algorithm (both TUIs) (WL-0MS8XIUXU005ZR44)** — the test suites that must be extended.
- **Add Critical priority group to wl next grouping (c9d9cc6a)** — commit that added the single "Critical" group, which this work item replaces with Critical Group N.
- **Establish file-path convention for intake_complete items (39a7eddb, WL-0MQS2AZD50099JT1)** — intake_complete items already carry `**Key Files:**` sections, enabling their inclusion in file-path grouping.
- **Change plan_complete group label to 'Plan Complete Group N' (9525db61, WL-0MQS135HC003TMEL)** — prior grouping/label change this work item supersedes for the plan/intake groups.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Duplication risk:** copying the grouping algorithm into two plugins (Herdr + Pi TUI) creates maintenance burden; mitigations: keep the algorithm pure/deterministic, mirror tests, and reference the duplication decision (Q2c) in comments.
- **In Review placement:** the user explicitly chose a dedicated In Review group that follows all other groups (after Other). Items with stage `in_review` (any status) belong to it; completed/in_review mandatory items must also land there.
- **"Other" ordering:** not specified; assumed to keep the existing `wl next` order (already priority-ranked). Assumption documented for the implementing agent.
- **Stage sub-sort for critical groups:** user confirmed critical groups use the same stage sub-sort as non-critical groups (`plan_complete` → `intake_complete` → remaining stages).
- **Scope creep:** opportunities discovered during implementation should be recorded as linked work items, not folded into this fix.
- **Failure mode:** if grouping is only fixed in `wl next` but not the plugin merge path, Herdr/Pi TUI will still show duplicate sections — ACs require the merged (plugin) display to be fixed, not just the CLI.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "The grouping of items in the herdr plugin is broken, for example there are two In Review sections..." — Answer (operator): desired order is critical at top, then group 1-x items in intake_complete or plan_complete stages (plan_complete then intake_complete sub-groups without headings, each sorted by priority), then idea (sorted by priority), then "other". Source: interactive reply.
- Q: "Where should in_review items go? Options: (a) keep a dedicated 'In Review' section — where? (b) fold into 'Other', (c) something else" — Answer (operator): "(a) a dedicated group that follows all other groups." Source: interactive reply.
- Q: "Group labels — 'Group 1', 'Group 2' for plan/intake sections and 'Critical Group 1', ... for critical?" — Answer (operator): "yes." Source: interactive reply.
- Q: "Ordering within a Critical Group N — same stage sub-sort as other groups or keep wl next order?" — Answer (operator): "same stage sub-sort." Source: interactive reply.
- New requirement (operator): "The critical items should be in their own groups rather than in a single all-inclusive group. So we will have Critical Group 1, Critical Group 2 etc. The grouping logic is the same as it is for non-critical items." Source: interactive reply. Research: reproduced the duplicate "In Review" sections via a script exercising the Herdr fetch/merge/select pipeline (see Problem statement).
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MM38CRQN18HDDKF** – Improve duplicate error message (completed)
- **WL-0MQEBM6OM004Q1Q7** – Chord dispatch and help text in browse views (completed)
- **WL-0MLFURRPW0K02R52** – update dialog not updating record (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `.worklog/tmp/intake-draft-herdr-grouping-WL-0MSAK8YLB0025EGW.md` — matched: broken, complete, critical, desired, duplicate, fix, group, grouping, herdr, idea, intake, intent, item, items, list, order, plan, plugin, review, sections, there, top, two, work, wrong
- `.worklog/worktrees/wl-WL-0MS5URWJG000A6O5-align-icons/CLI.md` — matched: complete, critical, duplicate, fix, group, grouping, idea, intake, item, items, list, order, plan, plugin, review, sections, top, work
- `.worklog/worktrees/wl-WL-0MS7YCCLV000YJCR-auto-downgrade-critical-children-when-pa/CLI.md` — matched: complete, critical, duplicate, fix, group, grouping, idea, intake, item, items, list, order, plan, plugin, review, sections, top, work

# Intake Brief — wl sync timeouts: 10s Herdr auto-sync safety timeout kills legitimate slow syncs (WL-0MSAKM838006RZNR)

## Problem statement

The Herdr worklist pane's background auto-sync (`runSync` in `packages/herdr/src/auto-sync.ts`) has a **10-second safety timeout** that kills the `wl sync` child process and reports "wl sync timed out". Recent syncs legitimately take **5–19 seconds** (log measurements) because the worklog JSONL has grown to **11.6 MB (2133 items, 7494 comments)** and every sync fully re-exports and SSH-pushes the entire file. Auto-sync fires every **30 s** minimum, so slow syncs churn continuously and the pane frequently reports spurious sync failures.

## Users

- **Operator and Herdr worklist pane users** — see recurring `[Sync failed: wl sync timed out]` status/toast notifications despite the underlying sync usually succeeding moments later.
- **Agents and collaborators relying on `wl sync`** — when a sync is killed mid-push, the canonical `refs/worklog/data` ref can lag until the next sync completes; killed syncs also waste a full 11.6 MB export+push cycle.

User story: *As a user of the Herdr work items pane, I want background syncs that take longer than 10 seconds to complete normally rather than being killed and reported as failures, so the pane stays in sync without spurious timeout errors.*

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The Herdr auto-sync safety timeout is raised from 10 s to a value ≥ 60 s (aligned with the Pi TUI extension's `DEFAULT_WL_TIMEOUT_MS`), so a `wl sync` taking 10–19 s on the current dataset completes and is reported as successful.
- [ ] The safety-net purpose is preserved: if the spawned `wl sync` process hangs without ever firing `close`/`error` (e.g., binary missing, spawn failure), the promise still settles and the in-flight guard is released (no dangling promise, no lock-storm regression per WL-0MSAB7ZUC004SK7E).
- [ ] The single-flight guard and `--if-idle` lock-aware skip behavior are unchanged (no regression of lock-storm protection).
- [ ] Sync churn is reduced: the auto-sync minimum/default interval is raised from 30 s to 60 s (or made adaptive so a new sync is not spawned while the previous one is still running).
- [ ] Unit tests updated in `packages/herdr/src/auto-sync.test.ts` (the "triggers safety timeout after 10s" test) to cover the new timeout; all existing auto-sync tests and the full project test suite pass.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.

> **Note:** CHANGELOG.md is **excluded**; it is managed automatically by the ship skill's release pipeline.

## Constraints

- The 10 s timeout was intentionally added during the lock-storm fix (WL-0MSAB7ZUC004SK7E) to prevent dangling promises/process pile-up — keep a working safety net, just not one that fires on healthy syncs.
- `wl sync --if-idle` semantics must be preserved (skip when the cross-process file lock is held).
- Keep the change surgical: do **not** redesign the sync pipeline in this item. Incremental sync (only changed items) is a larger architectural effort already listed as a planned improvement in `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` — record as a follow-up work item rather than expanding scope.
- Do not touch CHANGELOG.md (managed by the ship skill's release pipeline).

## Existing state

- `packages/herdr/src/auto-sync.ts` — `runSync()` has `setTimeout(() => { child.kill(); settle({ success: false, error: 'wl sync timed out' }); }, 10_000)`. `MIN_SYNC_INTERVAL_MS = 30_000`, `DEFAULT_SYNC_INTERVAL_MS = 30_000`. Single-flight guard `_syncInFlight`; `--if-idle` passed on auto-sync.
- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/tools.ts` — `DEFAULT_WL_TIMEOUT_MS = Number(process.env.WL_RUN_TIMEOUT_MS) || 60_000`; `browse.ts` `_triggerAutoSync` fires `runWl(['sync', '--if-idle'])` with the 60 s timeout. Pi TUI is therefore already tolerant of slow syncs — only Herdr has the 10 s kill.
- `.worklog/logs/sync.log` — recent sync durations 4.8–19.1 s, mean ~7 s, frequent outliers >10 s (10.8, 11.0, 11.2, 11.4, 12.1, 13.1, 15.2, 16.2, 19.1 s).
- `wl sync debug` — remote data 11,651,037 bytes (2133 items, 7494 comments). Measured locally: dry-run 2.4 s, full sync 5.8 s (fetch/show/merge/export/push).
- Sync flow (`src/commands/sync.ts`, `src/sync.ts`) — `git fetch` → stream `git show` of remote JSONL → parse 11.6 MB → merge all items/comments/audits/edges → `db.import` → `db.exportForSync` (full 11.6 MB JSONL) → `gitPushDataFileToBranch` (temp worktree, copy file, commit, SSH push). Push/network variance is the main driver of the >10 s outliers.

## Desired change

1. In `packages/herdr/src/auto-sync.ts`, raise the safety timeout from `10_000` to `60_000` ms (optionally env-overridable, mirroring `WL_RUN_TIMEOUT_MS`).
2. Raise `MIN_SYNC_INTERVAL_MS` / `DEFAULT_SYNC_INTERVAL_MS` from 30 s to 60 s (or skip a tick while a sync is in-flight — the single-flight guard already prevents overlap within a pane).
3. Update `packages/herdr/src/auto-sync.test.ts` to assert the new timeout and interval behavior.
4. Create a follow-up work item (related-to this one) for incremental sync to shrink the per-sync payload.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/auto-sync.ts` — raise 10 s safety timeout; raise/adjust auto-sync interval constants.
- `packages/herdr/src/auto-sync.test.ts` — update the "triggers safety timeout after 10s" test and any interval tests; add a test that a slow-but-completing sync is not killed.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — reference only, if sync failure copy is surfaced here.
- `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` — reference only; incremental sync already listed as a planned improvement (follow-up item).

## Related work

- **wl sync lock storm: 60+ stuck sync processes spawned by worklist pane auto-sync (WL-0MSAB7ZUC004SK7E, completed)** — introduced the single-flight guard, `--if-idle`, and the 10 s safety timeout this item tunes.
- **Add exponential back-off to file lock retry (WL-0MM0BT1FA0X23LTN, completed)** — lock acquisition backoff; relevant if the pane ever waits on a contended lock.
- **Process-level mutex for import/export/sync (WL-0MLG0DSFT09AKPTK, completed)** — concurrency guard for sync operations.
- **wl CLI Integration Layer (safe command runner) (WL-0MP0Y4C8M0065JRW, completed)** — the `runWl` layer and its 60 s default timeout.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** the 10 s timeout is the direct cause of the user-visible "wl sync timed out" failures (evidence: sync durations >10 s in the log align with the kill threshold; Pi TUI with its 60 s timeout does not report these).
- **Risk:** raising the timeout too high could mask a genuinely hung sync for longer; 60 s matches the Pi TUI's existing default and bounds the hang to a reasonable worst case.
- **Risk:** changing `MIN_SYNC_INTERVAL_MS` affects the staleness of the pane's data — 60 s is still far below the Pi TUI's default auto-sync interval (5 min), so acceptable.
- **Failure mode:** if only the timeout is raised but not the interval, the pane may still spawn overlapping syncs across the 30 s window when syncs take >15 s — the `--if-idle`/lock guard prevents pile-up but a longer interval reduces wasted work.
- **Scope-creep guard:** incremental sync, git-protocol optimizations, and any redesign of the sync pipeline are separate work items; record as linked items, do not fold into this fix.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Should we do anything about the sync timeouts?" — Answer (operator): asked during intake; pending confirmation of scope. Draft assumes yes, minimal fix (raise timeout + reduce churn) with incremental sync as a follow-up. Source: user's original request ("I notice some wl sync timeouts, why are they happening and should we do anything about them?").

## Summary

Update/extend `tests/grouping-utility.test.ts` to lock in the new `assignItemGroups` specification from the parent work item: new group order, Critical Group N splitting, within-group stage sub-sort + priority sort, and duplicate-section prevention at the unit level.

## Background

The current `assignItemGroups()` in `src/commands/grouping.ts` produces the wrong order (Critical, Other, Plan Complete Group N, In Review, Intake Complete, Idea) and lumps all critical items into a single "Critical" group. This test feature captures the desired behavior; tests are expected to FAIL (red) against the current implementation and PASS after the implementation feature lands.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `tests/grouping-utility.test.ts` contains tests asserting the full group order: **Critical Group 1..x** → **Group 1..x** → **Idea** → **Other** → **In Review** (In Review last).

## Summary

Rewrite `assignItemGroups()` in `src/commands/grouping.ts` to the new specification and apply the within-group ordering in `src/commands/next.ts` so `wl next -n N` emits groups in the correct order with correct labels.

## Desired behavior

1. **Critical Group N** — critical items partitioned by file-path conflicts (reuse `groupItemsByFilePaths`), labels `Critical Group 1..x`, placed first.
2. **Group N** — non-critical `plan_complete` + `intake_complete` items partitioned by file-path conflicts, labels `Group 1..x`.
3. **Idea** — single group, all `idea` items.
4. **Other** — single group, everything else (unknown/other stages).
5. **In Review** — single group, all `in_review` items, placed last.

Within-group ordering: stage sub-sort (`plan_complete` → `intake_complete` → remaining stages) with priority sort (high → medium → low) inside each stage sub-group; no headings between stage sub-groups. `src/commands/next.ts` must emit the sorted order in both JSON output (`group`/`groupLabel` on each result entry) and CLI text output.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `assignItemGroups()` produces groups in exactly the order: Critical Group 1..x, Group 1..x, Idea, Other, In Review.
- [ ] Critical items are partitioned into file-path conflict groups labeled `Critical Group 1..x` using the greedy first-fit algorithm; no single all-inclusive "Critical" group.
- [ ] Non-critical `plan_complete` + `intake_complete` items are partitioned into `Group 1..x` with `plan_complete` items first, then `intake_complete` items (no headings between sub-groups), each sub-group sorted by priority (high → medium → low).

- [ ] `idea` items appear in a single "Idea" section sorted by priority; remaining items in a single "Other" section; `in_review` items in a single "In Review" section placed after Other.
- [ ] `wl next -n N --include-in-progress` JSON output emits `group`/`groupLabel` per result entry in the new order, and the CLI text output renders the same order with correct `── <label> ──` headings.
