# Herdr plugin: reserve bottom 40% of selection list for item metadata and last command (WL-0MSAYNVBY006LM9X)

## Problem statement

The Herdr work item selection list uses the full pane height for the item list, so users cannot see any metadata about the currently selected work item without pressing Enter to open the detail view. There is also no visibility into which commands have been executed against an in-progress item, making it hard to see what work has already been done on it.

## Users

- **Herdr users (human and AI agent)** browsing the work item list in a pane, who want the selected item's key metadata visible at all times without switching to the detail view.
- **Producers** reviewing `in_progress` items, who want to know the most recent command executed on an item to understand its current state at a glance.

### User stories

- As a Herdr user, I want to see the selected item's metadata (ID, status, stage, priority, type, risk, effort, tags, timestamps, audit state, child count) in the lower part of the list pane, so I can triage without opening the detail view.
- As a Herdr user, when I move the selection (arrow keys, j/k, page keys, first/last), I want the metadata panel to update immediately to the newly selected item.
- As a producer, when the selected item is still `in_progress`, I want to see the most recent command executed on it, so I know what step it is on.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Responsive metadata panel**: The list renderer reserves a metadata panel at the bottom of the pane whose height scales with total pane height — between a minimum share (default **20%**) and a maximum share (default **40%**) — so the selection list always keeps the majority of the space (≥60%) and avoids scrolling on typical pane sizes. On taller panes the panel grows toward 40%; on shorter panes it shrinks toward 20%.
2. **Selection-driven updates**: The metadata panel reflects the currently selected item and updates immediately when the selection changes (up/down, j/k, PgUp/PgDn, g/G, wrap, filter changes).
3. **All metadata fields shown**: The panel shows all available `WorkItem` fields — id, title, status, stage, priority, issue type, risk, effort, tags, createdAt, updatedAt, childCount, needsProducerReview, auditResult/auditedAt, githubIssueNumber, parentId.
4. **Last command display**: When the selected item's stage is `in_progress`, the panel additionally shows the most recent command executed on that item, sourced from the plugin's command log.
5. **Command log**: The plugin records commands it executes/dispatches against a work item (agent skill invocations `/skill:*`, workflow commands `/intake`, `/plan`, and `wl`-routed commands that carry an item ID) into a local JSON log (default `~/.config/herdr/worklog-command-log.json`), keyed by work item ID, timestamped, with a bounded size (pruned/rotated).
6. **Scrollable metadata**: When the metadata content overflows the panel's current height, the panel scrolls (independent scroll offset); list navigation remains functional.
7. **No regression**: The existing detail view (Enter), keyboard navigation, filtering, group separators, and the last-row notification budget continue to work.
8. **Testing**: Unit tests cover the responsive layout split (20–40% metadata share), selection-driven metadata updates, command log write/read/prune, in_progress last-command display, and metadata scroll behaviour.
9. **Docs**: All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
10. **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

> **Note:** CHANGELOG.md is **excluded** from this list. It is managed automatically by the ship skill's release pipeline. Implementing agents should not manually update CHANGELOG.md.

## Constraints

- The command log is plugin-local — no new `wl` CLI features or backend schema changes are required.
- The command log must be safe with concurrent writes from multiple panes (single-flight / atomic append) and must never break the plugin if the file is missing or corrupt.
- The metadata panel must fit within the existing pane-height budget (last row reserved for notifications); group-separator accounting in the list must not overflow.
- Preserve existing keyboard bindings; any new key binding for metadata-panel scrolling must not conflict with list navigation.
- Commands executed outside the plugin (e.g., `wl` CLI in a separate terminal) are **not** visible in the log — this is a documented limitation.

## Existing state

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — `createListRenderer()` renders header + blank + filter bar + items + group separators + fill + footer, budgeting output to `rows - 1` lines (last row reserved for the notification line). `formatDetailContent()` already formats metadata for the detail view (Enter). `dispatchChordCommand()` / `resolveAndRouteCommand()` resolve `<id>` placeholders and route commands to `onCommand`.
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — `WorkItem` interface carries id, title, status, priority, stage, parentId, risk, effort, description, tags, issueType, childCount, createdAt, updatedAt, githubIssueNumber, needsProducerReview, auditResult, auditedAt, group/groupLabel, children, depth.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — entry point wires `onCommand`, routes agent commands to pi panes and `!!`/`!` commands to visible panes.
- No command log exists today; nothing tracks which commands were executed against which item.
- Settings are persisted in `~/.config/herdr/worklog-plugin.json` (via `settings.ts`).

## Desired change

1. Add a command log module (`command-log.ts`): `recordCommand(itemId, command)`, `getLastCommand(itemId)`, with persistence to `~/.config/herdr/worklog-command-log.json` (path configurable, e.g. via settings), bounded size (e.g., keep most recent N per item or global prune), and safe concurrent writes.
2. Wire the log into `index.ts` (and/or `worklist.ts` dispatch paths): every command executed against a work item records `{ itemId, command, timestamp }`.
3. Modify `createListRenderer()` to split the pane: top portion (≥60%) for the existing list rendering, bottom portion for a responsive metadata panel — height scaled between ~20% and ~40% of pane height based on `termSize.rows` (taller panes get a larger panel; shorter panes shrink it so the list keeps the majority of the space and does not scroll) — built from the selected `WorkItem` (reusing/normalizing `formatDetailContent` metadata sections) plus the last-command line when the item is `in_progress`.
4. Add metadata-panel scroll state (separate `metaScrollOffset`) and key handling for scrolling it when content overflows.
5. Re-render on selection change already occurs; ensure the metadata panel is derived from the selected item each render.
6. Update README (features, usage, settings, architecture) and code comments; add tests.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — renderer layout split (responsive 20–40% metadata panel), metadata panel rendering, meta scroll state/handling.
- `packages/herdr/src/command-log.ts` — new module: command log persistence (record/read/prune).
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — wire command recording at dispatch/execution points.
- `packages/herdr/src/settings.ts` — optional setting for command log path/limits.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` — unit tests for layout, selection updates, last-command display, scroll.
- `packages/herdr/src/command-log.test.ts` — unit tests for log write/read/prune/concurrency.
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — feature, usage, settings, architecture documentation.

## Related work

- **WL-0MS1W8Y1L0059AKP** — Create a work item selection list in Herdr (completed): the base selection list this work extends.
- **WL-0MLORPQUE1B7X8C3** — TUI: 50/50 split layout with metadata & details panes (completed): Pi TUI reference for a split list/metadata layout and metadata field set.
- **WL-0MS3ALBD40006RGD** — Add audit result display to Herdr plugin detail view (completed): precedent for metadata display in the Herdr plugin detail view.
- **WL-0MQ028WKW005I81L** — Verify and fix audit information display in TUI meta-data section (completed): metadata display conventions.
- **WL-0MQ9E164R0002DNF** — Replace confusing metadata lines in TUI work item detail view with clean metadata header (completed): metadata formatting conventions.
- **WL-0MS631PQ80024R6W** — Strip `!!` and `!` prefixes from Herdr plugin commands before sending to Herdr (completed): relevant to the command dispatch paths the command log will hook into.
- **WL-0MLB703EH1FNOQR1** — Exclude deleted from list (completed): list filtering behaviour in the same plugin.

## Related work (automated report)

Automated discovery (via find_related) flagged: WL-0MLB703EH1FNOQR1 (list filtering), WL-0MS631PQ80024R6W (Herdr command prefix stripping), WL-0MNX8MASB007TADZ (dialog focus tests).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption**: Commands dispatched by the plugin are the primary signal for "most recent command executed"; commands run externally (raw `wl` CLI, other tools) will not appear. Documented limitation.
- **Risk**: The command log grows unbounded. Mitigation: bounded entries per item and/or global cap with pruning on write.
- **Risk**: Concurrent writes from multiple herdr panes corrupt the log. Mitigation: atomic write (write temp + rename) or single-flight in-process guard (pattern already used by auto-sync).
- **Risk**: A fixed 40% may be excessive on small terminals (leaving too few rows for the list). Mitigation: the panel height scales between ~20% and ~40% of pane height — shrinking on short panes so the list keeps the majority of the space; metadata content that still overflows scrolls within the panel.
- **Risk**: Metadata panel scroll keys conflict with list navigation. Mitigation: keep scroll state tied to the list selection — metadata follows the selected item; use a dedicated key (e.g., `m`/`M` or `[`/`]`) only when metadata overflows, or auto-scroll to keep the last-command line visible.
- **Scope creep risk**: Adding richer metadata editing, command output history playback, or cross-pane command logs would expand scope — record as follow-up work items rather than extending this item.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1**: "Where should the 'most recent command executed' data come from?" — **Answer** (user): Option (a) — the plugin logs commands it dispatches/executes against a work item (skill invocations, `wl` updates, agent commands) to a local file (e.g. `~/.config/herdr/worklog-command-log.json`), keyed by work item ID. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q2**: "Which metadata fields should the panel show?" — **Answer** (user): All available fields (`id`, `title`, `status`, `stage`, `priority`, `type`, `risk`, `effort`, `tags`, `createdAt`, `updatedAt`, `childCount`, `auditResult`, `needsProducerReview`, and any others in `WorkItem`). Source: interactive reply.
- **Q3**: "Should the metadata panel scroll when content overflows?" — **Answer** (user): Yes, scroll. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q4**: "Can we make the metadata panel space expandable?" — **Answer** (user): Yes — the panel should grow/shrink based on the total pane height rather than a fixed 40%, using a min/max share (e.g., between 20% and 40%) and always giving the majority of the space to the selection list so the list does not need to scroll. Defaults of 20%/40% are assumed; adjustable. Source: interactive reply.
data.title: Herdr plugin: reserve bottom 40% of selection list for item metadata and last command

# Intake Brief — Central cache for wl read results to cut Herdr refresh spawn churn (WL-0MSAZQEQB008O7H3)

## Problem statement

Herdr Work Items panes each run an instance of the herdr plugin (`packages/herdr/src/index.ts`) that auto-refreshes every 30s. Each refresh shells out to the `wl` CLI 4–5 times per pane, and `auto-sync.ts` spawns `wl sync --if-idle` per instance. With 6 open panes sharing `.worklog` dirs this is ~100+ `wl` node-process spawns/minute, and many panes run **byte-identical queries**. On a loaded host each spawn is expensive (measured ~18s wall for a single `wl list` at load ~200), and the spawn churn and load feed each other. Refresh cadence must stay at 30s; the goal is to serve repeat read queries from a shared cache so identical results are computed once.

## Users

- **Herdr users** with multiple Work Items panes open against the same `.worklog` dir — they see the bulk of the spawn churn and system load.
- **Pi agents / status polling** — agent-driven `wl next`/`list`/`status` polling across projects dominates spawn count; they benefit from the same cache without any herdr-specific change.
- **Audit scripts and other CLI consumers** of read commands.

User stories:
- As a Herdr user with 6 panes open, I want repeat queries to be served from cache so my machine isn't pegged by ~100 wl process spawns/minute.
- As an agent running status checks, I want identical read queries to hit a shared cache so my polling doesn't add spawn load.
- As an operator, I want the refresh cadence (30s) unchanged while the wl process spawn rate drops by ≥60%.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Repeated identical read queries within the invalidation window return cached results without spawning a new wl process (verify via spawn instrumentation/logging or timing).
2. Cache invalidates when the SQLite DB changes (create/update/claim/status change) — must handle WAL mode (`worklog.db-wal`/`-shm` mtimes or content fingerprint); a write followed by a query returns fresh data immediately.
3. Writes (`create`/`update`/`claim`/`sync`) are never served from cache and invalidate the affected entries.
4. All covered read commands honor full argv as part of the cache key: `list` (incl. `--root-only`, `--status`, `--priority`, `--stage`, `-n`), `next` (incl. `-n`, `--include-in-progress`), `show`, `search`.
5. Cache is safe under concurrent readers/writers (multiple panes + agents); no corruption; bounded size with TTL/staleness cap.
6. All existing tests pass; new tests cover invalidation (WAL-mode write), key collisions, arg-variant separation, and concurrent access.
7. Measurable impact: with 6 panes on shared worklog dirs, wl process spawn rate drops by ≥60% (identical-query dedupe) while refresh cadence stays 30s.

## Constraints

- **Refresh cadence must NOT change** — 30s `refreshIntervalMs` stays as-is.
- Cache correctness is sound only if read results are a deterministic function of DB state + args — the cache must never serve stale data after a write.
- WAL mode: `.worklog/worklog.db` mtime alone is unreliable (writes land in `worklog.db-wal`, observed 16MB WAL); invalidation must watch db + `-wal` + `-shm`.
- Cache must be safe under concurrent readers/writers across processes (multiple panes + pi agents on the same worklog dir).
- No changes to work-item tracking tooling; everything tracked in wl.

## Existing state

- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` shells out via `execFileAsync` 4–5× per refresh (`next -n N --include-in-progress`, `list --priority critical --root-only`, `list --status completed --stage in_review --root-only`, `list --status open,in-progress,blocked`).
- `packages/herdr/src/auto-sync.ts` spawns `wl sync --if-idle` per instance (per-process single-flight guard already exists, but no cross-instance coordination).
- Read commands (`list`, `next`, `show`, `search`) live in `src/commands/*.ts`, registered in `src/cli.ts`; they read from SQLite via `src/database.ts`.
- No read cache exists anywhere today; every consumer spawns a fresh `wl` process per query.

## Desired change

Implement, in order of leverage:

- **A. wl CLI-level read cache (primary):** pure-read commands cache their JSON result keyed by (worklog-dir, argv) in **`~/.cache/wl/`** (XDG cache dir); invalidate when SQLite DB changed (WAL-aware: mtime/size of db + `-wal` + `-shm`, or cheap content fingerprint). TTL (e.g., 30–60s) as a bounding safety net. Benefits ALL consumers from one change in the wl core.
- **E. Coordinated sync (single-flight across instances):** coordinate `wl sync --if-idle` via a lock file (one owner per worklog-dir) to cut redundant git push/pull churn; sync also invalidates the read cache (post-sync data is fresh).
- **D. Per-instance in-process memoization:** dedupe concurrent identical queries within one pane process — cheap interim win layered on top.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/read-cache.ts` (new) — central cache module: key derivation (worklog-dir + argv), XDG cache dir resolution (`~/.cache/wl/`), WAL-aware invalidation, TTL/bounding, atomic concurrent-safe writes.
- `src/cli.ts` — wire cache lookup/backfill around pure-read commands (`list`, `next`, `show`, `search`); ensure write commands bypass and invalidate.
- `src/commands/list.ts`, `src/commands/next.ts`, `src/commands/show.ts`, `src/commands/search.ts`, `src/commands/status.ts` — route read results through the cache at the command layer.
- `src/commands/sync.ts` / `src/sync.ts` — invalidate cache entries after successful sync; coordinate `--if-idle` via lock file (option E).
- `src/database.ts` — invalidation relies on DB change detection (may need a cheap fingerprint helper for db + `-wal` + `-shm`).
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — optionally dedupe identical concurrent queries in-process (option D); no change to refresh cadence.
- `packages/herdr/src/auto-sync.ts` — cross-instance sync coordination hooks (option E).
- Tests: `tests/` for the wl core cache (`read-cache.test.ts`), plus existing herdr tests for fetcher/auto-sync.

## Related work

- **Investigate excessive wl process spawning (206 concurrent, ~17 GB RAM) (WL-0MSB19J56006E87J)** — completed investigation (bug) that quantified the spawn storm across five projects; the data (13 pi agents, 206 concurrent wl processes, ~17GB RAM) is the motivation for this item.
- **wl sync lock storm: 60+ stuck sync processes spawned by worklist pane auto-sync (WL-0MSAB7ZUC004SK7E)** — completed (feature); introduced per-process single-flight in `auto-sync.ts`; option E extends this to cross-instance coordination.
- **Implement spawn wrapper for wl commands (WL-0MP15AM1N001OBII)** — completed; `src/wl-integration/spawn.ts` provides safe spawn with timeout; relevant to instrumentation for spawn-rate verification (AC 1).
- **Process lifecycle utility module (WL-0MRTSOK8C009CDLA)** — completed; process lifecycle infra that may inform cache-process cleanup.
- **Investigate spawnImpl consistency in TUI controller (WL-0MN9FA47D008KLNG)** — completed; related spawn-churn context in the TUI.
- Docs: `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` (worklog architecture incl. SQLite/JSONL sync model); `packages/herdr/` plugin docs.

## Options analysis (from original description, retained)

- **A. wl CLI-level read cache (recommended primary)** — benefits ALL consumers (herdr panes, pi agents' status polling, audit scripts) from one change in the wl core. Correctness sound: read results are a deterministic function of DB state + args. Must be WAL-aware. TTL as safety net / cache bounding.
- **B. Shared on-disk cache in the herdr plugin (fallback)** — contained to herdr but doesn't help pi agents' `wl` polling; risk of two parallel cache implementations drifting. **Out of scope** (superseded by A).
- **C. Persistent wl daemon per worklog-dir (`wl server`)** — eliminates node startup + DB-open cost entirely; biggest architectural change; lifecycle/crash-recovery/version-skew concerns. Natural long-term successor — **tracked as future work, not in this item**.
- **D. Per-instance in-process memoization** — dedupe concurrent identical queries within one pane process. Cheap, low risk, tiny win. **In scope** (cheap interim layered on A).
- **E. Coordinated sync (single-flight across instances)** — `wl sync --if-idle` from 6 instances is redundant; coordinate via lock file or one owner per worklog-dir. Complements A/B; sync also invalidates the read cache. **In scope.**
- **F. Route plugin reads through the worklog API server (port 3000)** — requires a running server per project; new infra dependency. **Not preferred / out of scope.**

## Risks & assumptions

- **Stale-data risk:** any missed write → cached stale read served. Mitigation: WAL-aware invalidation + TTL bounding; writes bypass cache and invalidate.
- **Cross-version risk:** a wl binary upgrade with a changed output schema could serve stale-shaped cache entries. Mitigation: include wl version in cache key or validate schema on read.
- **Concurrency risk:** multiple panes/agents writing the cache simultaneously. Mitigation: atomic temp-file + rename writes; per-key locking; TTL bounding.
- **Cache pollution risk:** a malformed argv variant or unusual worklog-dir path creating unbounded distinct keys. Mitigation: bounded cache size / LRU-eviction + TTL.
- **Scope-creep risk:** `wl server` (option C) is attractive but out of scope; record as a linked future work item rather than expanding this item.
- **Assumption:** identical argv across panes yields byte-identical output today (i.e., output is deterministic given DB state) — verified in practice by the description's "byte-identical queries" observation.
- **Assumption:** load-induced spawn slowness (~18s wall for `wl list`) is scheduling contention, not per-command CPU — so spawn-count reduction directly cuts wall time.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Which options are in scope for this work item? A only, A+E, or A+E+D?" — Answer (operator): "A+E+D". Source: interactive reply. Rationale: A is the primary win, E cuts redundant sync churn, D is a cheap interim layer. B/F excluded (superseded / infra-dependent), C tracked as future work.
- Q2: "Preferred cache location?" — Answer (operator): "~/.cache/wl/ (XDG)". Source: interactive reply. Cache dir resolves under the XDG cache home.
- Q3: "TTL safety net acceptable alongside file-change invalidation, or strictly file-driven?" — Answer (operator): "as you prefer". Decision (agent): TTL (30–60s, aligned with the 30s refresh cadence) as a bounding safety net in addition to WAL-aware file-change invalidation; file-change detection is the primary freshness mechanism, TTL guards against missed invalidations and bounds cache size.

## Plan (approved 2026-08-06, /skill:plan)

4 vertical-slice child features (each cuts through code + tests + docs + observability; test-first via TDD within each slice). F1 is the tracer bullet, then breadth (F2), then E (F3) and D (F4).

1. **F1 — Read-cache core module with WAL-aware invalidation** (no deps): `src/read-cache.ts` + unit tests; XDG `~/.cache/wl/`; key = hash(worklog-dir, argv, wl version); WAL-aware freshness (db + `-wal` + `-shm`); TTL 30–60s; atomic concurrent-safe writes; bounded purge.
2. **F2 — Wire read commands through cache; spawn instrumentation** (deps: F1): route `list`/`next`/`show`/`search`/`status` (JSON mode) through cache in `src/cli.ts`; writes bypass + invalidate; env-gated spawn counter to verify ≥60% spawn reduction (AC7).
3. **F3 — Sync invalidation + cross-instance heartbeat** (deps: F1, F2): successful `wl sync` invalidates cache + writes per-worklog-dir heartbeat; `auto-sync.ts` skips spawning when heartbeat fresh.
4. **F4 — Herdr in-process memoization** (deps: F2): promise-keyed memo in `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` for concurrent identical fetches; cadence unchanged.

## Appendix: Planning Q&A (from /skill:plan session)

- Q1: "Command coverage beyond AC4's list? A) Strictly AC4 (list/next/show/search). B) AC4 + `status` (pi-agent polling is the top spawn source per the investigation). C) AC4 + `status` + `recent` + `in-progress`." — Answer (operator): "1. B". Final: covered commands = `list`, `next`, `show`, `search`, `status` (JSON mode).
- Q2: "Cache output scope? A) JSON-mode only (recommended — deterministic given DB state + argv; covers all real consumers). B) Cache raw stdout for all modes keyed incl. env/TTY fingerprint." — Answer (operator): "2. A". Final: JSON-mode only; text output bypasses cache.
- Q3: "Scope of E (sync coordination)? A) Only: successful `wl sync` invalidates the read cache. B) A + cross-instance sync heartbeat (auto-sync skips spawning `wl sync` if one succeeded recently)." — Answer (operator): "3. B". Final: invalidation + heartbeat.
- Q4: "Approve the 4-feature draft plan?" — Answer (operator): "approved". Final: approved as-is.

## Plan: changelog

- 2026-08-06 (Map, /skill:plan): Pre-check returned `plan` (risk High). Decomposed into 4 child features (F1–F4) with dependency edges. Scope confirmed via Q&A: covered commands = AC4 + `status`; JSON-mode-only cache; E = invalidation + heartbeat. Key Files updated (added `src/commands/status.ts`). Plan Q&A appendix appended above.

# Investigate Excessive wl Process Spawning

## Problem statement

Thirteen `pi` agent processes are spawning 206 concurrent `wl` CLI subprocesses across five projects (Tableau-Card-Engine, SorraAgents, ContextHub, open_source_llm, dev-scripts), consuming approximately 17 GB of RAM. These short-lived CLI processes — which should complete in seconds — accumulate without cleanup, suggesting a systematic lifecycle issue in the agent framework or skill implementations.

## Users

- **AI agent operators** — Agents running for 1–2+ hours should not accumulate orphaned subprocesses.
- **Release managers** — The release process relies on stable CI/agent infrastructure.
- **Developer agents (all)** — Every agent using the `wl` tool across any project is affected.

Example user stories:
- _"As an agent operator, I want each `wl` CLI invocation to terminate within seconds, so that agent sessions don't leak memory."_
- _"As an AI agent, I want repeated worklog queries (e.g., `wl next`, `wl list`) to reuse results or be batched, so I don't spawn hundreds of processes."_
- _"As a release manager, I want the dev-to-main release process to run on stable infrastructure without RAM exhaustion from leaked processes."_

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Root cause identified and documented** — A clear explanation of which component(s) in the `pi` agent framework or skill implementations spawn `wl` processes and why they are not being cleaned up.
2. **Spawn trace captured** — A process tree or spawn trace showing the parent-child relationship between `pi` agents and their `wl` subprocesses, including timestamps and command lines, sufficient to identify the spawning pattern.
3. **Actionable remediation plan** — A prioritized list of changes (framework-level or skill-level) to eliminate the excessive process spawning, with estimated effort for each change.
4. **Agent spawning behavior documented** — A description of how agents currently invoke `wl` commands (per-query spawning, batched, cached), including which skills or code paths are responsible for the bulk of the invocations (`wl list`, `wl next`, `wl sync`).
5. **Health check mechanism proposed** — A recommendation for a lightweight health check or watchdog (e.g., periodic `ps` count threshold alert) that can detect future regressions before they reach 200+ processes.

## Constraints

- Investigation must cover all five affected projects (Tableau-Card-Engine, SorraAgents, ContextHub, open_source_llm, dev-scripts).
- The `pi` agent framework code lives in `/usr/local/lib/node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/` — this is external to the worklog repo but must be inspected.
- The `wl` CLI is a Node.js binary (global npm install).
- Any remediation plan must not require changes to the global agent framework unless justified — prefer skill-level or agent-level fixes.

## Existing state

- A **process lifecycle utility module** (WL-0MRTSOK8C009CDLA, completed) tracks child PIDs against worktree paths, but only for worktree/git operations — not for `wl` CLI invocations.
- A **spawn wrapper for wl commands** (WL-0MP15AM1N001OBII, completed) provides safe spawning with timeouts, but it's unclear if agents use it or invoke `wl` directly via `bash`.
- The **heartbeat skill** polls `wl next` and `wl list` commands periodically; its scheduling behavior may contribute.
- Orphaned `wl create` processes were found in a test worktree (WL-0MSB447TJ000R3N8, open/high), which is related but distinct from the general spawning issue.
- 13 `pi` agent processes are running, each spawning dozens of `wl` subprocesses. Agents run for 1–2+ hours without cleanup.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/core/bash-command.ts` (or equivalent) in the `pi` agent framework — how the `bash` tool executes shell commands
- `src/core/wl-command.ts` (or equivalent) — how the `wl` tool invokes the CLI
- `skill/heartbeat/scripts/heartbeat.py` — heartbeat polling logic

# Pi extension polls wl list / wl next even when selection list is not visible

## Problem

Pi agent sessions continuously spawn `wl list` / `wl next` subprocesses even when the work-item selection list (browse pane) is not visible. Each `wl` invocation spawns a new Node.js process (~50 MB), and with 13 concurrent pi agents this produced **206 concurrent wl processes consuming ~17 GB RAM** and load averages of 150-225 on a 16-core host.

## Observed Evidence

- 13 `pi` agent processes running concurrently (4 min to 2.5 hours elapsed), each spawning dozens of `wl` subprocesses per minute
- Commands observed being respawned continuously:
  - `wl list --status open,in-progress,blocked --json`
  - `wl next -n 20 --include-in-progress --json`
  - `wl list --priority critical --root-only --json`
  - `wl list --status completed --stage in_review --root-only --json`
  - `wl sync --if-idle`
- Killing the wl processes frees memory only temporarily — the pi agents respawn them within seconds
- The 206-count snapshot was during a period when no selection list interaction was happening (agents were idle/processing elsewhere)

## Hypothesis

The pi extension's work-item selection list (browse pane) polls `wl list` / `wl next` on a refresh cadence regardless of whether the pane is actually visible/rendered. When the pane is hidden or the user is working in another context, the polling continues unnecessarily. The `wl sync --if-idle` spawns may also continue per-agent even when not needed.

## Expected Behaviour

- If a selection list / browse pane is not visible, it must not poll `wl list` / `wl next`
- Polling should only run when the pane is rendered and being viewed
- `wl sync --if-idle` should not run when no visible pane requires fresh data

## Investigation Steps

1. Locate the pi extension code that drives the work-item selection list polling (likely in the browse/selection pane lifecycle)
2. Determine when the pane is created/destroyed and whether polling starts/stops with visibility
3. Confirm whether hidden panes or non-visible tabs keep polling
4. Identify the refresh cadence and why it fires when invisible

## Acceptance Criteria

1. When no work-item selection list is visible in a pi session, no `wl list` / `wl next` processes are spawned by that session
2. When the selection list becomes visible, polling resumes
3. `wl sync --if-idle` only runs when needed (visible pane requiring fresh data)
4. Measurable: with N idle pi agents and no visible selection lists, wl process count stays near 0
5. All existing tests pass

## Related

- discovered-from: WL-0MSB19J56006E87J (Investigate excessive wl process spawning)
- related-to: WL-0MSAZQEQB008O7H3 (Central cache for wl read results to cut Herdr refresh spawn churn)

# Tests — Idle-gated auto-refresh/auto-sync in browse widget

## Summary

Test-first coverage for pausing the pi Worklog extension's 5-second auto-refresh (and auto-sync) while the browse selection widget is idle (no user keypresses within the idle threshold), so hidden or unused selection lists stop spawning `wl` processes.

## Context

Parent: Pi extension polls wl list / wl next even when selection list is not visible (WL-0MSB1N0HB0007N6N). Root-cause investigation (WL-0MSB19J56006E87J) confirmed the pi extension `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/browse.ts` `defaultChooseWorkItem` runs a 5s `setInterval` for the entire custom-widget session (`ctx.ui.custom(...)` until `done()`), regardless of user interaction or agent activity. Each tick spawns 4-5 wl processes (`next -n N --include-in-progress`, `list --priority critical --root-only`, `list --status completed --stage in_review --root-only`, `list --status open,in-progress,blocked`, plus `wl sync --if-idle` via `_triggerAutoSync`) ≈ 60 spawns/min per mounted widget. `WL_PIMAN=1` auto-opens the browse flow on `session_start`, so every piman-launched pi session mounts the poller by default. This feature writes the tests for the idle-gating behavior.

## User stories

- As an operator with N idle pi sessions, I want the browse selection widget to stop polling when it has had no keypresses for the idle threshold, so wl process churn drops to ~0 while agents work elsewhere.
- As a user actively browsing work items, I want the list to keep auto-refreshing at the existing cadence while I interact, so I don't lose live updates.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. New tests (in `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/browse.test.ts` or a new colocated test file) cover the idle-gated interval with fake timers; the fetcher is mocked so invocation counts are observable (no real `wl` spawns)
2. Tick within the idle window (interaction within `IDLE_PAUSE_MS`) → refresh fetch invoked (current behavior preserved while active)
3. Tick after the idle threshold (no keypresses for > `IDLE_PAUSE_MS`) → fetch NOT invoked (zero wl spawns)
4. Auto-sync trigger (`_triggerAutoSync`) is also skipped when idle
5. A keypress after an idle pause triggers an immediate refresh and resumes the cadence
6. Widget mount counts as interaction (freshly opened widget starts in active state)
7. Detail-view widget (which has no interval) is unaffected; manual actions (navigation, shortcuts, `r`/`S`-style refreshes) still work regardless of idle state
8. Tests run green: `npx vitest run packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/browse.test.ts` (plus any new test file)

## Minimal implementation

- Follow existing mock patterns in `browse.test.ts` (`vi.mock('@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent')`, mock `ctx.ui.custom` widget factory returning `{ render, invalidate, handleInput }`)
- Use `vi.useFakeTimers()` + `vi.advanceTimersByTime()` to drive the interval; mock the fetch path (e.g. `run`/`listWorkItems`) to count invocations
- Cover the resume-on-keypress path by calling the widget's `handleInput` after advancing time

## Dependencies

- None (test-first: precedes the implementation feature)

## Deliverables

- Test file changes under `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/`
- Green vitest suite demonstrating the idle-gating contract

# Impl — Idle-gated auto-refresh/auto-sync in browse widget

## Summary

Implement idle-gated polling in the pi Worklog extension's browse widget: pause the 5s auto-refresh interval (and auto-sync) when the user has not interacted with the selection list for the idle threshold, resuming immediately on the next keypress.

## Context

Parent: Pi extension polls wl list / wl next even when selection list is not visible (WL-0MSB1N0HB0007N6N). The pi extension `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/browse.ts` `defaultChooseWorkItem` starts a 5s `setInterval` when the browse widget mounts and keeps it running for the entire custom-widget session, spawning 4-5 wl processes per tick (~60/min) even when the user is not interacting and the agent is working elsewhere. Pi's `resetExtensionUI()` (session rebind/reload) does not close custom sessions, so the poller survives those too. This feature gates the interval on user interaction.

## User stories

- As an operator with N idle pi sessions, I want hidden/unused selection lists to stop spawning wl processes, so wl process count and memory stay near zero while agents are idle or working elsewhere.
- As a user actively browsing, I want the list to keep refreshing live while I interact, so I don't lose real-time updates.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `browse.ts` tracks `lastInteractionAt` — set when the browse widget mounts and updated on every `handleInput` keypress
2. The 5s refresh interval skips the fetch (and `_triggerAutoSync`) when `Date.now() - lastInteractionAt > IDLE_PAUSE_MS` (named module constant, default 30_000ms)
3. First keypress after an idle pause triggers an immediate refresh and resumes the normal cadence
4. No new settings/config toggles (consistent with the pause-when-hidden decision: always-on, fail-open); the idle threshold is a named constant
5. Active cadence unchanged: while the user interacts, refresh continues at the existing interval
6. Zero wl subprocesses spawned while idle (verified by the A1 test suite plus manual process-count observation)
7. All A1 tests and existing `browse.test.ts` tests pass; the package build (`tsc` via `npm run build` in the extension package or repo build) succeeds

## Minimal implementation

- In `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/browse.ts` `defaultChooseWorkItem`: add `IDLE_PAUSE_MS` constant; record `lastInteractionAt` at mount and at the top of `handleInput`; in the interval callback, skip fetch + auto-sync when idle; on resume, invalidate cache and trigger an immediate fetch
- Leave the detail-view widget path and manual actions untouched
- Note (pi-side limitation, out of scope): pi's `resetExtensionUI()` doesn't close custom sessions — idle gating covers that case

## Dependencies

- Depends on the A1 test feature (test-first)

## Deliverables

- `browse.ts` changes implementing idle-gated refresh/sync
- Green test suite (A1 + existing) and successful build

# Impl — Visibility-gated auto-refresh/sync in worklist TUI

## Summary

Wire the pane-visibility gate into the herdr worklist TUI: skip auto-refresh/auto-sync timer ticks when the pane is hidden (not focused), fail open when visibility can't be determined, keep the visible-pane cadence unchanged, and never gate manual actions.

## Context

Parent: Pi extension polls wl list / wl next even when selection list is not visible (WL-0MSB1N0HB0007N6N). In `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` `runWorklistTui`, `refreshTimer` (30s → `doRefresh(false)`) and `syncTimer` (30s → `doSync(true)`) run unconditionally while the pane process is alive. This feature gates both timers on the B2 visibility module (`isPaneVisible()` + `PollGate`): when the pane's tab is not focused, ticks are skipped; when the pane is focused (or visibility fails open), polling proceeds exactly as today. Follows the B3 test feature (test-first).

## User stories

- As an operator with hidden herdr work-item panes, I want auto-polling to pause when my pane is not focused, so hidden panes stop spawning wl processes (~4-5 per 30s tick per pane).
- As a user with a visible work-items pane, I want polling cadence unchanged (30s), so the list stays live as today.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `refreshTimer` ticks skip `doRefresh(false)` when `isPaneVisible()` reports hidden (no fetcher spawns)
2. `syncTimer` ticks skip `doSync(true)` when hidden (no `wl sync --if-idle`, no follow-up `doRefresh`)
3. Visible-pane cadence unchanged: when focused (or fail-open), timers fire on the existing 30s cadence (default `refreshIntervalMs` / `DEFAULT_SYNC_INTERVAL_MS`)
4. Fail-open: no `HERDR_PANE_ID` env or herdr CLI error → pane treated as visible (polling as today); standalone runs unaffected
5. Manual `r` (refresh) and `S` (sync) actions never gated
6. Header shows a `[paused — hidden]` indicator when gating is active (visible signal for operators); no settings toggle added (pause-when-hidden always on)
7. `PollGate` TTL (~2s) ensures refresh+sync ticks in one cycle share a single `herdr pane get` call
8. All B3 tests + existing suite green; `npm run build` in `packages/herdr` succeeds

## Minimal implementation

- In `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`: construct `PollGate` (from B2) with the pane id from `process.env.HERDR_PANE_ID`; gate `refreshTimer`/`syncTimer` tick handlers on `gate.visible()`; add the header indicator near the existing header renderer
- Wire the exec seam so the gate uses the same `execFileAsync` as the fetcher
- Do not touch auto-sync.ts's timer factory API beyond what's needed for gating (pass gate or skip-flag)

## Dependencies

- Depends on B3 (Tests: visibility-gated auto-refresh/sync in worklist TUI)

## Deliverables

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` (and minimal related) changes
- Green test suite (B3 + existing) and successful build

## Summary

Investigate and fix the leak of orphaned hung `wl create` subprocesses left behind by the `wl-WL-0MSAUI2MW002ETPF-init-pre-push-guards` test worktree, so test runs stop leaving zombie wl processes consuming memory and worklog locks.

# Herdr Worklist: Track Agents Spawned per Work Item and Show Their Status Icon

## Problem statement

When a user spawns a pi agent from the herdr worklist (via `/intake`, `/plan`, or `/skill:*` on a selected work item), the worklist has no knowledge of that agent afterwards. There is no way to see, directly in the list, that an agent is attached to a particular work item or what state that agent is in — even though the herdr sidebar already tracks this (idle / working / blocked).

## Users

- **Herdr worklist users** — Anyone who spawns agents from the worklist and wants to see, at a glance, which work items currently have an agent attached and what state that agent is in.

Example user stories:

- "As a worklist user, when I spawn an agent on `WL-XXXX` from the list, I want that row to show an icon reflecting the agent's status so I can see which items have active agents without switching panes."
- "As a worklist user, when the agent pane closes, I want the icon to disappear immediately so the list reflects reality."
- "As a worklist user, I want the agent icon's presence or absence to never shift the other icons or the item-ID column, so the list stays readable."
- "As a worklist user, when I restart the plugin or open a second worklist tab, I want the agent-to-work-item mapping to still be known."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. When an agent command (`/intake`, `/plan`, `/skill:*`) carrying a work-item ID is dispatched from the worklist, the plugin records the work-item ↔ agent-pane association (capturing the new pane ID from the spawn flow) before/while spawning the agent.
2. The list shows an agent-status icon at the **start of the icon prefix** for every row whose work item has a tracked agent, reflecting the agent's current state (`idle` / `working` / `blocked`) using the same state values the herdr sidebar shows.
3. **Alignment invariance:** the agent icon occupies a fixed-width reserved slot in the icon prefix. Rows with and without an agent icon keep the status/stage/review icons and the item-ID column at identical columns (unit test asserts no column shift).
4. The mapping persists across plugin restarts in a gitignored JSON state file (e.g. `.worklog/agent-panes.json`) and is shared across worklist panes/tabs.
5. When the agent pane is gone (closed/exited), the entry is pruned and the icon disappears on the next refresh cycle.
6. Only agents spawned from the worklist's agent commands are tracked; manually opened pi agent panes and commands without a work-item ID are not tracked.
7. Status lookup fails open: when the `herdr` CLI/socket is unavailable or an error occurs, no icons are rendered and the list continues to function normally (matching the existing `visibility.ts` fail-open pattern).
8. Unit tests cover: tracker record/prune/persistence, agent-state → icon mapping, fixed-slot alignment, and dispatch-time association capture.
9. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, `packages/herdr/README.md`, and the herdr agent-state protocol doc if relevant.
10. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

> **Note:** CHANGELOG.md is excluded from this list — it is managed automatically by the ship skill's release pipeline. CI/CD pipeline tests are out of scope.

## Constraints

- Must work with the existing `send-to-pi.sh` flow. The shared script (`packages/herdr/shared/send-to-pi.sh`) is consumed by other plugins (e.g. `herdr-podcast-editor` via git submodule), so any change must be **backward compatible** (new optional flag only).
- The plugin currently spawns `send-to-pi.sh` detached with `stdio: ignore`; pane-ID capture must not block the TUI event loop or change spawn behavior for other routes.
- Status refresh should reuse the `PollGate` TTL-memoizer pattern from `src/visibility.ts` to avoid `herdr` CLI spawn churn on every render tick.
- The state file must live in a gitignored location (`.worklog/` is already ignored).
- The planned Rust migration (WL-0MS8XGSE400374VS) means the TS implementation should be self-contained and portable (pure functions where feasible).
- Follow the existing icon conventions in `src/icons.ts` (emoji + `[TEXT]` fallback, `stringDisplayWidth` for width math).

## Existing state

- `src/index.ts` `onCommand` routes agent commands (`/skill:*`, `/intake`, `/plan`) to `scripts/send-to-pi.sh`, spawned **detached with stdio ignored**. The work-item ID is extracted via `extractWorkItemId()` and the item is claimed (`claimWorkItem`) before spawn, but the **new pane ID is discarded** — the script parses it internally and never surfaces it.
- Row rendering: `formatItemLine()` in `src/worklist.ts` composes each row via `getIconPrefix()` in `src/icons.ts`, which concatenates status → stage/audit → review → epic icons and pads to a fixed 12-cell width (`ICON_PREFIX_WIDTH`).
- `WorkItem` (src/fetcher.ts) has no agent-related field.
- The herdr CLI exposes agent status per pane: `herdr agent list` / `herdr agent get <pane_id>` return `agent_status` (observed values: `working`, `done`; protocol/CLI states: `idle`, `working`, `blocked`, `unknown`). The work-item association cannot be recovered from `herdr pane process-info` (cmdline is just `pi`), so it must be recorded at spawn time.

## Desired change

1. **`packages/herdr/shared/send-to-pi.sh`** (+ `scripts/send-to-pi.sh` passthrough): add an optional `--pane-id-file <path>` flag that writes the new pane ID immediately after `herdr pane split` succeeds. Backward compatible; absent flag = current behavior.
2. **New `src/agent-tracker.ts`**: in-memory + persisted (`.worklog/agent-panes.json`, atomic write) mapping `workItemId → paneId`; `recordAgentForWorkItem()`, pruning of entries whose pane no longer exists (via `herdr agent get`/`agent list`), and a cached `refreshStates()` returning `Map<workItemId, 'idle'|'working'|'blocked'|'done'>`. Fail-open on herdr errors.
3. **`src/index.ts`**: on agent-command dispatch, pass `--pane-id-file <tmpfile>` to the spawn; a fire-and-forget async task polls briefly for the file, reads the pane ID, and records the mapping. Never blocks the TUI.
4. **`src/fetcher.ts`**: add optional `agentState?: 'idle' | 'working' | 'blocked' | 'done'` to `WorkItem`; merge tracker state into fetched items (in fetcher or TUI refresh cycle).
5. **`src/icons.ts`**: add `agentStatusIcon(state, opts)`; `getIconPrefix()` gains a **fixed-width first slot** (2 cells, icon or blank) for the agent status so the remaining icons never shift.
6. **Tests**: `src/agent-tracker.test.ts` (new), icon-alignment tests, dispatch-association tests in `src/index.test.ts`/`worklist.test.ts`.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/agent-tracker.ts` — NEW: mapping store, persistence, pruning, status refresh (PollGate-cached, fail-open)
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — capture pane ID on agent dispatch (`--pane-id-file`) and record association
- `packages/herdr/shared/send-to-pi.sh` — optional `--pane-id-file` flag (backward compatible)
- `packages/herdr/scripts/send-to-pi.sh` — pass through `--pane-id-file`
- `packages/herdr/src/icons.ts` — `agentStatusIcon()` + fixed-width agent slot in `getIconPrefix()`
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — pass `agentState` through to icon prefix (`formatItemLine`)
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — `WorkItem.agentState` field; state merge
- `packages/herdr/src/agent-tracker.test.ts` — NEW: record/prune/persist/refresh tests
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` / `index.test.ts` — alignment + dispatch-association tests
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — document the new icon and behavior

## Related work

- `packages/herdr/shared/herdr-agent-state-protocol.md` — defines `pane.report_agent` and the sidebar states (`idle`, `working`, `blocked`) this feature mirrors.
- WL-0MS9NPHQU005Y3VE (completed) — "Herdr plugin should set work-item status to in_progress when instigating actions": same dispatch path; established `extractWorkItemId()` + claim-before-spawn. This feature extends that flow by capturing the pane ID.
- WL-0MS5CDIR1008VRTN (completed) — "Open pi agent pane for skill commands sent from herdr worklist": established the `send-to-pi.sh` dispatch mechanism.
- WL-0MS8XGSE400374VS (open) — "Migrate ContextHub herdr plugin to Rust": planned migration; TS work should be portable/self-contained.
- WL-0MSAZQEQB008O7H3 (open) — "Central cache for wl read results to cut Herdr refresh spawn churn": adjacent refresh-caching concern; PollGate reuse reduces overlap.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Icon glyph mapping:** confirmed by user — `working → 🟢` (green circle), `blocked → ⛔` (no-entry sign, user's stated preference), `idle → ⚪` (white circle, default if a state must be shown). `done`/pane-closed → no icon. Text fallbacks follow the `[TEXT]` convention.
- **Pane-ID capture race**: `--pane-id-file` may never appear if the split fails; tracker treats a missing pane as a no-op (no entry recorded). Icon appears on the next refresh after recording.
- **Persistence concurrency**: multiple worklist tabs writing `.worklog/agent-panes.json` — atomic write (write-temp-then-rename) plus last-writer-wins is acceptable; avoid holding file locks.
- **Stale entries**: an entry whose pane closes while the plugin is not running is pruned on the next refresh; `done` status may linger for one refresh before removal.
- **Scope-creep guard**: do NOT add sidebar-style agent panels, per-item agent history, or agent output previews. If desired, record as separate linked work items rather than expanding this item.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Should the worklist row icon mirror the sidebar's exact glyphs/colors, or is a status icon consistent with the worklist's existing emoji style (with text fallback) acceptable?" — Answer (user): "no entry sign (preference), or red circle. Go for consistency." Source: interactive reply. Interpretation: use the worklist's existing emoji icon style; glyph preference ⛔ or 🔴. **Follow-up clarification:** "make working a green circle" — Answer (user): working → 🟢 (green circle). Source: interactive reply. Final mapping: `working → 🟢`, `blocked → ⛔`, `idle → ⚪`, `done`/pane-closed → no icon.
- Q2: "Which agents to track — only worklist-spawned agent commands, or also manually opened pi agent panes working in the same project?" — Answer (user): "only worklist spawned". Source: interactive reply.
- Q3: "Should the mapping persist across plugin restarts, and should the icon disappear as soon as the agent pane closes?" — Answer (user): "yes persist, disappear immediately". Source: interactive reply.
- Q4 (follow-up): "When the agent icon is/is not present, alignment of other icons should not be affected" — Answer (user): "Note, when the icon is/is not present the alignment of other icons should not be affected". Source: interactive reply. Turned into AC 3 (fixed-width reserved slot) and a dedicated unit test.
data.title: Herdr worklist: track agents spawned per work item and show their status icon

# Code Freeze: herdr plugin blocks implement actions (banner + dialog) during ship-it process

## Problem statement

During a ship-it (dev→main release) process, developers and agents can still trigger `implement` workflows on work items, creating new commits on `dev` while a release is being prepared/merged. This can race the release merge and pollute the release with work that was not included in the PR. The project needs a "Code Freeze" state: while a ship-it process is running, all implement actions must be blocked, with clear user-visible warnings.

## Users

- **Producers / release managers** running a ship-it process — they need assurance that no new implementation work lands mid-release.
- **Developers using the herdr worklist pane** — they must be warned (banner) before attempting implement, and informed (dialog) if they try anyway.
- **AI agents** — the implement skill (tracked in SorraAgents) must refuse to start implementations while a freeze is active.

### Example user stories

- As a producer, when I start a ship-it release, I expect implement actions to be blocked everywhere until the release completes or aborts.
- As a developer in the herdr worklist, I expect a prominent banner to tell me the project is in Code Freeze.
- As a developer in the herdr worklist, when I press `i` (implement) during a Code Freeze, I expect a dialog explaining that implementation is blocked until the release finishes, and I expect no pi agent pane to spawn and no work-item claim to happen.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **Marker contract defined** — a code-freeze marker file `<worklog-dir>/code-freeze.json` (where `<worklog-dir>` is the project's `.worklog/` directory, resolved the same way the plugin resolves it today) holds `{ "active": true, "reason": "...", "startedAt": "<ISO>", "pid": <pid> }`. Presence of a marker with `active: true` means freeze is ON; absence (or `active: false`) means freeze is OFF. The contract is documented in the herdr README.
- [ ] **herdr detects freeze** — the plugin reads the marker on each refresh/render (fail-open: parse errors or missing file = no freeze) and exposes the freeze state to the TUI.
- [ ] **Banner on selection list** — when freeze is active, the list view renders a prominent banner (e.g. reversed/red `⛔ CODE FREEZE` line) above the header/filter, clearly warning users, without breaking the existing `rows - 1` line-count invariant.
- [ ] **Implement actions blocked** — when freeze is active, any `/skill:implement` command (single-key `i`, chord `i`, or typed dispatch) is NOT routed to the pi agent pane: no `send-to-pi.sh` spawn, no work-item claim, and no `<id>` substitution side effects.
- [ ] **Dialog on implement attempt** — when freeze is active and an implement command is issued, a dialog overlay informs the user of the Code Freeze (release in progress, implement blocked) and is dismissed with Esc/Enter, returning to the list without executing the command.
- [ ] **Non-implement commands unaffected** — audit, intake, plan, review, priority, search, sync, and navigation continue to work normally during a freeze.
- [ ] **Tests** — unit tests cover: marker parsing (active/absent/invalid), banner rendering (appears only when freeze is active), implement-command blocking (command is not routed), dialog rendering/dismissal, and that non-implement commands are unaffected.
- [ ] Full project test suite passes with the new changes.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant docs site entries.

> **Note:** CHANGELOG.md is excluded — it is managed automatically by the ship skill's release pipeline.

## Constraints

- The marker location/format is a cross-repo contract shared with the SorraAgents ship/implement skills (`SA-0MSBU4OBU005WJNB`) — do not change it unilaterally; document it so the ship skill can write it and the implement skill can read it.
- Fail-open: any error reading the marker (missing file, corrupt JSON) must NOT block browsing — treat as "no freeze".
- The block must be fail-safe client-side: the plugin must never spawn a pi pane for an implement command while the marker is active, even if the dialog is dismissed.
- Must not break the existing `rows - 1` pane-height invariant (WL-0MSAAON63003N6LO) — the banner must fit within the budget.
- Follow build → test → commit discipline (vitest suite in packages/herdr).

## Existing state

- The herdr plugin (`packages/herdr/`) provides the worklist TUI. Implement commands are `/skill:implement <id>` (single-key `i`, also chorded), dispatched via `executeResolvedCommand()` in `src/worklist.ts` and routed to a new pi agent pane by `onCommand` in `src/index.ts` (which also claims the work item).
- There is no notion of project state (code freeze) — the plugin only reads work items.
- The ship skill (`skill/ship/` in SorraAgents) runs the dev→main release; it does not currently set any freeze state. That work is tracked separately in `SA-0MSBU4OBU005WJNB`.
- The implement skill (`skill/implement/` in SorraAgents) does not gate on any project state.

## Desired change

1. Add `packages/herdr/src/code-freeze.ts`: read/parse the marker file at `<worklog-dir>/code-freeze.json`, returning `{ active, reason?, startedAt?, pid? }`; fail-open semantics.
2. Thread freeze state into the TUI: check on each refresh/render (cheap file stat/read), pass to the renderer and key handlers.
3. Renderer: when freeze is active, render a prominent banner line (fits the `rows - 1` budget; account for it like group separators are accounted for).
4. Command dispatch: in `executeResolvedCommand()` (and the single-key/chord paths in the TUI loop), when the command starts with `/skill:implement` and freeze is active, do NOT route — instead set a "code freeze notice" state that renders the dialog overlay.
5. Dialog: a notice overlay (similar to FormState render) with the freeze message and a dismiss key (Esc/Enter) returning to list mode.
6. Tests for all of the above.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/code-freeze.ts` — New module: marker path resolution + parse (`isCodeFreezeActive()`).
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — Renderer banner (createListRenderer), implement-command interception (executeResolvedCommand), notice/dialog state in runWorklistTui.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — Pass freeze awareness through (optional; fetcher already resolves the worklog dir via `getWorklogDir()`).
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — `getWorklogDir()` already exists; reuse for marker path (no change expected beyond possibly a helper).
- `packages/herdr/src/code-freeze.test.ts` — New unit tests.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` — Extend with banner/blocking/dialog tests.
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — Document the marker contract and freeze behavior.

## Related work

- `SA-0MSBU4OBU005WJNB` (SorraAgents) — "Implement skill: gate implementation on Code Freeze status; ship skill sets/clears the freeze marker" (dependent task; ship-side marker writing + implement-skill gating). The herdr-side contract defined here is the input for that item.
- `WL-0MSAAON63003N6LO` — pane line-count invariant that the banner must respect.
- `SA-0MS4TXDPB003EUKA` (SorraAgents, completed) — precedent for adding gating steps to `run-release.js`.
- `WL-0MSALIQJU0084V9U` — "Herdr worklist: remove 'Sent ...' toast" (dispatch behavior context).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** the marker lives in the project `.worklog/` directory (same resolution used by `wl --worklog-dir`), so herdr (which already passes `--worklog-dir`) and the ship/implement skills (which run inside the project) agree on its location. Documented as a contract.
- **Assumption:** only `/skill:implement` is gated. Other skills (intake/plan/audit) do not modify code and remain available.
- **Risk:** cross-repo contract drift — the ship skill must write exactly the format the plugin parses. Mitigation: document the contract in both work items and the herdr README; parse defensively (fail-open).
- **Risk:** banner pushes content out of the pane (line-count invariant). Mitigation: account for the banner row in the existing budget logic and extend the invariant test.
- **Risk:** scope creep — do NOT implement ship-side marker writing or implement-skill gating here; those belong to SA-0MSBU4OBU005WJNB.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Where should the code-freeze marker live and what format should it use?" — Answer (operator): not specified; agent decided. Final: `<project-root>/.worklog/code-freeze.json` with `{ "active": true, "reason": "...", "startedAt": "<ISO>", "pid": <pid> }`. Source: design decision (documented above), cross-repo contract referenced in SA-0MSBU4OBU005WJNB.
- Q: "Should ALL agent commands be blocked during freeze, or only implement?" — Answer (operator): only implement actions are to be blocked ("will block all implement actions"). Audit/intake/plan/review remain available. Source: user request.
- Q: "Who writes/clears the marker?" — Answer (operator): the ship-it process; tracked in the SorraAgents dependent task (SA-0MSBU4OBU005WJNB), which will make the ship skill set the freeze marker at release start and clear it at completion/abort. Source: user request ("raise a dependent task in ../SorraAgents").
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MSAK8YLB0025EGW** – Herdr plugin: fix work item list grouping (duplicate In Review sections, wrong group order) (completed)
- **WL-0MNRPFJDI001M169** – wl CLI SyntaxError: opencode-client.js invalid token 'let' (blocks programmatic wl) (completed)

# Wire showIcons setting and add settings reload mechanism for herdr worklog plugin

## Problem Statement

The `showIcons` setting is defined in the herdr worklog plugin settings (`~/.config/herdr/worklog-plugin.json`) and documented in the README, but it has **two issues**:

1. **showIcons is not wired into the renderer.** The `iconsEnabled()` function in `src/icons.ts` always returns `true` — it ignores the setting entirely. So editing `showIcons` in the config has no effect on whether icons appear in the list.
2. **No settings reload mechanism exists.** Several settings (`autoRefresh`, `refreshIntervalMs`, `autoSync`, `syncIntervalMs`) are read only once at startup in `main()`. After editing the config, the user must quit and reopen the pane for those settings to take effect.

## Root Cause Analysis

- `src/settings.ts` defines `showIcons: boolean` in `PluginSettings` and loads it from the JSON config file.
- `src/index.ts` calls `loadSettings()` but never passes `showIcons` to the TUI options.
- `src/worklist.ts` calls `iconsEnabled()` with no arguments — it always returns `true`.
- `src/icons.ts` `iconsEnabled()` has no connection to the settings file.
- `src/index.ts` reads settings once in `main()` and passes them to `runWorklistTui()`. No mechanism exists to re-read settings at runtime.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **showIcons is wired into the renderer.** When `showIcons` is `false` in the config, no icons appear in the worklist (status, stage, priority, audit icons are all omitted). When `showIcons` is `true` (default), behavior is unchanged.
2. **showIcons changes apply without restart.** The setting is re-read from disk on every render/fetch cycle (same pattern as `showHelpText` and `browseItemCount`).
3. **Settings reload is properly implemented.** The pattern mirrors `showHelpText`: a `getShowIcons` getter function re-reads from disk on every call.
4. **Tests added.** Unit tests verify that `iconsEnabled()` respects the noIcons flag when passed, and integration tests (or at least a test) confirm the settings re-read path.
5. **Backwards compatible.** Default behavior is unchanged — icons are shown by default.

## Implementation Plan

### Step 1: Wire showIcons through the TUI options

**Files: `src/index.ts`, `src/worklist.ts`**

- Add `showIcons` to the settings passed to `runWorklistTui()` (similar to `autoRefresh`, `refreshIntervalMs`, etc.)
- In `runWorklistTui()`, accept `showIcons` in the options and store a getter pattern like `getShowIcons: () => loadSettings().showIcons ?? true`
- Pass `noIcons` flag down to `renderWorklist()`

### Step 2: Update iconsEnabled() to respect the flag

**File: `src/icons.ts`**

- `iconsEnabled()` already accepts `{ noIcons?: boolean }` — it returns `false` when `noIcons === true`. This is correct; the bug is that callers never pass `noIcons: true`.
- **No changes needed here** — the function already works correctly when given the flag.

### Step 3: Pass noIcons through the render chain

**Files: `src/worklist.ts`**

- In the render function, replace `const noIcons = !iconsEnabled()` with the getter-based approach:
  ```ts
  const noIcons = !getShowIcons();
  ```
- Pass `noIcons` to `formatItemLine()` calls (already supported).

### Step 4: Add unit tests

**File: `src/settings.ts` or new test**

- Test that `showIcons: false` in config results in `noIcons: true`
- Test that the default value is `true`

## Key Files

- `src/settings.ts` — already loads `showIcons` from config
- `src/index.ts` — needs to pass `showIcons` to `runWorklistTui()` and add `getShowIcons` getter
- `src/worklist.ts` — needs to use the getter instead of always calling `iconsEnabled()` with no args
- `src/icons.ts` — already correct (accepts `noIcons` option)
- `src/icons.test.ts` — unit tests verifying `iconsEnabled()` respects the `noIcons` flag (AC4)
- `src/worklist.test.ts` — integration tests confirming the settings re-read path via the getter (AC4)

# Herdr worklist: expanded items momentarily collapse on list refresh (flicker)

## Problem statement

In the Herdr work-item selection list (`packages/herdr`), when a parent work item is expanded (Tab/Enter) to show its children, a list refresh (auto-refresh every 30s by default, auto-sync follow-up refresh, or manual refresh) momentarily collapses **all** expanded items before re-expanding them. This produces visible flicker and breaks the user's sense of stability while browsing the hierarchy.

## Users

Users of the Herdr worklist plugin who expand work items with children to inspect sub-tasks:

- As a user, I want expanded work items to remain open across list refreshes so the list does not flicker while I read or navigate.
- As a user, I want the children data of an expanded parent to still update from the worklog after a refresh (fresh data, stable view).

## Root cause

In `runWorklistTui`'s `doRefresh` (packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts):

1. `fetcher()` returns **fresh top-level item objects** — `normalizeItem()` in fetcher.ts never populates the `children` array, so the new objects have `childCount > 0` but **no `children`**.
2. `state.refreshItems(newItems)` synchronously swaps them into `_allItems`/`items`.
3. Only **after** the swap does `doRefresh` asynchronously re-fetch children for expanded parents (`await Promise.all(expanded.map(... fetchChildrenForItem ...))`) and attach them to the new parent objects.

`WorkItemListState.getFlattenedItems()` only includes children when `item.children && item.children.length > 0 && expandedItems.has(item.id)`. Therefore, between step 2 and the children re-fetch completing, the flattened list contains **no children** — every expanded item renders collapsed. Any render that fires in that window shows the collapsed list:

- `doRefresh` calls are **not awaited** by the auto-refresh timer or the auto-sync timer, so two refreshes can overlap: an earlier refresh's final `render()` can fire while a later refresh's swapped-in objects still lack children.
- The initial `fetchActionableCount().then(() => render())` can resolve inside the window.
- Manual refresh (`r` action) and resize also render.

The final render of a single, non-overlapping refresh restores the expanded view, so the collapse is transient — matching the reported "momentarily close" symptom.

The existing unit test `preserves selection with expanded children after refresh` (worklist.test.ts) reuses the **same parent object references** across the refresh, so `children` survives — it does not model the production fetcher path where new objects arrive without children, and therefore does not catch this bug.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Expanding a parent (Tab/Enter) and then triggering a refresh (auto-refresh tick, auto-sync follow-up refresh, or manual `r`) keeps the expanded parent **and its children visible continuously** — no momentary collapse/flicker.
- [ ] The expanded view remains stable even when a render fires mid-refresh (e.g., overlapping auto-refresh/auto-sync ticks, `fetchActionableCount` resolution) — the flattened list must never lose expanded children during a refresh cycle.
- [ ] Children of expanded parents are still refreshed from the worklog (stale titles/status are updated after the re-fetch completes) — data freshness is preserved, not sacrificed for stability.
- [ ] Selection is preserved across refresh, including when the selected item is a child of an expanded parent (no jump to the top of the list after refresh).
- [ ] Unit tests cover the production-shaped refresh: `refreshItems` called with **new item objects that lack `children`** (as returned by the fetcher) must keep expanded children in the flattened view; overlapping-refresh scenarios must not render a collapsed intermediate state.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments in `worklist.ts`/`fetcher.ts` and any README/docs entries describing refresh or hierarchy behaviour.
- [ ] Full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Do not change the fetcher's wire contract (`wl next`/`wl list` responses) or add N+1 child fetches for collapsed items — only expanded parents may fetch children.
- Keep the state update path deterministic: the fix should make the refresh atomic with respect to expanded state (children carried over or fetched before the swap), so any render at any time sees a consistent view.
- Match existing code style (TypeScript, no new runtime dependencies).

## Existing state

- `WorkItemListState.expandedItems: Set<string>` persists across refreshes (never cleared), but the expanded view also depends on `item.children` being present on the **current** item objects, which the fetcher never provides on refresh.
- `doRefresh` re-fetches children for expanded parents after the swap (good — this is where the collapsed window lives).
- `refreshItems` preserves selection by ID and clamps otherwise; a selected **child** is currently lost after refresh because the new flattened list (children missing) no longer contains it.
- The renderer derives the expand arrow from `expandedItems` and the children rows from `getFlattenedItems()` — both must stay consistent.

## Desired change

Suggested approach (implementer may choose a simpler equivalent that meets the ACs):

1. **Make the refresh atomic for expanded state** — in `WorkItemListState.refreshItems(newItems)`, before replacing `_allItems`, capture the previously fetched `children` of currently expanded parents (by ID). After the swap, for each new item that is in `expandedItems` with `childCount > 0` but no `children`, attach the carried-over children. This guarantees `getFlattenedItems()` never collapses mid-refresh regardless of when renders fire, and also restores selection for child items.
2. **Minimise/eliminate the collapsed window in `doRefresh`** — fetch the new top-level items and the children of expanded parents in **parallel** (`Promise.all([fetcher(), ...fetchChildrenForItem(...)])`) and apply both in one synchronous `refreshItems` step, followed by a single `render()`. This removes the source of the race (no window where state has items-without-children), including for overlapping timer ticks.
3. Optionally prune `expandedItems` entries whose parent no longer exists after a refresh (hygiene; harmless either way since orphans are never rendered).

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — `doRefresh` (children re-fetch after swap; un-awaited timer calls), `WorkItemListState.refreshItems` (item swap loses children), `getFlattenedItems` (children-gated expansion). Primary fix site.
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — context: `normalizeItem`/`extractItems` never populate `children`; `fetchChildrenForItem` is the async children source.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` — refresh/expansion unit tests; add production-shaped tests (new objects without children).
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist-visibility.test.ts` — existing TUI-level tests (pane gating) that exercise `runWorklistTui` timers; useful harness for overlap/refresh scenarios.

## Related work

- `WL-0MS98T99J009MR66` (completed) — "Fix navigation stack never pushed in production": added nav-stack/expand-survival tests for auto-refresh (Pi TUI lineage); same expand-across-refresh concern.
- `WL-0MS6AAW3M004JK9U` (completed) — "Reselect item after list reorder from status change": selection-preservation across refresh in the flattened list, incl. expanded children.
- `WL-0MS4OOLEF003L0VL` (completed) — "Fix: Children duplicated when expanding parent with Tab in Herdr TUI": prior expand/children fix in this module.
- `WL-0MSAZQEQB008O7H3` (open) — "Central cache for wl read results to cut Herdr refresh spawn churn": refresh-path performance; the parallel-fetch fix here reduces sequential spawns, complementary.
- `WL-0MR0Z7YW1002PXKR` (completed) — "Pi TUI selection list shows stale/empty data when sync races with browse refresh": analogous sync/refresh race in the Pi TUI.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** The observed flicker is the collapsed-window race described above; a fix that makes the state swap atomic (children present or carried over) resolves it. If a different mechanism (e.g., pane-level clear/redraw) contributes, the TUI-level tests will surface it.
- **Risk:** Carrying over stale children could briefly show outdated child data after a refresh. Mitigation: the parallel `doRefresh` re-fetch replaces them immediately; AC-3 verifies freshness.
- **Risk:** Overlapping un-awaited `doRefresh` calls can still interleave renders. Mitigation: parallel fetch + single atomic swap reduces the window to zero; consider also guarding `doRefresh` against re-entrancy (single-flight) if overlap proves problematic.
- **Scope-creep risk:** Related opportunities (single-flight refresh guard, stale-expanded-ID pruning, cache) should be recorded as separate work items, not folded into this fix.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Which refresh triggers the collapse — auto-refresh, manual refresh, or both?" — Answer (operator, seed context): "a list refresh" — both auto and manual go through the same `doRefresh` path; the fix covers all. Source: interactive seed + code analysis of `runWorklistTui`.
- Q: "Should expanded children still refresh their data, or just stay open?" — Answer (assumed from intent, no interview needed): stay open AND stay fresh — data must not be frozen; AC-3 makes this explicit. Source: code review of existing `doRefresh` children re-fetch (already re-fetches; the bug is ordering, not missing refresh).
- No other clarifying questions were required — the seed context and repository analysis were sufficient (intake skill step 4 skipped).

---

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MP14PWR60025V3P** – TUI: unit tests for empty-state message selection (completed)
- **WL-0MLWTZBZN1BMM5BN** – Sync locally-deleted items (completed)
