# Selection list refreshes immediately when its tab/pane regains focus

## Problem statement

The Worklog browse selection list pauses its 5-second auto-refresh after 30 seconds without keypresses (idle-gating added in WL-0MSB1N0HB0007N6N to stop hidden sessions spawning `wl` subprocesses). When the user switches to another terminal tab or tmux pane and returns, the list stays stale until the **first keypress** — if they just look at it, it does not update. The list should refresh immediately when the tab/pane it is displayed in regains focus, then resume the scheduled 5s cadence.

## Users

- **TUI users working in multiple tabs/panes** — they return to the Worklog browse pane and expect to see current data without pressing a key first.

User stories:
- _As a user running pi in tmux, I want the selection list to refresh immediately when I switch back to its pane, so I don't have to press a key to see fresh work items._
- _As a user who keeps the browse list open while working elsewhere, I want the list to resume its 5s refresh cadence as soon as its tab is focused again._

## Expected behaviour

1. While the browse widget is open, terminal focus reporting is enabled (DECSET 1004).
2. On focus-in (`\x1b[I`): the list re-fetches immediately and the 5s refresh cadence resumes (idle timer reset). This is the same refresh path already used by the "first keypress after idle" resume.
3. On focus-out (`\x1b[O`): no fetch; the existing idle-gating (no keypresses → pause after `IDLE_PAUSE_MS`) continues to apply, so hidden sessions still spawn zero `wl` subprocesses.
4. When the widget closes, focus reporting is disabled (DECSET 1004l) and the input listener is removed (no leaks).
5. Fail-open: terminals/tmux configurations that do not support focus reporting simply never send focus events — behaviour is unchanged from today (list resumes on first keypress after idle). No terminal should be negatively affected by the mode-set request (unsupported requests are ignored by terminals).

6. **Scope — tmux per-pane focus delivery:** tmux forwards focus events **only to the active pane**. If the Herdr/browse pane is *not* the active pane, it receives no focus-in/out events, so tab-level focus changes do **not** reach it. The immediate-on-focus refresh therefore fires when the browse pane itself is activated (click, `Ctrl+b` + arrow), not when a containing tab regains focus while another pane holds focus. The staleness indicator (WL-0MSBVCMNO00503QM) covers the UX for that case.

## Feasibility (verified during intake)

- pi-tui does **not** enable focus reporting today (no `\x1b[?1004h` is sent and no focus-in/out sequence handling exists).
- The extension **can** do it without framework changes:
  - The `custom()` UI factory receives the `TUI` object, which exposes `terminal` as a public field → `tui.terminal.write('\x1b[?1004h')` / `'\x1b[?1004l'`.
  - `onTerminalInput` (already in the browse `BrowseUi` interface) wires to the TUI input listeners, which receive raw data **before** the focused component; `\x1b[I` (focus-in) and `\x1b[O` (focus-out) are complete CSI sequences that pass through the stdin buffer.
- Constraints / caveats:
  - **tmux**: focus events are only forwarded with `set -g focus-events on` in `~/.tmux.conf` (document in README/settings help).
  - **Terminal support**: xterm, Kitty, Ghostty, WezTerm, iTerm2, Windows Terminal support focus reporting; others ignore the request (fail-open).
  - This detects OS/terminal-level tab/pane focus. Inside pi, the browse list always has input focus while open (it replaces the editor), so no intra-pi focus handling is needed.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Sending focus-in (`\x1b[I`) to the open browse widget while idle triggers an immediate re-fetch and resumes the 5s cadence (unit test with fake timers / injected input).
2. Sending focus-out (`\x1b[O`) does not trigger a fetch.
3. Focus reporting is enabled on widget open (`\x1b[?1004h` written to terminal) and disabled on widget close (`\x1b[?1004l`), with the input listener unregistered (no listener/interval leaks across consecutive browse sessions).
4. Fail-open verified: with no focus events delivered (unsupported terminal), existing idle-gating behaviour is unchanged — the first keypress after idle still refreshes, and idle sessions spawn zero `wl` subprocesses (existing browse-idle tests continue to pass).
5. New tests cover the focus-in/out handling; full project test suite passes.
6. Documentation updated (README or in-extension help) noting the tmux `set -g focus-events on` requirement for focus-based refresh.

## Constraints

- Must not regress the idle-gating from WL-0MSB1N0HB0007N6N (zero `wl` subprocesses when the pane is hidden/idle).
- No changes to the pi framework (`/usr/local/lib/node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/`) — the fix must live in the Worklog extension (`packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/`).
- Keep the implementation minimal: re-use the existing idle-resume refresh path; do not add a new fetch mechanism.

## Existing state

- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/browse.ts` — `defaultChooseWorkItem` runs a 5s `setInterval`; the fetch is skipped when `isIdle()` (> `IDLE_PAUSE_MS` = 30s since last keypress); `handleInput` does an immediate refresh when the first keypress follows an idle pause.
- `BrowseUi` interface already declares `onTerminalInput?: (handler: TerminalInputHandler) => () => void`.

- **WL-0MSB1N0HB0007N6N** — Pi extension polls wl list / wl next even when selection list is not visible (completed, in_review): introduced the 30s idle-gating this item refines.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk:** Focus reporting may not be forwarded in all environments (tmux without `focus-events on`, terminals without support). Mitigation: fail-open; the fallback staleness-indicator item (WL-0MSBVCMNO00503QM) covers the UX gap in those environments.
- **Risk:** The `\x1b[?1004h` mode-set could theoretically interfere with another application's handling of the terminal. Mitigation: only enabled while the browse widget is open, disabled on close; unsupported terminals ignore it.

- **Scope-creep risk:** Intra-pi focus (e.g., "widget vs editor focus") is out of scope — the list always holds input focus while open; only OS/terminal-level tab/pane focus is addressed.

# Show staleness indicator in selection list when its refresh is paused

## Problem statement

When terminal tab/pane focus cannot be detected (no focus reporting support, or tmux without `focus-events on`), the Worklog browse selection list's auto-refresh stays paused after 30s idle (idle-gating from WL-0MSB1N0HB0007N6N) until the first keypress. Users returning to the pane cannot tell whether the list is current or stale, so they wait blindly instead of knowing a keypress will refresh it immediately.

## Users

- **TUI users in environments without focus-event support** — they need a clear signal that the list is paused and how to refresh it.

User stories:
- _As a user whose terminal does not support focus events, I want the selection list to show that it is paused and when it was last updated, so I know pressing any key will refresh it immediately._
- _As a user returning to a long-open browse list, I want a visible "last updated Xs ago" indicator so I don't have to guess whether the data is fresh._

## Expected behaviour

1. While the browse widget is open, once it has been idle longer than `IDLE_PAUSE_MS` (30s — refresh paused), the widget title/help area shows a visible staleness indicator, e.g. `⏸ refresh paused — last updated 2m ago (press any key to refresh)` (dim styling).
2. The indicator clears as soon as a refresh happens (keypress-triggered resume, focus-in, or a scheduled refresh while active).
3. The indicator is render-only: it must not spawn `wl` processes or add fetch work.

## Implementation notes

- In `defaultChooseWorkItem` (packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/browse.ts), track `lastUpdatedAt` (set on every successful fetch and on widget mount) and `lastInteractionAt` (already tracked for idle-gating).
- In `render()`, when `Date.now() - lastInteractionAt > IDLE_PAUSE_MS`, append the staleness line using the existing theme helpers (`theme.fg('dim', ...)`), computing relative time since `lastUpdatedAt`.
- Optionally also surface a hint that any keypress refreshes (already true via the `wasIdle` path in `handleInput`).
- Keep text short to fit narrow terminals (reuse `truncateToWidth`).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. When the widget is idle > `IDLE_PAUSE_MS`, the rendered lines include a staleness indicator showing time since the last successful update.
2. The indicator is absent when the widget is active (within `IDLE_PAUSE_MS` of the last keypress) and disappears after any refresh (keypress resume or scheduled fetch).
3. The indicator renders correctly at narrow widths (truncated, no crash) and with icons disabled.
4. The indicator adds no `wl` subprocess spawning: an idle widget with the indicator visible spawns zero `wl` processes (assertable with existing test harness / spy on reFetch).
5. New unit tests cover the staleness computation and render output; full project test suite passes.
6. Documentation updated (in-extension help or README) describing the indicator.

## Constraints

- No changes to the pi framework; fix lives in the Worklog extension (`packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/`).
- Must not change the idle-gating spawn behaviour from WL-0MSB1N0HB0007N6N.
- Render-only change; do not introduce new polling.

## Existing state

- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/browse.ts` — `IDLE_PAUSE_MS = 30_000`; `isIdle()` compares `Date.now() - lastInteractionAt`; `handleInput` resumes with an immediate refresh when `wasIdle`; `render()` builds title/help lines with `theme.fg`/`truncateToWidth`.
- `browse-idle.test.ts` covers idle-gating; it injects a `custom` factory and fakes timers/`reFetchItems`.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/browse.ts` — track `lastUpdatedAt`; add staleness line in `render()`.
- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/browse-idle.test.ts` — new tests for indicator presence/absence and zero-spawn guarantee.
- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/README.md` (or in-extension help) — describe the indicator.

## Related work

- **WL-0MSBVBXEA0011OWF** — Selection list refreshes immediately when its tab/pane regains focus (new, related): the primary focus-detection approach; this item is the fallback for environments where focus events are unavailable.
- **WL-0MSB1N0HB0007N6N** — Pi extension polls wl list / wl next even when selection list is not visible (completed, in_review): idle-gating that pauses refresh.
- **WL-0MQJL1W3X0055WJH** — Auto-refresh the Pi TUI browse selection list every 5 seconds (completed): the refresh cadence.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** A render-only indicator is acceptable UX for environments without focus events; the primary item (WL-0MSBVBXEA0011OWF) should be implemented first so the indicator only shows where focus events are genuinely unavailable.
- **Risk:** Indicator text adds noise for users who are deliberately idle. Mitigation: dim styling, concise wording, only shown after the pause threshold.
- **Scope-creep risk:** No new refresh triggers are introduced here beyond what already exists (keypress resume); a manual refresh keybinding is out of scope unless requested.

# Herdr selection list refreshes immediately when its tab regains focus (hidden→visible transition)

## Problem statement

The Herdr worklist TUI pauses its auto-refresh when its tab is hidden (visibility gating via `herdr pane get <id>` → `pane.focused === false`, WL-0MSB1N0HB0007N6N). When the tab regains focus, the list only refreshes on the **next regular refresh tick** — up to `refreshIntervalMs` (default 30s) later. Users returning to the tab wait silently for the list to catch up, and cannot tell it will update at all. The list should refresh **immediately** on the hidden → visible transition, then resume the normal cadence.

## Users

- **Herdr users running multiple panes/tabs** — they switch away from a tab containing a work-item list and return expecting current data immediately.

User stories:
- _As a user with three panes in a tab where the Herdr list is not the focused pane, I want the list to refresh as soon as the tab regains focus, so I don't wait up to 30s for the next tick._
- _As a user returning to a long-hidden tab, I want the refresh to happen immediately and the paused indicator to clear right away._

## Expected behaviour

1. While the pane is hidden (`pane.focused === false`), refresh/sync ticks continue to be skipped (zero `wl` spawns — unchanged).
2. The plugin detects the **hidden → visible transition** (visibility state flips false → true) and triggers an immediate `doRefresh()` on that transition — not waiting for the next regular `refreshIntervalMs` tick.
3. After the transition refresh, the normal scheduled cadence resumes.
4. The transition is detected promptly: while paused, visibility is polled on a short interval (e.g. 2s, matching `DEFAULT_POLL_GATE_TTL_MS`) instead of only on the 30s refresh tick. The poll uses `herdr pane get` only — never `wl` — so the no-wl-when-hidden guarantee from WL-0MSB1N0HB0007N6N is preserved.
5. The existing `[paused — hidden]` header indicator clears as soon as the list refreshes after becoming visible.
6. Fail-open unchanged: when visibility cannot be determined (no `HERDR_PANE_ID`, CLI error), polling proceeds as today.

## Implementation notes

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — in `runWorklistTui`, track the previous visibility state alongside `panePaused`. In the refresh timer tick: if hidden → record `wasHidden = true`, skip; if visible and `wasHidden` → call `doRefresh(true)` (immediate, with the "refreshed" notification) and clear `wasHidden`; else normal tick behaviour.
- Prompt transition detection: while `panePaused`, run a lightweight resume poll (e.g. a 2s interval calling the existing `paneGate.visible()` — memoized by `PollGate`, one `herdr pane get` exec per poll) that flips to an immediate refresh the moment visibility returns. Stop the resume poll once visible; only the normal refresh timer runs.
- Keep the `PollGate` TTL (`DEFAULT_POLL_GATE_TTL_MS = 2000`) aligned with the resume poll interval so visibility state is never cached stale for longer than the poll.
- Tests: extend `worklist-visibility.test.ts` (inject `setExecFileAsync` seam; fake timers) for: (a) hidden → visible transition triggers an immediate fetch outside the normal tick; (b) while hidden the resume poll does not call the fetcher; (c) after the transition refresh, the cadence returns to `refreshIntervalMs`; (d) the header indicator clears.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — transition detection, immediate refresh on resume, resume poll while paused.
- `packages/herdr/src/visibility.ts` — possibly export a `PollGate` constructor variant with a shorter TTL for the resume poll (or reuse existing).
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist-visibility.test.ts` — new tests for transition + resume poll + cadence return.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. When a hidden pane becomes visible, the list re-fetches **immediately** (outside the regular `refreshIntervalMs` tick) — asserted with injected fetcher + fake timers.
2. While hidden, no `wl` fetches occur and the resume poll spawns only `herdr pane get` (no fetcher calls).
3. After the immediate transition refresh, subsequent refreshes follow the normal `refreshIntervalMs` cadence.
4. The `[paused — hidden]` header indicator clears once the transition refresh completes.
5. Fail-open preserved: no `HERDR_PANE_ID` / CLI error → behaves as today (no regression in existing visibility tests).
6. Full herdr package test suite passes (`packages/herdr`).

## Constraints

- Must not regress the zero-`wl`-spawn-when-hidden behaviour (WL-0MSB1N0HB0007N6N).
- No changes to the external herdr app/framework (the `herdr` CLI is the calling framework; `herdr pane get` output shape is a given).
- The visibility signal stays tab-level (`pane.focused`); active-pane-level focus (which pane in a tab has the cursor) is out of scope — the transition fix covers the tab-hidden case regardless of which pane is active.

## Related work

- **WL-0MSB1N0HB0007N6N** — Pi extension polls wl list / wl next even when selection list is not visible (completed, in_review): introduced visibility gating (`visibility.ts`, `PollGate`, paused header indicator).
- **WL-0MSBVBXEA0011OWF** / **WL-0MSBVCMNO00503QM** — closed (not needed): alternative focus-reporting and staleness-indicator approaches for the pi `/wl` browse extension; superseded by this item's use of herdr's own tab-level visibility signal.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** `pane.focused` flips false → true reliably when the tab regains focus while the pane itself is not the active pane. The visibility.ts comment ("a hidden (non-focused) tab reports focused === false") supports tab-level semantics; verify with a live herdr session during implementation.
- **Risk:** The 2s resume poll adds one `herdr pane get` exec every 2s per hidden pane. Mitigation: this is the same lightweight CLI already polled every 30s while hidden; make the resume poll interval a named constant/setting if churn concerns arise; never route it through `wl`.
- **Scope-creep risk:** Detecting "the active pane within a focused tab" (tmux-style pane focus) is out of scope; herdr's `focused` flag is tab-level and that is sufficient for the reported scenario.

## Problem

Each herdr worklist pane runs a refresh cycle every `refreshIntervalMs` that spawns 4 wl processes (`wl next`, `wl list --priority critical --root-only`, `wl list --status completed --stage in_review --root-only`, `wl list --status open,in-progress,blocked`). `doRefresh` in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` has **no in-flight guard**: if a refresh cycle is still awaiting its wl calls when the next interval tick fires (common under load — a single `wl list` can take ~18s wall on a contended host), cycles overlap and wl processes pile up. `doSync` already has a single-flight mechanism (`--if-idle`/timer guard); `doRefresh` does not.

Identified during investigation WL-0MSB19J56006E87J (excessive wl process spawning, 206 concurrent / ~17 GB RAM). Related: WL-0MSAB7ZUC004SK7E (sync-side lock storm), WL-0MSAZQEQB008O7H3 (central read cache).

discovered-from:WL-0MSB19J56006E87J

## User story

As a herdr user, I want the worklist pane to skip a refresh tick while the previous refresh is still running, so that refresh cycles never overlap and wl processes cannot accumulate during load.

## Acceptance criteria

1. `doRefresh` skips (or coalesces) a tick when the previous refresh cycle has not yet completed — no overlapping wl spawn bursts from a single pane.
2. No UI regression: a skipped tick does not leave the list stale forever; the next tick or a manual refresh still updates it.
3. A test verifies that two rapid consecutive refresh triggers produce at most one in-flight wl spawn set (single-flight behavior).
4. Existing herdr test suite passes; build succeeds.
5. Verified that pane refresh returns to normal cadence after the in-flight cycle completes.

## Suggested approach

Add a module-level or instance-level `isRefreshing` flag (or promise-based coalescing) set at the start of `doRefresh` and cleared in `finally`. If set on tick, return early (or schedule one trailing refresh). Mirror the existing `doSync` guard pattern in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` / `auto-sync.ts`.
data.title: Herdr worklist: add in-flight guard to doRefresh to prevent overlapping refresh cycles

## Problem

The excessive wl process spawning incident (WL-0MSB19J56006E87J: 206 concurrent wl processes, ~17 GB RAM) was detected only after it caused severe load (150–225 on a 16-core host). No lightweight mechanism exists to detect wl process accumulation early. The investigation report (docs/dev/wl-process-spawning-investigation.md, §6) proposes a health check mechanism.

discovered-from:WL-0MSB19J56006E87J

## User story

As an operator, I want a lightweight watchdog that alerts when the number of concurrent wl processes exceeds a threshold for a sustained period, so that process accumulation is detected before it degrades the host.

## Acceptance criteria

1. `scripts/wl-process-healthcheck.sh` exists and counts node `wl`/worklog CLI processes (`ps`-based, no external deps).
2. Alerts when count exceeds a threshold (default 50) for 3 consecutive checks; logs the count to `/tmp/wl-healthcheck-count` on OK/Watch levels.
3. Emits an alert with the process tree (`ps -eo pid,ppid,etime,args`) when sustained high counts are detected; non-zero exit code on alert.
4. CI regression gate: after the test suite, assert zero orphaned `tsx src/cli.ts` processes remain (covers the WL-0MSB447TJ000R3N8 fix).
5. README/docs note added with usage (cron/systemd timer, 5-min cadence).

## Suggested approach

- Follow the script template in docs/dev/wl-process-spawning-investigation.md §6.1.
- Add CI assertion as a small vitest or shell step in the repo's CI config (or a post-test hook in package.json).
- Thresholds: OK < 20, Watch 20–50, Alert > 50 sustained.

## Problem

Investigation WL-0MSB19J56006E87J found the herdr worklist pane refresh cadence is dominated by two live-system factors that code fixes cannot address retroactively:

1. `~/.config/herdr/worklog-plugin.json` sets `refreshIntervalMs: 1500` (1.5s vs 30s default) — a ~20x multiplier on wl process spawn rate.
2. 3 of the running herdr panes were started **before** the pane-focus-gating fix (`b8840d99`, Aug 2) and run pre-fix code (tsx does not hot-reload): they poll even when hidden.

discovered-from:WL-0MSB19J56006E87J

## User story

As an operator, I want the herdr worklist panes to run the gated code at the default refresh cadence, so that hidden panes spawn zero wl processes and the spawn rate is bounded.

## Acceptance criteria (manual)

1. `~/.config/herdr/worklog-plugin.json` has `refreshIntervalMs` set to 30000 (or the entry removed to use the default).
2. All running herdr panes are restarted so they load the current source (with visibility gating).
3. Verification: after 10 minutes idle with panes hidden, `ps -eo args | grep -E 'wl (next|list|sync)' | wc -l` shows ~0 auto-spawned wl processes; transient spawns only while actively viewing.

## Instructions

```bash
sed -i 's/"refreshIntervalMs": 1500/"refreshIntervalMs": 30000/' ~/.config/herdr/worklog-plugin.json
# restart herdr server or panes so gated code loads
herdr server restart
# verify
ps -eo args | grep -E 'wl (next|list|sync)' | grep -v grep | wc -l
```

See docs/dev/wl-process-spawning-investigation.md §4.1 and §6.3.

Add support for free-form prompts injected into a new pi agent pane from the herdr plugin chord shortcut system.

## Problem Statement

The herdr worklist plugin shortcut system (src/shortcuts.json) can open a new pi agent pane only when the shortcut command starts with one of three prefixes: `/skill:`, `/intake`, or `/plan` (see isAgentCommand() in src/index.ts). Any other command text — including an arbitrary user prompt like 'Review this code' — is routed to the stdout/pane channel and executed as a shell command instead of being injected into a fresh pi instance. There is no way to bind a chord to 'open a new pi instance and inject a custom prompt'.

## User Stories

- As a herdr worklist user, I want to press a chord that opens a new pi agent pane with my custom prompt pre-injected, so that I can kick off arbitrary agent work without typing it in pi manually.
- As a plugin maintainer, I want the routing extension to be minimal and covered by tests, so that existing shortcut routing behavior (agent vs pane vs stdout) is preserved.

## Expected Behaviour

1. A new agent-command prefix `/prompt:` is recognized by routeCommand()/isAgentCommand() in src/index.ts and routes to the agent channel (send-to-pi.sh), the same as /skill:, /intake, /plan.
2. When the command starts with `/prompt:`, the prefix is stripped before the remainder is passed to send-to-pi.sh, so pi receives only the prompt text (e.g. `pi "Review the current work item and suggest next steps"`), not the routing prefix.
3. A shortcut entry is added to src/shortcuts.json using the `/prompt:` prefix with a free chord (e.g. `o-p`), view both, with a descriptive label.
4. The claim-work-item step (claimItemForAgentCommand) still runs safely for /prompt: commands: commands without a work-item ID skip the status update; commands containing a work-item ID token still claim it, matching existing agent-command behaviour.
5. Existing routing behaviour is unchanged: /skill:, /intake, /plan still route to agent; !! / ! commands still route to pane; unprefixed commands still route to stdout.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `routeCommand('/prompt:Some prompt text')` returns `'agent'`.
2. The /prompt: prefix is stripped before spawning send-to-pi.sh (unit-testable via an exported helper or verified in the routing integration).
3. `routeCommand('/skill:implement <id>')`, `routeCommand('/intake <id>')`, `routeCommand('/plan <id>')` still return `'agent'`; `routeCommand('!!wl close <id>')` still returns `'pane'`; `routeCommand('/wl idea')` still returns `'stdout'`.
4. shortcuts.json contains a `/prompt:` entry with a free chord (not colliding with existing chords: a-a, a-y, a-f, a-r, c, n, p, i, r, s, u-p-*, u-s, u-t, x-c, x-d, f-*).
5. `npm run build` in packages/herdr succeeds and `dist/shortcuts.json` contains the new entry.
6. All tests in packages/herdr pass (npm test), including new tests for /prompt: routing.

## Implementation Notes

- Files: packages/herdr/src/index.ts (isAgentCommand + agent branch prefix strip), packages/herdr/src/shortcuts.json (new entry), packages/herdr/src/index.test.ts (new tests).
- The `!!`-prefixed wrapper-script alternative (option A) is explicitly out of scope.
- Related: existing herdr plugin work items (see wl search herdr).

# Intake Brief: Add model to the shortcut keys

## Problem statement

Herdr's `shortcuts.json` dispatches commands to a pi agent pane, but there is no way to select which LLM model pi uses when executing those LLM-bound commands. Every agent command currently runs with whatever model pi happens to have selected, forcing the user to switch models manually per workflow.

## Users

Herdr users who drive Worklog workflows via keyboard shortcuts (intake, plan, implement, audit, free-form prompts) and want each workflow to run on an appropriately specialised model without manual model switching.

User stories:

- As a user pressing the implement shortcut, I want the command to run with the `code` model so implementation work runs on the code-specialised model.
- As a user pressing the plan/intake/audit shortcuts, I want commands to run with the default `plan` model.
- As a user invoking a free-form `/prompt:` shortcut, I want the new pi pane to open with the `author` model for writing tasks.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `ShortcutEntry` in `packages/herdr/src/shortcut-config.ts` supports an optional `model` field, parsed and validated by `loadShortcutConfig`. When absent, the default is `plan`.
2. LLM-bound entries in `packages/herdr/src/shortcuts.json` carry explicit `model` values: `/plan`, `/intake` (both create and intake), and `/skill:audit` → `plan`; `/skill:implement` → `code`; `/prompt:` → `author`. Shell (`!!`) and `/wl` filter entries get no `model` field.
3. When an agent command with a model is dispatched, the pi CLI spawned via `packages/herdr/shared/send-to-pi.sh` is invoked with `--model <id>` (e.g. `pi --model code '/skill:implement <id>'`), via a new `--model` option on the shared script.
4. Commands without a `model` field, and non-agent routes (shell `!!` commands, `/wl` stage filters), are unaffected — no `--model` flag is passed.
5. Tests cover: config parsing of the `model` field (and defaulting), model propagation through chord dispatch → `onCommand` → agent routing, and `--model` flag forwarding in the send-to-pi.sh bash harness.
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
7. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

> **Note:** CHANGELOG.md is **excluded** from the documentation criterion — it is managed automatically by the ship skill's release pipeline.

## Constraints

- **Scope:** herdr only (`packages/herdr/`). The TUI extension (`packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/`) is explicitly out of scope — leave it untouched.
- Model values are pi model patterns; bare ids (`plan`, `code`, `author`) match the Local Proxy models registered in `~/.pi/agent/models.json` (`pi --model` supports bare id patterns).
- Existing command strings in `shortcuts.json` must remain unchanged — the model rides alongside the command (config field → CLI flag), not inside the command text.
- The `pi` CLI flag is `--model <pattern>` (supports `provider/id` and optional `:thinking`).

## Existing state

- Herdr's `shortcuts.json` entries have: `chord`, `command`, `view`, optional `stages`/`label`/`description`. No `model` concept.
- Chord dispatch chain: `worklist.ts` `handleChordKey` → `registry.lookupChord()` (returns command string) → `chordState.resolvedCommand` → `executeResolvedCommand()` → `dispatchChordCommand()` → `resolveAndRouteCommand()` → `onCommand(resolvedCommand)`.
- `index.ts` `onCommand` routes: `agent` (`/skill:`, `/intake`, `/plan`, `/prompt:`) → `spawn(SEND_TO_PI_SCRIPT, ['--cwd', cwd, prompt])`; `pane` (`!!`/plain shell) → `run-in-pane.sh`; `stdout` → `CMD:` protocol.
- `packages/herdr/shared/send-to-pi.sh` spawns the pane and runs `herdr pane run <np> exec pi "<command>"` — this is where the pi CLI invocation happens.
- `tests/herdr/send-to-pi.test.ts` already mocks the herdr CLI to assert invocation args (used for `--cwd`); it is the natural home for `--model` forwarding tests.
- Models `plan`, `code`, `author` exist as ids under the "Local Proxy" provider in `~/.pi/agent/models.json`.

## Desired change

1. Add optional `model?: string` to `ShortcutEntry` and parse it in `loadShortcutConfig` (validate string, ignore non-strings), defaulting to `plan` for agent-bound commands without the field.
2. Add explicit `model` values to the LLM-bound entries in `packages/herdr/src/shortcuts.json`.
3. Propagate the model through the herdr dispatch chain so `onCommand` receives it (signature change: `(command, model?)` or entry-carrying lookup).
4. Add a `--model <pattern>` option to `packages/herdr/shared/send-to-pi.sh` that forwards `--model <pattern>` to the `pi` CLI invocation; pass it from `index.ts` for agent-route commands.
5. Update tests and documentation.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/shortcut-config.ts` — add `model?: string` to `ShortcutEntry`; parse/validate in `loadShortcutConfig`.
- `packages/herdr/src/shortcuts.json` — add `model` values to LLM-bound entries (`plan`/`code`/`author` as agreed).
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — propagate model through chord dispatch, `executeResolvedCommand`, `dispatchChordCommand`, `resolveAndRouteCommand`, `onCommand`.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — pass the model to `send-to-pi.sh` for the `agent` route only.
- `packages/herdr/shared/send-to-pi.sh` — new `--model` option; pass `--model <pattern>` to the `pi` CLI.
- `packages/herdr/scripts/send-to-pi.sh` — passthrough wrapper (should need no change beyond forwarding args).
- Tests: `tests/herdr/shortcuts.test.ts`, `tests/herdr/send-to-pi.test.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/index.test.ts` (agent-routing asserts), `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` (dispatch chain).

## Related work

- `herdr /prompt: free-form prompt shortcut opens new pi agent pane (WL-0MSC0O8HN000EBFH)` — established the agent channel / send-to-pi.sh path this feature extends.
- `Default config entries and child item updates (WL-0MQD1NPAD000O7OB)` — created the default `shortcuts.json` config; the file this feature extends.
- `Dynamic shortcut dispatcher for browse list (WL-0MQD1NEY7004366H)` — origin of the config-driven shortcut dispatch architecture.
- `~/.pi/agent/models.json` — registers the `plan`/`code`/`author` model ids under the Local Proxy provider (environment, not repo).
- pi docs `models.md` and `--model` CLI flag — model pattern semantics.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MQP303A900780R0** – Escape key in Pi TUI work item detail view should navigate back to selection list (completed)
- **WL-0MKX5ZV3D0OHIIX2** – Add regression tests for mouse click crash and TUI behavior (completed)
- **WL-0MQFZ81MO000QSRL** – Recursive deletion of work items with children (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `.worklog/tmp/intake-draft-add-model-to-the-shortcut-keys-WL-0MSD48ZFC0043AO3.md` — matched: add, also, author, code, commands, default, entries, executing, implement, item, json, keys, llm, model, models, once, plan, shortcut, shortcuts, should, want, when, writing
- `.worklog/worktrees/wl-WL-0MS5URWJG000A6O5-align-icons/packages/tui/extensions/README.md` — matched: able, add, also, code, commands, complete, default, define, entries, executing, implement, item, json, keys, model, models, once, plan, shortcut, shortcuts, when
- `CLI.md` — matched: able, add, also, author, centric, code, commands, complete, default, entries, going, implement, item, json, once, plan, should, similar, specified, want, when

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** `pi --model <bare-id>` resolves the Local Proxy models correctly (bare-id pattern matching is documented; flag verified via `pi --help`).
- **Assumption:** default `plan` applies to any agent-bound command whose entry lacks a `model` field (per work item description).
- **Assumption:** invalid/unknown model ids surface as a pi startup/availability issue in the new pane rather than a herdr crash; config values are aligned with `models.json`.
- **Risk:** dispatch signature changes touch many call sites/tests — keep the change surgical (model as an additional optional parameter, defaulting to `plan`).
- **Scope creep risk:** TUI extension model support, model-cycle ordering, per-project model config, and model validation against `models.json` are all out of scope; create separate work items if requested.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "How should the model be applied when a shortcut fires? (a) extension calls `pi.setModel()` at dispatch; (b) editor text prefixed with `/model <id>`; (c) other?" — Answer (user@rgardler): "it should be in the pi cli command" — i.e., pass `--model <id>` on the `pi` CLI invocation when spawning the agent pane. Source: interactive reply.
- Q2: "Scope: TUI extension only, or also `packages/herdr/src/shortcuts.json`?" — Answer (user@rgardler): "herdr only, leave tui". Source: interactive reply.
- Q3: "Proposed command→model mapping: `/plan`, `/skill:audit` → plan; `/skill:implement` → code; `/intake`, `/prompt:` → author?" — Answer (user@rgardler): "/intake should be plan otherwise agree". Final mapping: `/plan`, `/skill:audit`, `/intake` (both entries) → `plan`; `/skill:implement` → `code`; `/prompt:` → `author`. Source: interactive reply.

# Add code_freeze field to herdr shortcuts.json to filter shortcut availability during code freeze

## Problem statement

Agents respect code freeze by refusing to start implementation work, but the herdr TUI's shortcuts.json has no way to declaratively hide shortcuts (e.g. `i` / implement) during a freeze. Users see the `i` key in help hints, press it, and then get the code-freeze dialog — a wasted keypress and poor UX. Shortcuts should be filtered out of the registry at load/lookup time when they are marked as blocked by code freeze.

## Users

- **Developers in the herdr TUI** — they should only see shortcuts that are actionable (no `i` visible during freeze).
- **Producers** — they need to know that certain shortcuts are intentionally hidden during freeze.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **`code_freeze` field parsed from shortcuts.json** — each entry may have `"code_freeze": "block"` (hide during freeze), `"code_freeze": "allow"` (always show), or omission (always show, backward compatible). Invalid values are logged and treated as omit.
- [ ] **Shortcut registry filters by freeze state** — `getEntriesForStage()`, `getChordByPrefix()`, and `lookupChord()` accept a `codeFreezeActive: boolean` parameter and exclude entries with `code_freeze: "block"` when frozen.
- [ ] **Shortcuts with `code_freeze: "block"` hidden from help hints** — chord hints and footer hints in the list view omit blocked shortcuts when freeze is active.
- [ ] **Implement shortcut blocked by default** — the `i` / `/skill:implement` entry in `shortcuts.json` gains `code_freeze: "block"` to hide it during freeze.
- [ ] **Tests pass** — new tests for the field parsing and registry filtering cover block/allow/omit cases.
- [ ] **Build passes** — `tsc` and full test suite (herdr only) pass.

## Constraints

- **herdr only** — no changes to the TUI extension (packages/tui).
- **Only implement shortcut affected for now** — the `i` chord gets `code_freeze: "block"`.
- **Fail-open** — missing file or parse error must not crash the registry or block other shortcuts.
- **Backward compatible** — existing entries without `code_freeze` behave unchanged.

## Existing state

- `packages/herdr/src/code-freeze.ts` — detects freeze state from `<worklog-dir>/code-freeze.json` with fail-open semantics. Exports `isCodeFreezeActive()` / `readCodeFreezeState()`.
- `packages/herdr/src/shortcut-config.ts` — `ShortcutRegistry` with methods: `lookupChord()`, `getEntriesForStage()`, `getChordByPrefix()`, `getChordByLeader()`. `ShortcutEntry` has `chord`, `command`, `view`, `stages`, `label`, `description`.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — `runWorklistTui()` computes `codeFreezeActive` via `readCodeFreezeState().active` and passes it to the renderer and keyboard dispatch paths.

# Intake Brief — When filtering by stage, show all open work items in that stage (WL-0MSDT8X1V003206G)

## Headline

When a stage filter is applied via `/wl <stage>`, the Pi TUI browse list shows **all** open work items in that stage (standard list order) instead of only the top `browseItemCount` items selected by the `wl next` algorithm.

## Problem Statement

The `/wl <stage>` browse filter (added in WL-0MQDRZ4DK007NK5P) caps the filtered results at `browseItemCount` (default 5) items, selected by the `wl next` priority algorithm. Users who filter by a stage to review its full pipeline see only a curated subset — open items beyond the top 5, or items the `wl next` algorithm deprioritises, are silently missing from the filtered view. Filtering should give a complete picture: every open work item in that stage.

## Users

- Pi TUI users (developers, producers, agents) who use `/wl <stage>` to review everything in a given stage.

### Example User Stories

- As a producer reviewing the pipeline, I want to type `/wl intake_complete` and see **every** open item awaiting planning, not just the top 5, so I know the full workload of that stage.
- As a developer, I want `/wl in_progress` to show all open items currently being worked, including items the `wl next` algorithm ranks lower.
- As an agent planning work, I want `/wl idea` to list all open idea-stage items so none are missed.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Typing `/wl <stage>` (canonical name or shorthand alias) shows **all** open work items in that stage — no cap by `browseItemCount` and no omission by the `wl next` selection algorithm.
2. "Open" means `status=open`. Items with status `blocked`, `in-progress`, or `completed` are not shown in the filtered list (even if their stage matches).
3. The filtered list shows root items only; child items remain hidden and are reachable via Tab drill-down exactly as in the unfiltered view.
4. Filtered results are ordered by the standard list order (sortIndex), consistent with the unfiltered browse list.
5. The default `/wl` (no arguments) behaviour is unchanged — it still shows `browseItemCount` items per existing smart-selection logic.
6. Invalid or whitespace-only stage arguments behave as today (error notification + fall back to default unfiltered list, no crash).
7. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.
8. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.

## Constraints

- **Scope is the `/wl <stage>` browse filter in the Pi TUI only.** The CLI `wl list --stage <stage>` output and the default `/wl` view are out of scope.
- **No new settings or flags.** The `browseItemCount` setting continues to govern the unfiltered view only.
- **Shorthand aliases (`intake`, `plan`, `progress`, `review`) keep working unchanged.**
- **Children remain hidden** in the filtered top-level list (consistent with WL-0MS964SIA0057ABR's root-only rule); drill-down is unchanged.

## Existing State

- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/tools.ts`:
  - `createListWorkItemsWithStage(run, count)` runs `wl next -n <count> --stage <stage> --include-in-progress`, normalises the payload, then `.slice(0, itemCount)` — capping at `browseItemCount` and inheriting `wl next`'s algorithm (which hides children and deprioritises items).
  - `createListWorkItemsWithStageDb(count)` uses `db.list({ stage, rootOnly: true })` (no status filter) and `.slice(0, itemCount)`.
- The extension wires the CLI-backed `createListWorkItemsWithStage` as the default in `index.ts` (`const listWorkItemsWithStage = deps.listWorkItemsWithStage ?? createListWorkItemsWithStage();`).
- `wl list` already supports `--status open --stage <stage> --root-only`, returning all open root items in the stage ordered by sortIndex (verified: `intake_complete` → 8 of 10 open items; the 2 excluded are child items).
- Tests live in `tests/extensions/worklog-browse-extension.test.ts` (stage-filter tests from WL-0MQDRZ4DK007NK5P) and package-level tests under `packages/tui/tests/`.
- Docs: `packages/tui/extensions/README.md` (## `/wl` Slash Command — Stage Filtering) describes the current capped behaviour.

## Desired Change

- In `createListWorkItemsWithStage` (CLI-backed): replace `wl next --stage <stage> -n <count> --include-in-progress` with `wl list --status open --stage <stage> --root-only` and drop the `.slice(0, itemCount)` cap. The `count` parameter becomes unused for the filtered view (or is removed).
- In `createListWorkItemsWithStageDb` (DB-backed, kept in sync): add `status: ['open']` to the `db.list` filter and remove the `.slice(0, itemCount)` cap.
- Update/extend tests in `tests/extensions/worklog-browse-extension.test.ts` to assert: all open root items in the stage are returned (no cap), blocked/in-progress/completed items are excluded, children are excluded but drill-down still works, ordering matches `wl list` sortIndex order, default `/wl` unchanged.
- Update `packages/tui/extensions/README.md` to describe the all-open-items behaviour of stage-filtered views.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/tools.ts` — change `createListWorkItemsWithStage` and `createListWorkItemsWithStageDb` to fetch all open root items in the stage (CLI + DB paths).
- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/index.ts` — likely no change (stage plumbing already passes the canonical stage through); verify wiring stays intact.
- `tests/extensions/worklog-browse-extension.test.ts` — update stage-filter tests for the new all-items behaviour.
- `packages/tui/extensions/README.md` — document that stage-filtered views show all open items in that stage.

## Related Work

- **WL-0MQDRZ4DK007NK5P — "Add stage-filter arguments to the /wl slash command in the Pi TUI extension"** (completed): Built the `/wl <stage>` filter this item refines (capped at 5 items via `wl next`).
- **WL-0MNUOLCB20008HVX — "Add --stage param to wl next"** (completed): Foundation for stage filtering in `wl next`.
- **WL-0MS964SIA0057ABR — root-only rule for the Pi TUI browse list** (referenced in code comments): Children hidden from top-level lists; preserved here.
- **WL-0MKW1UNLJ18Z9DUB — "Add TUI search filter using wl list"** (completed): Precedent for using `wl list` output in the TUI.
- **WL-0MP2ISZ8Q008Q19S — "Support comma-separated --status filters in wl list"** (completed): `--status open` filtering on `wl list`.

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Risk: Behaviour change in ordering.** Filtered views switch from `wl next` priority ordering to sortIndex order. Mitigation: user confirmed standard list order is desired (Appendix); documented in README.
- **Risk: Large stages produce long lists.** A stage with many open items will show them all in one scrollable list. Mitigation: none needed — the browse widget already supports scrolling; keep the list uncapped per AC #1.
- **Risk: DB-backed path diverging from CLI path.** Both `createListWorkItemsWithStage` and `createListWorkItemsWithStageDb` must be updated together or behaviour differs depending on which is wired. Mitigation: update both in the same change; tests cover the CLI-backed default.
- **Assumption:** `wl list --status open --stage <stage> --root-only` semantics are the single source of truth for "all open root items in a stage"; no additional client-side filtering is needed.
- **Assumption:** Child drill-down (Tab) in a filtered view continues to work unchanged (it uses `wl list --parent <id>`, which is stage-agnostic).
- **Scope-creep risk:** Requests for other filter types (priority, assignee) or a configurable filtered-view count should be recorded as new linked work items, not added here.

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions & Answers

- Q1: "Where should this apply?" — Answer (user): "(a) Only the `/wl <stage>` browse filter in the Pi TUI" (not the CLI `wl list --stage` output). Source: interactive reply.
- Q2: "What counts as 'open work items' in a stage?" — Answer (user): "all open only, children can be expanded out as is the case in the unfiltered view" — i.e., `status=open` only (no blocked/in-progress/completed); children remain hidden in the top-level list but reachable via Tab drill-down, same as the unfiltered view. Source: interactive reply.
- Q3: "Should the default unfiltered `/wl` view also show all open items?" — Answer (user): "the default /wl remains unchanged". Source: interactive reply.
- Q4: "Ordering of the filtered results: keep `wl next` priority ordering or standard list order?" — Answer (user): "(b) standard list order (sortIndex), matching the unfiltered view." Source: interactive reply.

## Summary

Write pytest unit tests for the herdr even-completion grid rebalance algorithm **before** implementing `packages/herdr/shared/grid.py`. Tests use a mocked Unix socket — no live herdr session required.

Parent: Add pane-launch option to shared herdr code: add-to-right vs resizing group (resizing group default) (WL-0MSAPRMRH002S10O)

## Context

The algorithm is validated (herdr 0.7.5) and embedded as reference implementations in the parent description: `dynamic_grid.py` (build from scratch k=1..N), `grid_step.py` (add to an existing perfect grid), and `herdr_rpc.py` (socket RPC client). The grid helper must reproduce the same growth policy:

- Tree invariant: `root:right [anchor, S1]`; `S1:down [R1, B]`; `B:right [L_col, R_col]`; each column is a down-chain (paths `[T,T,F...]` / `[T,T,T...]`).
- Growth: at odd k split the bottom-left cell DOWN; at even k split the bottom-right cell DOWN; then rebalance via `layout.set_split_ratio` (boolean path arrays; True = second child).
- Rebalance: base = max(len(L_col), len(R_col)); S1 ratio 1/(1+base); R1 0.5; B 0.5 (when both columns exist); chain ratios 1/(base-j).

## User Stories

- As a developer, I want automated tests for the grid transitions so regressions in the growth policy or emitted ratios are caught without a live herdr session.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Tests run with pytest and pass without any herdr session or real socket (mocked socket server)
- [ ] Growth policy tested at odd and even k (e.g. k=12 → 6×2, k=14 → 7×2; odd k shows one temporary tall cell)
- [ ] Emitted JSON-RPC messages asserted: `pane.split` direction/ratio and `layout.set_split_ratio` path arrays + ratios
- [ ] Anchor pane never split and keeps 50% × 100% (asserted across transitions)
- [ ] Grid continuation tested: adding panes to an existing perfect grid completes rows at even counts

## Suggested Implementation

- Tests live in `packages/herdr/shared/tests/` (e.g. `test_grid.py`).
- Mock the Unix socket: an in-memory capture of sent newline-delimited JSON-RPC frames, returning fixture layout snapshots shaped like `pane.layout` results.
- Expected messages derived from the parent's embedded `dynamic_grid.py` / `grid_step.py` outputs (also in /tmp).
- Fixtures mirror the verified geometry: equal row heights, equal column widths, anchor 50% × 100%.

## Summary

Implement `packages/herdr/shared/grid.py` — a Python helper for the herdr even-completion grid rebalance, used by the shared pane-launch scripts' `--resize` mode.

Parent: Add pane-launch option to shared herdr code: add-to-right vs resizing group (resizing group default) (WL-0MSAPRMRH002S10O)

## User Stories

- As an operator launching a new pane with resize mode, I want the pane to open on the right and existing panes rebalanced into an even grid automatically, so my workspace stays tidy without manual resizing.
- As an operator, I want the resizing-group behavior to work when panes are added one at a time without knowing the final count in advance, so I can build a grid incrementally.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Newline-delimited JSON-RPC over the herdr Unix socket; `HERDR_SOCKET_PATH` configurable (fallback to `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/herdr/herdr.sock` / `~/.config/herdr/herdr.sock`); frames shaped `{"id","method","params"}`
- [ ] Detects existing grid state (anchor + L_col/R_col chains) from the `pane.layout` snapshot; falls back to starting a fresh grid from the anchor when the right side is not a recognisable grid
- [ ] Growth policy: odd k → split bottom-left cell DOWN; even k → split bottom-right cell DOWN; then rebalance via `layout.set_split_ratio` with boolean path arrays (True = second child)
- [ ] Reproduces the verified shapes k=12 → 6×2 and k=14 → 7×2 (validated against herdr 0.7.5)
- [ ] Anchor pane never split; keeps 50% × 100%
- [ ] Only safe operations: `pane.split`, `layout.set_split_ratio`; no `layout.apply` with `command` nodes
- [ ] Prints the new pane id as JSON on stdout (e.g. `{"pane_id": "..."}`) so the calling bash script can launch/rename/focus it
- [ ] Clear non-zero exit with a helpful message on socket failure or RPC error

## Suggested Implementation

- Port the parent's embedded `herdr_rpc.py` + `dynamic_grid.py`/`grid_step.py` into a single module: socket client, layout parser, grid-state detector, growth step, rebalance.
- CLI interface usable from bash, e.g. `grid.py <anchor-pane-id>` (add one pane to the existing grid, or start a fresh grid if none).
- Keep boolean path arrays exactly as validated.
- Depends on the grid tests (child: Grid-rebalance Python tests) being written first.

## Related

- Reference implementations embedded in the parent description: `dynamic_grid.py`, `grid_step.py`, `herdr_rpc.py` (also present in /tmp).

## Summary

Add `--resize` (default) / `--no-resize` to the existing shared launch scripts `send-to-pi.sh` and `open-pi-agent.sh`. In resize mode the script resolves the anchor pane and invokes `packages/herdr/shared/grid.py` (which performs the split and prints the new pane id) before launching/renaming/focusing the pane.

Parent: Add pane-launch option to shared herdr code: add-to-right vs resizing group (resizing group default) (WL-0MSAPRMRH002S10O)

## User Stories

- As an operator launching a new pane, I want the pane to open on the right and existing panes to rebalance into an even grid automatically (default), so my workspace stays tidy without manual resizing.
- As an operator, I want an explicit opt-out (`--no-resize`, "add to right") that uses herdr's default split-without-resizing behavior.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `send-to-pi.sh` and `open-pi-agent.sh` both accept `--resize` / `--no-resize`; `--resize` is the default
- [ ] `--no-resize` behaves exactly as today: plain `herdr pane split --current --direction right`, no grid calls, no layout changes
- [ ] `--resize` resolves the anchor pane (`herdr pane current`), invokes `grid.py`, parses the returned pane id, then launches the pane (pi / command), renames and focuses it as today
- [ ] Existing options preserved with unchanged defaults: `--pane-name`, `--focus`/`--no-focus`, `--cwd`, `--model`, `--check-cli`
- [ ] If `grid.py` fails, the script exits non-zero with a clear message (operator can retry with `--no-resize`)
- [ ] `packages/herdr/shared/README.md` documents both modes and the grid helper
- [ ] All bash tests (child: Shared script resize-mode bash tests) pass

## Suggested Implementation

- Add flag parsing mirroring the existing `--no-focus` style in both scripts.
- Resize mode: `anchor=$(herdr pane current ...)`, then `python3 "$(dirname "$0")/grid.py" "$anchor"`; parse the pane id from its JSON output; proceed with the existing launch/rename/focus steps.
- `--no-resize` mode: current split logic unchanged.
- Update `shared/README.md` table and add a "Resize mode" section.

## Problem

When the user invokes the worklist plugin action (`prefix+l` → `open-worklist`) while a **terminal pane** is focused, `open.sh` correctly resolves the pane CWD from `herdr pane get` / `herdr pane current` and passes it as `HERDR_RESOLVED_CWD`.

However, when the invoking pane is a **Worklog plugin pane** (the `Work Items` pane itself, e.g. one displaying items from `../open-source-llm/.worklog`), `herdr pane get` reports `cwd` as the **plugin extension directory** (`/home/rgardler/projects/ContextHub/packages/herdr`) rather than the project root the pane is actually browsing. The worklist then always opens in the plugin directory instead of the desired directory.

## Root Cause

Plugin panes run from the plugin root, so their filesystem `cwd` is the plugin directory. The *logical* working directory (the worklog root being displayed) lives in the pane process's `HERDR_RESOLVED_CWD` environment variable — set via `--env` when the pane was opened — but this is NOT exposed by `herdr pane get` / `pane current` / `pane list`.

Additionally, `toggle.sh` tries to detect existing worklist panes via a `command` field in `pane list`, but plugin panes do not expose a `command` field (they are identified by `label: "Work Items"`), so the detection silently fails.

## Fix

In `open.sh` and `toggle.sh`:

1. After resolving the invoking pane's ID, read `HERDR_RESOLVED_CWD` from the pane's process environment via `herdr pane process-info` (shell_pid) → `/proc/<shell_pid>/environ` (Linux). If present, use it as the CWD instead of the plugin directory.
2. Fix worklist-pane detection in `toggle.sh` to also match `label == "Work Items"` (since `command` is not available for plugin panes).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Invoking the worklist action from a `Work Items` pane that displays project X items re-opens/continues showing project X items (not the plugin directory)
- [ ] Invoking from a regular terminal pane still resolves that terminal's CWD (unchanged behavior)
- [ ] Falling back gracefully when /proc is unavailable or the env var is absent (no crash, previous behavior)
- [ ] `toggle.sh` correctly detects an existing `Work Items` pane by label
- [ ] Shell syntax checks pass for both scripts
data.title: Fix: worklist pane CWD resolution when invoked from a Work Items plugin pane

# Herdr to consume local LLM in downtime

## Problem statement

The local LLM (llama-server behind the llama-proxy on the `ai` machine) has idle capacity whenever no user session is consuming it, and that compute is wasted. Herdr should detect this idle state and use it to autonomously advance the worklog backlog: run `/skill:plan` on the next `intake_complete` item, or fall back to `/skill:intake` on the next `idea` item, opening a visible pi agent pane for each dispatch.

## Users

- **Worklog operators** — Anyone who wants the backlog progressed automatically during local-LLM downtime instead of leaving idle compute unused.

Example user stories:

- "As an operator, when the local LLM has been idle for 4 minutes, I want Herdr to automatically run `/skill:plan` on the next `intake_complete` work item so the backlog advances without my involvement."
- "As an operator, when no `intake_complete` item exists, I want Herdr to run `/skill:intake` on the next `idea` item instead."
- "As an operator, when an automated skill run needs answers I haven't given, I want the questions recorded on the work item and the item flagged for producer review so nothing blocks silently."

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] When the proxy reports an idle state (llama-server running, no active query, no active local lease, no model switch in progress, and **at least `downtimeRequiredFreeSlots` slots available** — default: all slots, configurable to any positive integer N) continuously for ≥ `downtimeIdleThresholdMs` (default 4 minutes, configurable), the plugin dispatches a pi agent pane: `wl next --stage intake_complete` → `/skill:plan <id>`; if no such item, `wl next --stage idea` → `/skill:intake <id>`.

  > **Planning note (Q7):** same-slot (per-`slot_id`) tracking implementation is deferred to follow-up work item; this item implements AC3's fail-closed fallback (N < total slots without per-slot data → all slots free for the threshold). AC2 acceptance is verified by the follow-up item once LP-0MSG5TA7Y002GN39 is fulfilled.
- [ ] Same-slot stability: when `downtimeRequiredFreeSlots` < total slots, the worker tracks idle duration **per slot identity** (`slot_id`) and requires the *same* slot(s) to remain free for the full threshold — not any N slots; a slot that starts processing resets its own idle timer.
- [ ] Fallback when per-slot data is unavailable: if `downtimeRequiredFreeSlots` < total slots but the proxy does not yet provide per-slot details (LP-0MSG5TA7Y002GN39 not fulfilled), the worker fails closed to the default condition — **all slots free** for the threshold — rather than dispatching on "any N slots" without same-slot identity; it never silently relaxes the stability guarantee. (When the configured N equals total slots, no per-slot data is required.)
- [ ] Idle state is detected by polling the configured proxy URL (default `http://192.168.0.199:8000`) `GET /llama/local/status` on a configurable interval; endpoint failures, timeouts, or ambiguous responses are treated as busy (no dispatch) and never crash or block the plugin.
- [ ] No duplicate/concurrent dispatch: at most one downtime dispatch in flight per pane (single-flight), and no dispatch before the idle threshold has elapsed; a dispatch consumes the local slot (busy state) so the next dispatch only occurs after another full idle period.
- [ ] If a dispatched skill cannot proceed because answers are needed, the agent records the questions in a comment on the work item and marks it as needing producer review (`wl update <id> --needs-producer-review true`) instead of blocking indefinitely; the item then appears in the producer-review queue.
- [ ] Worker behaviour is configurable via plugin settings (`~/.config/herdr/worklog-plugin.json`): enabled toggle, idle threshold ms, required-free-slots count, poll interval ms, proxy URL, and pi model pattern (default `plan` — a local-proxy model); settings changes apply without a plugin restart.
- [ ] Unit tests cover idle detection, threshold timing, dispatch selection (intake_complete → plan, fallback idea → intake), single-flight guard, endpoint-failure handling, and blocked-questions handling. Full project test suite passes (`npx vitest run tests/herdr/`).
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, `packages/herdr/README.md`, and the plugin settings documentation.

## Constraints

- Runs inside the Herdr worklist plugin (TypeScript / Node); follows plugin conventions — `wl` CLI only (no direct DB access), settings in `~/.config/herdr/worklog-plugin.json`, toast notifications, pane-height budget.
- The proxy runs on the remote `ai` machine (`192.168.0.199:8000` on the home LAN; `100.79.231.101` remotely) — the URL must be configurable.
- Must not hammer the proxy: poll interval default 30s with a hard floor of 10s (`clampDowntimePollInterval`); each poll is a lightweight unauthenticated GET.
- Existing pause-when-hidden gating applies to refresh/sync timers; the downtime worker runs while the worklist pane is open (see Assumptions).
- `send-to-pi.sh` (shared script) is the dispatch mechanism: `--pane-name`, `--cwd`, `--model`, `--no-focus` supported.

## Existing state

- The llama-proxy on the `ai` machine already exposes `GET /llama/local/status` (unauthenticated, verified live from the Herdr host): returns `active_query`, `model_switch_in_progress`, `current_model`, `llama_server_running`, `available_slots`, `total_slots`, `local_owner_session_id`, `local_owner_lease_remaining_seconds`. The endpoint is suitable for count-based idle detection, **but it does not expose per-slot identity** — same-slot tracking requires per-slot details, which the proxy does not currently serve over HTTP (the internal `_query_slots_detail` in `proxy/observability.py` already computes them). Proxy feature request filed: **LP-0MSG5TA7Y002GN39** (expose `slot_id` + `is_processing` per slot).
- The Herdr worklist plugin already spawns visible pi agent panes for `/skill:plan`, `/skill:intake`, `/skill:*` via `send-to-pi.sh`, with optional `--model <pattern>` from shortcut entries; bare model ids (`plan`, `code`, `author`) route to local proxy models.
- `wl next --stage <stage> --json` supports the required stage-filtered selection.
- The plugin's periodic work is three independent `setInterval` loops (refresh 30s, sync 60s, dynamic 2s resume poll) — consolidation into a single scheduler is tracked in child WL-0MSG4NMF0000YBRP.
- Worklog items track `needsProducerReview`; `wl update --needs-producer-review true` sets it.

## Desired change

- New `downtime-worker.ts` module: proxy status poller (single-flight), idle-duration tracker (idle-since timestamp vs. threshold), **per-slot idle tracking keyed by `slot_id` when the required-free count < total slots**, dispatch orchestration.
- New settings in `settings.ts`: `downtimeEnabled`, `downtimeIdleThresholdMs` (default 240000), `downtimeRequiredFreeSlots` (default: all/0, configurable to a positive integer N), `downtimePollIntervalMs`, `downtimeProxyUrl`, `downtimeModel`.
- Integration into the consolidated timer loop (after WL-0MSG4NMF0000YBRP); dispatch via `send-to-pi.sh` (visible pane, `--no-focus`, `--cwd <wlRoot>`, `--model`).
- Blocked-questions handling: the dispatched prompt instructs the agent to record questions in a comment and set `needs-producer-review` when it cannot proceed, then stop.
- Unit tests for the worker; README documentation of the new settings.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — new: poller, idle tracking (count-based and per-slot `slot_id` stability), dispatch logic (testable core)
- `packages/herdr/src/settings.ts` — new downtime settings keys + defaults
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — integrate worker into the (consolidated) timer loop; optional status line/indicator
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — wire settings/options; route dispatch to `send-to-pi.sh`
- `packages/herdr/src/auto-sync.ts` — scheduler consolidation target (with WL-0MSG4NMF0000YBRP)
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts` — new: unit tests for worker logic
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — document new settings and behaviour

## Related work

- **WL-0MSG7P9N8009PCKG (related, deferred)** — Same-slot idle tracking (per-`slot_id` stability) once the proxy serves per-slot details (LP-0MSG5TA7Y002GN39). Created during planning (Q7); owns AC2 + the per-slot half of AC3.
- **WL-0MSG4NMF0000YBRP (child)** — Consolidate herdr plugin timers into a single loop; prerequisite so the worker's polling fits one scheduler.
- **WL-0MSBQUJQX005RAT9 (open)** — Herdr worklist: track agents spawned per work item and show their status icon; the downtime worker spawns agents, so agent-state visibility is directly relevant (related-to, not blocking).
- **WL-0MSD48ZFC0043AO3 (completed)** — Add model to the shortcut keys; documents that bare pi model ids (`plan`, `code`, `author`) match local proxy models — basis for `downtimeModel` default.
- **WL-0MSD502WQ001DTT0 (open)** — Web UI logs interface showing current logs per active slot; same proxy slot model on the `ai` machine.
- **LP-0MSG5TA7Y002GN39 (open, llm project)** — Proxy feature request: expose per-slot details (`slot_id` + `is_processing`) in `/llama/local/status`; prerequisite for same-slot idle tracking. Passed to the proxy team via the user.
- **LP-0MR9G183O004SJLO** — local dispatch lease mechanism in the proxy (referenced by the `/llama/local/status` handler); informs the "no active lease" idle condition.
- **proxy-usage-analysis skill** — slot schedule (6 day / 8 night) and proxy log analysis; background for idle-time estimation.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Cross-pane concurrent dispatch (risk)** — each worklist pane runs its own plugin process; two panes could both detect idle and dispatch. Mitigation (decided in planning, Q5): **no lock file** — rely on the idle→busy cadence (a dispatch consumes the local slot, so the next dispatch needs another full idle period) and on the pre-dispatch claim (item becomes in_progress, so a second pane's `wl next` picks a different item or nothing). Residual risk: two panes could dispatch simultaneously at the same idle boundary; acceptable — the claim prevents duplicate work on the same item.
- **Endpoint semantics (risk)** — a live sample returned `available_slots: 0, total_slots: 0` while a query was active; implementer must verify the idle condition against the endpoint when the server is genuinely idle (slot model per `_query_slots`). Same-slot stability depends on per-slot data from LP-0MSG5TA7Y002GN39. Per planning decision Q7: per-slot (same-slot) tracking implementation is **deferred** to follow-up work item (see Related work); this item delivers the count-based path and the fail-closed fallback — until per-slot data lands, a configured N < total slots degrades to all-slots-free (stricter than configured, never "any N slots" without same-slot identity), and N > total slots never dispatches. Fail-closed on ambiguity.
- **Assumption — worker not pane-visibility gated** — the worker polls and may dispatch while the worklist pane is open, regardless of focus; the dispatch pane uses `--no-focus` so it never steals focus.
- **Assumption — default enabled** — `downtimeEnabled` defaults to `true` (feature intent is autonomous background advancement) with an easy disable toggle.
- **Assumption — blocked-questions fallback** — implemented as guidance in the dispatched prompt/command; a visible pane lets a present user answer directly, and the comment + producer-review path covers the unattended case.
- **Assumption — fail-closed polling** — endpoint errors/timeouts count as busy (no dispatch), never crash the plugin.
- **Scope-creep risk** — opportunistic extras (agent-state visibility per WL-0MSBQUJQX005RAT9, pause-when-hidden for the worker) are recorded as linked work items, not folded into this scope.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Where should the downtime worker run? (a) A background loop inside the Herdr worklist plugin; (b) A standalone daemon/script independent of Herdr; (c) something else" — Answer (user): "(a)". Follow-up asked: are the refresh/sync/resume-poll timers already a single loop? — Research: inspected `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`; they are three independent `setInterval` loops → created child work item WL-0MSG4NMF0000YBRP "Consolidate herdr plugin timers into a single loop" (chore) per user instruction.
- Q2: "How should 'slot free for 4 minutes' be detected? (a) tail/parse proxy logs; (b) HTTP endpoint/API on the proxy or its web UI; (c) other" — Answer (user): "(b); if there is not currently a suitable endpoint create a feature request and I will pass it to the proxy team". Research: inspected the llama-proxy on the `ai` machine (`~/projects/llm/proxy`); `GET /llama/local/status` already exists and was verified live (unauthenticated, reachable from the Herdr host, returns `active_query`, `model_switch_in_progress`, `current_model`, `llama_server_running`, `available_slots`, `total_slots`, `local_owner_session_id`, `local_owner_lease_remaining_seconds`). A suitable endpoint exists — no feature request needed.
- Q3: "How should the skill (`/skill:plan` / `/skill:intake`) be executed when a slot is free? (a) headless `pi -p`; (b) visible pi agent pane via `send-to-pi.sh`; (c) direct script invocation" — Answer (user): "(b) — visible pi agent pane via the existing `send-to-pi.sh`, interactive like the current shortcuts".
- Q4: "Can we make the required number of free slots configurable, and require the *same* slot to be free for the 4 minutes when fewer than all slots are required?" — Answer (user): "Yes — add a configurable required-free-slots count (e.g. 2 slots, 1 slot); if required < total slots, the same slot must be free for the full threshold, not any slot". Action: added `downtimeRequiredFreeSlots` setting (default: all) with per-`slot_id` idle-stability tracking (AC1/AC2); research found the proxy status endpoint returns counts only → filed proxy feature request **LP-0MSG5TA7Y002GN39** in the llm project worklog to expose per-slot details, per the Q2 standing instruction.

- Q5: "Cross-pane concurrent dispatch — how should dispatch be serialized across plugin panes? (a) state-file lock under ~/.config/herdr/ with TTL; (b) no lock file — rely on idle→busy cadence + wl next/claim semantics; (c) lock file with no TTL" — Answer (user): "(b)". Rationale: a dispatch consumes the local slot (proxy busy) so the next dispatch only occurs after another full idle period; the dispatched item becomes in_progress via the pre-dispatch claim, so a second pane's `wl next` selects a different item or nothing. Documented in Risks & assumptions (replaces the earlier "state file" mitigation).
- Q6: "What poll interval default and floor for the proxy status endpoint?" — Answer (user): "(c) default 30s, floor 10s". Added `downtimePollIntervalMs` default 30000 with `clampDowntimePollInterval` floor 10000.
- Q7: "Should same-slot (per-slot_id) idle tracking be implemented now against the future proxy fields, or deferred until LP-0MSG5TA7Y002GN39 lands?" — Answer (user): "(b) defer; create a follow-up work item". Action: created follow-up work item (see Related work); this item delivers the count-based all-slots-free path and the fail-closed fallback (AC3): when `downtimeRequiredFreeSlots` N < total slots and no per-slot data is available, the worker requires **all** slots free for the threshold (stricter than configured, never "any N slots"). AC2 (same-slot stability) implementation is owned by the follow-up item.

# Herdr worklist: readable local timestamps

## Summary
The worklist UI (detail view and list-mode metadata panel) currently displays
timestamps (Created, Updated, Audited At) as raw ISO-8601 UTC strings, which
are hard to read. Format them as `DD/MM/YY HH:MM` in the user's **local** time
zone.

## User story
As a user of the herdr worklist, I want to see Created/Updated/Audited At
timestamps as `DD/MM/YY HH:MM` in my local time zone, so I can read them at a
glance without mentally converting UTC.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A `formatTimestamp(iso)` helper converts an ISO-8601 timestamp to local-time `DD/MM/YY HH:MM` (zero-padded, 24h)
- [ ] Invalid/unparseable timestamps are returned unchanged (graceful degradation)
- [ ] `buildMetaRows` renders Created, Updated, and Audited At via the helper (covers both the detail view and the list-mode metadata panel, which share `buildMetaRows`)
- [ ] Unit tests cover formatting, local-time conversion, zero-padding, and invalid input
- [ ] Full test suite passes; build passes; work pushed to `dev` (never `main`)
- [ ] CHANGELOG.md NOT manually updated

## Implementation notes
- File: `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` (add `formatTimestamp`, use in `buildMetaRows` around lines 795-799)
- Tests: `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts`
- discovered-from:WL-0MSAYNVBY006LM9X (enhancement to the just-shipped metadata panel)

# Herdr plugin: show description preview in the selection-list information panel (WL-0MSFZKQL700381P3)

## Problem statement

The Herdr work item selection list shows a metadata panel at the bottom of the pane (added in WL-0MSAYNVBY006LM9X) with the selected item's fields and last command, but **no part of the item's description**. Users must press Enter to open the detail view to see what an item is actually about, making triage slower.

## Users

- **Herdr users (human and AI agent)** browsing the work item list in a pane, who want to see what the selected item is about without opening the detail view.

### User stories

- As a Herdr user, when an item is selected in the list, I want to see the first few lines of its description in the information panel at the bottom of the list, so I can triage items at a glance.
- As a Herdr user, when I move the selection, I want the description preview to update to the newly selected item (or disappear when the item has no description).
- As a Herdr user, when the preview is longer than the panel's remaining space, I want it to scroll with the rest of the panel content (existing `m`/`M` behaviour).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Description preview in metadata panel**: `formatMetadataPanel()` in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` renders the first few lines of the selected item's `description` (a sensible default of up to **3 lines**, truncated to the terminal width), labelled clearly (e.g. a `Description` heading line) and placed after the metadata rows, before the last-command line.
2. **Selection-driven updates**: The preview reflects the currently selected item and updates on selection change; items without a description render no preview section.
3. **Markdown tolerated**: Markdown source lines are shown as-is (like the detail view), with each line truncated to the panel width; code fences and long lines must not corrupt rendering.
4. **Scrolling integration**: When the panel content (metadata + preview + last command) overflows the panel height, the existing independent `m`/`M` scroll keeps working; the preview participates in the scrollable content and the `[m/M scroll]` indicator behaviour is unchanged.
5. **No regression**: Existing metadata rows, last-command line, blank-panel behaviour, exact `panelRows` line count, and truncation all continue to work.
6. **Testing**: Unit tests in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` cover: preview rendered for items with a description, no preview when description is missing/empty, first-3-lines limit, line truncation to panel width, and preview participation in panel scrolling.
7. **Docs**: All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, `packages/herdr/README.md`, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
8. **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

> **Note:** CHANGELOG.md is **excluded** from this list. It is managed automatically by the ship skill's release pipeline. Implementing agents should not manually update CHANGELOG.md.

## Constraints

- The change is confined to the Herdr plugin's list renderer/panel formatter — no new `wl` CLI features, backend schema changes, or settings are required.
- Must keep the panel's invariant of returning exactly `panelRows` lines and fit within the existing pane-height budget (last row reserved for notifications).
- Preserve existing keyboard bindings (`m`/`M` panel scroll); no new keys.
- Description content is Markdown; rendering must not crash on any input (long lines, backticks, fences, ANSI-like bytes).

## Existing state

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — `formatMetadataPanel()` builds the bottom panel: a `── <id> ──` header, metadata rows via `buildMetaRows()`, and (for `in_progress` items) a last-command line. Panel height is responsive (20–40% of pane rows via `computeMetadataPanelHeight()`); content scrolls independently via `metaScrollOffset` (`m`/`M` keys).
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — `WorkItem.description?: string` already exists and is populated from `wl` data (line 113 / 193).
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` — `describe('formatMetadataPanel — field rendering and scrolling')` covers fields, exact line count, null item, independent scrolling, and truncation; `makeRichItem()` has no description today.

## Desired change

1. In `formatMetadataPanel()`, after the metadata rows and before the last-command line, add a description preview section when `item.description` is non-empty: a dim/underlined `Description` heading plus the first up-to-3 non-empty (or first 3, per convention decided in implementation) lines, each truncated to the panel width via the existing `truncateLine()`.
2. Keep the existing truncation pass and independent-scroll logic unchanged so the preview scrolls with the rest of the panel.
3. Add/extend unit tests in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` (see AC 6).
4. Update code comments and `packages/herdr/README.md` to document the preview.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — `formatMetadataPanel()` gains the description preview section.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` — new/extended tests for the preview (content, 3-line limit, truncation, scrolling, missing description).
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — document the panel's description preview.

## Related work

- **WL-0MSAYNVBY006LM9X** — Herdr plugin: reserve bottom 40% of selection list for item metadata and last command (completed): introduced the metadata panel this work extends.
- **WL-0MS1W8Y1L0059AKP** — Create a work item selection list in Herdr (completed): base selection list.

- **Assumption**: "First few lines" = up to 3 lines of the raw description, truncated to the panel width, rendered as a labelled `Description` section after the metadata rows. Adjustable in review.
- **Assumption**: The preview is part of the panel's existing scrollable content (no new key bindings); on short panes users scroll with `m`/`M` as today.
- **Assumption**: Markdown source is shown as-is (consistent with the detail view) — no markdown-to-plain-text stripping in this item.
- **Risk**: Adding lines to the panel increases overflow likelihood on small panes. Mitigation: preview is capped at 3 lines and participates in existing scrolling; the list keeps ≥60% of the pane regardless.
- **Risk**: Multi-line descriptions with long lines or fences could break truncation/ANSI handling. Mitigation: reuse the battle-tested `truncateLine()`; tests cover long-line and fence cases.
- **Scope creep risk**: Full markdown rendering, collapsible previews, or configurable preview length would expand scope — record as follow-up work items rather than extending this item.

- **Q1**: "How many lines of the description should the panel show?" — **Answer** (user): "The first few lines" — assumed default of 3, documented as an assumption (AC 1). Source: intake seed intent.
- **Q2**: "Should markdown markup be stripped for the preview?" — **Answer**: Assumed no — show source lines as-is, matching the existing detail view. Documented as an assumption (Risks & assumptions). Source: intake seed intent.
