# Herdr worklist: render command input form as a simple page layout (no dialog box)

## Problem statement

The command input form shown by the herdr worklist for chords with unknown `<identifier>` placeholders (e.g. the `c` / create-new command `/intake <description>`) currently renders as a bordered, centered dialog box overlay (`FormState` in `packages/herdr/src/form-dialog.ts`). The user wants the form rendered as a simple page layout — full-pane content with no border or centering decorations — while keeping the existing modal keyboard interaction.

## Users

- **Herdr users** firing shortcuts/chords whose commands carry parameter placeholders (`<description>`, `<status>`, `<stage>`, `<reason>`, etc.) and who must type values into the form.
- **User story:** "As a Herdr user, when I trigger a shortcut with parameters, I want the input form to look like a normal full-width page of the worklist pane — not a floating dialog box — so it feels consistent with the rest of the TUI and gives me the full width to read and type."

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `FormState.render()` output contains no border box decoration: no `┌ ┐ └ ┘` corners, no `│` side borders, and no `─` box edges.
- [ ] The form content is not centered: it starts at the top-left of the pane (no horizontal `leftPad` centering, no leading blank lines above the content).
- [ ] Content wraps at the **full pane width** (`maxCols`), replacing the current 80%-of-pane clamp.
- [ ] Existing inner content is retained: the "⌨ Command Input" heading, the description, labeled fields, action hints, and the active-field cursor indicator — with a visible space between icon glyphs (e.g. `⌨`, `▶`) and adjacent text.
- [ ] Modal keyboard interaction is preserved: Tab/↑↓ navigate fields, Enter submits, Esc cancels, `<id>` auto-substitution, and submit dispatch via `FormState.onSubmit` (no double dispatch — see WL-0MSAL0RN1009YNJ7).
- [ ] The `render()` contract is unchanged: it returns full-screen output bounded by `maxRows`, consumed by `worklist.ts` (`ANSI.clear` + `cursorHome` + output), and the output never exceeds the terminal height.
- [ ] Unit tests in `form-dialog.test.ts` are updated to cover the new page layout (no border, no centering, full-width wrap, content within pane bounds) while existing interaction/substitution tests still pass.
- [ ] Full project test suite passes with the new changes.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.

> **Note:** CHANGELOG.md is excluded from the documentation criterion — it is managed automatically by the ship skill's release pipeline.

## Constraints

- Terminal rendering is ANSI-based; wrap/width calculations must remain ANSI-aware (strip `\x1b[...m` sequences when measuring visible width) — reuse the existing `visibleWidth`/`wrapContent`/`truncateToWidth` helpers in `form-dialog.ts`; no new dependencies.
- The form remains full-screen/modal: the worklist is hidden while the form page is shown, and keypresses are intercepted by `formState.handleInput` (unchanged).
- No protocol changes: `render(maxCols, maxRows)` keeps its signature and the call site in `worklist.ts` is unchanged.
- Changes are confined to `packages/herdr/src/form-dialog.ts` and its tests (plus doc comments); shortcut routing, submission, and `worklist.ts` behavior are unchanged.

## Existing state

- `FormState.render(maxCols, maxRows)` in `packages/herdr/src/form-dialog.ts` builds a bordered box: width = 80% of pane width (clamped 40..maxCols-4), centered via `leftPad`, with `┌─┐`/`│`/`└─┘` decorations, a blank line above/below the box, and trailing blank-line fill to `maxRows`.
- `packages/herdr/src/form-dialog.test.ts` (24 tests) currently asserts the box behavior: 80% width, 40-column minimum clamp, border alignment (all lines equal width), wrapping at the inner box width, and downward expansion within `maxRows`. These rendering assertions must be rewritten for the page layout.
- `worklist.ts` renders the form full-screen when `formState !== null` (~L2494) and intercepts keys in `onData` (~L2204); both remain unchanged.

## Desired change

1. In `FormState.render()`: drop the border-line construction (`borderLine`/`padLine`), the `leftPad` centering, and the leading blank lines; render content lines directly at full pane width.
2. Wrap description and field values at `maxCols` (full width) instead of the 80% inner width.
3. Keep the row budget bounded by `maxRows` (current `availableRows`/`pushContent` mechanism) so the page never exceeds the terminal.
4. Keep the content styling and icon spacing (space between `⌨`/`▶` glyphs and following text).
5. Update `form-dialog.test.ts` rendering tests to assert the new layout; keep interaction/substitution tests.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/form-dialog.ts` — `FormState.render()` layout change (primary change): remove border/centering, full-width wrap.
- `packages/herdr/src/form-dialog.test.ts` — update rendering tests for the page layout (no border, no centering, full-width wrap, bounds).
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — unchanged; the `formState.render(termSize.cols, termSize.rows)` call site (~L2494) is the contract that must keep working.

## Related work

- `Form input dialog for unknown identifiers in Herdr chord commands (WL-0MS690SJG003H7WK)` — the original feature that introduced `form-dialog.ts` (completed, shipped v1.0.5); this item is a follow-up visual change to that feature.
- `Herdr command input dialog: too narrow, misaligned border; wrap at 80% width and expand downward (WL-0MSAKRBOC005T320)` — the prior dialog-layout polish that set the 80% width/border/wrap behavior this item replaces (completed).
- `Herdr plugin: creating a new intake (c key) fires up two pi instances (WL-0MSAL0RN1009YNJ7)` — form submit dispatch bug fixed previously; the no-double-dispatch behavior must be preserved.
- `Wire text-insertion template commands (WL-0MS4GIMBD008GWVM)` — chord dispatch infrastructure (`executeResolvedCommand`, `onCommand` routing) the form builds on.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** "Full pane" means content wraps at 100% of `maxCols` (confirmed with user: "full pane").
- **Assumption:** all existing inner content (heading, description, labels, hints, cursor indicator) is retained, with a visible space between icons and text (confirmed with user: "Yes keep (put a space between icons and text though)").
- **Assumption:** the page starts at the top-left of the pane; trailing blank-line fill to `maxRows` may be kept or dropped (the screen is cleared before rendering, so trailing blanks are cosmetic).
- **Risk:** emoji/ANSI width handling in wrapped lines at full width — reuse the existing width-aware helpers (`visibleWidth`, `wrapContent`, `truncateToWidth`) to avoid drift with double-width characters.
- **Risk (scope creep):** multi-line editing within fields, layout changes to the worklist itself, or changing the modal behavior are out of scope; record as separate work items if requested.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "For the new page layout, should content wrap at the full pane width (100%), or keep the 80% wrap width and only remove the border/centering?" — Answer (Map): "full pane". Source: interactive reply.
- Q: "Keep the existing inner content styling (heading, colored description, field labels, action hints, cursor indicator) and only remove the border box + centering padding? Or also simplify (e.g., drop heading/hints)?" — Answer (Map): "Yes keep (put a space between icons and text though)". Source: interactive reply. Interpretation: retain all existing content and styling; ensure a visible space between icon glyphs (e.g. `⌨`, `▶`) and adjacent text in the rendered page.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MSAKRBOC005T320** – Herdr command input dialog: too narrow, misaligned border; wrap at 80% width and expand downward (completed)
- **WL-0MSG4VSP10020NL7** – Evaluate Pi subprocess mechanisms: headless pi -p vs herdr pane (send-to-pi.sh) (completed)
- **WL-0MKZ4GAUQ1DFA6TC** – Benchmark sort_index migration at 1000 items per level (completed)

## Summary

The herdr worklist plugin (`packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`) currently runs three independent `setInterval` loops:

1. `resumePollTimer` — 2s visibility poll (dynamic, started/stopped on hidden/visible transitions)
2. `refreshTimer` — auto-refresh (`refreshIntervalMs`, default 30s)
3. `syncTimer` — auto-sync (`syncIntervalMs`, default 60s, via `SyncTimer` in `auto-sync.ts`)

A fourth timer (the downtime worker, WL-0MSF49FMW009M06K) will be added. Consolidate all periodic timers into a single scheduler loop (one `setInterval` ticking at the finest needed granularity, e.g. 1-2s, that dispatches due work by deadline) so tick cadence, pause-when-hidden gating, and shutdown cleanup live in one place.

## User stories

- As a developer, I want all plugin periodic work (refresh, sync, resume poll, downtime worker) driven by one loop so I can reason about cadence and lifecycle in one place.
- As a user, I want hidden-pane gating and shutdown behavior unchanged after the consolidation.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A single timer loop drives refresh, sync, visibility resume-poll, and (future) downtime-worker work; no independent `setInterval` remains for these concerns.
- [ ] Existing behaviors preserved: refresh/sync intervals still configurable via settings; single-flight sync guard; zero-wl-when-hidden; immediate refresh on visible transition; timers unref'd (don't keep process alive); cleanup on pane exit.
- [ ] Unit tests cover the scheduler (due-work dispatch, hidden-pane skipping, single-flight, stop).
- [ ] Full project test suite passes (vitest for packages/herdr).

# Evaluate Pi Subprocess Mechanisms: Headless `pi -p` vs Herdr Pane (`send-to-pi.sh`)

## Problem statement

The system currently creates Pi subprocesses two ways: **headless** (`pi -p
--mode json`, non-interactive, programmatic) and **herdr pane**
(`send-to-pi.sh`, which splits a herdr pane, launches interactive `pi` with an
injected prompt, and renames the pane). Both are used in different places by
skills and herdr code, with overlapping use (notably `/skill:audit`, which is
dispatched both ways). The question is whether both mechanisms are needed, or
whether work visibility would improve by using only the pane method.

## Users

- **Producers / operators** — want to see what agents are doing, catch errors
  early, and intervene; currently headless invocations are invisible.
- **Skills authors** (audit, heartbeat) — need programmatic, batchable,
  concurrent, non-interactive agent calls with parseable output.
- **Herdr worklist users** — spawn interactive agent workflows (`/intake`,
  `/plan`, `/skill:*`) from the list and expect live visibility.

Example user stories:

- "As a producer, when the heartbeat runs an audit in the background, I want
  to know it is running and see its result — right now it is invisible until
  it completes."
- "As a skills author, I need to fan out N concurrent Pi calls for audit
  Phase 2 analysis without opening N terminal panes."
- "As a worklist user, when I press `i` on a work item, I want a live pi pane
  so I can watch the implement workflow and intervene if it stalls."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The evaluation inventories **every** current consumer of both mechanisms
   in skills (`~/.pi/agent/skills/`) and herdr code (`packages/herdr/`,
   `experimental/herdr-podcast-editor`), with file:line evidence for each.
2. The evaluation categorizes each use as (a) automated/batch/nested — only
   headless works, (b) interactive/user-initiated — only a pane works, or
   (c) either (overlap), and identifies the overlap cases.
3. The evaluation gives an explicit recommendation on whether both mechanisms
   should be kept (with rationale) and, if visibility is the concern,
   concrete options for increasing visibility of headless work
   (e.g. worklist agent status icons, heartbeat progress notifications,
   command log, pane-with-headless-fallback).
4. The evaluation documents pros and cons of keeping both mechanisms.
5. Findings are captured in the work item description as a durable
   evaluation report (this task's deliverable is the report itself, not a
   code change).
6. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes (N/A — analysis
   task; no code changes expected).

## Constraints

- No new runtime dependencies; evaluation must be based on the current
  codebase state.
- `pi` headless mode (`--mode json`) is the only way to parse verdicts
  programmatically (audit runner's `_call_pi` and `pi_utils.py` rely on the
  JSON-stream protocol).
- Panes require a herdr environment (TTY, `herdr pane split/run/rename`);
  headless works anywhere (cron, CI, ssh).
- The audit skill already has concurrency caps (`--max-concurrency`,
  `AUDIT_PHASE2_PARALLELISM`) designed around headless subprocesses; a
  pane-only model would need a different concurrency story.
- Do not modify agent-framework infrastructure (`.pi/`, skills, herdr
  internals) as part of the evaluation itself — the report may *recommend*
  changes, tracked as separate work items.

## Existing state — inventory of both mechanisms

### Mechanism A: Headless subprocess (`pi -p --mode json`)

| Consumer | Location | Use |
|---|---|---|
| Audit skill Phase 1/2 (`_call_pi`) | `~/.pi/agent/skills/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py:851-940` | `pi -p --mode json --model <m> <prompt>`; bare calls for Phase 1, agent mode (`--tools read,bash,grep,find,ls --exclude-tools ask_question`) for Phase 2; concurrency caps, retries, timeouts; parses verdict/evidence from JSON stream |
| Audit Phase 2 child fan-out | `audit_runner.py` (see `_PHASE2_DEFAULT_PARALLELISM=2`, `AUDIT_PHASE2_PARALLELISM`) | up to N concurrent `phase2_child:<i>` pi subprocesses per audit |
| Audit PR flow | `~/.pi/agent/skills/audit/audit_pr.py:173-186` | `pi -p --mode json "/audit <wl-id>"` in a worktree, output extracted to log |
| Heartbeat skill | `~/.pi/agent/skills/heartbeat/SKILL.md:99` + `scripts/heartbeat.py:147` | `pi -p --mode json --no-session /skill:audit <id>` for automated queue audits (queue >= 10 items) |
| Shared JSON-stream parser | `~/.pi/agent/skills/scripts/pi_utils.py` | `extract_pi_text`/`parse_pi_json_line` used by audit and others |
| Legacy TUI PiAdapter (inactive) | `dist/tui/pi-adapter.js` (src/tui removed, see WL-0MQRXOY85001WH4Q) | `pi --mode json --print` streaming — no longer built from source |

### Mechanism B: Herdr pi agent pane (`send-to-pi.sh`)

| Consumer | Location | Use |
|---|---|---|
| Herdr worklist plugin routing | `packages/herdr/src/index.ts:329` (spawn of `SEND_TO_PI_SCRIPT`) | routes `/skill:*`, `/intake`, `/plan`, `/prompt:` to a new pane via `send-to-pi.sh --cwd <wlRoot> [--model <m>] <command>`; claims work item in_progress first (WL-0MS9NPHQU005Y3VE) |
| Herdr shortcuts | `packages/herdr/src/shortcuts.json` | agent-channel commands: `c`/`n` `/intake`, `p` `/plan`, `i` `/skill:implement`, `a a` `/skill:audit`, `o p` `/prompt:...`; per-shortcut `model` forwarding |
| Shared script | `packages/herdr/shared/send-to-pi.sh` | `herdr pane split --current --direction right` → `herdr pane run <id> exec pi [--model] <cmd>` → rename "Pi Agent"; `--cwd`/`HERDR_RESOLVED_CWD` propagation |
| Interactive pane (no command) | `packages/herdr/shared/open-pi-agent.sh` | plain interactive pi pane |
| Podcast editor (open_source_llm) | `experimental/herdr-podcast-editor/README.md:38-90` | review (`/skill:wiki-podcast-script --review-rewrite`) and TTS dispatch via `send-to-pi.sh` when `HERDR_ENV==1`; **falls back to direct subprocess when not in a herdr env** |
| Other pane execution (related) | `packages/herdr/scripts/run-in-pane.sh` | visible shell execution for `!!`/`!` prefixed commands — not pi-specific but same pane model |

### Categorisation

- **Automated / batch / nested — headless only:** audit Phase 1 & Phase 2
  sub-calls (nested agent calls inside the audit skill; N concurrent), PR
  audits, heartbeat audits (unattended). No user is watching; parseable
  verdicts required; panes would flood the UI and block automation.
- **Interactive / user-initiated — pane only:** `/intake`, `/plan`,
  `/skill:implement` from the worklist; free-form `/prompt:`; podcast
  review/TTS dispatch. Long-running, user watches and can intervene.
- **Overlap (both used for the same skill):** `/skill:audit` —
  user-initiated from worklist (`a a` chord → pane) vs automated from
  heartbeat (headless). Same skill, different intent (interactive audit vs
  unattended queue audit). This is the visibility gap: pane audits are
  visible; heartbeat audits are invisible until the result lands.

### Assessment: are both needed?

**Yes.** They serve orthogonal requirements:

1. Headless is the *only* workable mechanism for fan-out and automation.
   Audit Phase 2 already opens up to N concurrent pi processes per item
   (bounded by `--max-concurrency` / `AUDIT_PHASE2_PARALLELISM`); a pane per
   call would consume unbounded terminal space and defeat concurrency caps.
   Heartbeat, cron, CI, and PR triggers run unattended with no pane to watch.
   Verdict extraction requires `--mode json` programmatic output.
2. The pane is the right mechanism for interactive, user-initiated
   workflows where the user wants live visibility and the ability to answer
   questions (implement/plan/intake are long-running and interactive; the
   audit agent-mode explicitly *disables* `ask_question` headless).
3. Pane-only dispatch would not work for the audit's nested sub-calls: each
   audit would spawn many panes, and automated contexts have no viewer.

### Pros and cons of keeping both

**Pros of headless (`pi -p --mode json`)**:

- Enables unattended automation (heartbeat, cron, CI, PR-triggered audits).
- Supports fan-out with bounded concurrency (audit Phase 2 children) without
  flooding the UI with panes.
- Programmatic, parseable output (`--mode json` → verdict/evidence via
  `pi_utils.py`) is the only way the audit runner can record structured
  results.
- No dependency on a herdr session/TTY — works over ssh, in CI, in scripts.
- Deterministic timeouts, retries, and concurrency caps (`CALL_PI_TIMEOUT`,
  `_PI_MAX_RETRIES`, `--max-concurrency`).

**Cons of headless**:

- Invisible: no live view of the agent's work; only log files after the fact.
- Non-interactive: cannot answer questions (audit agent-mode explicitly
  excludes `ask_question`), so blocked/failed runs are harder to recover.
- Harder to debug and supervise (no pane to interrupt mid-run).
- Results are only visible once recorded — a producer cannot see the work
  in progress.

**Pros of pane (`send-to-pi.sh`)**:

- Full live visibility — the user watches the agent work and can intervene.
- Interactive — the agent can ask questions (e.g. implement/plan/intake).
- Consistent herdr UX: work item claimed (in_progress) before dispatch, model
  selected per shortcut, pane named "Pi Agent".
- Work appears visibly attached to the item (status icons in progress via
  WL-0MSBQUJQX005RAT9).

**Cons of pane**:

- Requires a herdr session/TTY; unusable from cron, CI, or ssh.
- Pane proliferation: one pane per dispatch (a-a audit, i implement, etc.);
  no singleton guard in some consumers (podcast editor README notes each
  press of `r` opens another pane); a nested fan-out would be unmanageable.
- Fire-and-forget from the caller's perspective: no programmatic result
  capture — the caller cannot parse verdicts from a pane.
- Consumes terminal space; panes must be closed manually.

### Recommendation

Keep both, but close the visibility gap for headless work:

- **Keep headless** for all automated/batch/nested calls (audit Phase 1/2
  sub-calls, heartbeat, PR/CI audits).
- **Keep the pane** for user-initiated interactive workflows from herdr.
- **Increase visibility of headless work** (instead of replacing it):
  - Agent status icons / spawned-agent tracking in the worklist (already
    planned: WL-0MSBQUJQX005RAT9).
  - Heartbeat audit progress + completion notification (toast or item
    comment) instead of silent background runs.
  - Command log per work item (already exists in herdr worklist).
  - Consider a *hybrid* for user-initiated audits from contexts where a pane
    is not available — the podcast editor already implements exactly this
    pattern (`HERDR_ENV` check → pane, else subprocess).
  - If a fully-visible audit is ever desired for the heartbeat path, route
    the heartbeat's audit through the same pane dispatch when a herdr
    session is present (mirroring the podcast-editor fallback pattern).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** the codebase (skills in `~/.pi/agent/skills/`, herdr in `packages/herdr/` and `experimental/`) is the authoritative inventory of both mechanisms. Findings are point-in-time and will drift as code changes.
- **Assumption:** `pi -p --mode json` remains the supported programmatic interface for pi (the audit runner, `pi_utils.py`, and heartbeat depend on it).
- **Risk:** the evaluation report becomes stale quickly — mitigation: keep the report focused on the decision (keep both + visibility options), not exhaustive line-level detail.
- **Risk (scope creep):** visibility improvements are attractive follow-ups but are separate concerns — record them as linked work items (WL-0MSBQUJQX005RAT9 already tracks the icon feature) rather than expanding this task.

## Desired change

No code change is required to answer the evaluation question. The deliverable
is this report (stored in the work item description). Any follow-up work
(e.g. visibility improvements for headless audits, hybrid dispatch) should be
spawned as separate linked work items.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `~/.pi/agent/skills/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — `_call_pi` headless consumer; concurrency caps; Phase 1/2 fan-out.
- `~/.pi/agent/skills/audit/audit_pr.py` — headless audit in worktrees.
- `~/.pi/agent/skills/heartbeat/scripts/heartbeat.py` — headless `/skill:audit` invocation.

# Heartbeat: Surface Audit Progress and Completion Notifications

## Problem statement

The heartbeat skill runs audits headlessly via `pi -p --mode json --no-session /skill:audit <id>` when the completed/in_review queue reaches 10+ items. From the producer's perspective this work is invisible: there is no live view, no progress signal, and no notification when the audit completes. The audit either lands silently or fails silently (timeout/error) — see the evaluation of Pi subprocess mechanisms (discovered-from:WL-0MSG4VSP10020NL7), which identified this as the main visibility gap of headless pi usage.

## Users

- **Producers / operators** — want to know when a background heartbeat audit starts, is running, and finishes (with its verdict), so they can review results without polling the worklog.

Example user stories:

- "As a producer, when the heartbeat starts an audit, I want to see a notification so I know background work is happening."
- "As a producer, when a heartbeat audit completes, I want the result (Ready to close: Yes/No) surfaced so I don't have to discover it by chance."
- "As a producer, when a heartbeat audit fails or times out, I want that surfaced too, with the reason."

## Expected behaviour

- On heartbeat audit start: surface a notification (e.g. herdr toast and/or a work-item comment).
- On completion: surface the verdict ('Ready to close: Yes/No') — e.g. via toast, work-item comment, or both.
- On failure/timeout: surface the failure reason.

## Suggested implementation approach

- Extend the heartbeat skill (`.pi/skills/heartbeat/SKILL.md` and `scripts/heartbeat.py`) to emit notifications around the `pi -p` audit invocation.
- Reuse existing notification plumbing where available (herdr `notification show` used by the worklist plugin's `notify.ts`; `wl comment add` for a durable record on the audited item).
- Consider an opt-out flag/env var so automated environments (cron, CI) can suppress noisy notifications.

## Acceptance criteria

1. When the heartbeat dispatches an audit, a visible start notification is produced.
2. When the audit completes, the verdict ('Ready to close: Yes/No') is surfaced via a notification and/or a comment on the work item.
3. When the audit fails or times out, the failure is surfaced with the reason.
4. Notifications are non-blocking (heartbeat continues to exit 0 on success) and can be suppressed for unattended environments.
5. Existing heartbeat tests still pass; new tests cover start/completion/failure notification paths.
6. All related documentation (SKILL.md) is updated to reflect the changes.
7. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

# Hybrid Pi Dispatch: Pane When in a Herdr Session, Headless Fallback Otherwise

## Problem statement

The evaluation of Pi subprocess mechanisms (discovered-from:WL-0MSG4VSP10020NL7) found that /skill:audit is dispatched two ways: user-initiated audits open a visible herdr pi pane via send-to-pi.sh, while automated contexts (heartbeat, cron, CI, ssh) must run headless via `pi -p --mode json`. Currently the choice of mechanism is hard-wired per caller and there is no shared way to get a visible pane when a herdr session exists and fall back to a headless subprocess when it does not. The podcast editor (open_source_llm/experimental/herdr-podcast-editor) already implements exactly this hybrid pattern via a HERDR_ENV check; it is a proven precedent to generalise.

## Users

- **Producers / operators** — want agent work to be visible whenever a herdr session is present, even when the invocation originates from a script or automated context.
- **Skills authors / plugin authors** — want a single reusable dispatch primitive instead of maintaining two mechanisms.

Example user stories:

- "As a producer, when an audit is triggered from a context that has a herdr session available, I want it to open in a visible pi pane so I can watch it."
- "As a producer, when no herdr session is available, I want the same invocation to fall back to headless execution so the work still happens."
- "As a plugin author, I want to dispatch a skill to pi once and have it choose pane-vs-headless automatically."

## Expected behaviour

- A shared dispatch helper determines at runtime whether a herdr session/pane environment is available (e.g. HERDR_ENV or herdr CLI/socket presence, mirroring the podcast editor).
- When available: dispatch via send-to-pi.sh (visible pane).
- When unavailable: fall back to `pi -p --mode json` headless execution with the same command.
- Existing callers keep their behaviour; new callers (e.g. heartbeat audits, user-initiated audits outside the worklist) opt in.

## Suggested implementation approach

- Add the helper to the shared herdr scripts (packages/herdr/shared/) and/or a small skill-level utility so both herdr code and skills can use it.
- Model the fallback on the podcast editor's send-to-pi.sh wrapper + direct-subprocess branch.
- Wire the heartbeat audit dispatch to use the hybrid helper (pane when herdr present, headless otherwise), which also delivers visibility (see WL-0MSG5THFC004WJEI).

## Acceptance criteria

1. A shared dispatch helper exists that selects pane vs headless at runtime based on herdr availability.
2. With a herdr environment present, dispatch opens a visible pi pane running the given command.
3. Without a herdr environment, dispatch runs the command headless via `pi -p --mode json` and returns programmatic output.
4. At least one existing caller (e.g. heartbeat audit dispatch) is converted to use the helper without regressing its current behaviour.
5. Tests cover both branches (herdr present / absent).
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant docs entries.
7. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

# Test suite for scripts/install-herdr.sh

## Summary

Vitest suite that executes the bash install script (`scripts/install-herdr.sh`) against temp directories, following the precedent of `tests/scripts/install-pi-extension.test.ts` (which runs the script via `execFileSync('bash', [scriptPath], ...)` with an overridden HOME). Covers config-insertion logic (idempotence, missing-file creation, existing-binding skip, `HERDR_CONFIG_PATH` override) and failure modes (herdr missing on PATH, unwritable config).

## User story

"As a developer running the install script, I want tests that prove the herdr config keybinding is inserted exactly once (never duplicated), the file is created when missing, and the script never fails the build even when herdr is absent."

## Acceptance Criteria

- Running the script twice against a temp `HERDR_CONFIG_PATH` leaves exactly one `[[keys.command]]` block for `worklog-selection-list.open-worklist` (idempotence).
- Running the script with a non-existent config path creates the parent directory and file, containing the exact TOML block:

  [[keys.command]]
  key = "prefix+l"
  command = "herdr plugin action invoke worklog-selection-list.open-worklist"
  description = "Open the Worklog work item selection pane in a new tab."

# scripts/install-herdr.sh — idempotent herdr integration installer

## Summary

Bash install script (following `scripts/install-pi-extension.sh` conventions: `set -euo pipefail`, clear echo output, tolerant of missing binaries) that (a) links the Worklog herdr plugin via `herdr plugin link packages/herdr/herdr-plugin.toml` (resolved from repo root) and (b) inserts the `prefix+l` → `worklog-selection-list.open-worklist` `[[keys.command]]` block into the herdr config only if not already present. Wired into `npm run build` via a `postbuild` hook (see sibling work item for wiring/docs).

## User story

"As a developer installing the Worklog repo, when I run the install script, I want the herdr worklist plugin linked and its prefix+l shortcut registered in my herdr config without duplicate entries if I re-run it, so the worklist just works."

## Acceptance Criteria

- Script resolves the config path from `HERDR_CONFIG_PATH` when set, else `~/.config/herdr/config.toml` (same resolution herdr uses).
- Script creates the config parent directory and file when missing (file may start empty with just the inserted block).
- Script appends the exact `[[keys.command]]` block (`key = "prefix+l"`, `command = "herdr plugin action invoke worklog-selection-list.open-worklist"`, `description = "Open the Worklog work item selection pane in a new tab."`) only when a binding for `worklog-selection-list.open-worklist` is not already present (grep-based existence check on the command string).
- Script appends with a leading newline when the existing file lacks a trailing newline; no other edits to the config (no reordering, no comment changes).
- Script runs `herdr plugin link packages/herdr/herdr-plugin.toml` (path resolved relative to repo root) when herdr is on PATH; re-link is safe/no-op (herdr's own idempotence, verified at runtime — Q2 answer).
- Script exits 0 with a warning when `herdr` is not on PATH (link skipped; config insertion still attempted) or when the config cannot be written — `npm run build` must not fail in CI/offline environments.
- Follows `install-pi-extension.sh` style: `set -euo pipefail`, `SCRIPT_DIR`/`REPO_ROOT` resolution, friendly echo output.
- All tests in `tests/scripts/install-herdr.test.ts` pass (green).

## Minimal implementation

- Single file `scripts/install-herdr.sh`:
  - Resolve `SCRIPT_DIR`/`REPO_ROOT` (same pattern as `install-pi-extension.sh`).
  - `CONFIG_PATH="${HERDR_CONFIG_PATH:-$HOME/.config/herdr/config.toml}"`.
  - `grep -qF 'worklog-selection-list.open-worklist'` existence check; if absent, `mkdir -p` the dir and append the block (leading newline when needed) via `printf`/`cat >>`.
  - `command -v herdr` guard; if present run `herdr plugin link "${REPO_ROOT}/packages/herdr/herdr-plugin.toml"`, else warn and continue.
  - Never exit non-zero on herdr-missing or write failure — warn to stderr and exit 0.

## Dependencies

- Blocked by: Tests for install-herdr script behaviors (test-first; this feature turns those tests green).

## Deliverables

- `scripts/install-herdr.sh`

## Key Files

- `scripts/install-herdr.sh`
- `tests/scripts/install-herdr.test.ts` (tests that must pass)

## Summary

The pane-launch grid feature (WL-0MSAPRMRH002S10O) is broken: launching a new pane in resize mode (the default) fails with 'Error: Could not resolve the current pane.'

## Root cause

Both shared launch scripts resolve the anchor pane with:

```bash
anchor="$("$herdr_bin" pane current --json 2>/dev/null | sed -n 's/.*"pane_id":"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p' | head -n1)"
```

herdr 0.7.5's `pane current` does NOT accept `--json` (exit 2, 'unknown option: --json'); it emits JSON by default. Since stderr is suppressed, `anchor` is empty and the script exits 1 before any split. The plugin spawns the script detached with stdio ignored, so the user sees nothing happen when launching from a newly opened plugin pane (prefix+l).

The bash tests missed this because the mock herdr CLI accepts any arguments.

## Steps to reproduce

1. herdr 0.7.5 session; open the worklist plugin (prefix+l)
2. Trigger an agent command that launches a pi pane (e.g. /prompt: or a /skill: shortcut)
3. No pane opens; `herdr pane current --json` fails

## Fix

- Drop `--json` from the `pane current` call in packages/herdr/shared/send-to-pi.sh and packages/herdr/shared/open-pi-agent.sh
- Harden grid.py grid-state detection: unrecognisable layout shapes (anchor not resolvable) should fall back to a fresh right-split of the current pane instead of misbehaving
- Add bash test coverage asserting `pane current` is invoked without `--json`

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `herdr pane current` is called without `--json` in both shared scripts
- [ ] Resize mode resolves the anchor and launches a pane in a live herdr 0.7.5 session
- [ ] grid.py falls back to a fresh right-split when the layout is not a recognised grid
- [ ] Bash tests and Python tests pass

## Summary

Deferred follow-up for WL-0MSF49FMW009M06K (Herdr to consume local LLM in downtime). When the llama-proxy serves per-slot details (`slot_id` + `is_processing`) in `GET /llama/local/status` (proxy feature request **LP-0MSG5TA7Y002GN39**), the herdr downtime worker must track idle duration **per slot identity** so a configured `downtimeRequiredFreeSlots` N < total slots requires the *same* slot(s) free for the full threshold — not any N slots.

discovered-from:WL-0MSF49FMW009M06K

## User stories

- As an operator, when I configure the downtime worker to require fewer than all slots free (e.g. 2 of 6), I want the same slot(s) to remain free for the full idle threshold so dispatch reflects genuine capacity stability, not transient any-N-slot availability.

## Expected behaviour

- Worker parses optional per-slot fields (`slots: [{slot_id, is_processing}]`) from `/llama/local/status` when present.
- When `downtimeRequiredFreeSlots` N < total slots: idle-duration is tracked per `slot_id`; a slot that starts processing resets its own idle timer; dispatch fires only when the same N slots have been continuously free for ≥ `downtimeIdleThresholdMs`.
- When per-slot data is absent: fail closed to the default all-slots-free condition (the behavior delivered by WL-0MSF49FMW009M06K) — never "any N slots" without same-slot identity.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] When the proxy response includes per-slot details, the worker requires the same N slots free for the full threshold; a slot starting processing resets that slot's idle timer.
- [ ] When per-slot details are absent (LP-0MSG5TA7Y002GN39 not fulfilled), the worker degrades to all-slots-free (identical to the current-item behavior) and never dispatches on "any N slots".
- [ ] Unit tests cover per-slot idle tracking, slot-identity reset, and the no-per-slot-data fallback.
- [ ] Full project test suite passes (vitest for packages/herdr).
- [ ] README documents the per-slot behaviour and the N < total slots configuration.

## Dependencies

- blocked-by:LP-0MSG5TA7Y002GN39 (proxy must expose per-slot fields first)
- Blocks/extends WL-0MSF49FMW009M06K AC2 (same-slot stability)

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — extend idle tracker with per-slot_id tracking

- `packages/herdr/README.md` — document per-slot behaviour

## Summary

Implementation feature for WL-0MSF49FMW009M06K. Adds the six downtime settings with defaults/clamps to the herdr worklist plugin and implements the single-flight poller for `GET /llama/local/status` with fail-closed parsing.

## User stories

- As an operator, I want to configure downtime behaviour (enabled, idle threshold, required free slots, poll interval, proxy URL, model) in `~/.config/herdr/worklog-plugin.json` without a plugin restart.
- As a developer, I want a poller that treats endpoint failures as busy so the plugin never crashes or hammers the proxy.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] New settings keys in `settings.ts` with defaults: `downtimeEnabled` (true), `downtimeIdleThresholdMs` (240000), `downtimeRequiredFreeSlots` (0 = all slots), `downtimePollIntervalMs` (30000, floor 10000 via `clampDowntimePollInterval`), `downtimeProxyUrl` (http://192.168.0.199:8000), `downtimeModel` (`plan`). Load/merge/clamp covered by unit tests.
- [ ] `downtimeRequiredFreeSlots` semantics: 0 = all slots free required; any positive integer N is accepted and validated against total slots at runtime (N > total → never idle).
- [ ] Poller (`downtime-worker.ts`): GET `{proxyUrl}/llama/local/status` on `downtimePollIntervalMs`; single-flight (no overlapping polls); per-poll timeout (fail closed).
- [ ] Fail-closed parsing: HTTP errors, timeouts, network failures, invalid JSON, missing/ambiguous fields are treated as busy (no dispatch) and never throw or crash the plugin.
- [ ] Idle condition implemented per F1 contract: llama_server_running true, no active query, no model switch, no active local lease, `available_slots >= total_slots` with `total_slots > 0`. When `downtimeRequiredFreeSlots` N is 0→all free; N < total slots without per-slot data → all slots free (fail closed, never "any N slots"); N > total → never idle.
- [ ] Settings are re-read each poll/tick so changes apply without a plugin restart.
- [ ] F1 poller/idle-detection/settings-clamp tests pass; full suite green at repo root (`npx vitest run`).

## Minimal Implementation

- Extend `PluginSettings` + `defaultSettings` + load/merge in `settings.ts`; add `clampDowntimePollInterval` and any other clamps.
- `downtime-worker.ts`: `fetchLocalStatus(url, timeoutMs)` with AbortSignal timeout; `evaluateIdle(status, requiredFreeSlots): boolean` (pure, testable); poll-loop scaffold with single-flight flag.
- Wire settings through `loadSettings()` calls; no independent setInterval yet (F4 integrates into the consolidated scheduler).

Includes the pre-dispatch claim, single-flight guard, and blocked-questions prompt instruction.

## User stories

- As an operator, when the local LLM has been idle for the configured threshold, I want the backlog to advance automatically: a visible (non-focus-stealing) pi agent pane runs /skill:plan on the next intake_complete item, or /skill:intake on the next idea item.
- As an operator, when an automated skill run needs answers I haven't given, I want the questions recorded on the work item and the item flagged for producer review so nothing blocks silently.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Idle-duration tracker: `idleSince` timestamp set on first idle poll, advanced each consecutive idle poll; any busy poll resets it; dispatch fires only when idle duration ≥ `downtimeIdleThresholdMs` continuously (AC1/AC5).
- [ ] Dispatch selection: run `wl next --stage intake_complete --json` → first item → `/skill:plan <id>`; if empty, `wl next --stage idea --json` → `/skill:intake <id>`; if both empty, no dispatch (wait for next idle period).
- [ ] **Tier fallthrough on CLI error**: when the `intake_complete` lookup fails (`ok: false`), the `idea` lookup is STILL performed; a tier-3 candidate dispatches `/skill:intake`. A tier-2 error followed by a genuinely empty tier 3 is fail-closed to busy (no dispatch, no cooldown — the backlog is not provably empty).
- [ ] **Three-strike rule on CLI errors**: three consecutive `wl-error` dispatch outcomes enter the no-candidate cooldown (full pause, no dispatch) AFTER logging the persistent error to the rolling downtime log via `deps.recordError`. Any successful dispatch or genuine no-candidate outcome resets the strike counter; a single transient error does not pause the worker; `dispatch-in-flight` is neutral (no strike).
- [ ] Item is claimed before dispatch (`wl update <id> --status in_progress`) so it appears in_progress immediately and a second pane's `wl next` cannot select it (cross-pane serialization decision Q5: no lock file).
- [ ] Dispatch via shared `send-to-pi.sh`: `--no-focus`, `--cwd <wlRoot>`, `--model <downtimeModel>`, pane name `Downtime plan`/`Downtime intake`; spawn detached and unref'd like existing dispatches.
- [ ] Single-flight: at most one dispatch in flight per plugin process; no dispatch before the idle threshold; after a dispatch the worker does not dispatch again until another full idle period (dispatch consumes the local slot → proxy busy).
- [ ] Blocked-questions handling: the dispatched prompt appends the instruction — "If you cannot proceed because you need answers from the operator, record the questions in a comment on the work item and run `wl update <id> --needs-producer-review true`, then stop." (AC6).
- [ ] F1 dispatch-selection / single-flight / blocked-questions / threshold-timing tests pass; full suite green at repo root (`npx vitest run`).

## Minimal Implementation

- `downtime-worker.ts`: `IdleTracker` (idleSince, recordPoll(isIdle), isThresholdMet(now)); `selectNextItem(wlNextFn)`; `buildDispatchPrompt(command, itemId)`; `dispatch(sendToPiArgs)` using `spawn` + claim via `wl update`.
- `dispatchDowntimeWork`: always attempt the `idea` lookup after a non-candidate/errored `intake_complete` lookup (tier fallthrough).
- `createDowntimeWorker`: consecutive-error strike counter (`DOWNTIME_ERROR_STRIKE_LIMIT = 3`); on the 3rd consecutive `wl-error` outcome call `deps.recordError(...)` then enter the no-candidate cooldown; reset the counter on dispatched / no-candidate / cooldown expiry. Expose the counter as a readonly getter for tests.
- New dep `DowntimeWorkerDeps.recordError(event)` — fail-closed, must never throw; wired in `createDowntimeDeps` (index.ts) to `appendDowntimeLogEntry` (rolling `.worklog` log).
- Prompt is passed directly to send-to-pi.sh (worker does not route through the TUI's routeCommand).

## Dependencies

- Depends on WL-0MSG80254005ZNE9 (settings + poller).
- Parent: WL-0MSF49FMW009M06K. Related: WL-0MSI7DQL10016QYX (no-candidate cooldown mechanism reused for the three-strike pause).

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — tracker, selection, dispatch
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts` — tests
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — deps wiring (recordError → rolling log)

## Problem

During the excessive-spawn investigation (WL-0MSB19J56006E87J) and in normal operation, `worklog.db-wal` grows large under concurrent writer load (16MB WAL observed). Worklog uses SQLite in WAL mode by design (`src/persistent-store.ts` sets `journal_mode = WAL` for concurrency).

Observations:

- Writes land in `worklog.db-wal` first; `worklog.db` mtime/size stays unchanged until a checkpoint merges the WAL back. A 66KB `worklog.db-wal` was observed in `open_source_llm/.worklog` while `worklog.db` sat untouched — and the WAL files disappear once all processes close (checkpoint on close / auto-checkpoint).
- Under the spawn storm (206 concurrent wl processes), the WAL reached ~16MB, meaning auto-checkpointing was not keeping up with write volume.

Why this matters:

1. **Read cost:** SQLite reads must scan the WAL, so a large WAL slows every read query.
2. **Cache invalidation:** mtime/size of `worklog.db` alone is unreliable while a large WAL holds live writes (see WL-0MSAZQEQB008O7H3 AC #2 — cache must be WAL-aware).
3. **Crash/recovery:** a large WAL means longer recovery time on abnormal exit.

## Goals

- Understand current checkpointing behavior: default auto-checkpoint threshold, when/where wl checkpoints (per-write? on close? explicit wal_checkpoint?), and how concurrent writers interact.
- Determine whether a large-WAL state is a correctness risk or only a performance cost.
- Decide if wl should checkpoint after write batches (e.g., after `wl sync` or bulk mutations) or rely on auto-checkpoint.

## Suggested approach

- Inspect `src/persistent-store.ts` and `src/database.ts` for pragma settings and any checkpoint logic.
- Reproduce: run N concurrent write processes against one worklog and measure WAL growth, read latency, and checkpoint behavior.
- Consider adding an explicit `PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(PASSIVE/TRUNCATE)` after write-heavy operations if evidence supports it.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Documented understanding of when/where checkpointing happens and why a 16MB WAL occurred (root cause identified, reproduced, or ruled out).
2. Measured impact of large WAL on read latency (before/after numbers).
3. A recommendation recorded on this item: leave as-is, add explicit checkpointing, or tune auto-checkpoint threshold — with rationale and risk notes.
4. Any code change is tested and does not regress the full test suite.

# Herdr selection list: no indication of items below the fold

## Problem statement

When the herdr worklist selection list (`createListRenderer` in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`) has more work items than fit in the visible list area, the renderer silently trims the visible window to fit the pane height. There is no visual cue (scroll marker, count, ellipsis) that additional items exist below the fold, so users cannot tell the list is truncated and may miss items.

## Users

Anyone using the herdr worklist pane (`worklog-selection-list` plug) to browse/select work items, in particular with more items than fit on screen (the default list of 20+ items on smaller panes, or with the metadata panel reserving 20–40% of the height).

User story: *"As a herdr user, when the worklist pane shows more items than fit, I want to see a `▼ more` marker so I know the list continues below the fold and I can scroll (j/k) to see the rest."*

User story: *"As a herdr user who has scrolled down, I want to see an `▲ more` marker at the top of the list so I know there are items above the current viewport."*

## Acceptance Criteria

- When the flattened item list exceeds the visible list area at scroll offset 0, the rendered list output contains a dim-styled `▼ more` marker at the bottom of the items region (after the last visible item, before the footer/fill rows).
- When the list is scrolled down (scrollOffset > 0) with items above the viewport, the rendered output contains a dim-styled `▲ more` marker at the top of the items region (before the first visible item/group separator).
- When all items fit in the visible area (no overflow, scrollOffset = 0), no indicators are rendered.
- The `rows - 1` line-count invariant is preserved with indicators active: rendered output plus the notification line still fits the pane height (regression guard for WL-0MSAAON63003N6LO).
- Indicators are non-selectable display-only rows: they do not consume navigation state, selection index, or hierarchy scroll offset (`getVisibleItems`, `_adjustScroll` semantics unchanged).
- New unit tests in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` cover: indicator shown when items exist below the fold; `▲ more` shown when scrolled; no indicators when the list fits; line-count invariant with indicators active.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.

> **Note:** CHANGELOG.md is **excluded** from this list. It is managed automatically by the ship skill's release pipeline. Implementing agents should not manually update CHANGELOG.md.

## Constraints

- Must preserve the `rows - 1` line-count invariant established in WL-0MSAAON63003N6LO (notification line always fits; header never scrolls off the top).
- Indicator wording is generic ("more"), not exact counts — group separator rows make exact "N more" counts unreliable.
- Scope is list mode only: the detail view and the metadata panel (WL-0MSAYNVBY006LM9X) are unchanged.
- Match existing styling conventions: dim-styled (`ANSI.dim`), consistent with other non-interactive chrome (footer hints, filter bar).
- Indicator rows must be included in the render budget (the `visible` trimming loop and the fill-blank count) so output never exceeds the pane.

## Existing state

- `createListRenderer` sizes the visible window with `flatItems.slice(scrollOffset, scrollOffset + listHeight)` and trims it with `visible.slice(0, -1)` when items + group separators exceed `budgetForItemsAndSeps`. Nothing signals that trimming happened.
- The pane header shows `(top N of M)` only when the *fetch* was truncated (`totalCount > items.length`), not when the *display* is truncated by the viewport — so a full fetch with a small pane shows no cue at all.
- Scrolling works (j/k via `scrollOffset`, `_adjustScroll` keeps the selection visible), but at rest positions there is no indication of hidden items in either direction.
- The Pi TUI browse list (`packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/browse.ts`) is a separate surface and already shows `(top N of M)` in its title; pi's built-in `SelectList` component renders a `(N/M)` scroll-info line when overflow exists — the established pattern this change mirrors.

## Desired change

- In `createListRenderer` (list mode), after the visible window is trimmed to fit:
  - Emit a dim `▼ more` line at the bottom of the items region when `scrollOffset + visible.length < flatItems.length` (items below the fold).
  - Emit a dim `▲ more` line at the top of the items region when `scrollOffset > 0` (items above the viewport).
  - Account for indicator rows in the budget: include them in the trimming calculation and in the fill-blank `used` count so the `rows - 1` invariant holds.
  - Edge case: if reserving the bottom indicator row trims the window so that `scrollOffset + visible.length == flatItems.length`, the bottom indicator is omitted (the list then fully fits); this must terminate in a single pass (no loop).

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — `createListRenderer`: compute indicator presence from `scrollOffset`/the trimmed visible window, emit `▼ more`/`▲ more` rows, and include them in the budget (`budgetForItemsAndSeps` trimming loop + fill-blank `used` count).
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` — add unit tests: indicator shown when items below fold; `▲ more` shown when scrolled; no indicators when list fits; line-count invariant with indicators active; indicators are non-selectable display rows.

## Related work

- [Herdr plugin: selection list header and top lines cut off top of pane (WL-0MSAAON63003N6LO)] — completed; established the `rows - 1` line-count invariant and the visible-window trimming logic this change extends.
- [Herdr plugin: reserve bottom 40% of selection list for item metadata and last command (WL-0MSAYNVBY006LM9X)] — completed; defines `listArea`/`panelHeight`, the fold boundary of the list region.
- [Create a work item selection list in Herdr (WL-0MS1W8Y1L0059AKP)] — origin of the selection list.
- pi-tui `SelectList` component (`node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-tui/dist/components/select-list.js`) — reference pattern: `(N/M)` scroll-info line when the list overflows `maxVisible`.

## Risks & assumptions

- Assumption: generic "more" wording is sufficient (user: "more" is fine); exact counts are intentionally avoided because group separators make them unreliable.
- Risk: indicator rows shrink the visible item window by up to 2 rows when overflow exists. Acceptable — the alternative (no indicator) is the bug being fixed.
- Risk: budget accounting bugs could regress the WL-0MSAAON63003N6LO line-count invariant. Mitigation: the existing invariant tests plus new tests with indicators active cover both top and bottom indicators.
- Edge case: bottom indicator row reservation could trim the window to fully fit, making the indicator unnecessary — handle without looping.
- Scope-creep guard: the Pi TUI browse list also lacks a fold indicator, but it already shows `(top N of M)`; improving that surface is out of scope and could be tracked as a separate work item.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Indicator style — which do you prefer? (a) a footer line in the items region like `▼ N more` (dim), shown when items exist below the fold; (b) a position indicator like `(N/M)`; (c) both: `▼ N more` footer plus a `▲ N more` header when scrolled down" — Answer (user): "(c) Both". Source: interactive reply.
- Q: "Scope — should this cover only the list-mode pane (herdr worklist), or also the detail-view scroll indicator (which already exists via the metadata panel scroll)?" — Answer (user): "confirm" (list-mode only). Source: interactive reply.
- Q: "Count precision — exact remaining count (e.g. `▼ 5 more`) vs. a generic marker (e.g. `▼ more`)? Exact counts can be wrong when group separators consume rows." — Answer (user): "`more` is fine". Source: interactive reply.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MP15YJEQ000FVWS** – Documentation: colour mapping & fallbacks (completed)
- **WL-0MLRFF0771A8NAVW** – TUI: prevent mouse click-through from dialogs to underlying widgets (completed)
- **WL-0MLOS7X1C1P82B5J** – Append no-questions instruction to OpenCode prompt (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `.worklog/tmp/intake-draft-herdr-below-fold-indicator-WL-0MSG8YXYJ008PWJJ.md` — matched: additional, area, cannot, count, createlistrenderer, exist, fit, fold, height, herdr, indication, indicator, items, list, marker, packages, pane, renderer, scroll, selection, silently, src, tell, there, trims, truncated, users, visible, visual, when, window, work, worklist
- `.worklog/worktrees/wl-WL-0MSDZ64J8005Q2JJ-grid-rebalance-python-tests-mocked-socke/packages/herdr/README.md` — matched: additional, area, cannot, count, exist, height, herdr, indicator, items, list, marker, packages, pane, renderer, scroll, selection, silently, src, tell, there, visible, when, work, worklist
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — matched: additional, area, cannot, count, exist, height, herdr, indicator, items, list, marker, packages, pane, renderer, scroll, selection, silently, src, tell, there, visible, when, work, worklist

## Summary

Implement `src/read-cache.ts` — an on-disk read cache for the wl CLI at `~/.cache/wl/` (XDG cache dir), keyed by (worklog-dir, full argv, wl version), serving JSON-mode results only. Freshness is WAL-aware (watches `worklog.db` + `worklog.db-wal` + `worklog.db-shm`), bounded by TTL (30–60s), and safe under concurrent readers/writers (atomic temp-file + rename). This is option A (primary) from the parent item WL-0MSAZQEQB008O7H3 and the tracer-bullet slice: module + unit tests, before CLI wiring (F2).

## User Experience Change

No user-visible change on its own. This establishes the cache substrate that F2 wires into the read commands; the observable win (fewer `wl` process spawns, lower load) lands with F2+.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Cache entry key is a deterministic hash of (absolute worklog-dir, full argv, wl version); different dirs or arg variants never collide (key collisions / arg-variant separation covered by tests).
2. Freshness is WAL-aware: a write touching `worklog.db`, `worklog.db-wal`, or `worklog.db-shm` invalidates the affected entries; write-then-read returns fresh data immediately (parent AC #2).
3. Entries expire after TTL (default 30–60s, configurable); stale entries are never served; cache is bounded (size/LRU purge).
4. Concurrent readers/writers across processes never corrupt the cache; writes are atomic (temp file + rename); no partial entries readable.
5. Unit tests cover: invalidation under WAL-mode write, key collisions, arg-variant separation, TTL staleness, concurrent access — all pass.

## Implementation Approach

- Implement `src/read-cache.ts`:
  - XDG cache dir resolution (`~/.cache/wl/`, honoring `XDG_CACHE_HOME`).
  - Cache-key hash from (resolved absolute worklog-dir, full argv, `WORKLOG_VERSION` from `src/version.ts` — guards schema drift across wl upgrades).
  - DB-state fingerprint: mtime+size of `worklog.db`, `worklog.db-wal`, `worklog.db-shm`; cheap content fingerprint fallback for coarse-mtime filesystems. Store the fingerprint in the entry header; compare on read.
  - `get`/`set` with atomic temp-file + rename; per-key concurrency safety; TTL check on read; bounded purge (access-time LRU) to prevent unbounded key growth.
- Write tests first (TDD) in `tests/read-cache.test.ts` per the parent's AC #6 (WAL-mode invalidation, collisions, arg variants, concurrency).
- Document cache layout + invalidation semantics in `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`.

## Dependencies

None (foundational slice).

## Deliverables

- `src/read-cache.ts` (new module)
- `tests/read-cache.test.ts` (new test suite)
- `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` section on cache layout/invalidation

## Summary

Wire the F1 read cache into the wl CLI: route `list`, `next`, `show`, `search`, and `status` (JSON mode only) through cache lookup/backfill in `src/cli.ts`; write commands bypass the cache and invalidate affected entries; add env-gated spawn instrumentation so the ≥60% spawn-reduction target (parent AC #7) can be measured and verified.

## User Experience Change

Herdr panes and pi-agent polling stop spawning redundant `wl` processes for byte-identical queries: repeat reads within the invalidation window are served from the shared cache. Refresh cadence stays 30s; nothing user-visible changes except lower system load and faster repeat queries.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Repeat identical JSON queries for `list`, `next`, `show`, `search`, `status` are served from cache without spawning a new `wl` process (parent AC #1; verified via spawn instrumentation).
2. Write commands (`create`, `update`, `close`, `delete`, `comment`, `dep`, `import`, `sync`) are never served from cache; an identical read immediately after a write returns fresh data (parent AC #3).
3. Full argv participates in the cache key: `--status open` vs `--status completed`, `-n 1` vs `-n 5`, `--include-in-progress`, `--root-only` variants all produce separate, non-colliding entries (parent AC #4).
4. Write-byproducts of read commands are accounted for: `next`'s auto re-sort and FTS index builds count as writes (invalidate), so cached `next`/`search` results stay sound.
5. Spawn-counter instrumentation (env-gated, e.g. `WL_SPAWN_COUNT`/log line) records `wl` process spawns; a simulated 6-pane refresh issuing identical queries shows ≥60% fewer spawns vs baseline (parent AC #7).

## Implementation Approach

- Cache lookup/backfill around read-command dispatch in `src/cli.ts`; JSON mode only (all real consumers — herdr, pi agents, audit scripts — use `--json`; text output is terminal/env-dependent and non-deterministic).
- Explicit invalidation on write-command paths (belt-and-braces atop the F1 DB-fingerprint detection).
- Env-gated spawn counter; reuse patterns from `src/wl-integration/spawn.ts` (WL-0MP15AM1N001OBII) where relevant.
- CLI integration tests in `tests/cli/`: key collisions, arg-variant separation, write-invalidation freshness, concurrent access; plus a baseline-vs-cached spawn report for AC #5.

## Dependencies

- F1: Read-cache core module with WAL-aware invalidation (WL-0MSGAE35E001557V) — the module and unit tests must land first.

## Deliverables

- `src/cli.ts` + `src/commands/{list,next,show,search,status}.ts` wiring
- Spawn instrumentation
- CLI integration tests + spawn-reduction report

## Summary

Option E from the parent item WL-0MSAZQEQB008O7H3: (1) a successful `wl sync` explicitly invalidates the read cache for that worklog dir so post-pull/merge reads are always fresh, and (2) a per-worklog-dir sync heartbeat (marker file with last-success timestamp) lets herdr auto-sync skip spawning `wl sync` entirely when one succeeded recently — cutting the remaining redundant sync spawns across panes.

## User Experience Change

With 6 panes on one worklog dir, only the first pane's auto-sync tick spawns `wl sync` per heartbeat window instead of all 6; sync-triggered data refreshes never show stale cached reads. No user-visible behavior change otherwise (sync cadence and semantics unchanged).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. After a successful `wl sync`, identical reads return post-pull data (no stale cache served).
2. With 6 panes on one worklog dir, only the first spawns `wl sync` within the heartbeat window; the other 5 skip without spawning a process (measured).
3. Failed or skipped syncs do not refresh the heartbeat; heartbeat age + TTL bound staleness (no indefinite skip).
4. Tests cover heartbeat skip logic and sync→cache invalidation.

## Implementation Approach

- In `src/commands/sync.ts` (or `src/sync.ts`): on successful sync, invalidate the F1 read-cache entries for the worklog dir and write the heartbeat marker (dir, timestamp).
- In `packages/herdr/src/auto-sync.ts`: before spawning `wl sync`, check the heartbeat age for the target worklog dir and skip when fresh. Retain the existing per-process single-flight guard; extend with cross-instance coordination.
- Tests: sync→invalidation in `tests/`; heartbeat skip in herdr auto-sync tests (mock spawn, verify no spawn when heartbeat fresh).

## Dependencies

- F1: Read-cache core module with WAL-aware invalidation (WL-0MSGAE35E001557V) — cache invalidation API needed.
- F2: Wire read commands through cache (WL-0MSGAEC5N006W5QA) — cache must be live in the CLI before sync invalidation matters.

## Deliverables

- `src/commands/sync.ts` / `src/sync.ts` invalidation + heartbeat write
- `packages/herdr/src/auto-sync.ts` heartbeat-aware skip
- Tests for both behaviors

## Summary

Option D from the parent item WL-0MSAZQEQB008O7H3: per-instance in-process memoization in `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — dedupe concurrent identical `runWl` fetches within one pane process via a promise-keyed memo so racing refreshes spawn `wl` once.

## User Experience Change

Racing identical fetches inside one pane (e.g., overlapping refresh ticks or duplicate pane queries) resolve from the in-process memo instead of spawning duplicate `wl` processes — lower spawn churn and faster refresh. Refresh cadence (30s) is unchanged.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Two racing identical fetches (same worklog-dir + args) spawn `wl` once; the second call awaits the first's result (mock-exec unit test).
2. The memo is per-process, bounded, and cleared on refresh-cycle / `setWorklogDir` changes; it never serves results across DB writes.
3. Refresh cadence unchanged: `refreshIntervalMs` stays 30s (no modification).

## Implementation Approach

- Promise-keyed memo map in `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` around `runWl`, keyed by (worklog-dir, args); bounded + TTL to avoid unbounded growth.
- Tests in `packages/herdr/src` (fetcher tests already inject a mock via `setExecFileAsync`).

## Dependencies

- F2: Wire read commands through cache (WL-0MSGAEC5N006W5QA) — instrumentation gives visibility into spawn counts for verification. Independent of F3.

## Deliverables

- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` memoization
- Herdr fetcher tests

# Intake Brief: Pi agent pane opened via `a+a` (audit) starts in herdr plugin source dir

## Problem statement

When the user triggers an automatic audit from the Worklog herdr plugin with the `a+a`
chord (`audit automatic` → `/skill:audit <id>`), the new pi agent pane opens in the
**herdr plugin source directory** (e.g. `/home/rgardler/projects/ContextHub/packages/herdr`)
instead of the project root of the selected work item (e.g. `/home/rgardler/projects/ContextHub`).
The audit skill then operates against the wrong project — it cannot find the work item's
`.worklog/`, and any changes it makes land in the wrong repository.

## Users

- **Developer auditing a work item from herdr** — presses `a+a` expecting the audit to run
  in the project that owns the selected work item, but pi starts in the plugin's own source
  directory.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Pressing `a+a` (audit automatic) on an `in_review` item opens the pi agent pane in the
      resolved project root (the directory the worklist pane resolved as its worklog root),
      not in the herdr plugin source directory.
- [ ] The `--cwd` / `HERDR_RESOLVED_CWD` target is honored in the **default resize mode** of
      `send-to-pi.sh` (not only in `--no-resize` mode).
- [ ] The same fix applies to `open-pi-agent.sh` (Open Pi Agent action), which shares the
      resize-mode grid path.
- [ ] The grid helper (`shared/grid.py`) passes the requested `cwd` to the herdr `pane.split`
      RPC for the newly created pane; when no `cwd` is provided behaviour is unchanged
      (backward compatible).
- [ ] Tests cover: (a) the bash launch scripts forward `--cwd` to the grid helper in resize
      mode, and (b) `grid.py` includes `cwd` in the `pane.split` RPC payload.
- [ ] All existing tests pass (bash `shared/tests/test_scripts.sh`, pytest `shared/tests/test_grid.py`,
      and the TS suite in `src/`).
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes (script headers/usage text in
      `shared/send-to-pi.sh` and `shared/open-pi-agent.sh`, and the plugin README if it documents
      the audit dispatch flow).

## Constraints

- herdr 0.7.5: `pane.split` RPC accepts `cwd` (`string | null`) — verified via
  `herdr api schema --json` (PaneSplitParams). The CLI `herdr pane split --cwd <path>` exists.
- `grid.py` is a shared, generic helper used by multiple plugins; any interface change must be
  optional and backward compatible.
- No live herdr session is required for tests — bash and python test suites use mocks
  (`HERDR_BIN_PATH`, `HERDR_GRID_BIN`, `HERDR_SOCKET_PORT`).

## Existing state

- `shared/send-to-pi.sh` (default `--resize` mode): resolves `target_cwd` (priority
  `--cwd` > `HERDR_RESOLVED_CWD` > `$PWD`) but then calls
  `python3 "$grid_bin" "$anchor"` **without forwarding the cwd**; only the `--no-resize`
  fallback path passes `--cwd "$target_cwd"` to `herdr pane split`.
- `shared/open-pi-agent.sh`: identical defect.
- `shared/grid.py` `_split()` sends `{"target_pane_id", "direction", "ratio", "focus"}`
  to the `pane.split` RPC — no `cwd` key. The new pane therefore inherits the CWD of the
  split target, which is the worklist pane running from the plugin source directory.
- `index.ts` already computes the correct `targetCwd` (`wlRoot ?? HERDR_RESOLVED_CWD ?? cwd`)
  and passes it as `--cwd` to `send-to-pi.sh` — the data path is correct; only the resize
  launch path drops it.

## Desired change

1. `shared/grid.py`: accept an optional `--cwd <path>` CLI argument; store it on the
   `GridBuilder` and include `cwd` in the `pane.split` RPC params when set.
2. `shared/send-to-pi.sh` and `shared/open-pi-agent.sh`: in resize mode, invoke the grid
   helper as `python3 "$grid_bin" --cwd "$target_cwd" "$anchor"` (keep `--no-resize` path
   as-is; it already passes `--cwd`).
3. Extend `shared/tests/test_scripts.sh` and `shared/tests/test_grid.py` to assert the new
   forwarding behaviour, plus a regression check that no `--cwd` still works.

## Key Files

- `shared/grid.py` — add optional `--cwd` handling; include `cwd` in `pane.split` RPC params.
- `shared/send-to-pi.sh` — forward `target_cwd` to the grid helper in resize mode.
- `shared/open-pi-agent.sh` — same forwarding fix.
- `shared/tests/test_scripts.sh` — mock-grid assertions that `--cwd` is forwarded in resize mode.
- `shared/tests/test_grid.py` — assert `cwd` appears in split RPC frames when provided.
- `src/index.ts` — no change expected (already passes `--cwd`); verify only.

## Related work

- `WL-0MS6AU1PI0076GYB` (completed) — "Herdr plugin should operate from Herdr tab working
  directory, not ContextHub": established tab-CWD resolution; this bug is the remaining
  launch-path gap (AC "Agent commands sent via send-to-pi.sh from the correct working
  directory" is only met in `--no-resize` mode).
- `WL-0MS8SVY7P0094K6D` (completed) — "Fix: skills and commands must run in correct project
  directory".
- `WL-0MSG6ZI3D003VYZZ` (completed) — "Fix resize-mode anchor resolution" (herdr `pane current`
  rejects `--json`): introduced the current resize-mode code path.
- `WL-0MSDZ6A6M0014SHB` / `WL-0MSDZ69HO0008MF8` (completed) — resize mode in shared launch
  scripts + bash tests.
- `WL-0MSDZ64J8005Q2JJ` / `WL-0MSDZ69TZ00962IO` (completed) — even-completion grid rebalance
  (`grid.py`) + Python tests.

## Risks & assumptions

- Assumption: herdr 0.7.5's `pane.split` RPC honors `cwd` the same way the CLI
  `pane split --cwd` does. Mitigation: verify against the live herdr socket during
  implementation (or add a `--no-resize` fallback note if RPC cwd is unsupported).
- Risk: existing pi panes created before the fix retain the wrong CWD. Mitigation:
  out of scope for this fix (only newly opened panes are affected); note in docs/comment.
- Risk (scope creep): do not refactor grid.py's growth algorithm or add cwd propagation to
  pre-existing panes. Keep the change surgical.
- `run-in-pane.sh` is NOT affected (always passes `--cwd` on the plain-split path).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Which herdr version is in use, and does `pane.split` RPC accept a cwd param?" —
  Answer (agent research): herdr 0.7.5; `herdr api schema --json` shows
  `PaneSplitParams.cwd: ["string", "null"]`. Source: `herdr api schema --json`, interactive
  research.
- Q: "Are `a+y` / `a+r` (audit approve/reject) affected?" — Answer (agent research): No —
  they are `!!wl` commands routed via `run-in-pane.sh`, which always passes `--cwd` on its
  plain-split path. Source: `src/shortcuts.json`, `scripts/run-in-pane.sh`.
- Q: "Does the Open Pi Agent action share the defect?" — Answer (agent research): Yes —
  `open-pi-agent.sh` has the same resize-mode grid path without cwd forwarding. Source:
  `shared/open-pi-agent.sh` line 121 vs line 130.

## Problem

The generic md viewer (OSL-0MSDYOVP6005T1X5, commit acc4246b) does not render episode `.podcast.md` files. Repro: open the worklist (`prefix+l`), open item **irish-folklore-fine-tuning (OSL-0MSG82DKE002LOYM)** — the detail view shows only the raw description; no `Episode file (md viewer)` section.

## Root cause (two stacked issues)

1. **Wrong base dir (ContextHub plugin):** `readKeyFile` in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` resolves Key Files paths against `process.cwd()`, which for herdr plugin panes is the plugin source dir (`/home/rgardler/projects/ContextHub/packages/herdr` — confirmed via `herdr pane list`: every "Work Items" pane has `cwd=.../packages/herdr`), NOT the worklog root. The code comment claims "the process CWD when the plugin runs in a pane" is the worklog root — that is false; the real root is in `HERDR_RESOLVED_CWD` (used by `configureWorklogTarget`).
2. **Data-side convention (open_source_llm):** even relative to the worklog root (`/home/rgardler/projects/open_source_llm`), the item key path `irish-folklore-fine-tuning/irish-folklore-fine-tuning.podcast.md` does not exist — the file is at `.llm-wiki/wiki/podcast/irish-folklore-fine-tuning/irish-folklore-fine-tuning.podcast.md`. The migration script `migrate_paragraph_format.py` (line 472/533) writes `Key Files:` paths relative to the podcast dir (`.llm-wiki/wiki/podcast`), while the documented convention (`docs/pipeline-metadata-format.md` §2.7) is relative to the wiki root.

Verified: `resolve(pluginCwd, keyPath)` -> false; `resolve(wlRoot, keyPath)` -> false; `resolve(wlRoot, ".llm-wiki/wiki/podcast/" + keyPath)` -> true.

## Proposed fix

- Plugin: resolve Key Files md paths against the resolved worklog root (`HERDR_RESOLVED_CWD` / `wlRoot`), not `process.cwd()`; consider fallback candidates (worklog root, `.llm-wiki/wiki/podcast/`) so existing podcast-relative paths work.
- Data (optional): fix `migrate_paragraph_format.py` relpath convention and/or existing episode item descriptions to root-relative paths.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Opening an episode item whose `Key Files:` points at an existing `.podcast.md` renders the md viewer section in the detail view.
- [ ] Path-resolution regression test (red before the fix): a Key Files `.md` path resolves against the resolved worklog root (`HERDR_RESOLVED_CWD` / `wlRoot`), and falls back to the `.llm-wiki/wiki/podcast/`-prefixed candidate when the root-relative path does not exist — covering the affected item's podcast-relative path.
- [ ] Existing chord/smart-selection/needsProducerReview behavior unchanged.
- [ ] Full plugin test suite passes (repo-root `npm test` = `vitest run`, covers `packages/herdr`) and `tsc` is clean.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — `readKeyFile` (line ~2597) resolves Key Files paths against `process.cwd()`; must resolve against the worklog root with fallback candidates. Also `formatDetailContent` (line ~923), `renderFileViewer` (line ~1020), `firstMarkdownKeyFile` (line ~1040).
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — `configureWorklogTarget` (line ~293) / `HERDR_RESOLVED_CWD` (line ~339) / `wlRoot`; the resolved root must be threaded into `runWorklistTui` options so `readKeyFile` can use it.
- `packages/herdr/src/md-viewer.ts` — `renderMarkdownViewer`, `renderNoteLinks` (md rendering helpers).
- `packages/herdr/src/md-viewer.test.ts` — existing Key Files md viewer tests (injected `readFile`); extend for root/fallback resolution regression.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` — TUI-level tests (chord/smart-selection/needsProducerReview guards; AC: unchanged behavior).
- External (open_source_llm worklog — NOT present on this machine, verify remotely): `.llm-wiki/wiki/podcast/irish-folklore-fine-tuning/irish-folklore-fine-tuning.podcast.md` (affected file), `migrate_paragraph_format.py` (relpath convention, lines ~472/533), `docs/pipeline-metadata-format.md` §2.7 (documented convention).

Related: WL-0MSGAEXER000707R (same class: plugin uses wrong CWD), OSL-0MSDYOVP6005T1X5 (md viewer feature), OSL-0MSG82DKE002LOYM (affected item).

## Plan: changelog

- 2026-08-07 ~00:44 UTC: Plan pre-check (`plan-if-needed`) → decision **skip** (Effort: Extra Small, Risk: Low — see auto-plan decision comment WL-C0MSI7OZ2S007O3YU). Six automated review stages run against existing content; no child decomposition created. Changes: added fallback-resolution AC and path-resolution regression-test AC (Stage 1); added `## Key Files` section, external OSL paths marked as not mounted locally (Stage 2); clarified test command to repo-root `npm test`/`vitest run` + `tsc` (Stage 5). No clarifying questions needed — the description already had measurable ACs and a concrete fix; the optional data-side fix (open_source_llm) is out of scope for the plugin fix and not verifiable on this machine (OPEN QUESTION for the producer: whether to also run the optional data-side fix on the open_source_llm side).
