# Tests: Related Docs row, detail ToC and open-in-viewer

## Summary

Unit tests for the `Related Docs` metadata row, the detail-view Table of Contents (ToC), and the open-in-viewer behavior described in WL-0MSGTLSUT002NF29. Written first (test-first, expected red), then made green by the sibling implementation features `Add Related Docs metadata row` and `Detail view ToC for Related Docs`.

## Expected behaviour under test

- `buildMetaRows` emits a `Related Docs` row listing every `.md` path from the item's `Key Files:` section in both the list-mode metadata panel (`formatMetadataPanel`) and the detail-view metadata table (`formatDetailContent`); the row is omitted when there are no `.md` Key Files.
- The detail view renders a ToC at the top listing the Related Docs with a focus indicator; arrow/j/k navigate; Enter renders the selected doc; navigating past the end of the ToC transfers focus to document scrolling; the ToC stays visible while the document scrolls.
- Opening a listed document renders that specific file's content (not just the first one); missing/unreadable files fail open; paths resolve against the resolved worklog root, never `process.cwd()` (regression coverage for WL-0MSGEA9AY0080V4Q).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `buildMetaRows` tests cover: `Related Docs` row lists every `.md` path from `Key Files:` (via `extractFilePaths` + `.md` filter), joined with the compact delimiter, in both `formatMetadataPanel` and `formatDetailContent` output.
2. Row omitted when the item has no `.md` files in `Key Files:` (or no `Key Files:` section at all) — asserted for both the metadata panel and the detail table.
3. Mixed `Key Files` lists (`.ts`/`.json`/`.md`): only `.md` paths appear in the `Related Docs` row; non-markdown paths are excluded.
4. Detail-view ToC tests: ToC at the top of the detail view lists all Related Docs; a focus indicator marks the selected entry; arrow keys and j/k move selection within the ToC; navigating past the last entry transfers focus to document scrolling and navigating up past the top returns focus to the ToC; the ToC remains visible while the viewed document scrolls.
5. Open-in-viewer tests: activating a ToC entry renders that specific file's content via `renderMarkdownViewer` (supersedes the auto-first-file render for the selected doc; auto-render of the first file remains the initial default); unreadable/missing files fail open without crashing; path resolution uses the resolved worklog root (`HERDR_RESOLVED_CWD` / `resolveKeyFilePath`) — a regression test asserting `process.cwd()` is never used.
6. All tests pass as part of the full project test suite once implementation lands (they may be red at creation time — test-first).

## Implementation approach

- Add/extend `describe` blocks in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` (and `grouping.test.ts` if an `extractMdPaths` helper is introduced).
- Reuse existing test fixtures (`makeItem`, `makeRichItem`) and the `TERM_80x24`/`panelHeight` helpers already used by the metadata-panel tests.
- Follow the existing pattern of asserting on joined output lines from `formatMetadataPanel`/`formatDetailContent`.

## Related work

- Parent: WL-0MSGTLSUT002NF29 (Herdr plugin: add Related Docs row to metadata section listing .md Key Files (openable in the markdown viewer))

# Detail view ToC for Related Docs

## Summary

The detail view gains a persistent Table of Contents (ToC) at the top listing the selected item's Related Docs (the `.md` Key Files surfaced by the `Related Docs` metadata row). Arrow keys and j/k navigate the ToC; Enter renders the selected document in the markdown viewer. The ToC stays visible on all renders; navigating past the end of the ToC moves focus to scrolling the viewed document, and navigating up past the top returns to the ToC.

## Expected behaviour

- Opening a detail view for an item with `.md` Key Files shows a ToC (e.g. numbered entries) at the top, with a focus indicator on the selected entry. The first `.md` file is rendered by default (existing auto-render behavior preserved).
- `↑`/`↓` and j/k move the ToC selection. Enter renders the selected document's content via `renderMarkdownViewer`.
- Below the last ToC entry, `↓`/j moves focus into the document scroll area (existing detail scroll keys apply there); `↑`/k at the top of the document returns focus to the ToC. The ToC remains pinned/visible while the document scrolls.
- Items with no `.md` Key Files render the detail view exactly as today (no ToC).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. When the item has at least one `.md` Key File, the detail view renders a ToC at the top listing every Related Doc with a focus indicator on the selected entry; no ToC is rendered when there are no `.md` Key Files.
2. Arrow keys (↑/↓) and j/k navigate the ToC entries; selection clamps to the list bounds.
3. Enter on a ToC entry renders that file's content in the markdown viewer via `renderMarkdownViewer` (supersedes the auto-first-file render for the selected doc; auto-render of the first file remains the initial default).
4. The ToC stays visible on all renders: while the viewed document scrolls, the ToC remains pinned at the top of the detail view.
5. Navigating past the last ToC entry transfers focus to document scrolling; navigating up past the top of the document returns focus to the ToC. Esc/back and `q` exit the detail view as they do today.
6. Path resolution uses the resolved worklog root via `readKeyFile`/`resolveKeyFilePath` (never `process.cwd()`); unreadable or missing files fail open (detail view falls back to the raw description, no crash).
7. Existing detail keys keep working in the appropriate focus mode (j/k scroll, g/G top/bottom, pgup/pgdn, esc/q); the detail scroll model is reconciled with the pinned ToC.

## Implementation approach

- Add ToC/focus state to the detail view (e.g. `detailToCIndex` / a focus-mode flag alongside `detailScrollOffset`); render the ToC as a pinned header in `formatDetailContent` (or a new helper) with the document region below it.
- Reuse `extractFilePaths` (or the new `extractMdPaths` from the row feature) to build the ToC entries, and `readKeyFile`/`resolveKeyFilePath` for rendering.
- Reconcile the existing single-scroll detail model: the ToC is pinned; the document area scrolls independently.
- Coordinate with `Tests: Related Docs row, detail ToC and open-in-viewer` for expected test names/behavior.

## Related work

- Parent: WL-0MSGTLSUT002NF29 (Herdr plugin: add Related Docs row to metadata section listing .md Key Files (openable in the markdown viewer))
- Prereqs: `Tests: Related Docs row, detail ToC and open-in-viewer`; `Add Related Docs metadata row`

Extend loadShortcutConfig() in packages/herdr/src/shortcut-config.ts to accept an optional worklog root and merge <worklog-root>/shortcuts.json over the bundled defaults with local-wins override semantics. Bundled defaults remain the base; no bundled entries change.

- Merge via a Map keyed by view+chord (bundled first, then local entries overwrite/add), preserving bundled order for untouched entries; output a deduplicated array.

# Intake Brief: Create `npm run install` routine for install steps and add `install:plugin` rule

## Problem statement

Install steps for the Worklog repo are currently scattered: the herdr plugin install (link plugin + insert `prefix+l` keybinding) runs automatically via the root `postbuild` hook on every `npm run build`, while the pi-extension install exists as a separate manual rule (`install:pi-extension`). There is no single, discoverable `npm run install` routine that performs all install steps, so developers cannot install all integrations with one command and the build doubles as an installer.

## Users

- **Developers installing the Worklog repo from source** who want a single `npm run install` command that performs all install steps (herdr plugin + pi extension), while `npm run build` keeps its current auto-install behaviour.
- **User story:** "As a developer working on the Worklog repo, when I run `npm run install`, I want the herdr plugin linked/keybound and the pi extension installed in one step, so I don't have to remember each install rule — while `npm run build` keeps working exactly as before."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Root `package.json` gains an `install` script that chains the install rules in order, e.g. `"install": "npm run install:plugin && npm run install:pi-extension"`.
2. Root `package.json` gains an `install:plugin` script invoking the existing install script, e.g. `"install:plugin": "bash ./scripts/install-herdr.sh"`.
3. The existing `postbuild` hook (`bash ./scripts/install-herdr.sh`) and the `install:pi-extension` rule are unchanged — `npm run build` still auto-installs the herdr plugin as today (user confirmed: keep).
4. `npm run install` completes successfully (exit 0) in an environment without `herdr` on PATH — the herdr step warns and continues, the pi-extension step completes (verified by running `npm run install` with herdr absent).
5. Re-running `npm run install` is idempotent — no duplicate keybindings and no duplicate links (existing `install-herdr.sh` and `install-pi-extension.sh` behaviour).
6. Unit tests cover the new script wiring — e.g. `tests/scripts/package-scripts.test.ts` reads root `package.json` and asserts `install` chains `install:plugin` then `install:pi-extension`, and `install:plugin` targets `scripts/install-herdr.sh` (matching the `tests/scripts/` convention).
7. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries (root `README.md` Pi agent plugin section and `packages/herdr/README.md` mention the `npm run install` routine as an alternative to `npm run build`).
8. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

> **Note:** CHANGELOG.md is **excluded** from this list. It is managed automatically by the ship skill's release pipeline. Do not include CI/CD pipeline tests.

## Constraints

- `install` is a reserved npm lifecycle script name: in addition to `npm run install`, it auto-runs during `npm install` / `npm ci` in the project (and during a global install of the package). Both chained rules are already safe in such contexts (herdr-missing → warn exit 0; pi-extension symlink creation is idempotent). Use `--ignore-scripts` to opt out of lifecycle auto-runs if ever needed.
- Keep `postbuild` and `install:pi-extension` unchanged (user Q1/Q3 answers) — the diff is additive for the new `install`/`install:plugin` rules.
- No changes to `scripts/install-herdr.sh` or `scripts/install-pi-extension.sh` themselves unless implementation finds otherwise.
- Do not clutter repo root with planning documents.

## Existing state

- `package.json` scripts: `"build": "npm run build:shared && tsc && node ./scripts/generate-version.cjs"`, `"postbuild": "bash ./scripts/install-herdr.sh"`, `"install:pi-extension": "bash ./scripts/install-pi-extension.sh"`.
- `scripts/install-herdr.sh` — idempotent herdr installer (links `worklog-selection-list` plugin, inserts/migrates the `prefix+l` keybinding, warns-not-fails when herdr is absent); invoked by `postbuild`.
- `scripts/install-pi-extension.sh` — creates the `~/.pi/agent/extensions/worklog` symlink; invoked by `install:pi-extension`.
- `README.md` § "Pi agent plugin" documents `npm run install:pi-extension`; `packages/herdr/README.md` § "From source (development)" documents auto-install via `npm run build`.
- No `install` script exists today; no tests reference the install rules.

## Desired change

1. **`package.json`** — add two scripts (additive; nothing removed):
   - `"install": "npm run install:plugin && npm run install:pi-extension"`
   - `"install:plugin": "bash ./scripts/install-herdr.sh"`
   - `postbuild` and `install:pi-extension` stay exactly as they are.
2. **Tests** — new test file (e.g. `tests/scripts/package-scripts.test.ts`) asserting the script definitions and the `install` chaining order, following the existing `tests/scripts/` convention.
3. **Docs** — mention the `npm run install` routine in root `README.md` (Pi agent plugin section) and `packages/herdr/README.md` (as an alternative to `npm run build` for the herdr install); keep existing instructions intact.

**Key Files:**

- `./package.json` — Add `install` and `install:plugin` scripts (postbuild/install:pi-extension unchanged).
- `tests/scripts/package-scripts.test.ts` — New tests asserting the install-rule wiring (location subject to confirmation during /plan, matching `tests/scripts/install-herdr.test.ts` / `install-pi-extension.test.ts` precedent).
- `README.md` — Pi agent plugin section: mention `npm run install` routine.
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — Installation section: mention `npm run install` as an alternative to `npm run build` for the herdr install.

## Related work

- WL-0MSHZR0J2000Q9SW — this item (seed: "Create npm run install routine … add install:plugin rule. Priority: high.").
- WL-0MSAPMGLS0034BTR — "Install script: insert herdr shortcut key into herdr config (runs on npm run build)" (completed): created `scripts/install-herdr.sh` and the `postbuild` wiring; context for the herdr install step this item consolidates.
- WL-0MSG6ODD5002X2OF — "Wire postbuild hook and update docs" (completed): added `"postbuild": "bash ./scripts/install-herdr.sh"`; docs updated there must be kept consistent.
- WL-0MSG6OA2K003GY27 — "Implement install-herdr.sh script" (completed): the script `install:plugin` will invoke.
- `scripts/install-pi-extension.sh` / `install:pi-extension` — existing install rule chained by the new `install` routine.
- README.md § "Pi agent plugin", packages/herdr/README.md § "From source (development)" — docs that reference the install rules.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk (lifecycle side-effect):** naming the routine `install` makes npm auto-run it on `npm install`/`npm ci` in the repo (and on global/local package installs), which will touch the user's herdr config and `~/.pi/agent/extensions`. Mitigation: both chained scripts are idempotent and warn-not-fail, so no failures; the behavior is intentional per the requested "npm run install" naming and is documented in the brief so it can be vetoed at review.
- **Risk:** `npm run install` runs `install:pi-extension` which writes a symlink under `$HOME/.pi`; in CI that is a harmless ephemeral side effect (verified: CI uses `npm ci`, herdr absent, both scripts exit 0).
- **Assumption:** `install` chains exactly the two existing rules in the order `install:plugin` then `install:pi-extension` (user Q2: "all").
- **Assumption:** `install:plugin` runs the existing `scripts/install-herdr.sh` (user Q3: "existing"); no new install logic.
- **Assumption:** `postbuild` stays as-is (user Q1: "keep") — `npm run build` keeps auto-installing the herdr plugin.
- **Scope-creep risk:** no changes to the install scripts themselves, no new install steps, no changes to build output — purely additive npm script wiring + tests + docs. Any additional install concerns should be separate work items.

### Related work (automated report)

Automated findings from find_related (WL-0MSHZR0J2000Q9SW): WL-0MQFB8N990056T8P (test-failure: controller-watch re-renders), WL-0MSB445R1004PM3I (Impl: idle-gated auto-refresh/auto-sync in browse widget), WL-0MKXTCQZM1O8YCNH (Core FTS Index) — all keyword matches on generic terms (build/install/add/plugin); weak relevance, informational only. Repo file matches were the draft itself and stale worktree copies of `packages/herdr/README.md`; full report persisted at `.worklog/tmp/find-related-full-WL-0MSHZR0J2000Q9SW.md`.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Should the `postbuild` hook (and thus the herdr install) be removed from `npm run build` so installs only run via the new `npm run install` (build stays pure), or should `npm run build` keep auto-installing as today?" — Answer (user): "keep" — keep the `postbuild` hook; `npm run build` continues to auto-install the herdr plugin. Source: interactive reply (2026-08-07).
- Q: "Should `npm run install` chain all install rules — i.e. `install:plugin` (herdr, from postbuild) plus `install:pi-extension` (existing rule) — or only the herdr/plugin install?" — Answer (user): "all" — `npm run install` chains all install rules: `install:plugin` then `install:pi-extension`. Source: interactive reply.
- Q: "Should `install:plugin` run the existing `install-herdr.sh` script (link plugin + insert keybinding), or is something else expected (e.g. a different plugin, or it should also cover the pi extension)?" — Answer (user): "existing" — `install:plugin` runs the existing `scripts/install-herdr.sh`. Source: interactive reply.
- OPEN QUESTION: none — the npm `install` lifecycle auto-run side-effect (runs on `npm ci`/`npm install`) is documented as a risk/assumption above; flag for user veto at review if unintended.

# Herdr selection list: sort by priority first, then stage (WL-0MSI1LVTJ001M9EY)

## Problem statement

The work item selection list in the Herdr Worklog plugin does not put priority first: a high-priority `in_progress` item lands in the "Other" section while a medium-priority `plan_complete` item sits in an earlier "Group N" section, so the most important work is not at the top. The list should be sorted by priority first, then by stage.

## Users

- **Herdr users** (human and AI agents) who browse the work item selection list and expect the highest-priority work to appear first.

### User stories

- As a Herdr user, I want the highest-priority work items to appear at the top of the selection list, so I can see what matters most without scanning.
- As a Herdr user, I want items of equal priority ordered by their workflow stage, so the list stays predictable and mirrors the work item's recorded lifecycle.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Priority is the primary sort key.** Items in the selection list sort by priority in descending order: `critical` → `high` → `medium` → `low` (matching the existing priority ranking `critical=4 > high=3 > medium=2 > low=1` in `src/commands/helpers.ts`). Items with unknown/empty priority sort as `medium` (existing `DEFAULT_PRIORITY` convention).
2. **Stage is the secondary sort key.** Within the same priority, items sort by stage in the order recorded in the work item record / default config (`src/config.ts`): `idea` → `intake_complete` → `plan_complete` → `in_progress` → `in_review` → `done`. Unknown stages sort after known ones. Item `id` is the deterministic tie-break.
3. **Section headers follow priority order.** The existing group-header rendering (`── <label> ──`) is preserved, with one section per priority bucket ordered Critical → High → Medium → Low. No stage sub-headers are rendered (within-bucket stage order is implicit, matching current behavior).
4. **Applies to all rendered lists.** The ordering applies to every list rendered by the plugin: the default worklist, stage-filtered views (e.g. `/wl idea`, `/wl in_review`), expanded child lists, and search results when rendered in-TUI. Implementation may reuse one shared comparator across list types.
5. **Smart-selection guarantee preserved.** All critical items and all `completed`/`in_review` items remain always visible regardless of the `browseItemCount` setting (WL-0MS8W5LTW006YZ4B).
6. **Tests.** Unit tests in `packages/herdr/src/grouping.test.ts` (plus any grouping-order assertions in `worklist.test.ts` and `md-viewer.test.ts`) cover the new priority→stage ordering, including unknown priority/stage fallbacks and the smart-selection merge path.
7. **Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, the plugin README's "Stage grouping" feature description, and any relevant docs site entries.
8. **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Scope is the **Herdr plugin selection list only**. Do not change the `wl` CLI ordering, the core grouping in `src/commands/grouping.ts`, or the Pi TUI extension's mirrored copy (`packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/grouping.ts`) unless explicitly requested. The mirrored copies must remain in sync for whatever is changed (the Herdr copy is intentionally duplicated with zero npm deps — decision Q2c in WL-0MS8W5LTW006YZ4B).
- The plugin keeps using the existing `wl` CLI as its data source; no new fetch paths or `wl` flags are introduced.
- `stage=done` items remain excluded from the default list (WL-0MS94VAII00054L9); child items remain hidden from top-level lists (WL-0MS964SIA0057ABR).
- No new UI features (search-as-a-list, new filters) are introduced by this work item.

## Existing state

- The Herdr worklist fetches via `fetchNextItems(count)` (`packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts`): `wl next -n N --include-in-progress` merged with mandatory subsets (`wl list --priority critical`, `wl list --status completed --stage in_review`), then `selectWorkItems` (critical → reviews → others) and `regroupWorkItems`.
- `regroupWorkItems` (`packages/herdr/src/grouping.ts`) calls `assignItemGroups`, which currently produces groups in this order: **Critical Group N** (critical, file-path partitioned) → **Group N** (plan_complete + intake_complete, file-path partitioned) → **Idea** → **Other** → **In Review** (last). Within a group, `compareGroupableItems` sorts by stage sub-order (plan_complete → intake_complete → remaining) then priority (high → medium → low) then id.
- Net effect today: a high-priority `in_progress` item is in the "Other" section (4th), while a medium-priority `plan_complete` item is in "Group N" (2nd) — priority is not the primary ordering.
- Stage filters (`/wl <stage>`, worklist.ts) filter the fetched list client-side, so they inherit whatever order the fetched list has. The `s` key inserts a `!!wl search <search_term>` command dispatched to an external pane; there is no in-TUI search results list today.

## Desired change

- Rework `assignItemGroups` / `regroupWorkItems` / `compareGroupableItems` in `packages/herdr/src/grouping.ts` so the group order is priority-first: one section per priority bucket (Critical → High → Medium → Low), and within each bucket items sort by stage (workflow order: idea → intake_complete → plan_complete → in_progress → in_review → done) then id.
- `selectWorkItems` in `packages/herdr/src/smart-selection.ts` keeps its always-show guarantee; its pre-group ordering is superseded by the regroup ordering, so it can be simplified to a stable sort if convenient.
- Because the sort lives at the display-prep step (regrouping), stage-filtered views and any other rendered list inherit it automatically.
- Update the grouping tests and README "Stage grouping" description to match.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/grouping.ts` — Rework `assignItemGroups` (priority-bucket group order), `compareGroupableItems` (priority → stage → id), and `regroupWorkItems` (unchanged contract, new ordering).
- `packages/herdr/src/smart-selection.ts` — Preserve the mandatory-set guarantee; adjust ordering contract only as needed.
- `packages/herdr/src/grouping.test.ts` — Update/expand tests for group order, within-group stage order, and unknown priority/stage fallbacks.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` — Update any assertions that depend on group labels/order in rendered lists.
- `packages/herdr/src/md-viewer.test.ts` — Update `regroupWorkItems` assertions if affected.
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — Update the "Stage grouping" feature description to reflect priority-first ordering.

## Related work

- **Create a work item selection list in Herdr (WL-0MS1W8Y1L0059AKP)** [completed] — Parent feature that introduced the selection list this change modifies.
- **Selection list must always show all completed/in_review and critical items regardless of browseItemCount setting (WL-0MS8W5LTW006YZ4B)** [completed] — Defines the smart-selection guarantee (AC 5) and the per-TUI duplication decision.
- **Rewrite assignItemGroups + next.ts ordering (WL-0MSAKPVR9005B6XJ)** [completed] — Authored the current group ordering algorithm this work item reorders.
- **Herdr plugin: fix work item list grouping (duplicate In Review sections, wrong group order) (WL-0MSAK8YLB0025EGW)** [completed] — Introduced `regroupWorkItems`/`assignItemGroups`; the group-order logic this change reorders.
- **Exclude stage=done items from default selection lists (both TUIs) (WL-0MS94VAII00054L9)** [completed] — The done-exclusion this change must preserve.
- **Hide child work items from top-level selection lists (Pi and Herdr) (WL-0MS964SIA0057ABR)** [completed] — Root-only behavior this change must preserve.
- **Show plugin version in Herdr work item selection list (WL-0MSGKEBFU004T3N3)** [open] — Another open change to the same selection list; coordinate to avoid merge conflicts in `worklist.ts`/tests.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption: "sort-order in the work item record"** (user's answer to the stage-order question) means the canonical stage order recorded in the work item config: `idea` → `intake_complete` → `plan_complete` → `in_progress` → `in_review` → `done` (`src/config.ts` defaults).
- **Assumption: smart-selection guarantee stays** (confirmed with the user; AC 5).
- **Assumption: no in-TUI search list exists today** — search is dispatched via `!!wl search <term>`; AC 4 covers "when rendered in-TUI" so future search rendering inherits the sort.
- **Risk: file-path conflict partitioning may be dropped.** The current "Critical Group N" / "Group N" labels partition by file-path conflicts (groups items touching the same files for agent sessions). Priority-bucket sections may drop this partitioning. Preserve the partitioning within buckets if it is still wanted; otherwise document the removal. Flag for implementer review.
- **Risk: algorithm duplication.** `grouping.ts` logic is mirrored in `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/grouping.ts` and `src/commands/grouping.ts`. Changing only the Herdr copy creates divergence; a follow-up to align the Pi TUI list is a candidate separate work item (scope-creep guard).
- **Scope-creep guard:** Do not change `wl` CLI ordering, add new `wl` flags, or add new plugin UI features. Record extra opportunities as linked work items rather than expanding scope.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Which selection lists should get the new sort? (A) Default worklist only, (B) Default + stage-filtered, (C) All lists including search results" — Answer (user): **C — All lists including search results**. Source: interactive reply. Note: search is currently dispatched externally (`!!wl search <term>`), so in practice this means the default worklist, stage-filtered views, and any list the plugin renders (search results if rendered in-TUI later). AC 4 captures this.
- Q2: "Within the same priority, what order should stages appear? (A) Workflow order, (B) Most-advanced-first, (C) No preference" — Answer (user): **"sort-order in the work item record"**. Research: the canonical stage order recorded in the work item record defaults (`src/config.ts` stages) is `idea` → `intake_complete` → `plan_complete` → `in_progress` → `in_review` → `done`. Final accepted answer: workflow order as recorded in the record (AC 2).
- Q3: "With priority-first sorting, should the list (A) keep section headers reordered into priority buckets, (B) drop group headers for a flat list, (C) keep current group structure and only fix within-group sort?" — Answer (user): **A — keep section headers, priority buckets first** (Critical → High → Medium → Low sections). Source: interactive reply. AC 3.
- Follow-up (assumption stated, no objection): "the smart-selection guarantee (critical + completed/in_review always shown) should be preserved" — Answer: no objection; captured as AC 5.
- Note: `find-related` was run (WL-0MSI1LVTJ001M9EY). Its automated report returned mostly false positives: its repo-file scan resolved to the wrong repository (SorraAgents `skill/audit/...` and tmp files) and the three ranked items are unrelated (a TUI test-failure, a Local Proxy lease item, and a Pi TUI filter bug). None were added to the curated Related work section per the conservative policy; the curated section above is authoritative.

# Detail view ToC overflows pane — first lines scroll off the top of the screen

## Problem statement

In the Herdr plugin's work-item detail view, when an item has a `Related Docs` Table of Contents (ToC) (i.e. ≥1 `.md` Key File), the rendered output exceeds the pane height: the header (id/title) and the first ToC lines scroll off the top of the screen, so the ToC is not entirely visible. The ToC is also rendered twice and the item header is dropped entirely.

## Users

- **Herdr users** viewing a work item's detail view in the plugin pane, who need the item header and the full `Related Docs` ToC visible at the top of the pane while the metadata/description/document body scrolls beneath.

### Example User Stories

- As a Herdr user, I want to see the item id, title, and the complete Related Docs ToC when I open a work item's detail view, so nothing important is cut off at the top of the screen.
- As a Herdr user, I want the ToC to stay pinned while I scroll the document, so I can always see which documents are linked to the item.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. When an item has a ToC (≥1 `.md` Key File), the detail view shows the header (id, title, separator) and the **full** ToC at the top of the pane at scroll 0 — no lines cut off. The ToC is rendered **exactly once** (no duplication), and the item header is present.
2. Detail-view output never exceeds the pane: `formatDetailView` returns at most `viewportHeight` lines, and the full renderer (`createListRenderer` detail mode) returns at most `rows - 1` lines — the line-count invariant from WL-0MSAAON63003N6LO holds for detail mode with a ToC present.
3. The header + ToC block stays **pinned** at the top while the body (metadata table, description, md viewer) scrolls beneath it; scrolling is limited to the body region (viewport height minus the pinned block height), and `WorkItemListState.detailScrollDown` clamps against the same reduced body viewport. No dead/blank region at the bottom when fully scrolled.
4. Items **without** `.md` Key Files (no ToC) keep the existing full-scroll behavior unchanged (regression check — no behavior change for the no-ToC path).
5. Unit tests in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` cover: line-count invariant for detail mode with ToC (renderer ≤ `rows - 1`; `formatDetailView` ≤ `viewportHeight`), header + ToC fully visible at scroll 0, ToC not duplicated, pinned-ToC scroll regression (existing `'keeps the ToC pinned at the top while the document scrolls'` test kept green/updated), and no-ToC behavior unchanged.
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments and any relevant README/docs entries describing the detail-view ToC layout (`packages/herdr/README.md`).
7. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

> **Note:** CHANGELOG.md is excluded from this list — it is managed automatically by the ship skill's release pipeline.

## Constraints

- Preserve the pinned-ToC design from WL-0MSHWHULZ001FL8I / WL-0MSGTLSUT002NF29: the ToC stays visible on all renders; only the body below it scrolls.
- Respect the line-count invariant established in WL-0MSAAON63003N6LO: the renderer must never emit more than `rows - 1` lines, otherwise the terminal scrolls the top of the output off the pane.
- Surgical change: do not alter scrolling behavior for items without a ToC (the pre-existing full-scroll path).
- No new dependencies; reuse the existing `formatDetailToC` / `formatDetailContent` helpers.

## Existing state

- `formatDetailView` (`packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`, ~line 1223) builds the detail output as `[...tocLines, ...bodyLines.slice(safeOffset, safeOffset + viewportHeight)]` where `bodyLines = allLines.slice(tocLines.length)`.
- The slicing assumes the ToC occupies the first `tocLines.length` lines of `allLines`, but `formatDetailContent` emits the header first (blank, id, title, separator = 4 lines) and the ToC **after** it. Consequences (verified by reproduction): (a) the header is dropped from the output, (b) the ToC is duplicated (once from `tocLines`, once inside `bodyLines`), (c) total output = `viewportHeight + tocLines.length` lines, which overflows the pane (`viewportHeight = rows - 1` in the renderer). Reproduction: `formatDetailView(item, 80, 0, 20)` with a 2-entry ToC returns 26 lines; the renderer on a 24-row terminal emits 29 lines (max allowed 23).
- Regression introduced in commit `76a52c9f` (WL-0MSHWHULZ001FL8I, "Implementation complete").
- `WorkItemListState.detailScrollDown` (~line 496) computes `maxScroll` against the full `viewportHeight` instead of the body region, so clamping is also wrong for the pinned layout.
- The existing test `'keeps the ToC pinned at the top while the document scrolls'` only asserts the ToC appears in the first 8 lines — it never checks the total line count, so it passes despite the overflow.

## Desired change

1. In `formatDetailView`, compute a **pinned block** = header (4 lines: blank, id, title, separator) + `tocLines`; the scrollable **body** = `allLines.slice(pinnedHeight)`; the **body viewport** = `max(1, viewportHeight - pinnedHeight)`; `maxScroll = max(0, bodyLines.length - bodyViewport)`. Render `[...pinned, ...bodyLines.slice(safeOffset, safeOffset + bodyViewport)]` and update the scroll-indicator percentage math to use `bodyViewport`.
2. Keep the no-ToC path (`tocLines.length === 0`) identical to the pre-ToC behavior (whole content scrolls, header included) to avoid scope creep.
3. Update `WorkItemListState.detailScrollDown` to clamp against the reduced body viewport (subtract the pinned height) so `j`/`G` behave consistently with the renderer.
4. Optionally introduce a named constant (e.g. `DETAIL_HEADER_LINES = 4`) documenting the fixed header shape so the slicing is self-explanatory.
5. Add/extend unit tests per AC5; update `packages/herdr/README.md` if it describes the detail-view layout.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — `formatDetailView` pinned header+ToC slicing and body-viewport math; `WorkItemListState.detailScrollDown` clamp; optional header-lines constant.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` — line-count invariant tests for detail mode with ToC, header/ToC visibility at scroll 0, no-duplication check, no-ToC regression, updated pinned-ToC test.
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — document the pinned header + ToC detail-view layout if it describes the ToC behavior.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Header-shape fragility:** the fix relies on the header being exactly 4 lines (blank, id, title, separator). Mitigate by introducing a named `DETAIL_HEADER_LINES` constant next to `formatDetailContent` and by an AC1 test asserting the header is visible at scroll 0.
- **No-ToC regression:** altering `formatDetailView` slicing could accidentally change the full-scroll path for items without `.md` Key Files. Mitigate with AC4 regression test asserting the no-ToC path is unchanged.
- **Viewport-height mismatch:** the state class uses `rows - 4` while the renderer uses `rows - 1`; today the renderer's clamp absorbs the difference. The fix must subtract the pinned height consistently in both `formatDetailView` and `detailScrollDown` so `j`/`G` and the on-screen clamp agree.
- **Scope creep:** pinning the header for ALL items (even without a ToC) is deliberately out of scope — it is a UX change beyond the reported bug. Recorded as an assumption; can be tracked as a separate work item if desired.
- **Assumption:** the fix pins header + ToC together (the header sits above the ToC in the content stream, so pinning the ToC keeps the header visible) and scrolls only the body (metadata/description/md viewer) beneath — faithful to the pinned-ToC design intent (WL-0MSGTLSUT002NF29 AC3) and the user's expectation that the first lines be visible.

## Related work

- `WL-0MSHWHULZ001FL8I` (completed) — "Herdr: detail-view ToC for Related Docs (arrow/j/k navigate, Enter renders)" — the pinned-ToC implementation that introduced this regression (commit `76a52c9f`).
- `WL-0MSGTLSUT002NF29` (completed) — "Herdr plugin: add Related Docs row to metadata section listing .md Key Files (openable in the markdown viewer)" — defines the pinned-ToC design intent.
- `WL-0MSAAON63003N6LO` (completed) — "Herdr: pane line-count invariant (rows - 1)" — the invariant the detail view now violates.
- `WL-0MS31WX9C008FIQR` (completed) — "Full scrollable detail view" — original detail-view scrolling design (whole content scrolls).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No interview questions were required for this intake.

- The seed report ("The table of contents on the detail view of work items is not entirely visible — the first few lines are off the top of the screen") combined with repository analysis was conclusive: the root cause was located by inspection of `formatDetailView`/`formatDetailContent` in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`, confirmed by a reproduction test (26 lines emitted for a 20-line viewport; 29 lines for a 24-row terminal vs. the 23-line invariant), and pinned to the regression commit `76a52c9f` (WL-0MSHWHULZ001FL8I) via `git log -S`.
- Assumption (documented, user can override): the fix pins the **header + ToC** block at the top of the detail view (the header is above the ToC in the content stream, so pinning the ToC necessarily keeps the header visible) while the body scrolls beneath — this is the faithful reading of the pinned-ToC design intent in WL-0MSGTLSUT002NF29 AC3 ("The ToC stays visible on all renders") and the user's expectation that the first lines be visible.
- Assumption (documented, user can override): items **without** `.md` Key Files keep the existing full-scroll behavior unchanged (surgical scope).

---

### Related work items

- **WL-0MRMCO4WX0073W30** – Arbitrary-depth chords in detail view (completed)

# Intake Brief — Herdr downtime worker: find work items in the tab's working directory; 60-min pause when none found

## Problem statement

The Herdr downtime worker (local-LLM idle dispatch) selects its next work item via `wl next --stage intake_complete|idea`, but those calls run **without** the `--worklog-dir` override the worklist uses, so they always resolve against the plugin process's own cwd (ContextHub) instead of the folder the user is currently working in (e.g. SorraAgents). As a result, downtime dispatch only ever picks items from the ContextHub backlog, even when the Herdr tab is browsing another project. Additionally, when no suitable items exist, the worker keeps polling and attempting dispatch on every idle period — the user wants it to stop looking for downtime entirely for 60 minutes.

## Users

- **Developer working on multiple projects** (e.g. SorraAgents, ContextHub): Opens a Herdr worklist tab in a project other than ContextHub, and wants the automatic downtime worker to fill idle LLM time from *that* project's backlog — not ContextHub's.
- **Developer with an empty/finished backlog**: When the current project has no suitable work items, wants the worker to stop burning cycles (proxy polling + `wl next` spawns) and back off for 60 minutes instead of retrying every idle period.

**User stories:**
- As a developer with a Herdr tab open in `/projects/SorraAgents`, I want downtime dispatch to select items from SorraAgents' worklog, so the idle LLM works on the project I'm actually in.
- As a developer whose current project has no work items available, I want the downtime worker to pause for 60 minutes, so it doesn't repeatedly query the proxy and spawn `wl` processes for an hour.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The downtime worker's `wl next --stage intake_complete|idea` selection resolves against the **same worklog root the worklist uses** (the tab's `HERDR_RESOLVED_CWD`-resolved root, via the existing `--worklog-dir` override). Verified by a test that asserts `--worklog-dir` is passed to `wl next` when the override is set, and by the live behavior: a SorraAgents tab dispatches an `SA-…` item, never a `WL-…` item.
- [ ] The downtime dispatch audit trail (`wl comment add` in `recordDispatch`) also targets the resolved worklog root (same `--worklog-dir` fix), so the auto-dispatch comment lands on the item in its own project's DB (currently it silently fails for non-ContextHub items).
- [ ] When both `wl next --stage intake_complete` and `wl next --stage idea` return no candidate, the worker enters a **60-minute cooldown (new setting, default 3,600,000 ms)** during which `tick()` performs no proxy polling, no idle tracking, and no dispatch. Cooldown is triggered only by a genuine "no candidate" outcome — never by transient `wl` errors (which continue to fail closed to "busy") or by an in-flight dispatch guard.
- [ ] After the cooldown expires, the worker resumes polling; the idle tracker requires a fresh full idle period before the next dispatch (no stale idle credit from before the pause).
- [ ] The new setting is clamped and persisted with the other downtime settings; a live settings change takes effect on the next tick (settings re-read each tick, matching existing behavior).
- [ ] The worklist header no longer shows a stale `[⏳ downtime idle m:ss]` during the pause; it reflects the paused state (e.g. `[downtime paused]`) so the UI is honest about the worker not looking.
- [ ] Unit tests cover: cooldown entry/exit, no poll during cooldown, no cooldown on transient error or in-flight guard, clamp behavior, `--worklog-dir` forwarding on `wl next` and `wl comment add`, and the header paused render.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments and the plugin docs/settings reference (e.g. `packages/herdr/shared/README.md`) — the new `downtimeNoCandidateCooldownMs` setting must be documented.
- [ ] Full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Must not change the worklist's own (working) worklog-root resolution — only the downtime worker's `wl` invocations.
- Must not modify files outside the ContextHub repository (`.pi/`, `skill/`, etc.).
- Fail-closed behavior must be preserved: every boundary (wl failure, proxy timeout, audit failure) must never throw or crash the worker.
- Follow the existing test-first/injectable-seam patterns in `packages/herdr/src` (fixtures, `setExecFileAsync`, injected `DowntimeSpawn`).
- The 60-minute value is a default, not a hardcoded constant — it must be a new setting with a sane floor so the pause cannot be accidentally disabled or set trivially small.

## Existing state

- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — `main()` resolves the tab's worklog root via `configureWorklogTarget(resolvedCwd)` and installs the `--worklog-dir` override with `setWorklogDir()`. The worklist's `fetchNextItems()` runs `wl` through `runWl()` which prepends `--worklog-dir`, so the list is correct.
- `createDowntimeDeps.getNextItem()` bypasses that seam: it calls `getExecFileAsync()('wl', ['next', '--stage', stage, '--json'])` directly — no `--worklog-dir` — so `wl next` resolves against the plugin process cwd (ContextHub). Verified live: from ContextHub cwd `wl next --stage intake_complete` returns `WL-0MSGI7UIH008USVB`; with `--worklog-dir /home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents/.worklog` it returns `SA-0MSI51QTA009WDFO`.
- `recordDispatch` (audit comment) has the same gap: `wl comment add` without `--worklog-dir` fails silently for non-ContextHub items (the `catch` swallows it, so the durable trail is lost).
- `claimItem` is already correct — it routes through `claimWorkItem()` → `runWl()` which applies the override.
- `createDowntimeWorker.tick()` currently: poll → evaluate idle → track → (threshold met) → dispatch; a `no-candidate` outcome just returns `{ dispatched: false, reason: 'no-candidate' }` and the next idle period retries. There is no cooldown/backoff state.
- Header status (`renderDowntimeStatus` in `worklist.ts`) renders from `worker.dispatching / enabled / idleSince`; during a full pause `idleSince` would be stale and the header would misreport "idle m:ss".

## Desired change

1. **Worklog-root routing (bug fix):** Route the downtime worker's `wl next` and `wl comment add` invocations through the same `--worklog-dir` override as the worklist (e.g. reuse the fetcher seam or prepend `--worklog-dir` from `getWorklogDir()`). Dispatch then selects and audits items from the folder the user is working in.
2. **60-minute cooldown (feature):** Add setting `downtimeNoCandidateCooldownMs` (default `3_600_000`; clamp with a floor, e.g. 60,000 ms). In `createDowntimeWorker`, when `dispatchDowntimeWork` returns `no-candidate`, set a `cooldownUntil` timestamp; while `now < cooldownUntil`, `tick()` returns immediately (no poll, no track, no dispatch). On cooldown entry, reset the idle tracker so a fresh full idle period is required after the pause. Expose the paused state on the worker so the header can render it.
3. **Tests + docs:** Unit tests for cooldown and `--worklog-dir` forwarding; update the header renderer and its tests; document the new setting.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — cooldown state (`cooldownUntil`) in `createDowntimeWorker`; early-return in `tick()`; reset idle tracker on pause; `clampDowntimeNoCandidateCooldownMs` + `DEFAULT_DOWNTIME_NO_CANDIDATE_COOLDOWN_MS`.
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — expose the `--worklog-dir`-aware `wl` seam (e.g. a small `runWl`/`buildWlArgs` helper) so `index.ts` can reuse it.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — `createDowntimeDeps.getNextItem()` and `recordDispatch()` use the seam / `getWorklogDir()` so `wl next` and `wl comment add` target the resolved root.
- `packages/herdr/src/settings.ts` — new `downtimeNoCandidateCooldownMs` key + default + clamp wiring.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — `renderDowntimeStatus` paused branch (e.g. `[downtime paused]`).
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts` / `index.test.ts` / `settings.test.ts` / `worklist.test.ts` — new tests (cooldown lifecycle, no-cooldown-on-error, clamp, `--worklog-dir` forwarding, header paused render).
- Docs: `packages/herdr/shared/README.md` or plugin docs for the new setting.

## Related work

- **WL-0MS6AU1PI0076GYB** (completed) — "Herdr plugin should operate from Herdr tab working directory, not ContextHub": fixed the worklist's cwd resolution (`HERDR_RESOLVED_CWD`, `resolveWorklogRoot`, `setWorklogDir`); the downtime worker was not covered by that fix — this item completes the gap.
- **WL-0MS6LOUP5003GWNE** (completed) — SPIKE on how Herdr communicates tab cwd to plugins; evidence base for `HERDR_RESOLVED_CWD`.
- **WL-0MSF49FMW009M06K** (completed) — "Herdr to consume local LLM in downtime": parent of the downtime worker itself (contract + wiring).
- **WL-0MSG7P9N8009PCKG** (open) — "Same-slot idle tracking for herdr downtime worker (per slot_id)": separate follow-up on per-slot identity; not blocking this item, but touches the same worker.
- **WL-0MSAZQEQB008O7H3** (in-progress) — "Central cache for wl read results to cut Herdr refresh spawn churn": the cooldown complements this by cutting `wl next` spawn churn during empty-backlog periods.

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Risk:** Changing `getNextItem` to always pass `--worklog-dir` could break a setup where the override is unset — mitigated: the seam only prepends the flag when the override exists (current behavior preserved otherwise).
- **Risk:** A too-long cooldown (user-configured) could starve the LLM of work after a project's backlog fills back up — mitigated by making it a setting with a documented default; the 60-min default matches the request.
- **Risk (scope creep):** Surfacing a richer paused-state UI (countdown, per-project status) is out of scope; only a minimal honest header label is included. Additional polish can be separate work items.
- **Assumption:** One plugin instance per Herdr tab/pane, so a per-worker cooldown is naturally per-project — no cross-tab coordination needed.
- **Assumption:** "No suitable items" == both `wl next --stage intake_complete` and `wl next --stage idea` return no candidate (the worker's existing selection semantics). The cooldown does NOT trigger on transient `wl`/CLI errors or proxy failures (user confirmed: "genuine only").
- **Assumption:** Cooldown = full pause (user confirmed: "pause completely") — no proxy polling or idle tracking during the 60 minutes.

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions & Answers

- Q: "When no suitable items are found, should the worker pause completely for 60 minutes (no proxy idle polling, no idle tracking — a full stop), or keep monitoring LLM idle state and only skip the work-item lookup during the cooldown?" — Answer (user): "pause completely". Source: interactive reply (intake round 1).
- Q: "Should the 60-minute pause be a fixed constant, or a new downtime setting (like the existing downtimePollIntervalMs / downtimeIdleThresholdMs), defaulting to 60 minutes?" — Answer (user): "new setting". Source: interactive reply (intake round 1).
- Q: "Should the 60-minute pause apply only when the lookup genuinely returns no suitable items (both intake_complete and idea empty), or also on transient wl CLI errors (which currently fail closed to 'no dispatch')?" — Answer (user): "genuine only". Source: interactive reply (intake round 1).

Source: intake analysis of `createDowntimeDeps` (packages/herdr/src/index.ts) + live `wl next` verification from both cwds.

# Allow /skill:audit on complete/in_review items without a valid audit

## Problem statement

The herdr downtime worker (`dispatchDowntimeWork` in `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts`) currently dispatches only two kinds of work during local-LLM idle time: `/skill:plan` on `intake_complete` items and `/skill:intake` on `idea` items. It never dispatches `/skill:audit` on `completed`/`in_review` items, so items sitting in the producer-review queue without a valid audit are never audited during downtime — despite the queue being the release gate (items are closed only after a valid audit shows "Ready to close: Yes").

## Users

- **Worklog operators / producers** — anyone who wants completed/in_review items automatically audited during local-LLM downtime so the review queue is drained and release readiness is known.
  - *User story:* "When my local LLM is idle, I want herdr to audit my completed/in_review items that lack a valid audit, so I don't have to manually run `/skill:audit` on each one."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. When the downtime worker is idle (per existing idle-detection), the first dispatch attempt targets a `completed`/`in_review` item **without a valid audit** — priority: audit tier before the existing plan/intake tiers.
2. "Valid audit" is defined by the herdr review-icon algorithm: the audit is *current* — i.e. the review icon is NOT the hourglass (⏳ stale passed) and NOT the magnifying glass (🔍 no audit / stale failed). Concretely: `isAuditFresh(auditedAt, updatedAt)` returns `true` (auditedAt within the 60s staleness buffer of updatedAt).
3. The dispatched pane runs `/skill:audit <item-id>` (visible pane, `--no-focus`, named e.g. `Downtime audit`), following the existing `buildDowntimePaneArgs`/`spawnDowntimePane` pattern; the audit result persists via the audit skill's own lifecycle (no dispatch-side status changes needed beyond the existing claim pattern).
4. When no audit candidate exists, the worker falls back to the existing plan (`intake_complete`) then intake (`idea`) tiers, unchanged.
5. Dispatch audit trail: successful audit dispatches are recorded like other downtime dispatches (item comment + rolling `.worklog` downtime log) with kind `audit`.
6. Selection is deterministic and single-flight: at most one dispatch per idle period (existing tracker/`dispatchInFlight` behaviour); candidates are selected by sortIndex order like the heartbeat skill.
7. Tests cover: candidate selection (valid vs invalid audit), freshness boundary (60s buffer), audit-tier priority, fallback order, no-candidate handling, and dispatch audit logging.
8. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes (code comments, README, and any relevant docs; CHANGELOG.md is managed by the ship skill and excluded).
9. Full project test suite passes with the new changes (pytest + Node, quiet mode).

## Constraints

- The downtime worker lives in the **Herdr plugin** (`packages/herdr/`); changes must follow the existing injectable-deps, fail-closed, single-flight patterns in `downtime-worker.ts`.
- Selection must reuse the existing `isAuditFresh` (or equivalent) freshness logic already present in `packages/herdr/src/icons.ts` — do not introduce a competing "valid audit" definition.
- Do NOT change the audit skill's freshness gate (`_check_audit_freshness` in SorraAgents) as part of this work — the dispatcher must select items whose audit is genuinely stale/missing so the runner's own gate falls through. (If a dispatched audit still hits "Skipping: audit still fresh", that's a separate issue to track.)
- The herdr review-icon algorithm (⏳/🔍) is the source of truth for "valid audit" — matches Q1 answer.

## Existing state

- `dispatchDowntimeWork` (packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts) selects: (1) `wl next --stage intake_complete` → `/skill:plan <id>`, (2) fallback `wl next --stage idea` → `/skill:intake <id>`, else no dispatch. **No audit tier exists.**
- `getIconPrefix` (packages/herdr/src/icons.ts): for `in_review` items, fresh audit → ✅/❌/❓ based on `auditResult`; stale audit → ⏳ (if passed) or 🔍 (stage icon) — the 🔍/⏳ state is exactly "no valid audit".
- Heartbeat skill (`.pi/skills/heartbeat/scripts/heartbeat.py`) audits completed/in_review items lacking "Ready to close: Yes" — but only when queue ≥ 10 items and only via one-off `/skill:heartbeat` invocations; sparse queues never audit, and fresh-but-failed audits get skipped by the runner's freshness gate.
- `wl list --status completed --stage in_review --json` returns auditResult/auditedAt/updatedAt (verified: 50 items today, 43 without audit).
- Audit runner (`_check_audit_freshness` in SorraAgents skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py): skips when `auditedAt > updatedAt + 60s`; otherwise runs a full audit. Items selected by the new tier (stale/missing audit) fall through this gate.

## Desired change

Add a third dispatch tier to the herdr downtime worker, **before** the existing plan/intake tiers:

1. Query completed/in_review items: `wl list --status completed --stage in_review --json`.
2. Filter to items without a valid audit: `!isAuditFresh(auditedAt, updatedAt)`.
3. Sort by `sortIndex` (like the heartbeat), take the first.
4. Claim the item (existing `claimItem` pattern) and spawn a pane running `/skill:audit <id>` via `buildDowntimePrompt('audit', candidate)` / `buildDowntimePaneArgs('audit', ...)`.
5. Extend `DowntimeSkillKind`/`DowntimeStage` types with `'audit'`, update `skillKindFromPrompt`, `buildDowntimePrompt`, pane naming, and the downtime-log event kind.
6. If no audit candidate: fall through to existing plan → intake tiers (unchanged).
7. Wire the new selection into `createDowntimeWorker` tick flow (same idle → dispatch path).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Freshness-gate interaction (assumption):** items selected by the new tier (stale/missing audit) fall through the audit runner's `_check_audit_freshness` gate (which only skips when `auditedAt > updatedAt + 60s`). If a dispatched audit still reports "Skipping: audit still fresh", that is a separate issue — do not modify the SorraAgents audit skill here.
- **`isAuditFresh` handles missing audit:** verified — `isAuditFresh` returns `false` when `auditedAt` or `updatedAt` is absent, so unaudited items are correctly selected.
- **Claim-before-dispatch for audits:** the existing `claimItem` (sets `status in_progress`) is applied before the pane spawns, consistent with the plan/intake tiers and the audit runner's own status lifecycle (runner demotes on "No", keeps `completed`/`in_review` on "Yes", restores on infra failure).
- **Scope-creep guard:** out of scope — changing the audit skill's freshness gate, adding audit-tier configuration, changing the heartbeat skill, or altering `wl next` selection semantics. Any such follow-ups get their own work items.
- **Model for audit pane:** dispatched audit panes use the configured downtime model (same as plan/intake), matching `buildDowntimePaneArgs` behaviour.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — add audit tier to `dispatchDowntimeWork`; extend types (`DowntimeSkillKind` + `'audit'`); new `getNextAuditCandidate` dep; update `buildDowntimePrompt`, `skillKindFromPrompt`, pane name.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — `createDowntimeDeps`: implement `getNextAuditCandidate` using `wl list --status completed --stage in_review --json` + `isAuditFresh` filter.
- `packages/herdr/src/icons.ts` — reuse `isAuditFresh` (no change expected; verify it handles the missing-audit case → returns false).
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-log.ts` — audit event kind type if it restricts kinds.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts` — tests for selection, freshness, priority, fallback, logging.

## Related work

- **Herdr to consume local LLM in downtime (WL-0MSF49FMW009M06K)** — parent epic: downtime worker contract; this work extends it with the audit tier.
- **Log herdr downtime dispatches (WL-0MSGPI4AR000YOK8)** — dispatch audit trail; new audit events should follow the same pattern.
- **Same-slot idle tracking for herdr downtime worker (WL-0MSG7P9N8009PCKG)** — related idle-tracking refinement.
- **Heartbeat skill (WL-0MRIHB4Q100946QD)** — the manual/queue-gated audit path that this work complements.
- **Herdr plugin: eliminate the 'Other' group (WL-0MSAR110S002V26K)** — related worklist grouping.
- **Herdr worklist: render command input form (WL-0MSFZUS4Z006IRI3)** — related herdr UI work.
- **Rebuild wl next algorithm (WL-0MM2FKKOW1H0C0G4)** — selection queries rely on `wl next`/`wl list`; relevant if `wl next --stage in_review` behaviour affects candidate selection.
- **Extensible shortcut key system for Pi extension (WL-0MQD0YW40007RTKU)** — herdr shortcuts (`a a` audit chord) context.
- **Test: wl show includes audit summary (WL-0MPZNK1IC001JPTT)** — audit data exposure used by selection.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "What counts as a 'valid audit' for this work?" — Answer (user@ContextHub): "if the herdr algorithm for showing the review icon says it is current (i.e. does not show the hour glass icon or the magnifying glass) then it is valid". Research: `getIconPrefix` in packages/herdr/src/icons.ts shows ⏳ (stale passed) or 🔍 (no audit / stale failed) exactly when `!isAuditFresh(auditedAt, updatedAt)`; fresh audits show ✅/❌/❓. Source: interactive reply + packages/herdr/src/icons.ts.
- Q2: "What's the primary blocker you're hitting today?" — Answer (user@ContextHub): "I don't think the downtime dispatcher will select items ready for audit at all. If I am mistaken explain the existing algorithm." Research: confirmed — `dispatchDowntimeWork` selects only `intake_complete`→`/skill:plan` and `idea`→`/skill:intake`; there is no audit tier. The user was correct; the existing algorithm was documented in "Existing state". Source: interactive reply + packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts.
- Q3: "Where should the fix land?" — Answer (user@ContextHub): "the downtime detector and dispatcher in the Herdr plugin". Source: interactive reply.
- Q4 (follow-up): "Dispatch priority order — where should the audit tier sit?" — Recommendation (agent): audit first (completed/in_review items are release-critical). Answer (user@ContextHub): "agree". Source: interactive reply.


## Plan: features (plan skill, WL-0MSI8H3HP000K0RG)

Four child features, test-first (chain F0 → F1 → F2 → F3 via wl dep edges):

- **F0 — Audit-tier downtime dispatch tests** (WL-0MSI9FDPI005Z0BV, task): extend `downtime-worker.test.ts` + `index.test.ts` for candidate selection, freshness boundary (60s), audit-tier priority, fallback order, no-candidate, dispatch audit logging (kind `audit`), and `getNextAuditCandidate` fail-closed parsing. Satisfies parent AC7/AC9.
- **F1 — Audit candidate selection** (WL-0MSI9FK2Q0074C31, feature): pure `parseAuditCandidatesOutput`/`selectAuditCandidate` in `downtime-worker.ts`; filter `!isAuditFresh` (reuse `icons.ts`), sort ascending by `sortIndex`, first or null. Satisfies parent AC2/AC6.
- **F2 — Audit dispatch tier** (WL-0MSI9WPNI0044RL8, feature): extend `DowntimeSkillKind`/`DowntimeStage` with `audit`; add `getNextAuditCandidate` dep; dispatch audit → plan → intake; claim → spawn `/skill:audit <id>` (pane `Downtime audit`, `--no-focus`) → `recordDispatch` kind `audit`; kind-aware prompt/comment helpers. Satisfies parent AC1/AC3/AC4/AC5.
- **F3 — Wire audit tier and docs** (WL-0MSI9FXJH000GKIW, feature): `createDowntimeDeps.getNextAuditCandidate` runs `wl list --status completed --stage in_review --json` (fail-closed → null); README + code-comment updates; CHANGELOG.md excluded. Satisfies parent AC8/AC9.

Vertical-slice note: single small vertical slice (selection → dispatch → wiring → docs); no horizontal phasing required (effort Small). Between features, review and update the next item's description.

## Appendix: Planning session (WL-0MSI8H3HP000K0RG)

- Q5: "Approve the proposed feature plan (4 features, test-first, audit tier before plan/intake)?" — Answer (user@ContextHub): "lgtm" — approved as proposed. Evidence: interactive reply; plan recorded above. Final: accepted.
- OPEN QUESTION (operational, directed to producer/operator): a concurrent `wl sync` merge (worklog under active sync testing — many `Test item` rows, sync at 2026-08-07T01:22:49Z, itemsAdded=0) dropped the first-created child "Audit dispatch tier" (WL-0MSI9FRAB005FJ0N) from the DB seconds after creation. Recovered by recreating it as WL-0MSI9WPNI0044RL8 (same title/description, parented, stage intake_complete, priority high) and re-adding dependency edges F2→F1 and F3→F2 (F1→F0 survived). Why it matters: concurrent-sync merge races can silently lose freshly created items; the environment had multiple `wl` processes writing/merging at the same time. No code or data beyond the single lost row was affected.

## Plan: changelog

- 2026-08-07: Created 4 child features (F0 tests → F1 selection → F2 dispatch tier → F3 wiring+docs), wired dependency edges, approved by user ("lgtm"). F2 first creation lost to a concurrent-sync merge race; recreated as WL-0MSI9WPNI0044RL8 and edges re-added. Item advanced to plan_complete (status open).

## Summary

Pure selection logic in `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` that turns `wl list --status completed --stage in_review --json` output into the first stale/missing-audit candidate for the herdr downtime worker audit tier (parent WL-0MSI8H3HP000K0RG). Reuses `isAuditFresh` from `packages/herdr/src/icons.ts` as the single source of truth for "valid audit".

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Parses `wl list --status completed --stage in_review --json` stdout (both array and `{workItems: [...]}` shapes) into typed audit candidates (id, title, auditedAt, updatedAt, sortIndex); malformed/empty output yields null (fail-closed).
- [ ] Filters to items WITHOUT a valid audit using `!isAuditFresh(auditedAt, updatedAt)` imported from `icons.ts` — no competing freshness definition is introduced.
- [ ] Missing `auditedAt` or `updatedAt` is selected (isAuditFresh returns false) — verified against `icons.ts`.
- [ ] Candidates are sorted ascending by `sortIndex` (heartbeat convention) and the first is returned; a fresh-audit-only result set yields null.
- [ ] **7-day recency filter**: candidates must have been modified within the last 7 days (`updatedAt` within `DOWNTIME_AUDIT_RECENCY_WINDOW_MS`). Items with a MISSING `updatedAt` are still included (recency cannot be verified → include, operator decision); items with an unparseable `updatedAt` are excluded (fail-closed). `selectAuditCandidate(candidates, now?)` takes an injectable clock for deterministic tests.
- [ ] Pure function(s) exported for unit testing; no wl CLI invocation inside the selection logic.

## Minimal Implementation

- Add `AuditCandidate` interface (id, title, auditedAt?, updatedAt?, sortIndex?) and `parseAuditCandidatesOutput(stdout: string): AuditCandidate[] | null` in `downtime-worker.ts`.
- Add `selectAuditCandidate(candidates: AuditCandidate[], now = Date.now()): AuditCandidate | null` — filter `!isAuditFresh` AND 7-day recency (missing `updatedAt` included), sort by sortIndex ascending, return first.
- Add `DOWNTIME_AUDIT_RECENCY_WINDOW_MS = 7 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000`.
- Import `isAuditFresh` from `./icons.js`; verify icons.ts needs no change (returns false for missing fields).

## Dependencies

- Parent: WL-0MSI8H3HP000K0RG. Prereq: F0 tests (WL-0MSI9FDPI005Z0BV). Prereq of F2 (dispatch tier).

## Deliverables

- Exported selection helpers in `downtime-worker.ts`; unit tests green (F0).

## Summary

Extend the herdr downtime worker dispatch orchestration (parent WL-0MSI8H3HP000K0RG): add the audit tier BEFORE the existing plan/intake tiers so a completed/in_review item without a valid audit is claimed and a visible `/skill:audit <id>` pane is spawned during local-LLM idle time.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `DowntimeSkillKind` and `DowntimeStage` extended with `"audit"`; `DowntimeWorkerDeps` gains `getNextAuditCandidate(): Promise<DowntimeCandidate | null>`.
- [ ] `dispatchDowntimeWork` tries audit first, then plan (`intake_complete`), then intake (`idea`); no candidate anywhere → no dispatch (`no-candidate`).
- [ ] Audit path: claim the item BEFORE the pane spawns (existing claim pattern), spawn `buildDowntimePrompt("audit", candidate)` via `buildDowntimePaneArgs` (pane named `Downtime audit`, `--no-focus`), record dispatch audit with kind `audit`.
- [ ] `skillKindFromPrompt`, `buildDowntimePrompt`, `buildDowntimeDispatchComment` handle kind `audit` (comment renders `/skill:audit <id>`).
- [ ] Single-flight guard and idle→dispatch tick flow (`createDowntimeWorker`) unchanged; at most one dispatch per idle period.
- [ ] No change to the audit skill freshness gate (SorraAgents `_check_audit_freshness`) — out of scope by design.

## Minimal Implementation

- Extend `DowntimeStage = "intake_complete" | "idea" | "audit"` and `DowntimeSkillKind = "plan" | "intake" | "audit"`.
- Add `getNextAuditCandidate` to `DowntimeWorkerDeps` and to the dispatch: audit candidate → claim → spawn `/skill:audit <id>` → `recordDispatch` kind `audit`.
- Update `buildDowntimePrompt` (skill map plan→/skill:plan, intake→/skill:intake, audit→/skill:audit), `skillKindFromPrompt`, and `buildDowntimeDispatchComment` (kind → skill mapping) to cover `"audit"`.
- No changes to `downtime-log.ts` unless its event-kind type restricts kinds (verify; extend if needed).

## Dependencies

- Parent: WL-0MSI8H3HP000K0RG. Prereqs: F0 tests (WL-0MSI9FDPI005Z0BV), F1 selection (WL-0MSI9FK2Q0074C31). Prereq of F3 (wiring + docs).

## Deliverables

- Audit tier in `dispatchDowntimeWork` + kind-aware prompt/comment helpers; F0 tests green.

## Summary

Ensure the herdr audit-freshness predicate enforces the canonical "at-or-near"
semantics and is the **single source of truth** shared by both the icon display
and the downtime (audit-dispatch) worker.

Audit freshness currently lives only in `isAuditFresh()` in
`packages/herdr/src/icons.ts`. It is the basis for the icon display
(`auditIcon` in `icons.ts`) AND is the documented freshness gate reused by the
downtime dispatch audit tier (`selectAuditCandidate` /
`getNextAuditCandidate` in `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts`, which
treats `!isAuditFresh(auditedAt, updatedAt)` as "needs a fresh `/skill:audit`").

Running an audit itself bumps the work item's `updatedAt` to within a fraction
of a second of its `auditedAt` (`wl audit-set` + `wl update --audit-text` +
the verdict-driven status transition). A freshness rule that requires a strict
gap on one side (e.g. only `auditedAt` comfortably ahead of `updatedAt`) can
therefore disagree with the just-persisted state. The canonical fix in
SorraAgents (SA-0MSI3XH34001LLU4) treats an audit as fresh when its
`auditedAt` is **at or near** the item's `updatedAt` (within a small
tolerance) because a near-simultaneous `updatedAt` bump is the audit's own
persistence write.

This item makes ContextHub's herdr audit-freshness logic follow the same
at-or-near rule so the icon display and the downtime dispatcher agree, and
never disagree on a just-persisted audit.

## Expected behaviour

- `isAuditFresh(auditedAt, updatedAt)` returns true (fresh) when `auditedAt`
  is at-or-near `updatedAt` within a small, named tolerance (the audit's own
  persistence write), and false otherwise.
- The icon (`auditIcon` in `icons.ts`) shows the fresh icon for a
  just-persisted audit (no longer shows the stale glyph for an audit the run
  just persisted).
- The downtime audit candidate selection (`selectAuditCandidate` /
  `getNextAuditCandidate` in `downtime-worker.ts`) uses the SAME
  `isAuditFresh` predicate, so a just-persisted fresh audit is NOT a dispatch
  candidate (no redundant `/skill:audit` re-run).
- Only one freshness definition exists; neither consumer re-implements its
  own comparison.

## Acceptance criteria

1. `isAuditFresh` in `icons.ts` treats `auditedAt` at-or-near `updatedAt`
   (within a documented tolerance constant) as fresh, covering the
   audit-persistence case (`auditedAt ~ updatedAt`, delta well under the
   tolerance).
2. A unit test asserts `isAuditFresh(auditedAt, updatedAt)` is true for a
   just-persisted audit (auditedAt and updatedAt differ by milliseconds).
3. A unit test asserts a genuinely stale audit (item updated well after the
   audit) is still false (stale), unchanged.
4. `selectAuditCandidate` / `getNextAuditCandidate` in `downtime-worker.ts`
   continue to use the imported `isAuditFresh` as the sole filter; a
   just-persisted fresh item is excluded from candidates.
5. Both consumers import the same helper; no competing freshness comparison
   is introduced in the dispatch or icon paths.

## Notes / Open questions

- `isAuditFresh` currently hard-codes a magic `60000` ms literal. Prefer
  naming a constant (e.g. `AUDIT_FRESHNESS_AT_NEAR_TOLERANCE_MS`) and routing
  both consumers through it.
- Reconcile the comparison shape of `isAuditFresh` (`auditTime > updateTime -
  buffer`) with the canonical at-or-near semantics from the SorraAgents fix so
  both projects express the same intent. Confirm the target semantics with the
  operator before implementing.

## References

- discovered-from: SA-0MSI3XH34001LLU4 (SorraAgents audit_runner child
  freshness at-or-near fix) — canonical reference implementation.
- related-to: WL-0MSI9FK2Q0074C31 (Audit candidate selection),
  WL-0MSI9WPNI0044R (Audit dispatch tier), parent WL-0MSI8H3HP700K0RG.
data.title: Unify audit-freshness at-or-near logic across icon display and downtime dispatcher

# Tests for header version rendering

## Summary
Unit tests (TDD, written first) for the Herdr work item selection list header version suffix: presence, right-alignment to pane width, dimmed ANSI style, and graceful fallback when no version is available. Expected to FAIL against the current header renderer (no version suffix) and PASS after implementation (F2).

## Acceptance Criteria
- New/extended tests in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` exercise the list-mode header renderer with a version value available.
- Test asserts the header contains a dimmed `v<version>` suffix rendered with the dim ANSI style (`\x1b[2m`), matching the `[auto-refresh on]` treatment.
- Test asserts the version suffix is right-aligned to the pane width (`cols`): visible-width padding computed with ANSI codes stripped before padding.
- Test asserts graceful fallback when the version cannot be read (suffix omitted or replaced with a safe placeholder), and that existing `'Work Items'` presence assertions still hold.
- Tests FAIL against the current implementation (no version suffix in header) and PASS after the implementation feature (F2) lands.

## Minimal Implementation
- Extend the existing header tests in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` (lines ~86-100 region) with version-suffix cases.
- Prefer injecting the version via the renderer's existing testability seam (e.g. a `readFile`-style callback already present in the render signature, or an explicit version parameter) so tests stay hermetic.

## Dependencies
- None (first item, TDD precursor). The implementation item (F2) is blocked by this item.

## Deliverables
- Extended `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` (+ `.meta` if applicable).

# Implement version read + dimmed right-aligned header display

## Summary
Read the plugin version at runtime from `packages/herdr/package.json` and render it as a dimmed, right-aligned `v<version>` suffix in the work item selection list header, without disturbing the left-aligned title.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A runtime helper reads the plugin version from `packages/herdr/package.json` (JSON parse via `readFileSync`, following the `shortcut-config.ts` pattern); when the file is missing or unparseable it falls back gracefully (e.g. `'?'` or omit) without throwing.
- The list-mode header renders `v<version>` right-aligned to `cols` (visible-width padding computed with ANSI codes stripped before padding), dimmed via `ANSI.dim`, matching the `[auto-refresh on]` treatment; the left-aligned `Work Items — N item(s)` title is unchanged.
- The version is read at runtime from the manifest, not hardcoded in the renderer (stays in sync with the manifest version).
- On narrow panes where the suffix would overlap the title, the suffix is dropped or truncated (guard on `cols`) — no layout breakage, no overflow beyond the pane width.
- Full project test suite passes with the new changes, including the header version tests (F1).

## Minimal Implementation
- Add a small version-read helper in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` (or a sibling module) using the `readFileSync`/`dirname` pattern from `shortcut-config.ts`, with a safe fallback.
- In the list-mode header renderer (near line ~1585): compute the header's visible width, pad to `cols`, and append the dimmed `v<version>` suffix right-aligned; reuse `truncateLine`/visible-length logic; guard on `cols` for narrow panes.
- Keep the renderer testable via the existing `readFile`-style injection seam where practical.

## Dependencies
- Blocked by: header version rendering tests (F1) — test-first ordering.

## Deliverables
- Updated `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`; version helper; no change to `packages/herdr/package.json` (version source only).

# Test harness: mock herdr socket + subscriber contract tests

Parent: Subscribe to herdr window events instead of polling active window status (WL-0MSHB7DHO004RHBJ)

## Summary

Build the test foundation for the event-driven path: a reusable in-memory herdr Unix-socket server (newline-delimited JSON-RPC) that answers `events.subscribe` with `subscription_started` and pushes scripted `{"data":{...},"event":"..."}` frames, plus TDD-red tests defining the `HerdrEventSubscriber` contract (connect/subscribe/dispatch/reconnect/fail-open).

## User story

As a developer, I want a deterministic mock of the herdr event socket so the subscriber, visibility gate and agent tracker can be tested without spawning real herdr processes.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A reusable mock socket (net.createServer on a temp path, or an injectable connect seam) accepts `events.subscribe` requests with the documented subscription shape and replies `{"result":{"type":"subscription_started"}}`.
- Red tests assert the subscriber contract: connects to the resolved socket path; sends one subscribe call with the global subscriptions (`pane.focused`, `pane.agent_detected`, `pane.closed`, `pane.exited`) plus per-pane `pane.agent_status_changed` for each tracked pane; dispatches a typed callback per received event frame; reconnects with backoff on socket error; reports "events unavailable" (fail-open) on unreachable socket without throwing.
- Fixtures usable by worklist/visibility/agent-tracker integration tests (scripted `pane_focused` / `pane_agent_status_changed` / `pane_agent_detected` / `pane_closed` / `pane_exited` sequences).
- Existing tests compile and pass; only the intentionally-red new assertions fail.

## Minimal Implementation

- New `packages/herdr/src/events.test.ts` with the mock socket server and red contract tests.
- Shared test fixture module (e.g. `packages/herdr/src/test-utils/mock-herdr-socket.ts`) with scripted event emitters.
- Follow the existing exec-seam / mocked-child_process test patterns in the repo.

## Dependencies

- None (foundation).

## Deliverables

- `events.test.ts` (red contract tests), mock socket fixture, README note in tests if needed.

## Key Files

- packages/herdr/src/events.test.ts (new)
- packages/herdr/src/test-utils/mock-herdr-socket.ts (new)

# events.ts: HerdrEventSubscriber socket module

Parent: Subscribe to herdr window events instead of polling active window status (WL-0MSHB7DHO004RHBJ)

## Summary

New module `packages/herdr/src/events.ts` implementing `HerdrEventSubscriber`: a long-lived JSON-RPC-over-Unix-socket client that subscribes to herdr window events (global + per-pane), dispatches typed callbacks, reconnects with backoff, and fails open when the socket is unavailable.

## User story

As the worklist plugin, I want to receive herdr window events (pane focus/visibility, agent status changes, agent detected/closed/exited) pushed over the herdr socket instead of polling, so icons and visibility gating react immediately.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Connects via `HERDR_SOCKET_PATH` with fallback to `~/.config/herdr/herdr.sock`; unreachable socket → fail-open "events unavailable" (no throw, no unhandled rejection).
- Sends one `events.subscribe` request containing the global subscriptions (`pane.focused`, `pane.agent_detected`, `pane.closed`, `pane.exited`) plus a per-pane `pane.agent_status_changed` subscription for each pane currently tracked in `.worklog/agent-panes.json`.
- Parses newline-delimited JSON-RPC frames; dispatches typed callbacks for `pane_focused`, `pane_agent_status_changed`, `pane_agent_detected`, `pane_closed`, `pane_exited` (per verified live payload shape `{"data":{...},"event":"..."}`).
- Reconnects with backoff on socket errors (e.g. 500ms/1s/2s capped); transient errors never propagate to callers.
- `addPaneSubscription(paneId)` / `removePaneSubscription(paneId)` maintain per-pane subscriptions as panes appear/close.
- `close()` unsubscribes and closes the socket (no leaked connections).
- All F1 contract tests pass (mocked socket); live smoke check against the local herdr socket is optional but recommended.

## Minimal Implementation

- New `packages/herdr/src/events.ts` modelled on the JSON-RPC framing in `packages/herdr/shared/grid.py`.
- Typed event union + callback map; reconnect/backoff state machine; fail-open error surface.
- Wire env resolution (`HERDR_SOCKET_PATH` → default path → poll fallback signal).

## Dependencies

- F1 (test harness/contract) — implementation makes the red tests green.

## Deliverables

- `events.ts` (new module) + green F1 tests + optional live smoke-check evidence comment.

## Key Files

- packages/herdr/src/events.ts (new)
- packages/herdr/src/events.test.ts (new)
- packages/herdr/shared/grid.py (reference framing pattern)
