## Problem

In the herdr worklog-selection-list plugin, an OPEN detail view is never refreshed. `doRefresh()` → `state.refreshItems(newItems)` replaces `_allItems`/`items`, but `state.detailItem` is set only in `selectItem()` (worklist.ts:482) and cleared in `back()` (:497). While `mode === 'detail'`, render() always draws the same snapshot object. So even with the pane focused and auto-refresh running, the visible detail content (Status, Updated, audit icons, description) stays frozen — user-reported symptom: `I have had it focused and it does not update`.

## Evidence (live, 2026-08-08)

- Pane w1:p41 currently displays the detail view of LP-0MSF9RUSQ007M346: `Status: completed`, `Updated 07/08/26 22:21`, `Audited At 07/08/26 22:18`.
- Live worklog: `status: in-progress`, `updatedAt: 2026-08-08T00:21:58.992Z` (claimed ~5 min earlier via a dispatch from the same pane; agent-panes.json records spawned pane w1:p4W).
- The list portion does refresh while focused (scrollback renders evolve), so the stale detail is not a fetch failure — it is the refresh path never writing to `detailItem`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A refresh while a detail view is open updates the rendered detail content to the freshly fetched item state (without closing the view or resetting scroll/ToC position unless the item identity changes).
- [ ] Selection/scroll restoration semantics from refreshItems are preserved for the list.
- [ ] Unit tests: refresh while in detail mode updates detailItem by ID; item removed from results → detail falls back gracefully (keeps last known or closes).
- [ ] The selected-item metadata panel (list mode) also reflects refreshed data (it already does via items; verify no regression).

## Suggested approach

In `doRefresh` (or `refreshItems`), after swapping items, look up the refreshed object matching `state.detailItem?.id` and assign it to `detailItem` (preserving `detailScrollOffset`/ToC state). If the item disappeared from the fetched set, keep the last snapshot or exit to list mode (decide + test).

## Problem

In the herdr worklog-selection-list plugin, every fetch used by the auto-refresh cycle spawns `wl` via execFile WITHOUT a timeout: `runWl(args)` (fetcher.ts:376) passes `timeout` to execFileAsync only when `timeoutMs !== undefined` (:356), and no caller in the refresh path supplies one (fetchNextItems, fetchItemsByStage, fetchMandatorySubsets, fetchActionableCount). `doRefresh` awaits these inside a `refreshInFlight` single-flight guard (worklist.ts:2497-2503); if a spawn hangs (e.g. waiting on the worklog lock during a long `wl sync`, or a stuck child), the guard stays true forever and EVERY subsequent refresh is skipped — the pane freezes even while focused, with no error surfaced.

Note: runSync (auto-sync.ts:226) already has a 60s spawn safety timeout; the refresh read path does not.

related-to: WL-0MSJIPHD0001L1J9 (same bug class in the downtime worker path — getNextItem/getNextAuditCandidate in index.ts use direct execFileAsync with no timeout; a single fix adding bounded timeouts to ALL wl spawns would close both).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every wl spawn in the refresh/sync fetch path has a bounded timeout (recommend 30-60s, configurable or aligned with existing constants).
- [ ] A timed-out refresh fails gracefully: toast (`Refresh failed`), guard cleared, next tick retries — never a permanently wedged refreshInFlight.
- [ ] Unit tests: hung execFile resolves to failure after the timeout and the next refresh tick proceeds.

## Suggested approach

Pass a default timeoutMs inside runWl (or runWlInner) when the caller omits one, e.g. `DEFAULT_WL_TIMEOUT_MS = 60_000`, keeping the option to override. Verify no existing tests depend on unbounded spawns.

## Goal

Root-cause why **zero downtime dispatches** were sent during the night of 2026-08-07/08, despite evidence that multiple clients polled `GET /llama/local/status` continuously — including for the full 7-hour idle window — while the proxy reported an idle local model with free slots. Determine whether any of the pollers were herdr downtime workers that failed to dispatch (wedge, silent wl failure, candidate-selection fail-closed, claim conflict) or whether none of the pollers were dispatch-capable at all.

## Log observations (evidence)

### 1. Continuous status polling all night — including the entire idle window

`/var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log` `status_request` entries (proxy = 192.168.0.199:8000, the herdr downtime worker's `DEFAULT_DOWNTIME_PROXY_URL`):

| Window (local) | Poll rate |
|---|---|
| 03:00–04:15 (audit-wave tail) | 15.9/min |
| 04:20–05:00 (idle start) | 15.9/min |
| 05:00–09:00 (idle) | 15.5/min |
| 09:00–11:00 (idle) | 15.9/min |

- Inter-poll gap histogram over 05:10–09:00 (3654 gaps): smooth decay 0–9s, mean gap 3.78s → consistent with **~8 independent periodic pollers at ~30s cadence** (exponential inter-arrival for uniform random phases). Rate did NOT pause during idle (a healthy herdr worker polls regardless, but a *wedged* one stops — WL-0MSJIPHD0001L1J9).
- The local worklist pane (sole `tsx src/index.ts` on this host) was **wedged since 21:55:26Z** (see item WL-0MSJIPHD0001L1J9; it ran pre-fix source, HEAD 7ea7cae4) → contributed ~0 polls after 21:55Z. So the ~8 pollers are NOT explained by the local pane.

### 2. Proxy healthy and idle-capable throughout

- `proxy.log.2026-08-08_05` contains ONLY `status_request` (5722) and `lease_released` (51) — no restarts, no watchdog events, no server failures.
- llama-server up with Qwen3 loaded: 104,657 `GET /slots` responses in `/var/log/llama-proxy/llama-server.log`; proxy broadcast loop only queries `/slots` when `llama_server_running=true`.
- Zero local model requests 04:18–11:26 local → status would have reported `active_query=false`, `available_slots=3/3` (idle), and fail-open even without a model (LP-0MSI06HPB0043MV1). A ≥4-min idle window existed repeatedly for 7h09m.

### 3. Persistent remote (192.168.0.191) connections to the proxy

- `ss -tnp` at multiple snapshots showed 3–4 concurrent ESTAB `.191 → :8000` connections (ports 44902/64396/59704, then 64396/40258/37498; one with a 276KB in-flight send queue). The remote host also holds 6+ SSH sessions to this host (port 22; herdr TUIs run via SSH — see clients 66/68 in `~/.config/herdr/herdr-server.log` at 02:14/02:55 local).
- **Caveat:** the proxy does NOT log client IPs for `status_request`, so the poller identity is inferred from connection snapshots, not proven. The pollers could be (a) herdr downtime workers on 192.168.0.191 (each worklist pane polls the same LAN proxy URL every 30s), (b) the opencode TUI statusline on .191, or (c) other.

### 4. Zero dispatches anywhere

- Only dispatch log present: `/home/rgardler/projects/llm/.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log` — last entry `2026-08-07T21:55:26.274Z audit LP-0MSI06HPB0043MV1`. No dispatches after that.
- No `downtime-dispatches.log` in ContextHub/SorraAgents/piman/etc. worklogs.
- No dispatch lease activity during idle: `proxy.log.2026-08-08_05` has no `dispatch_cleanup`, `local_dispatch_denied`, or `lease_renewed` events — only `lease_released` for evicted sessions (leftover audit-wave leases expiring on the 5-min sweep).

## The RCA question

If any of the ~8 pollers were herdr downtime workers (remote or local), they observed a fully idle local model with free slots for 7h09m and still dispatched nothing. Why?

## Candidate hypotheses to evaluate

1. **Wedge bug (WL-0MSJIPHD0001L1J9):** no-timeout `wl` exec in `getNextItem`/`getNextAuditCandidate` permanently wedges the dispatch task until pane restart. Fix 810afbe1 exists ONLY on `origin/dev` — the local ContextHub checkout was stale at 7ea7cae4 and the pane restarted 2026-08-08 11:53:21 local still loads the pre-fix source (`DOWNTIME_WL_TIMEOUT_MS` absent). Any pre-fix pane would wedge on its first dispatch attempt (e.g., under worklog lock contention from the audit wave).
2. **Pollers are not dispatch-capable** (e.g., opencode statusline) → no dispatch expected; the RCA must identify the pollers first (add client IP to the proxy `status_request` structured log, or tcpdump :8000; check processes/worklogs on 192.168.0.191).
3. **Silent dispatch failure:** wl failures/lock contention, candidate selection fail-closed (`wl next --stage` returns nothing), claim conflict, `send-to-pi.sh` spawn failure. Check what the downtime worker logs on failure vs success (dispatch log only written on success?).
4. **Config/disablement:** downtime worker disabled, paused (no-candidate cooldown), or dispatch window rules on the remote panes.
5. **Worklog-root mismatch:** remote panes write dispatch logs to `.191` filesystems (invisible here); verify on .191 whether dispatches were attempted/logged there.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Poller identity established: each `status_request` poller attributed (herdr worklist pane vs other) with evidence (proxy access-log client IPs, tcpdump capture, or .191 inspection)
- [ ] For each herdr poller that saw an idle window: the exact point of failure determined (wedge / wl failure / fail-closed selection / claim / spawn) with log or repro evidence
- [ ] If the wedge bug is implicated: confirm the fix (810afbe1) is deployed to every running worklist pane (working tree updated + pane restarted), or a follow-up item created for deployment
- [ ] Recommend an observability fix (e.g., client IP in `status_request` structured log) so poller attribution is possible in future
- [ ] Dispatches resume: a dispatch observed in `downtime-dispatches.log` on the next idle window ≥4 min
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MSJIPHD0001L1J9** – herdr downtime worker: hung wl exec (no timeout) permanently wedges the dispatch task until pane restart (completed)
- **WL-0MNC77YBM000ONUO** – Use colour on the audit summary in the meta data. (completed)
- **WL-0MPN6LCLO006N5U8** – In /wl browser, Enter renders wl show markdown in above-editor widget (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `.worklog/worktrees/wl-WL-0MSGJDSMJ004128E-herdr-selection-list-shortcut-hint-bar-e/packages/herdr/README.md` — matched: 168, 192, 199, 2026, 30s (+175 more)
- `.worklog/worktrees/wl-WL-0MSKSZBEL0025CN3-test-failure-tests-cli-init-test-ts-shou/packages/herdr/README.md` — matched: 168, 192, 199, 2026, 30s (+173 more)

data.description:
# Intake Brief — Herdr: filter by priority via f-p-* chords, stage filters become f-s-* (WL-0MSKC8T46006999S) ## Headline Add priority filtering to the Herdr worklist, complementing the existing stage filter: the filter chord gains an axis key — stage filters become `f s ` and new priority filters are `f p ` — with a single active filter (replace semantics), a typed `/wl --priority

` command for parity, and sprint clearing all filters. ## Problem Statement The Herdr worklist currently filters only by stage via single-key chords (`f i`, `f n`, `f p`, `f r`, `f s`). Producers and agents frequently want to see everything at a given priority (e.g. all `critical` items) regardless of stage, which is not possible today. The filter chord needs an axis dimension: `f `. Re-using the existing single-key chords would collide (`f p` currently means "filter plan"), so stage filters move under `f s *` and priority filters take `f p *`. ## Users - Herdr plugin users (producers, developers, agents) who browse the worklist inside a Herdr pane. ### Example User Stories - As a producer, I want to press `f p c` to see every open critical item so I can prioritise review, regardless of stage. - As a developer, I want to type `/wl --priority high` to see all open high-priority work when deciding what to pick up next. - As an agent, I want `f s i` to keep filtering idea-stage items with the same keystroke muscle memory I had for `f i`. ## Acceptance Criteria 1. New priority filter chords work: `f p c` (critical), `f p h` (high), `f p m` (medium), `f p l` (low) filter the worklist to items of that priority. 2. Stage filter chords are remapped under the stage axis: `f s i` (idea), `f s n` (intake), `f s p` (plan), `f s r` (review) filter by stage; the old single-key stage chords (`f i`, `f n`, `f p`, `f r`) no longer trigger filters, and `f s` alone no longer resolves to a command (it is a chord prefix only). 3. Replace semantics (single filter slot): applying a priority filter clears any active stage filter, and vice versa; the list header shows which filter is active. 4. Sprint clears all filters: `f s s` and `/wl` (no arguments) restore the default unfiltered view, clearing both stage and priority filters; a priority-axis clear exists (proposed `f p s`) that returns to the unfiltered view. 5. Typed parity command: `/wl --priority ` filters by priority, accepting canonical names `critical`, `high`, `medium`, `low`; invalid/unknown priority values fall back gracefully (no crash, no filter change), matching the current `/wl ` behaviour. 6. Priority-filtered views follow the same semantics as stage-filtered views: every open root item with that priority (`wl list --status open --priority

--root-only`) — no `browseItemCount` cap, no `wl next` selection omission, children hidden and reachable via expand, standard sortIndex order. 7. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes, with new unit tests covering chord registration, dispatch, replace semantics, and the priority fetcher. 8. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes (Herdr README filter sections, code comments). ## Constraints - **Scope is the Herdr plugin** (`packages/herdr/`): `shortcuts.json`, `worklist.ts`, `fetcher.ts`, tests, and README. The Pi TUI extension and the `wl` CLI are out of scope (the CLI already supports `--priority`). - **No new settings or configuration flags.** The chord scheme and `/wl --priority` command are the only interfaces. - **Single active filter.** Stage and priority filters are mutually exclusive (user decision: replace, not combine). - Keep the existing stage-filter fetch semantics (open, root-only, uncapped, sortIndex order) — the priority filter mirrors them. ## Existing State - Filter chords in `packages/herdr/src/shortcuts.json`: `f i` → `/wl idea`, `f n` → `/wl intake`, `f p` → `/wl plan`, `f r` → `/wl review`, `f s` → `/wl` (sprint, unfiltered). - `dispatchChordCommand` in `worklist.ts` maps `/wl ` (via `STAGE_MAP`) to `state.applyFilter(stage)` and `/wl` (no args) to `state.clearFilter()`; `isWlViewCommand` triggers a refetch after a filter dispatch (WL-0MSDT8X1V003206G). - `WorkItemListState.activeFilter` holds the single stage filter; `_applyFilters()` filters `item.stage === activeFilter`; the header renders `(filtered: )`. - `fetchItemsForView(activeFilter, defaultFetcher)` → `fetchItemsByStage(stage)` → `wl list --status open --stage --root-only` (fetcher.ts). - `wl list` natively supports `--priority` (already used by `fetchMandatorySubsets` for the critical subset). - A legacy digit-based filter mode (`state.mode === 'filter'`, `formatFilterPrompt`) exists but is unreachable from the keyboard since the `/` prompt was removed — out of scope unless trivially affected. ## Desired Change 1. **`shortcuts.json`** — Remove the `f i`/`f n`/`f p`/`f r` stage chords and the single `f s` sprint chord. Add stage-axis chords `f s i|n|p|r` (→ `/wl idea|intake|plan|review`) and `f s s` (→ `/wl` sprint, clears all filters). Add priority-axis chords `f p l|m|h|c` (→ `/wl --priority low|medium|high|critical`) and `f p s` (→ `/wl`, clear-priority, returns to unfiltered). 2. **`worklist.ts`** — Add a priority filter slot to `WorkItemListState` with replace semantics (`applyFilter` clears priority; new `applyPriorityFilter` clears stage; `clearFilter` clears both). Extend `_applyFilters` to match stage OR priority. Extend `dispatchChordCommand` and `isWlViewCommand` to handle `/wl --priority

`. Update the header filter label to show the active axis+value. `fetchItemsForView` routes priority filters to the new fetcher. 3. **`fetcher.ts`** — Add `fetchItemsByPriority(priority)` running `wl list --status open --priority

--root-only`, mirroring `fetchItemsByStage`. 4. **Tests** — Update `shortcut-config.test.ts` (chord registration: `f s *`, `f p *`, removal of old single-key chords) and `worklist.test.ts` (dispatch of `/wl --priority

`, replace semantics, clear-all sprint, header label); add `fetchItemsByPriority` coverage in the fetcher tests. 5. **README** — Update the filter-by-stage chord documentation to the `f s *` scheme and document `f p *` priority filters and `/wl --priority

`. ## Key Files (predicted) - `packages/herdr/src/shortcuts.json` — Replace the single-key stage chords with `f s *` stage chords and add `f p *` priority chords. - `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — Priority filter slot with replace semantics, `/wl --priority` dispatch, header label, `isWlViewCommand` update. - `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — New `fetchItemsByPriority` mirroring `fetchItemsByStage`. - `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` — Dispatch, replace-semantics, clear-all, and header tests. - `packages/herdr/src/shortcut-config.test.ts` — Chord registration tests for the new `f s *` / `f p *` scheme. - `tests/herdr/fetcher.test.ts` — `fetchItemsByPriority` mocked-socket tests. - `packages/herdr/README.md` — Filter documentation updates. ## Related Work - **WL-0MSDT8X1V003206G** (in-progress) — "When filtering by stage, show all open work items in that stage": established the stage-filter fetch semantics (open, root-only, uncapped) and `/wl ` dispatch that this work extends to priorities. - **WL-0MSGSE15000746F7** — sprint `/wl` chord returning to the default view; the `f s` chord being remapped here. - **WL-0MS964SIA0057ABR** — root-only top-level lists; semantics reused by the priority filter. - **WL-0MS1W8Y1L0059AKP** — Herdr work item selection list (origin of the plugin's list/filter UI). - **WL-0MSGTSPXK007POB1** — header shows the active filter; the header label changes here for priorities. ### Related work (automated report) Automated report from the find-related skill (full report: `.worklog/tmp/find-related-full-WL-0MSKC8T46006999S.md`). Low relevance — flagged for traceability only: - **WL-0MSB19J56006E87J** – Investigate excessive wl process spawning (206 concurrent, ~17 GB RAM) (completed) - **WL-0MQFB8N990056T8P** – [test-failure] tests/tui/controller-watch.test.ts > TuiController - Database Watch > always re-renders on watch refresh even when dataset appears unchanged (completed) - **WL-0MQF95NCC0024H61** – wl next Stage 3 blocker surfacing still returns child items (completed) ## Risks & Assumptions - **Chord conflict risk (medium):** `f p` changes meaning from "filter plan" to "priority axis leader". Mitigation: remove the old `f p` plan chord; `f p` alone must not resolve (registry prefix semantics already support this); tests assert the old chords no longer resolve. - **Muscle memory regression (low):** existing users of `f i`/`f n`/`f r` must learn `f s i`/`f s n`/`f s r`. Mitigation: README documents the new scheme; `f s` hints show in the chord help line. - **Assumption — priority clear chord:** the exact key for the priority-axis clear is proposed as `f p s` (symmetric with the stage sprint). Final key choice is a product detail; the brief records the proposal (user confirmed a priority-clear exists). - **Assumption — typed command syntax:** `/wl --priority ` mirrors the existing `/wl ` syntax; alternative syntaxes (e.g. `/wl priority:

`) are possible but the `--priority` form matches the `wl list` flag naming. - **Scope creep:** the legacy unreachable digit-based filter mode (`formatFilterPrompt`) is out of scope; any change to it should be a separate work item. ## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers - Q1: "Can a stage filter and a priority filter be active simultaneously (e.g., `f s i` then `f p c` → critical idea items), or does each new filter chord replace the previous one (single filter slot)?" — Answer (user): "replace". Source: interactive reply (this intake session). Final: single active filter; applying one axis clears the other. - Q2: "Should sprint clear *all* filters (stage + priority), and is a way to clear just the priority filter needed (e.g., a `f p` clear chord)?" — Answer (user): "yes". Source: interactive reply (this intake session). Final: `f s s` and `/wl` clear all filters; a priority-axis clear chord exists (proposed `f p s`, equivalent to returning to the unfiltered view under replace semantics). - Q3: "Should the priority filter also be reachable via a typed command (e.g., `/wl --priority critical`) for parity with `/wl `, or is the chord-only approach sufficient?" — Answer (user): "yes". Source: interactive reply (this intake session). Final: `/wl --priority ` is a supported typed command with graceful fallback for invalid values.

## Summary

Filtering the herdr plugin by in_review using the shortcut `f-r` (which resolves to `/wl review`) results in **0 items** being displayed, even though there are 70 items in the in_review stage.

## Expected behaviour

`f-r` (filter in_review) shows all root work items in the in_review stage.

## Observed behaviour

`f-r` shows an empty list (0 items).

## Root cause (investigated)

`fetchItemsByStage` (packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts) runs:

```
wl list --status open --stage <stage> --root-only
```

Per the project workflow convention (AGENTS.md), advancing an item to `in_review` sets its status to `completed`; some in_review items are still `in-progress`. Live data confirms: stage=in_review → 65 items with status `completed`, 5 with `in-progress`, **0 with `open`**. The `--status open` restriction therefore excludes every in_review item and the filter shows 0 items.

Other stage filters are also lossy (idea: 30/35, intake_complete: 21/33 missing 12 blocked, plan_complete: 10/13), but in_review is the only one that is 100% empty.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Open the herdr worklist plugin pane.
2. Press `f` then `r` (filter in_review).
3. Observe the list shows 0 item(s).

## Suggested implementation approach

Change `fetchItemsByStage` so a stage-filtered view shows every root item in the stage regardless of status (drop the `--status open` restriction), or map each stage to its conventional statuses (in_review → completed/in-progress). Decision pending user confirmation on scope.

## Acceptance Criteria (draft)

- [ ] `f-r` shows all 70 root in_review items (not 0).
- [ ] Stage-filtered fetch no longer silently drops items whose status does not match `open` for the in_review stage.
- [ ] Unit tests cover the in_review stage-filter fetch (items with completed/in-progress status are returned).
- [ ] Full project test suite passes with the new changes.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated (code comments, packages/herdr/README.md).

# Intake Brief — Herdr: in_review stage filter (f-r) shows 0 items (WL-0MSKCRX730052IIW)

## Headline

Filtering the herdr worklist by in_review (shortcut `f-r`, resolving to `/wl review`) shows an empty list, because the stage-filtered fetch restricts results to `status=open` while in_review items carry `completed`/`in-progress` status per the project workflow.

## Problem Statement

The herdr plugin's stage filter for in_review (`f-r` → `/wl review` → `STAGE_MAP.review = 'in_review'`) displays **0 items** even though 70 items are in the in_review stage. `fetchItemsByStage` (packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts) runs `wl list --status open --stage <stage> --root-only`; per the AGENTS.md workflow convention, advancing an item to `in_review` sets its status to `completed` (65 items) or leaves it `in-progress` (5 items) — **none are `open`**. The `--status open` restriction therefore excludes every in_review item and the filter shows 0 items.

## Users

- Herdr worklist users (producers, developers, agents) who press `f-r` to review everything awaiting producer review.

### Example User Stories

- As a producer, I want to press `f-r` in the herdr worklist and see every item awaiting review, so I know the full review queue.
- As a developer, I want the in_review filter to list items I have submitted for review (status `completed`) and items being re-worked after review feedback (status `in-progress`).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Pressing `f-r` in the herdr worklist shows every root work item in the in_review stage (all 70 in the current dataset), not 0.
2. `fetchItemsByStage('in_review')` issues a `wl list` query whose status filter includes `completed` and `in-progress` (verified by a unit test asserting the exec args), while preserving `--root-only` and the standard list order.
3. Stage filters for other stages keep their existing behaviour unchanged (status=open per WL-0MSDT8X1V003206G) — verified by the existing stage-filter tests.
4. Unit tests cover the in_review stage fetch returning `completed` and `in-progress` items, and a regression test asserts the client-side stage filter (`_applyFilters`) still works for in_review.
5. Full project test suite passes with the new changes.
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments and `packages/herdr/README.md`.

> **Note:** CHANGELOG.md is excluded — it is managed automatically by the ship skill's release pipeline.

## Constraints

- Fix is confined to the herdr plugin (`packages/herdr`); no `wl` CLI changes.
- Do not regress the semantics of the other stage filters (WL-0MSDT8X1V003206G keeps `status=open` for idea/intake_complete/plan_complete).
- Fail-open behaviour preserved: if the stage fetch fails, fall back to the default fetcher (never blank the list).
- `wl list --status` accepts comma-separated statuses (already used by `fetchActionableCount`), so no CLI change is needed.

## Existing State

- `f-r` (shortcuts.json) → `/wl review` → `dispatchChordCommand` matches `/^\/wl\s+(\S+)$/` → `STAGE_MAP['review']='in_review'` → `state.applyFilter('in_review')` → `doRefresh(true)` → `fetchItemsForView('in_review', fetcher)` → `fetchItemsByStage('in_review')`.
- `fetchItemsByStage` (fetcher.ts:510) runs `wl list --status open --stage <stage> --root-only`.
- Live data: stage=in_review → 65 `completed`, 5 `in-progress`, 0 `open`. Other stages: idea 30/35 open, intake_complete 21/33 open (12 blocked), plan_complete 10/13 open — lossy but non-empty; user chose to leave these unchanged.
- The `--status open` restriction originates from WL-0MSDT8X1V003206G (in-progress) whose AC#2 defined "open" as `status=open` — that decision conflicts with the workflow rule that in_review items have `completed` status.

## Desired Change

- In `fetchItemsByStage`, add a status-per-stage override: for the `in_review` stage, query with `--status completed,in-progress` (optionally including `open` for robustness) instead of `--status open`. Other stages keep `--status open`.
- Update/extend unit tests in `worklist.test.ts` (the `fetchItemsForView — stage-filtered fetch` block) to cover the in_review status set.
- Update the code comment in fetcher.ts (and README if it documents filter semantics) to reflect the per-stage status rule.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — `fetchItemsByStage` (line ~510): apply the in_review status override in the `wl list` args.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` — the `fetchItemsForView — stage-filtered fetch` describe block (line ~676): extend with in_review status assertions; keep other-stage tests green.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — only if the status-per-stage mapping is better placed next to `STAGE_MAP`/`STAGES` (optional; otherwise comment-only).
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — document the in_review filter status semantics if the filter behaviour is described there.

## Related Work

- **WL-0MSDT8X1V003206G (in-progress)** — "When filtering by stage, show all open work items in that stage": source of the `--status open` restriction that broke the in_review filter. The fix relaxes that restriction for in_review only.
- **WL-0MQDRZ4DK007NK5P (completed)** — "Add stage-filter arguments to the /wl slash command in the Pi TUI extension": original stage-filter feature this bug extends.
- **WL-0MSKC8T46006999S (open)** — "Herdr: filter by priority via f-p-* chords (stage filters become f-s-*)": will re-map the filter chords; same code path, related-to (not blocking).
- **WL-0MSGSE15000746F7 (in-progress)** — "Add key/chord to return to default browse view": the `f-s` clear-filter shortcut, same shortcut family.
- **WL-0MM0DTK1B1Z0VMIB / WL-0MM0DBM6I1PHQBFI (completed)** — "wl list --stage in_review returns nothing while --json shows content": similar symptom at the wl CLI rendering layer, both closed; this bug is in the herdr plugin's query construction.

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Scope discipline (risk):** the same `--status open` restriction makes idea/intake_complete/plan_complete filters lossy. Per user decision (Q1) those are out of scope; if a follow-up is wanted, record it as a new work item rather than expanding this one.
- **Assumption — in_review statuses:** the fix targets `completed` + `in-progress`; including `open` as well is harmless and future-proof (no in_review item is `open` today).
- **Assumption — no wl CLI change:** `wl list --status` already accepts comma-separated statuses; verified via `fetchActionableCount`.
- **Regression risk:** the existing stage-filter tests assert `--status open`; they must be kept green for non-in_review stages (tests will need per-stage expectations).
- **Stale-data assumption:** numbers (70 items, 65/5 split) reflect the dataset at intake time; ACs are stated in behaviour terms so they hold as the dataset evolves.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "How should the stage-filter fetch behave? (a) Minimal — fix in_review only: include completed/in-progress statuses for the in_review stage (status-per-stage map), leave other stages as-is. (b) All stages — drop `--status open`: show every root item in the stage regardless of status. (c) Other." — Answer (user): "(a)". Source: interactive reply during intake. Research: confirmed other stage filters are lossy but non-empty (idea 30/35, intake_complete 21/33, plan_complete 10/13); only in_review is 100% empty. Per the user's choice, other stages keep `status=open` semantics.
- Q2 (implicit, documented): Should the 5 in-progress/in_review items appear in the filter? — Resolved by the (a) choice: `completed` and `in-progress` both included; a producer reviewing the queue sees both the submitted-for-review items and those being re-worked after review feedback.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0ML6GP3OQ15UO20F** – Investigate sort-operations performance test timeout (completed)
- **WL-0MKW48NQ913SQ212** – Refactor wl next selection paths (completed)

- `.worklog/worktrees/wl-SA-0MSKB6VJA005N43F-audit-parent-first-child-pass-through-au/skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner.py` — matched: 100, acceptance, agents, also, approach (+71 more)
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner.py` — matched: 100, acceptance, agents, also, approach (+71 more)

As an operator, I want to understand whether templates/AGENTS.md is the right way to handle worklog installation/configuration, so that the install model is clean, maintainable, and clearly documented.

## Context
templates/AGENTS.md is the worklog agent-instruction template copied by `wl init` into new projects (see src/commands/init.ts, WORKLOG_AGENT_TEMPLATE_RELATIVE_PATH). It duplicates guidance that also lives in the SorraAgents global AGENTS_GLOBAL.md (installed to ~/.pi/agent/AGENTS.md), which creates drift risk — e.g. the recent 'docs' issue-type change had to be applied to both files.

## Questions to investigate

## User story

As a producer reviewing work items in the herdr worklist, I want the detail view description and the `Episode file (md viewer)` pane to render real markdown (headings hierarchy, bold/italic, inline code, links, tables, ordered/nested lists, blockquotes) so my episode `.podcast.md` files and GFM-heavy descriptions read properly instead of as raw text.

## Current state

- **Detail view description** (`formatDetailContent`, `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` ~line 1076): raw line-splitting + wrap + `[NOTE <id>: ...]` link substitution only. No tables, bold/italic, inline code, links, lists, or headings rendered.
- **md viewer** (`renderMarkdownViewer`, `packages/herdr/src/md-viewer.ts`): hand-rolled minimal renderer supporting only YAML frontmatter skip, fenced code blocks, ATX headings (all levels rendered identically), top-level `-*+` bullet lists, and paragraphs. Missing: tables, ordered lists, nested lists, blockquotes, inline code, bold/italic, links, horizontal rules.

## Proposed approach

Replace the hand-rolled parsing with a proper markdown renderer while keeping the existing pure-function, dependency-injectable design (tests inject `readFile`; no terminal/pane harness):

- Add **`marked`** (v18.x — already in the pi agent dependency tree, so compatibility is proven) as a dependency of `packages/herdr`, with a **custom renderer** that emits ANSI-styled terminal lines (headings bold/distinct levels, `codespan`/`code` glyphs, links underlined/colored, tables as aligned columns, blockquotes indented, ordered lists numbered). Alternative: `marked-terminal` if a ready-made terminal renderer fits better. Decide in planning; document the choice.
- Thread the renderer through both call sites: the description section of `formatDetailContent` and `renderFileViewer` → `renderMarkdownViewer`.
- Preserve the existing `[NOTE <id>: ...]` → `<id>↗` link behavior (`renderNoteLinks`) inside rendered output — likely via a marked extension/custom token renderer so NOTE markers stay clickable in both views.
- Keep YAML frontmatter skipping in the md viewer, the `Related Docs` ToC, and the keyboard nav (`↑↓/j:k`, `Enter`, `g/G`) unchanged.
- Note: herdr panes run with cwd = plugin source dir; `marked` must be a declared dependency of `packages/herdr` (installed into `packages/herdr/node_modules` and reflected in `dist/` build), not assumed from a parent node_modules.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/md-viewer.ts` — `renderMarkdownViewer`, `renderNoteLinks`, `NOTE_MARKER_RE`; the renderer replacement lives here.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — `formatDetailContent` (description section ~line 1076), `renderFileViewer` (~line 1162), `firstMarkdownKeyFile` (~line 1185).
- `packages/herdr/src/md-viewer.test.ts` — existing Key Files md viewer tests (injected `readFile`); extend with GFM rendering cases.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` — TUI-level tests (chord/smart-selection/needsProducerReview guards must stay green).
- `packages/herdr/package.json` — new `marked` dependency.
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — `Markdown viewer` section (line ~425) documents supported constructs; update for full GFM support and the new dependency.

Related: WL-0MSGEA9AY0080V4Q (md viewer Key Files path-resolution fix), OSL-0MSDYOVP6005T1X5 (original md viewer feature).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The detail view description renders GFM: at least tables (aligned columns), bold, italic, inline code, links, and lists — verified by unit tests rendering a sample GFM description.
- [ ] The md viewer renders the full set of GFM constructs used in `.podcast.md` files: heading hierarchy, ordered + nested bullet lists, blockquotes, tables, inline code, bold/italic, links — verified by unit tests.
- [ ] `[NOTE <id>: ...]` markers still render as `<id>↗` links in both the description and the md viewer (regression, existing tests stay green).
- [ ] YAML frontmatter still skipped in the md viewer; `Related Docs` ToC and keyboard navigation behavior unchanged (TUI-level tests pass).
- [ ] `marked` is a declared dependency of `packages/herdr` and the plugin builds/runs with it (repo-root `npm test` = `vitest run` covers `packages/herdr`; `tsc` clean).
- [ ] `packages/herdr/README.md` Markdown viewer section updated to document supported GFM constructs and the renderer dependency.

# Intake Brief: Add issue-type gating to herdr shortcuts; limit code-focused shortcuts to code work item types

## Problem statement

The herdr worklist plugin's chord shortcut system
(`packages/herdr/src/shortcuts.json` + `shortcut-config.ts`) gates shortcuts
by chord keys, `view`, `stages`, `model`, and `code_freeze` — but has **no
work-item-type (issueType) gating**. Every bundled shortcut (`n` intake,
`p` plan, `i` implement, `a-a`/`a-y`/`a-r` audit, `r` producer-review,
`u-*` updates, `x-*` close/delete, `P-*` prompts, `f-*` filters) is visible
on every work item regardless of its issue type. Consumer projects that use
non-code work item types (e.g. open_source_llm's `podcast` episodes) see
code-workflow chords (`n`/`p`/`i`) on items where they are the wrong tools —
and podcast-progression chords (defined in the consumer's project-local
`shortcuts.json`, see OSL-0MSKFXM380098LFL) cannot be restricted to podcast
items. This item adds an issue-type allowlist field to shortcut entries and
applies it to the code-focused bundled shortcuts so they appear only on code
work item types.

## Users

Producers and agents using the herdr worklist plugin in projects with mixed
work item types (code + non-code such as podcast).

**Example user stories:**

- As a podcast producer, when I select a `podcast`-typed work item in herdr,
  I want the code workflow chords (`n`/`p`/`i`) to be absent so I cannot
  accidentally run a code intake/plan/implement against an episode.
- As a plugin maintainer, I want bundled defaults to restrict code-focused
  shortcuts to code types (`bug`, `feature`, `task`, `chore`, `epic`) so all
  consumer projects inherit the fix without editing the bundle.
- As a consumer-project operator, I want to add my own chords gated to my own
  issue type (e.g. `podcast`) via the existing project-local
  `<worklogRoot>/shortcuts.json` mechanism — no plugin edits.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1 — `ShortcutEntry` gains an optional `workItemTypes` allowlist field
  (JSON key `work_item_types`, parsed to `workItemTypes` following the
  existing `code_freeze`→`codeFreeze` convention); invalid values are logged
  and treated as omitted (never crash, mirroring `code_freeze` handling).
- [ ] AC2 — Registry filtering honors the allowlist when the caller supplies
  the selected item's `issueType`: `lookupChordEntry`, `getEntriesForStage`,
  `getChordByPrefix`, and the footer/help hint paths exclude an entry whose
  `workItemTypes` is present and does not include the item's type. When no
  `issueType` is supplied (or the entry has no allowlist), behavior is
  unchanged from today.
- [ ] AC3 — The selected item's `issueType` (already fetched in
  `fetcher.ts`) is threaded through the `worklist.ts` shortcut lookup/hint
  call sites (currently ~5 sites: lookupChordEntry at 1330/2726,
  getChordByPrefix at 1340/2805, getEntriesForStage at 2924).
- [ ] AC4 — The bundled code-focused shortcuts `n` (intake), `p` (plan), and
  `i` (implement) carry `work_item_types: ["bug","feature","task","chore",
  "epic"]`; `i` keeps its existing `code_freeze: "block"`. All other bundled
  shortcuts (generic `u-*`, `x-*`, `a-*`, `r`, `c`, `s`, `P-*`, `f-*`)
  remain untyped (available on all types).
- [ ] AC5 — Plugin unit tests cover: parsing `work_item_types` (valid,
  invalid, missing), allowlist filtering on all lookup methods, and the
  bundled `n`/`p`/`i` restrictions (extending `shortcut-config.test.ts` /
  `worklist.test.ts`); full ContextHub `npm test` suite passes.
- [ ] AC6 — Plugin README documents the new `work_item_types` field, its
  naming convention, and the bundled code-shortcut restriction.

> **Note:** CHANGELOG.md is excluded from the above — it is managed
> automatically by the ship skill's release pipeline.

## Constraints

- **Backward compatibility:** entries without `work_item_types` behave
  exactly as today; a missing `issueType` at lookup time must not hide any
  shortcut. No consumer project is broken by the plugin change alone.
- **Naming:** JSON uses snake_case (`work_item_types`) matching
  `code_freeze`; the TS interface uses camelCase (`workItemTypes`) matching
  `codeFreeze`.
- **Scope:** this item only adds the gating capability + restricts the three
  bundled code-workflow chords. Consumer-specific chords (podcast) live in
  consumer project-local `shortcuts.json` files (see OSL-0MSKFXM380098LFL).
- **Cross-worklog dependency:** WL ↔ OSL dependencies cannot be recorded via
  `wl dep`; tracked via description cross-references.

## Risks & assumptions

- **R1 (blast radius):** a bug in allowlist filtering could hide shortcuts
  globally. Mitigation: AC5 requires unit tests on all lookup paths plus
  backward-compat cases (no allowlist / no issueType); default behavior
  unchanged.
- **R2 (call-site plumbing):** the `issueType` must reach ~5 lookup/hint
  sites in `worklist.ts`; missing one causes inconsistent hints vs dispatch.
  Mitigation: thread it at the same places `stage` is threaded today, with
  tests for hint and dispatch paths.
- **A1:** "code related work items" = explicit allowlist `bug`, `feature`,
  `task`, `chore`, `epic` (per operator decision); `podcast` and `docs` are
  excluded.
- **A2:** the bundled restriction targets only `n`/`p`/`i` — the chords that
  dispatch the code lifecycle skills. Audit/approve/reject (`a-*`), producer
  review (`r`), and housekeeping remain available on all types per operator
  decision (hybrid model).

## Existing state

- `ShortcutEntry` (shortcut-config.ts) supports `chord`, `command`, `view`,
  `stages`, `model`, `codeFreeze`; no issue-type field.
- `fetcher.ts` already parses `issueType` onto fetched work items
  (lines 136/222) — available at selection time in the TUI.
- `worklist.ts` performs shortcut lookups at lines 1330, 1340, 2726, 2805,
  2924, passing `view`/`stage`/`codeFreezeActive` but not `issueType`.
- Bundled `src/shortcuts.json` has no `work_item_types` on any entry.
- Project-local override mechanism landed (WL-0MSHUMX5C004NC4O) — local
  `shortcuts.json` merges over bundled defaults; consumer projects can add
  type-gated chords once this field exists.

## Desired change

1. Add `workItemTypes?: string[]` to `ShortcutEntry`; parse
   `work_item_types` in `parseShortcutEntry` (log + ignore invalid, matching
   `code_freeze` handling).
2. Add an `issueType?: string` parameter to the registry lookup/filter
   methods; exclude entries whose allowlist does not include the type.
3. Thread the selected item's `issueType` through the `worklist.ts` call
   sites.
4. Add `"work_item_types": ["bug","feature","task","chore","epic"]` to the
   bundled `n`/`p`/`i` entries.
5. Extend unit tests + README; run the full test suite.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/shortcut-config.ts` — `workItemTypes` field, parsing,
  registry filtering.
- `packages/herdr/src/shortcuts.json` — `work_item_types` on `n`/`p`/`i`.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — thread `issueType` into lookups/hints.
- `packages/herdr/src/shortcut-config.test.ts` / `worklist.test.ts` — tests.
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — document the field + bundled restriction.

## Related work

- `Project-specific shortcuts.json for podcast progression (podcast-type
  gated) (OSL-0MSKFXM380098LFL)` — open_source_llm consumer item this item
  blocks; its podcast chords rely on this item's `work_item_types` support.
- `Extensible shortcuts.json: bundled defaults + project-local overrides
  (WL-0MSHUMX5C004NC4O)` — landed prerequisite providing the project-local
  merge mechanism consumer chords are defined through.
- `Add code_freeze field to herdr shortcuts.json to filter shortcut
  availability during code freeze (WL-0MSD81VEL009XHWA)` — precedent for
  adding a per-entry shortcut config field with parse/filter/tests.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1 (from OSL intake): "For the ContextHub change, how should 'code related
  work items' be defined?" — A (operator, interactive): **(a) Explicit
  allowlist** — code shortcuts only on `bug`, `feature`, `task`, `chore`,
  `epic` (everything else — e.g. `podcast`, `docs` — excluded). Source:
  interactive reply.
- Q2 (from OSL intake): "Which chords should the podcast progression
  shortcuts use?" — A (operator, interactive): **(c) Hybrid** — podcast-
  specific chords for pipeline skills (`w`, `t`, …) while keeping generic
  ones (`u-s`, `u-t`, `x-c`, `a-a`/`a-y`/`a-r`, `f-*`) available; therefore
  this item restricts only the code lifecycle chords `n`/`p`/`i`. Source:
  interactive reply.
- Q3: "Should the bundled audit (`a-*`) / producer-review (`r`) chords also
  be code-restricted?" — A (operator, via Q1/Q2 answers): no — they are
  generic and remain available on all types. Source: inferred from
  interactive answers (recorded as assumption A2).

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MQFB8N990056T8P** – [test-failure] tests/tui/controller-watch.test.ts > TuiController - Database Watch > always re-renders on watch refresh even when dataset appears unchanged (completed)
- **WL-0MP0Y4DFG007UBJJ** – E2E Agent Flow Tests & UX Parity Checklist (completed)
- **WL-0MQ3LYSPS006V60H** – TUI does not auto-refresh after CLI audit update (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — matched: add, appear, audit, chord, close, code, config, delete, docs, entries, feature, focused, freeze, gating, herdr, implement, intake, issue, item, json, keys, like, limit, non, packages, plan, plugin, podcast, producer, prompts, result, review, shortcut, shortcuts, src, stages, system, task, type, types, updates, view, work, workflow, worklist

# Auto-revert in_review items to plan_complete when marked not ready to close

## Problem Statement

When a work item in the `in_review` stage (status `completed`) is marked "not ready to close" — via `wl update <id> --audit-text "Ready to close: No"` or `wl audit-set <id> --ready-to-close no` — nothing happens to the item's lifecycle state. The item remains `completed`/`in_review`, which signals to the heartbeat and release tooling that it is awaiting closure. An item whose audit says it is *not* ready to close should no longer be presented as awaiting closure; its stage should revert to `plan_complete` so it returns to the planning queue for further work.

## Users

- **Producers / reviewers** who audit an `in_review` item, find it lacking, and mark it "not ready to close".
  - *As a producer, I want an in_review item I mark as "not ready to close" to drop out of the ready-to-close queue automatically, so it isn't swept up by heartbeat/release tooling.*
- **Agents / automation** that run audits and write `Ready to close: No` verdicts.
  - *As an agent, I want the lifecycle state to stay consistent automatically when I mark an item not ready, so I don't have to remember to reset status/stage manually.*

## Acceptance Criteria

1. When `wl update <id> --audit-text "Ready to close: No"` is run on an item with stage `in_review` (status `completed`), the item is automatically reverted to status `open` / stage `plan_complete`.
2. When `wl audit-set <id> --ready-to-close no` is run on an item with stage `in_review` (status `completed`), the item is automatically reverted to status `open` / stage `plan_complete`.
3. The item's priority is unchanged by the reversion (priority is preserved, not reset).
4. No reversion occurs when the item is not in the `in_review`/`completed` state (e.g., `done` stage, or already `open`/`in-progress`), or when the audit verdict is "Ready to close: Yes" — behavior is otherwise unchanged.
5. The reversion is reported: JSON output includes the reverted item's `from`/`to` status and stage, and human-readable output prints a summary line (e.g. `[WL-XXX reverted from completed/in_review to open/plan_complete]`), following the reporting style of the priority-downgrade cascade.
6. Unit tests cover: reversion via `--audit-text`, reversion via `audit-set`, no-op on `done` items, no-op on non-in_review items, no-op on "Ready to close: Yes", and priority preservation.
7. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, docs/AUDIT_STATUS.md, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
8. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- The reversion must only fire on the "not ready to close" verdict (`Ready to close: No` / `--ready-to-close no`), not on any other audit text.
- The transition must respect `statusStageCompatibility`: `open` status already permits `plan_complete` stage, so the target state is valid per existing rules.
- The audit write must remain best-effort; if the reversion's `db.update` fails (e.g., file lock), the command should not crash — surface a warning (mirroring the sibling demotion item's best-effort guidance).
- The audit text write path must not be blocked by the existing "skip db.update() when no fields changed" safety guard in `update.ts` — the reversion is an intentional lifecycle consequence of the audit verdict, not an accidental field change.

## Existing State

- `wl update --audit-text` writes to the `audit_results` table via `db.saveAuditResult()` in `src/commands/update.ts` (~line 219–246); a safety guard skips `db.update()` when no work-item fields changed (~line 358).
- `wl audit-set` writes the audit result in `src/commands/audit-result.ts` (~line 154–165) without touching status/stage.
- The API-level audit write path in `src/api.ts` (`normalizeUpdateInputWithAudit`, `writeAuditResult`) also persists audit results without lifecycle changes.
- `statusStageCompatibility` in `config.defaults.yaml`: `open: [idea, intake_complete, plan_complete, in_progress]` — `open`/`plan_complete` is a valid combination.
- Sibling item WL-0MSJL00P5004Y0L6 implements the same demotion pattern (`completed`/`in_review` → `open`/`plan_complete`) triggered by adding a child — same target state, different trigger, and shares the reporting convention.

## Desired Change

Implement the reversion as a shared helper (e.g., `revertToPlanComplete(item, db)` or similar) called after an audit write whenever the verdict is not-ready-to-close and the item's stage is `in_review` / status `completed`:

1. **`src/commands/update.ts`** — after a successful `db.saveAuditResult` when the parsed verdict is `Ready to close: No`, check the item state and revert if `in_review`/`completed`.
2. **`src/commands/audit-result.ts`** — in the `audit-set` action, after `db.saveAuditResult` when `--ready-to-close no`, apply the same reversion.
3. **`src/api.ts`** — decide whether the API audit write path (`writeAuditResult` / `normalizeUpdateInputWithAudit`) should also trigger the reversion for consistency; if yes, apply the same helper.
4. **Reporting** — extend JSON output with a `reverted` field (`{ from: { status, stage }, to: { status, stage } }`) and add a human summary line, following the priority-downgrade cascade style.
5. **Tests** — add unit/integration tests covering AC 1–6 (see `tests/cli/audit-results-cli.test.ts`, `tests/cli/audit.test.ts`, and any update-command test files).

## Key Files

- `src/commands/update.ts` — `--audit-text` write path; add reversion after not-ready verdict
- `src/commands/audit-result.ts` — `wl audit-set` action; add reversion after `--ready-to-close no`
- `src/api.ts` — API-level audit write path; apply reversion for consistency (decision needed)
- `src/audit.ts` — audit parsing helpers (`inspectAuditFirstLine`, `buildAuditEntry`) already produce the ready-to-close verdict
- `src/persistent-store.ts` — `saveAuditResult` / `getAuditResult`; `update` for the reversion write
- `docs/AUDIT_STATUS.md` — document the reversion behavior
- `tests/cli/audit-results-cli.test.ts`, `tests/cli/audit.test.ts` — audit CLI test coverage

## Related Work

- **WL-0MSJL00P5004Y0L6** ("Demote completed/in_review parent to plan_complete when a child is added", ContextHub, open/intake_complete) — implements the same `completed`/`in_review` → `open`/`plan_complete` demotion triggered by adding a child. This item is the mirror trigger (not-ready-to-close audit verdict). Shared helper and reporting convention; the two should not conflict.
- **WL-0MMS4EUMU15LEU7B** ("Audit Write Path (CLI/API)", ContextHub, completed) — established the audit write paths that this change hooks into.
- **WL-0MPZNK0UW009CI6C** ("Implementation: wl audit set subcommand", ContextHub, completed) — the `audit-set` command this change extends.
- **WL-0MRSGMTYU009OZCF** ("Add --audit-file to wl audit-set", ContextHub, completed) — related `audit-set` surface area.
- **WL-0MNFSCMDU0075BMH** ("Audit parser rejects valid 'Ready to close' audits; improve error message", ContextHub, completed) — the first-line audit parsing that determines the verdict.

## Risks and Assumptions

- **Scope-creep risk**: extending the reversion to the API path (`src/api.ts`) may surface API consumers that depend on audit writes not changing lifecycle state. Mitigation: if the API path proves risky, restrict reversion to the two CLI commands and record API consistency as a separate follow-up item.
- **Assumption**: "not ready to close" means exactly the audit verdict `Ready to close: No` (or `--ready-to-close no`); no other audit text triggers reversion.
- **Assumption**: reversion target is status `open` / stage `plan_complete` per user answers; priority is preserved (user answer: "the medium is for this item, for the items being reset the priority should remain unchanged").
- **Assumption**: reversion is reported in output (JSON field + human line), mirroring the priority-downgrade cascade and the sibling demotion item's reporting convention.
- **Risk**: the existing safety guard in `update.ts` ("skip db.update() when no fields changed") must be deliberately bypassed only for the intentional reversion — implement carefully to avoid accidental transitions on other audit texts.
- **Risk**: batch `wl update` over multiple ids where some are in_review will revert each qualifying item independently; must not break non-qualifying items in the same batch.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: What triggers the "not ready to close" flag — a manual `wl update --stage plan_complete` action by the producer, or automated (heartbeat/audit system detecting issues)? — Answer (user, interactive reply): "wl update command".
- Q: What happens to the item's status? Should it remain `completed` (just the stage reverts), or go back to `in_progress`/`open` so work can resume? — Answer (user, interactive reply): "open".
- Q: Priority reset? The seed intent says `--priority medium` — should this override the item's current priority? — Answer (user, interactive reply): "No the medium is for this item, for the items being reset the priority should remain unchanged" → `medium` is the priority of THIS work item; reverted items keep their priority.
- Q: Where does the "not ready to close" trigger live — Option A (setting `--audit-text "Ready to close: No"` or `wl audit-set --ready-to-close no` on an in_review item automatically reverts) or Option B (new explicit flag/command)? — Answer (user, interactive reply): "A".
- Q: When the item reverts to `open`/`plan_complete`, should status also be `in_progress` (so an agent can claim and continue immediately), or leave it `open` so it must be formally claimed first? — Answer (user, interactive reply): status is `open`; the item must be formally claimed again (consistent with the sibling demotion item WL-0MSJL00P5004Y0L6).

# Intake Draft — Create shortcut to open Pi session without prompt (WL-0MSKIL6P00045UOC)

## Problem statement

The Worklog TUI shortcut palette has `P-p` (free-form prompt via command input form) and `P-a` (audit-gaps prompt), but no way to open a brand-new, blank Pi agent session with one chord. A user who wants a fresh session must either run `pi` elsewhere or trigger a shortcut that injects prompt text. We need a chord that opens a new Pi agent pane with an **empty prompt** — blank, ready to type.

## Users

Operators who use the Worklog TUI to manage work items and want to open a clean Pi session without typing a prompt or attaching a work item.

- As a Worklog TUI user, I want to press `P n` and get a new Pi agent pane with a blank prompt, so I can start a fresh session immediately.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: A new shortcut entry with chord `P n` exists in `packages/herdr/src/shortcuts.json`: command `/prompt:` (empty prompt — no `<prompt>` placeholder, so the command-input form does NOT open), `view: both`, `model: plan`, with a label and description.
- AC2: Pressing `P n` in the Worklog TUI (list or detail view) opens a new Pi agent pane with a blank prompt, ready to type. No form dialog appears and no prompt text is injected.
- AC3: The fresh session carries no work-item context: the command contains no `<id>` placeholder, so no work-item claim happens and no pane↔item association is recorded (consistent with the existing "commands without an ID are not tracked" behavior).
- AC4: The chord is free — no collision with existing chords (`P p`, `P a`, or any other entry) — and `routeCommand('/prompt:')` returns `agent`, dispatching via the agent channel.
- AC5: Existing `P p` / `P a` behavior is unchanged.
- AC6: Unit tests updated: `packages/herdr/src/index.test.ts` binds test extended to cover `P n` (command, view, model, route), and the "free chord for /prompt: entries" test still passes with the new entry.
- AC7: `packages/herdr/README.md` (Agent-channel / prompt shortcuts section) documents the `P n` shortcut.
- AC8: Full project test suite passes with the new changes (pytest + Node, quiet mode).

## Constraints

- Follow the existing shortcut schema in `packages/herdr/src/shortcuts.json` (chord, command, view, label, description, model).
- Do not add net-new mechanisms unless required — an empty `/prompt:` command already routes to the agent channel and strips to an empty prompt via `stripAgentPromptPrefix` (see `buildSendToPiArgs` in `packages/herdr/src/index.ts`).
- No work-item claim / pane association for this shortcut (no `<id>`).
- Priority: high (user-specified).

## Existing state

- `P p` (`/prompt:<prompt>`) opens the command-input form (the `<prompt>` unknown identifier triggers `FormState`); `P a` (`/prompt:What are the audit gaps reported in the most recent audit for <id>`) injects a fixed prompt with the selected item ID substituted.
- `routeCommand` routes any command starting with `/prompt:` to the agent channel ('agent'), and `buildSendToPiArgs` strips the `/prompt:` prefix so pi receives the bare prompt text.
- The form dialog only opens when the resolved command contains unknown `<identifier>` placeholders (`hasUnknownIdentifiers`). An empty `/prompt:` command has no placeholders → dispatches immediately with no form.

## Desired change

- Add one entry to `packages/herdr/src/shortcuts.json`:

  ```json
  {
    "chord": ["P", "n"],
    "command": "/prompt:",
    "view": "both",
    "label": "new session",
    "description": "Open a new Pi agent session with a blank prompt.",
    "model": "plan"
  }
  ```

- Extend the P-chord binding test in `packages/herdr/src/index.test.ts` and update `packages/herdr/README.md`.

**Key Files:**
- `packages/herdr/src/shortcuts.json` — Add the `P n` entry (empty `/prompt:` command, model `plan`, view `both`).
- `packages/herdr/src/index.test.ts` — Extend the "binds P-p to the free-form prompt and P-a to the audit-gaps prompt" test (or add a sibling) to assert `P n` binds to `/prompt:`, view `both`, model `plan`, and routes to `agent`.
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — Document the `P n` shortcut in the agent-channel / prompt-shortcuts section.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — Verify only; `stripAgentPromptPrefix('/prompt:')` yields `''`, which flows through `buildSendToPiArgs` unchanged. No code change expected unless the empty-prompt path needs hardening.
- `packages/herdr/shared/send-to-pi.sh` — Verify only; an empty command argument still satisfies the `$# -eq 0` guard and runs `pi ''`.

## Related work

- `Add per-shortcut option to control whether a shortcut opens a command pane` (WL-0MSJLD1I70045ZUL) — open, related-to: controls pane behavior per shortcut, orthogonal to this blank-session shortcut.
- `Chord shortcut key system for Pi extension` (WL-0MQDZBKO9003CD8K) — completed; foundation for chord dispatch this entry builds on.
- Existing `P p` (free-form prompt) and `P a` (audit gaps prompt) shortcut entries in `packages/herdr/src/shortcuts.json`.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** "No project context" is satisfied by a blank prompt and no work-item association (per user answer Q2: completely fresh — no work-item, no project context). The pane still spawns in the resolved project root (`--cwd` from `send-to-pi.sh`, which requires a working directory) and `pi` will load its normal startup context; the shortcut itself injects nothing and attaches nothing.
- **Risk:** If `pi ''` with an empty quoted argument is treated as a non-empty prompt or errors, the implementation may need to omit the trailing argument in `buildSendToPiArgs`/`send-to-pi.sh` for the empty case. Mitigation: verify behavior of `send-to-pi.sh` with an empty command during implementation; add a unit test for `buildSendToPiArgs('/prompt:', ...)`.
- **Risk (scope creep):** This item is deliberately minimal (one shortcut entry + tests + docs). If a user later wants truly context-free sessions (spawn outside the project root, skip AGENTS.md), that is a separate work item — do not expand scope here.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "What should the fresh session do? (a) Open a new Pi agent pane with an empty prompt (blank, ready to type)? (b) Open a new Pi agent pane and immediately start talking to the model? (c) Something else?" — Answer (user): **(a)** blank pane, ready to type. Source: interactive reply.
- Q: "What context should the fresh session have? (a) Start completely fresh (no work-item, no project context)? (b) Inherit the currently selected work-item? (c) Include the full project context (like a normal Pi session)?" — Answer (user): **(a)** completely fresh. Source: interactive reply.
- Q: "Should this replace the existing `P p` shortcut, or use a different key combination?" — Answer (user): **use `P n`**. Source: interactive reply.
- Q: "Which model should the fresh session use? (a) default model, or (b) `plan` model matching existing P-chords?" — Answer (user): **(b)** `plan` model. Source: interactive reply.

- **WL-0MKXTCQZM1O8YCNH** – Core FTS Index (completed)
- **WL-0MLW5FR66175H8YZ** – Fix failing tests (completed)

- `.worklog/tmp/intake-draft-create-shortcut-to-open-pi-session-without-prompt-WL-0MSKIL6P00045UOC.md` — matched: create, fresh, open, opens, prompt (+2 more)
- `.worklog/worktrees/wl-WL-0MS5URWJG000A6O5-align-icons/packages/tui/extensions/README.md` — matched: create, fresh, open, opens, prompt (+2 more)
- `.worklog/worktrees/wl-WL-0MSDZ64J8005Q2JJ-grid-rebalance-python-tests-mocked-socke/CHANGELOG.md` — matched: create, fresh, open, opens, prompt (+2 more)

## Summary

The shared test runner (`skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py`) defines a static `NODE_SUITE_DIRS = ("tests/node", "tests/cli", "tests/unit")`. ContextHub has no `tests/node` directory (git ls-files confirms it was never tracked), so the canonical full-suite command `npm --silent test -- tests/node` always exits 1 with 'No test files found'.

## Impact

The audit skill's automatic full-suite verification (SA-0MSIU5HFI0024D7W) queries the per-repo test cache for EVERY canonical suite command and requires exit code 0. The permanently-failing `tests/node` entry means the audit runner can NEVER inject automatic green-run evidence for ContextHub audits — execution-dependent acceptance criteria (e.g. 'Full project test suite passes') stay `partial` and block closure.

## Workaround used in release v1.0.9

Operator ran pytest (103 passed) + `npx vitest run` (4117 passed) at the release HEAD and passed `--green-run HEAD` to each audit — honest attestation, but manual.

## Suggested fix

Either (a) filter `NODE_SUITE_DIRS` by directory existence in the shared runner, or (b) make ContextHub's suite definition explicit. Discovered during release v1.0.9 remediation (discovered-from:WL-0MSG80FQ9000C8GE).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The canonical full-suite command set for ContextHub (as resolved by `full_suite_commands()`) matches the suites that actually exist in the repo.
- [ ] `run_tests.py --summary --suite all` reports green for every suite in the canonical set at a green HEAD.

## Summary

Herdr currently renders `.podcast.md` scripts (and any `.md` Key File) in a **read-only** markdown viewer: inline `[NOTE <id>: ...]` markers (PRD §7.1) render as clickable `<id>↗` links to the note work items, but there is no way for a human reviewer to **add, edit, or delete** a note on a paragraph while reviewing the document.

This feature adds an interactive note-edit mode to the markdown viewer so a human can review any markdown document and annotate paragraphs with `[NOTE <id>: ...]` markers — not just podcasts.

## User Stories

- As a podcast producer, I want to review a `.podcast.md` script, move the cursor onto a paragraph, and press a key to add or edit an inline `[NOTE ...]` marker on that paragraph, so I can give editorial feedback without leaving Herdr.
- As a reviewer, I want to press another key to delete an existing note from a paragraph, so I can withdraw or clear feedback.
- As a user, I want this to work on any markdown file (not just podcast scripts), so I can annotate docs, wiki pages, and other `.md` content with the same mechanism.

## Expected Behaviour

1. In the markdown viewer, the cursor can move paragraph-by-paragraph (or line-based selection within a paragraph) to select the target paragraph.
2. A key chord (e.g. `n` for note) opens an input form pre-filled with the existing note text if the paragraph already has a `[NOTE <id>: ...]` marker (edit mode); otherwise empty (add mode).
3. Saving writes the marker inline in the paragraph at a stable position, following the PRD §7.1 convention `[NOTE <id>: ...]`, with `<id>` generated appropriately (Worklog note-child id when the document is linked to an episode work item; otherwise a local placeholder scheme).
4. A different key chord deletes the existing note marker from the selected paragraph.
5. The edited markdown is written back to the file.
6. Non-podcast markdown documents are supported identically.

## Suggested Implementation Approach

- Extend the existing generic markdown viewer (see the "Generic md viewer" section of `packages/herdr/README.md`) with a cursor/selection model over dialogue paragraphs and normal markdown blocks.
- Reuse the existing inline-note link rendering to detect whether the selected paragraph already carries a `[NOTE ...]` marker (edit vs add).
- Reuse the plugin's existing modal input form machinery (used for chord command placeholders) for note text entry.
- Follow the existing keybinding patterns (`shortcuts.json`, chord sequences) for the add/edit and delete keys.
- Note-child sync: when the document is a podcast script and the episode work item id is known, notes should follow the PRD §7.3 note-child lifecycle (create child work item on add, resolve/close on delete). For generic markdown this sync is skipped or handled with local ids.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] In the markdown viewer, cursor navigation can select any paragraph/block of a `.md` document.
- [ ] Pressing the add/edit key on a selected paragraph with no existing note creates an inline `[NOTE <id>: ...]` marker with the entered text.
- [ ] Pressing the add/edit key on a paragraph that already has a note opens the form pre-filled with the current note text; saving updates the marker in place.
- [ ] Pressing the delete key on a paragraph with a note removes the marker from the file.
- [ ] The edited document is persisted to disk and the viewer reflects the change.
- [ ] Behaviour works identically for any markdown file, not only podcast scripts.
- [ ] Existing inline-note link rendering (`<id>↗`) still works after edits.
- [ ] When editing a podcast script with a known episode id, note-child work items are created/resolved per PRD §7.3.
- [ ] Automated tests cover add, edit, delete, and persistence for both podcast and generic markdown documents.

## References

- `packages/herdr/README.md` — "Generic md viewer" and "Inline note links" sections (current read-only behaviour)
- Related work: WL-0MSGTLSUT002NF29 (Related Docs row + open in viewer), WL-0MSGEA9AY0080V4Q (md viewer path resolution), WL-0MSKFFJWD002BQJ5 (proper markdown renderer), WL-0MSHWHULZ001FL8I (detail view ToC)
- `.pi/skills/wiki-podcast-script/SKILL.md` — `[NOTE <id>: ...]` marker convention (PRD §7.1) and note-child lifecycle (PRD §7.3) in open_source_llm

## Summary

`wl sync`'s merge logic can enter a self-sustaining conflict loop that silently corrupts item state. Observed in the field (LP-0MSDRRPV0001TCLX in /home/rgardler/projects/llm): a completed, audit-approved item's local `updatedAt` advanced at every sync (21:36:19Z → 21:53:40Z → 21:57:35Z) and the final sync chose a local `deleted` state (empty `deletedBy`/`deleteReason`) over the remote `open` state — soft-deleting the item while the remote `worklog/data` ref still had it `open`/`plan_complete`. No agent ran `wl delete`; the state arose purely from merge behavior. The item had to be manually restored via `StatusLifecycle`.

## Root-cause hypothesis (verified against src/sync.ts)

1. **Same-timestamp merge bumps `updatedAt` unconditionally.** `mergeSameTimestampItems` (src/sync.ts ~L423) sets `merged.updatedAt = new Date().toISOString()` whenever local and remote have the same `updatedAt` but different content (e.g. a `sortIndex` conflict from concurrent `wl re-sort`, or any divergent field). This bump makes the item *newer* than the remote on the next sync, so the local value keeps winning and the timestamp keeps advancing on every sync — a conflict loop with no real user edit behind it. Under auto-sync / multi-pane / multi-agent use this can repeat indefinitely.

2. **Unattributed soft-delete wins over a live remote item.** `deleteSingle` (node_modules/@worklog/shared/src/database.ts) sets `status: 'deleted'` but leaves `deletedBy`/`deleteReason` empty. In `mergeDifferentTimestampItems`, `status` is resolved by plain timestamp recency: `status='deleted'` is a non-default value, so if the local copy is (artifactually) newer, `status` flips to `deleted` even though `deletedBy`/`deleteReason` are empty — silently soft-deleting an item the remote still considers open. There is no delete-side equivalent of the close-preservation logic that protects `status='completed'`/`stage='done'`.

## Expected behaviour

- Repeated syncs of the same divergent state must converge: once both sides hold the merged item, `updatedAt` must stop advancing and the item must not flip-flop.
- An unattributed delete marker (status='deleted' with empty deletedBy/deleteReason) must never override a remote item that is open/in-progress/completed. Deletes should only propagate when they are real, attributed deletes (non-empty deletedBy or deleteReason), mirroring the close-preservation model.

## Suggested approach

- In `mergeSameTimestampItems`, only bump `updatedAt` when the merge actually changed a user-visible field (or converge without bumping when the merged result equals one side). Consider whether `sortIndex` conflicts alone should bump at all.
- Add delete-side protection in `mergeDifferentTimestampItems` (and same-timestamp path): treat `status='deleted'` like `status='completed'` — require the delete to be the newer change AND attributed (deletedBy/deleteReason non-empty) before propagating it; otherwise keep the remote live status.
- Add regression tests in tests/sync.test.ts reproducing both failure modes.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1: Regression test: two divergent copies with the same `updatedAt` (differing only in `sortIndex` or one metadata field) synced repeatedly converge — `updatedAt` stops advancing after the merged state is present on both sides (no unbounded bumping).
- AC2: Regression test: local `status='deleted'` with empty `deletedBy`/`deleteReason` vs remote `status='open'` — merge keeps the remote `open` state (or at minimum never produces a soft-deleted item with no attribution).
- AC3: Regression test: an *attributed* delete (non-empty `deletedBy`) that is newer than the remote still propagates (delete remains possible when intentional).
- AC4: Full existing test suite (npm test) passes with no regressions.
data.title: Fix sync-conflict loop: same-timestamp merge bumps updatedAt indefinitely and unattributed soft-delete wins over remote open item

## Goal

As a herdr downtime worker, I want idle detection to reflect LOCAL model activity only, so that remote provider streams (opencode-go → deepseek-v4-flash) — which consume zero local slots — do not prevent downtime dispatch.

## Background

Follow-up to RCA WL-0MSK9TUCA00206M7. The proxy's /llama/local/status `active_query` is the GLOBAL counter = any request in flight (local + remote). herdr's parseLlamaStatus() (packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts) maps `active_query` directly, and isIdleStatus() returns false whenever it is true. Live evidence: status active_query=true with 3/3 slots free, no lease, while the only streams in flight are provider=opencode-go (remote). Local Qwen3 is idle but herdr never sees idle.

The proxy is adding `local_active_query` (derived from its local_active_queries counter) — see LP-0MSL2ZLLS009RVKR (llm-manager worklog). This task makes herdr consume it.

## Expected behaviour

1. parseLlamaPayload accepts `local_active_query` (bool) when present and prefers it for idle evaluation when the field exists; falls back to `active_query` when absent (backward compatible with pre-fix proxies).
2. isIdleStatus uses the LOCAL signal — remote-only traffic no longer blocks dispatch.
3. When `local_active_query` is absent, no behavior change (uses active_query path).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] parseLlamaPayload derives/uses local_active_query when present
- [ ] isIdleStatus returns TRUE with local_active_query=false + 3/3 free slots during remote-only traffic (integration test against a stub status payload)
- [ ] isIdleStatus returns FALSE with local_active_query=true (local busy)
- [ ] Backward compatible: payloads without local_active_query behave exactly as today (unit tests unchanged pass)
- [ ] Docs: the LlamaStatus interface comment documents the field semantics

## Related (cross-repo)

- LLM-manager: LP-0MSL2ZLLS009RVKR exposes local_active_query in the payload (this work item must land together or sequence after it; herdr falls back safely either way)
- Parent RCA: WL-0MSK9TUCA00206M7
- related-to:LP-0MSL2ZLLS009RVKR, LP-0MSL1OX51003DOP4
