# Intake Draft — Herdr selection list: collapsible group headings with item counts

**Work item:** WL-0MSL5MPSZ003TG94

## Problem statement

The Herdr work-item selection list renders group separators (`── Group 1 ──`, `── Idea ──`, `── In Review ──`) between items, but these heading rows are pure chrome: they carry no item count, they cannot be collapsed to hide a group's items, and up/down navigation skips over them entirely (the cursor can never land on a heading). With several groups on screen this wastes vertical space and gives the user no way to focus on one group.

## Users

- **Herdr plugin users** (operators running the work-item selection list pane).

User stories:
- "As a producer reviewing the worklist, I want each group heading to show how many items it contains, so I can see at a glance where the bulk of the work is."
- "As a producer, I want to collapse a group by pressing Tab while its heading is selected, so I can hide items I'm not interested in and focus on the rest."
- "As a producer, I want up/down navigation to land on heading rows, so I can reach them to collapse/expand them."

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: Each group heading row displays the label plus the number of items in that group (e.g. `── Group 1 (4) ──`). The count reflects the top-level items assigned to the group in the current view (post stage-filter), regardless of collapse state.
- AC2: Up/down navigation (j/k and arrow keys) moves the selection onto heading rows as well as items; headings are no longer skipped. Page up/down, first/last, and wrap-around behave consistently with the heading rows included.
- AC3: Pressing Tab while a heading row is selected toggles that group's collapse state: collapsed hides the group's items from both the render and navigation; expanded shows them. Tab on an item row keeps its existing expand/collapse-children behaviour unchanged.
- AC4: Collapsed-group state lives in memory for the session (like `expandedItems`), survives list refreshes, and does not persist across pane restarts.
- AC5: When a heading is selected, the metadata panel shows the group info (label + count) rather than stale item metadata; Enter on a heading is a no-op (only Tab toggles).
- AC6: The `rows - 1` line-count invariant, code-freeze banner, metadata-panel sizing, and stage-filter views keep working; full Herdr test suite (vitest for packages/herdr) passes.
- AC7: All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments and any relevant docs site entries.

## Constraints

- The change is confined to the Herdr plugin (`packages/herdr`) — the Pi TUI Worklog extension has its own browse implementation and is out of scope.
- `packages/herdr` has zero npm dependencies; the implementation must stay self-contained (the existing duplicated `grouping.ts` pattern).
- Tab already toggles hierarchy expand/collapse for items with children — that behaviour must not regress.
- The renderer must never exceed `rows - 1` lines (pane line-count invariant, WL-0MSAAON63003N6LO).

## Existing state

- Group separators are rendered by `createListRenderer` in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` when the `group` field changes between items in the flattened list; they are derived at render time and are NOT rows in any navigation model.
- Navigation (`WorkItemListState.moveUp/moveDown/pageUp/pageDown`, `_clampSelection`, `_adjustScroll`, `flatCount`) indexes into the flattened items list, so headings are never selected.
- Tab maps to the `'toggle-expand'` action (`keyToAction`), which expands/collapses top-level items with children; the main TUI loop fetches children on demand for that action.
- Group assignments come from `regroupWorkItems` (packages/herdr/src/grouping.ts), which stamps every selected item with a numeric `group` and a `groupLabel` (`Critical Group N`, `Group N`, `Idea`, `Other`, `In Review`).

## Desired change

Introduce a first-class **display-rows model** in `WorkItemListState` that interleaves heading rows with item rows:

- New heading entry type (e.g. `{ kind: 'heading', group, groupLabel, count, collapsed }`) produced by a `getDisplayRows()`-style method over the flattened items (children of expanded parents included; items of collapsed groups excluded).
- Navigation, clamping, and scrolling operate over display rows so the cursor lands on headings; `getSelectedItem()` returns `null` for a heading selection (metadata panel then renders group info).
- New collapsed-groups state (`Set<number>` in memory) with toggle on Tab when a heading row is selected; refresh carries the set over (by group number, mirroring `expandedItems` handling).
- `createListRenderer` renders heading rows directly from the display model (label + `(count)` + collapse arrow) and stops deriving separators from group transitions; the visible-window budget logic (`countSeparators`) is reworked for heading rows.
- Tab routing: heading row → toggle group; item row → existing expand/collapse-children path (including the on-demand children fetch in the TUI loop).

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — display-rows model, heading type, collapse state, navigation over rows, Tab routing, renderer heading rows + counts.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` — heading rendering (counts, collapse arrow), navigation onto/over headings, Tab toggle, metadata panel on heading selection.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist-expand-refresh.test.ts` — collapsed groups survive refresh; Tab-on-item children fetch unaffected.

## Assumptions

- "Headings" = the group separator rows (`── <Group Label> ──`) produced by `regroupWorkItems` group assignments. No other heading type exists in the list.
- Count = top-level items in the group in the current view; children of expanded parents do not add to the count (they never carry group metadata).
- Count is shown whether the group is collapsed or expanded.
- Enter on a heading is a no-op; Tab is the only toggle key (per request).
- Collapsed state is in-memory only, consistent with `expandedItems` (no settings persistence).
- Collapse keyed by group number; if a refresh regroups and renumbers groups, the collapsed set may apply to a shifted group — acceptable in-session, same class of behaviour as `expandedItems`.
- **Scope-creep risk:** extending this to the Pi TUI Worklog extension or persisting collapse state to settings would expand scope — record such follow-ups as separate work items rather than folding them in.
- **Regression risk:** reworking the navigation model from `flatCount` (items only) to display rows touches clamping, scroll adjustment, wrap-around, refresh selection-restore, and the renderer's line budget — the existing expand/refresh and line-count tests must stay green.

## Related work

- WL-0MSAK8YLB0025EGW — Herdr plugin: fix work item list grouping (duplicate In Review sections, wrong group order): introduced the render-time group separators this feature builds on.
- WL-0MSAKPVR9005B6XJ — Rewrite assignItemGroups + next.ts ordering: canonical group ordering/labelling used by the headings.
- WL-0MS8XOOMN0022LLH — Pi TUI browse flow: re-fetch + heading count: heading counts exist in the Pi TUI browse widget; Herdr parity for counts.
- WL-0MS4L81QF0013081 — Tab key to expand/collapse children in selection browser: established the Tab expand/collapse pattern this feature extends.
- WL-0MSBVBNGH002RDP5 — Herdr worklist: expanded items momentarily collapse on list refresh (flicker): refresh/children handling this feature must preserve.
- WL-0MSAAON63003N6LO — pane line-count invariant (renderer budget) this feature's heading-row accounting must preserve.
- WL-0MS39YPR5005MJ81 — Feature gap analysis: Pi TUI Worklog extension vs Herdr plugin: prior comparison of the two selection lists (find_related automated match).

Automated find_related report: full (untruncated) version persisted at `.worklog/tmp/find-related-full-WL-0MSL5MPSZ003TG94.md`.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: Should up/down navigation land on heading rows? — Answer (operator): the request notes "moving up and down does not select the heading lines" as the current gap; selectable headings are required for Tab-on-heading to work, so the feature includes heading selection. Source: interactive request.
- Q: What does the count show? — Answer (assumption documented, no question asked): top-level items in the group, current view, both collapsed and expanded. Source: reasonable default consistent with the data model.
- Q: Should collapsed state persist across restarts? — Answer (assumption documented, no question asked): no — in-memory like `expandedItems`. Source: consistent with existing hierarchy expand state.

# Downtime dispatcher triggers multiple identical sessions

**Headline:** The herdr downtime worker re-dispatches the same work item more than once. The audit tier selects an already-dispatched item again because the dispatched `/skill:audit` run reverts the item to `completed`/`in_review` without recording a fresh audit, re-exposing it to the candidate query. Fix: exclude items already dispatched by the downtime worker (durable dispatched-marker) from audit-tier selection.

## Problem statement

The herdr downtime worker (`dispatchDowntimeWork` in `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts`) dispatched the same work item for `/skill:audit` **twice**: `WL-0MSGTLSUT002NF29` at `2026-08-09T01:51:29Z` and again at `2026-08-09T10:59:50Z` (both entries in `.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log`). The item has no valid audit (`auditResult: None`, `auditedAt: None`), so it remains a candidate. Mechanism: the audit tier selects from `wl list --status completed --stage in_review`; the dispatched audit run's verdict lifecycle transitions the item status back to `completed` (stage stays `in_review`) when it finishes, and with no fresh audit recorded the item re-enters the candidate set and is re-dispatched on the next idle window. The plan (`intake_complete → /skill:plan`) and intake (`idea → /skill:intake`) tiers self-guard via stage transitions, so the duplicate is audit-tier-specific.

## Users

- **Operators running herdr worklist panes with the downtime worker enabled** — want at most one automatic dispatch per work item per skill; duplicate sessions waste local-LLM time and create confusing repeated agent panes.
- **User story:** "As an operator, when the downtime worker dispatches `/skill:audit` on an item, I want that item never to be auto-dispatched again (until a human or a fresh audit resolves it), so I don't get multiple identical agent sessions for the same item."

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **Durable exclusion (regression for the observed duplicate):** `getNextAuditCandidate`/`selectAuditCandidate` never returns an item that was already dispatched by the herdr downtime worker when no fresh valid audit exists since that dispatch. Verified by a unit test reproducing the `WL-0MSGTLSUT002NF29` scenario: an item present in the shared dispatch log (`.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log`) with `auditedAt`/`updatedAt` not fresh is excluded, even though it is `completed`/`in_review`.
- [ ] **Composes with audit freshness:** the marker exclusion only suppresses re-dispatch when the item has no fresh audit since its last dispatch; an item whose most recent audit is fresh is governed by the existing `isAuditFresh` logic (fresh → not a candidate, unchanged).
- [ ] **Marker lookup is fail-safe:** a missing or unreadable dispatch log is treated as empty (audit-tier dispatch still works on a fresh worklog); malformed JSONL lines are skipped without failing the lookup or the dispatch.
- [ ] **Scope:** the exclusion applies to the audit tier only; plan/intake tier selection behaviour is unchanged.
- [ ] **End-to-end:** with a single unaudited `completed`/`in_review` candidate and two consecutive idle windows (no audit recorded between), the worker dispatches exactly once.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, `packages/herdr/README.md` (downtime section), and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Fail-closed dispatch philosophy** (existing module contract): the worker must never dispatch on ambiguous signals and must never crash; logging/lookup failures must be contained. The marker lookup failure mode is deliberately fail-*safe* (allow dispatch on unreadable log) because a missing log is the normal first-run state — blocking dispatch on it would silently disable the audit tier.
- **Durability across status changes:** the marker must survive the item's status reverting to `completed`/`in_review` (the root cause of the re-selection) — a status-based check alone is insufficient.
- **Shared per-worklog root:** all panes using the same worklog root share `.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log` (the `--worklog-dir` override, WL-0MSI7DQL10016QYX), so the log-based marker covers same-root multi-pane setups. The log is bounded (`DOWNTIME_LOG_MAX_ENTRIES = 100`); protection windows beyond the roll are out of scope for this item (noted as a risk).
- The existing pre-dispatch claim (`wl update <id> --status in_progress`) and `wl next`'s default exclusion of in-progress items remain unchanged — per the operator's scoping decision this item does **not** rework the claim path (option A, not C).

## Existing state

- `dispatchDowntimeWork` already claims the item (`claimItem` → `wl update <id> --status in_progress --assignee Map`) before the pane spawns, and `wl next` excludes `in_progress` items by default (`filterCandidates`, `includeInProgress=false`). These protect against the same-instant cross-pane race but not against the observed 9-hour re-selection.
- `getNextAuditCandidate` (packages/herdr/src/index.ts) runs `wl list --status completed --stage in_review --json` and `selectAuditCandidate` picks the first item without a fresh audit (`isAuditFresh`), modified within `DOWNTIME_AUDIT_RECENCY_WINDOW_MS` (7 days), sorted by `sortIndex`. There is no exclusion of previously dispatched items.
- Dispatches are already logged durably per worklog root: `appendDowntimeLogEntry` (packages/herdr/src/downtime-log.ts) writes JSONL entries (`itemId`, `kind`, `dispatchedAt`, `cwd`, `title`) to `<cwd>/.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log`; a per-item comment ("Auto-dispatched by the herdr downtime worker…") is added via `wl comment add` and is the durable cross-machine trail.
- Evidence: `WL-0MSGTLSUT002NF29` in `.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log` at 01:51:29Z and 10:59:50Z (2026-08-09); item currently `in-progress`/`in_review` with `auditResult: None`.

## Desired change

1. **Add a dispatched-marker exclusion to the audit tier.** In `selectAuditCandidate` (or its caller `getNextAuditCandidate`), exclude candidates whose `itemId` has a downtime-dispatch marker and no fresh audit since. Preferred marker source: the shared rolling dispatch log `.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log` (same worklog root; already written on every dispatch; `dispatchedAt` available for the "since" comparison). The per-item `herdr-downtime` worklog comment is the documented durable cross-machine trail and is the fallback/alternative if a field or comment-based marker is preferred during implementation. The exclusion must compose with `isAuditFresh` (fresh audit → item already excluded by existing logic).
2. **Parse the marker fail-safely.** Missing/unreadable log → empty; malformed lines skipped; no throw, no dispatch-blocking side effects.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Bounded log roll (`DOWNTIME_LOG_MAX_ENTRIES = 100`):** if an item sits unaudited while the log rolls past 100 dispatches, the marker is lost and the item could be re-selected. Acceptable for the observed recurrence window (hours); documenting the bound and, if cheap, preferring the durable per-item comment marker (or a field/comment-based marker) mitigates. Out of scope to extend the log bound unless trivially safe.
- **Cross-host duplicates:** the log is per-worklog-root on a single host; two hosts sharing a worklog root over the network could still double-dispatch. The observed duplicate is same-host; cross-host protection (via the synced per-item comment) is a noted extension, not required by this item.
- **Assumption — the exclusion is audit-tier-only.** Plan/intake tiers self-guard via stage transitions; no change to their selection.
- **Scope-creep guard:** claim hardening (verified/atomic claim) and audit-lifecycle changes were explicitly out of scope (operator chose option A). If implementation surfaces a need for them, capture as a new work item rather than expanding this one.
- **Fail-safe lookup:** treating an unreadable/missing log as empty means a corrupted log cannot silently disable the audit tier; the trade-off (a corrupted log also cannot exclude anything) is acceptable.

## Key Files:

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — `selectAuditCandidate` gains the dispatched-marker exclusion; doc comment updates for the audit-tier selection contract.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — `getNextAuditCandidate` reads the dispatch log (or passes it in) and applies the exclusion; wiring stays fail-closed.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-log.ts` — possibly a read helper for the bounded log (e.g., `readDowntimeLogEntries`); currently only `appendDowntimeLogEntry` exists.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts` / `downtime-worker.fixtures.ts` — regression tests: duplicate-scenario exclusion, fail-safe lookup, composition with `isAuditFresh`, single-dispatch end-to-end.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-log.test.ts` — fail-safe `readDowntimeLogEntries` tests (missing/unreadable log → empty; malformed JSONL lines skipped).
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — downtime worker docs: audit-tier selection now excludes previously dispatched items.

## Related work

- `WL-0MSGTLSUT002NF29` — the item observed duplicated (dispatched twice for audit, 2026-08-09). Evidence source for this bug.
- `WL-0MSI8H3HP000K0RG` — audit-tier dispatch (parent of the tier logic that re-selects items).
- `WL-0MSGPI4AR000YOK8` — dispatch audit logging (the `.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log` the marker will parse).
- `WL-0MSI9FDPI005Z0BV` — audit-tier downtime dispatch tests (extend with the re-dispatch regression).
- `WL-0MSI7DQL10016QYX` — per-worklog-dir candidate selection (why the shared log is per worklog root).
- `WL-0MSIAOFI70075REE` — unify audit-freshness at-or-near logic across icon display and downtime dispatcher (open; related freshness logic).
- `WL-0MSK9TUCA00206M7` — RCA of zero-dispatch night; documents the multi-pane poller environment where duplicates can occur.
- `WL-0MSG7ZTC000163FL` — Downtime worker test suite (test-first); the suite this fix extends with the re-dispatch regression.

### Related work (automated report)

See the automated find_related report in the item's edit history; high-signal additions beyond the curated list above: `WL-0MSG4NMF0000YBRP` (timer consolidation) and `WL-0MSJIPHD0001L1J9` (dispatch-task wedge robustness).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "The observed duplicate is audit-tier-only: a dispatched audit run reverts the item to `completed`/`in_review` without a fresh audit, so it becomes selectable again. Hardening the claim (verified + never-select-in-progress) prevents the cross-pane race but **not** this re-selection. How should the guard prevent re-dispatch of an item the downtime worker has already dispatched for audit? (A) Durable dispatched-marker exclusion — audit tier skips items already dispatched by the downtime worker (e.g., parsed from the shared `.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log`, or a per-item marker), unless a fresh audit exists since. Stays entirely in the dispatcher. (B) Lifecycle change — dispatched audit runs keep the item `in_progress` until a valid audit is recorded (touches the audit skill/AGENTS.md workflow, not just the dispatcher). (C) Both A + verified claim hardening." — Answer (user): **"A"** — durable dispatched-marker exclusion, dispatcher-scoped, no claim-path rework, no lifecycle change. Source: interactive reply (intake session).
- Note: The user's original suggestions (mark in_progress on dispatch; never select in_progress) were investigated — both already exist in the code (`claimItem` before pane spawn; `wl next` excludes in-progress by default) but do not prevent the audit-tier re-selection; the dispatched-marker exclusion (option A) closes that gap.

## Plan: changelog

- 2026-08-09T13:29:40Z — `/skill:plan` (session 019fe6b1-e8a7-705f-9cc5-4e9673957c2c): created child features **1. Regression tests for audit-tier re-dispatch exclusion** (test-first) and **2. Dispatched-marker exclusion in audit-tier selection**; dependency edge F2←F1; approval gate passed (risk Medium, operator approved); six automated review stages run — Stage 2 (completeness) added `packages/herdr/src/downtime-log.test.ts` to Key Files. Effort/risk estimate retained from intake (Small / Medium — scope unchanged).

# Regression tests for audit-tier re-dispatch exclusion

**Summary:** Extend the herdr downtime test suite to lock down the duplicate-dispatch regression (WL-0MSGTLSUT002NF29), fail-safe marker lookup, composition with audit freshness, and single-dispatch end-to-end behavior. Test-first foundation for the dispatched-marker exclusion (parent WL-0MSLIY8ZR004QUSY).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Reproduces the `WL-0MSGTLSUT002NF29` scenario: an item present in the shared dispatch log (`.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log`, `kind: audit`) with no fresh audit is excluded from audit-candidate selection, even though it is `completed`/`in_review`.
- [ ] Fresh audit → item is not a candidate (existing `isAuditFresh` behavior unchanged); stale/absent audit + `kind: audit` dispatch marker → excluded.
- [ ] `kind: plan` / `kind: intake` log markers do NOT suppress audit-tier selection (audit-tier-only scope guard).

None — foundation for parent WL-0MSLIY8ZR004QUSY implementation. Blocks: Dispatched-marker exclusion in audit-tier selection.

# Dispatched-marker exclusion in audit-tier selection

**Summary:** Add a fail-safe read helper for the rolling dispatch log and exclude items the downtime worker has already dispatched for `/skill:audit` from audit-tier candidate selection (parent WL-0MSLIY8ZR004QUSY, option A — dispatcher-scoped, no claim-path rework). Closes the re-selection loop where a dispatched audit run reverts the item to `completed`/`in_review` without a fresh audit.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `readDowntimeLogEntries(cwd)` returns `[]` on a missing or unreadable dispatch log and skips malformed JSONL lines without throwing (fail-safe — dispatch is never blocked by a log failure).
- [ ] `selectAuditCandidate` excludes candidates whose `itemId` has an audit-kind dispatch marker; composes with `isAuditFresh` (fresh audit → not a candidate, unchanged).
- [ ] `getNextAuditCandidate` loads the marker set from `<cwd>/.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log` (filtered to `kind === 'audit'`) and applies the exclusion; plan/intake tier selection is unchanged.
- [ ] All regression tests from WL-0MSLUANM5004NNPU pass; full project test suite green.
- [ ] Documentation updated: code comments (audit-tier selection contract), `packages/herdr/README.md` downtime section.

## Minimal Implementation

- `readDowntimeLogEntries(cwd)` in `packages/herdr/src/downtime-log.ts` (parse JSONL, skip malformed lines, missing/unreadable → `[]`, never throw).
- Optional exclusion parameter (e.g. `Set<string>` of audit-kind dispatched itemIds) on `selectAuditCandidate` in `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — keeps the pure function deterministic and injectable.
- Wiring in `getNextAuditCandidate` (`packages/herdr/src/index.ts`): read log, build marker set, pass to selection; keep fail-closed semantics.
- README + code-comment updates.

## Dependencies

Prereq: WL-0MSLUANM5004NNPU (regression tests, test-first).

## Deliverables

- Code changes in `downtime-log.ts`, `downtime-worker.ts`, `index.ts`; docs in README; green test suite.

# Feature Request: `--fields` field-selection for `wl list` / `wl search`

## Problem statement

`wl list` and `wl search` return full work-item records (or compact snippets for search), with no way to request only the fields a caller needs. Full-record dumps are the root cause of token waste documented in SA-0MSLVQMKF000ESPZ (SorraAgents): bare `wl list --json` = 5.3 MB / 1,861 records; `wl list --status completed` = 4.9 MB; scripts (ship gates, triage, code-review) download tens-to-hundreds of KB of fields they never read (e.g. full descriptions) when they only need `id`, `title`, `status`, `stage`, `priority`.

## User stories

- As a release-gate script, I want `wl list --stage in_review --fields id,title,status,stage,needsProducerReview --json` so I stop downloading 4.9 MB of descriptions I discard.
- As an agent running `/skill:audit`, I want a compact project-status query (`--fields id,title,status,stage,priority`) so the worklog overview stays in the low-KB range.
- As a triage helper, I want `wl list --priority critical --tags test-failure --fields id,title,description --json` so my match heuristics get exactly the fields they need.

## Expected behaviour

- New option on `wl list` and `wl search`: `--fields <comma-separated>` (e.g. `id,title,status,stage,priority`).
- Output objects contain ONLY the requested fields (plus `id` always, for usability); unknown field names are rejected with a clear error listing valid fields.
- `wl list` and `wl search` share the same field vocabulary: id, title, description, status, stage, priority, issueType, assignee, tags, createdAt, updatedAt, parentId, needsProducerReview, sortIndex, audit fields (as applicable).
- `--json` output shape unchanged (same keys; omitted fields absent). Human output uses the same projection for concise display.
- Aliases: `-f` as shorthand is acceptable; must not clash with existing flags (`-F/--format` already taken — use long-only or another short letter).

## Suggested implementation approach

1. Add `--fields` parsing (comma-split, validate against a known field list) in `dist/commands/list.js` and `dist/commands/search.js`.
2. Apply projection in the JSON serialization layer (single helper, e.g. `pickFields(item, fields)` in a shared module) so list, search, and future commands stay consistent.
3. Search snippet/score fields remain when `--semantic` is used; `--fields` applies to the item object only.
4. Unit tests: field whitelist validation, unknown-field rejection, id always present, search+list parity.

## Acceptance criteria

1. `wl list --fields id,title --json` returns objects with only id/title; verified for filters and bare queries.
2. `wl search <term> --fields id,title,status --json` returns compact objects with only those fields.
3. Invalid field names produce a non-zero exit and a clear error listing valid fields.
4. Output size reduction verified: `wl list --stage in_review --fields id,title --json` is smaller than the full-record equivalent (target: ≥90% reduction for the completed-status case cited above).
5. Existing output without `--fields` is unchanged (backward compatible); full test suite passes.

## Related work

- related-to: SA-0MSLVQMKF000ESPZ (SorraAgents) — token-waste audit of `wl list` usage; this option is the root-cause fix it proposes as the ideal outcome.
- See AGENTS.md (SorraAgents) `wl list` guidance: term + filter discipline, and the measured payload sizes it cites.

# Feature Request / Bug: FTS index freshness + silent query-error swallowing

## Problem statement

`wl search` help advertises "Full-text search over work items (title, description, comments, tags)" — and comment indexing is implemented and *works after a manual rebuild* (verified: column-scoped `comments:"Closed with reason"` MATCH returns rows; 1,567/2,462 indexed rows contain comment text; `wl search '"v0.1.11"'` returns comment matches). Two defects make comment search unreliable in practice:

1. **The FTS index is never updated incrementally.** `upsertFtsEntry(item)` (dist/persistent-store.js:963) is defined but has **zero call sites** — it is dead code. `saveWorkItem` / `saveComment` do not touch `worklog_fts`. The index only refreshes via the manual `wl search --rebuild-index` command. Any work item or comment created/edited since the last rebuild is invisible to search — silently stale results (recent items/comments missing, duplicates not detected by triage heuristics).

2. **Malformed FTS5 queries fail silently.** An unquoted punctuated query such as `wl search v0.1.11` produces an FTS5 syntax error (`fts5: syntax error near "."`) that the catch block (persistent-store.js ~1157) swallows, returning `[]` with no warning. Users cannot distinguish "no matches" from "invalid query". Version strings, file paths, and ids (all common search targets in this tool) are exactly the strings that trip this.

## User stories

- As an agent deduplicating test-failure work items, I want recently added comments and items to appear in `wl search` without requiring a manual `--rebuild-index`, so I don't create duplicates.
- As a user searching for `v0.1.11` or a file path, I want either correct matches or an explicit "invalid query" error, not a silent empty result.

## Expected behaviour

- Creating/updating a work item or adding/deleting a comment keeps the FTS index current (call `upsertFtsEntry` from the save paths; call `deleteFtsEntry` from item/comment delete paths).
- FTS5 query syntax errors are surfaced to the user (non-zero exit + clear message), not swallowed; only genuinely zero-match queries return empty results.
- Consider quoting/escaping hygiene: document (and optionally auto-quote) punctuated terms; an option like `--rebuild-index` remains as the backstop for bulk migrations.
- Optional: automatic index rebuild (or per-item reindex) when the index is detected empty/stale (e.g. hash-based staleness already used for embeddings).

## Suggested implementation approach

1. Wire `upsertFtsEntry` into `saveWorkItem` (dist/persistent-store.js:299) and into `saveComment`/comment-delete paths (comments currently don't trigger any FTS update at all).
2. Change `searchFts`'s catch block to rethrow/flag syntax errors (or validate the query with a dry MATCH first) so the command layer can report `error: invalid query syntax` with the offending term.
3. Add unit tests: new item searchable immediately after save; new comment searchable immediately after add; punctuated query error surfaces; delete removes from index.

## Acceptance criteria

1. After `wl create` + `wl comment add`, both the title and the comment text are found by `wl search` WITHOUT running `--rebuild-index`.
2. `wl search v0.1.11` (unquoted punctuated term) exits non-zero with a clear "invalid query — quote phrases" message instead of silently returning 0.
3. Deleting an item/comment removes it from subsequent search results.
4. `wl search --rebuild-index` still works as the manual backstop; full test suite passes.

## Related work

- related-to: SA-0MSLVQMKF000ESPZ (SorraAgents) — its analysis assumed comments were not searchable; this request resolves that gap and would enable comment-based remediation queries (e.g. `shipped in v1.0.0` close-reason sweep).
- related-to: WL-0MSLW8GHQ0092PJK — `--fields` projection for list/search; both improve wl CLI efficiency.
data.title: FTS search: keep index fresh (wire upsertFtsEntry into save paths) and surface query syntax errors

# Downtime audit-tier wl failure silently collapses to null

**discovered-from:** WL-0MSKUG2WW0058A7W (audit gap AC3, follow-up 1 of 3)

## Problem

The downtime worker's audit tier swallows wl failures as if the tier were empty. `getNextAuditCandidate` (packages/herdr/src/index.ts:389-391) returns `null` in its catch block for ANY wl CLI error or unparseable output — identical to a genuinely empty audit tier (`packages/herdr/src/index.ts:374`). The caller `dispatchDowntimeWork` (packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts:523) cannot distinguish the two, so:

- An audit-tier wl failure counts as NO strike (the three-strike rule never fires for it — only plan/intake-tier failures do).
- No log entry is written — the failure is invisible.
- The worker falls through to the plan tier and appears healthy even when the audit query is persistently broken (e.g. a wl failure specific to `wl list --status completed --stage in_review`), silently disabling the audit dispatch tier forever.

Contrast: the plan/intake tiers use `DowntimeNextResult` with an `ok:false` channel that the worker counts as a CLI-error strike (downtime-worker.ts:555-566). The audit tier has no error channel.

## User story

"As an operator, when the downtime audit tier's wl lookup fails, I want that failure to be observable (a strike or a log entry) rather than silently treated as 'no audit candidates', so a persistently broken audit tier cannot silently stop producing audits."

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `getNextAuditCandidate` distinguishes a wl/parse failure from a genuinely empty tier (returns an error outcome, not `null`).
- [ ] An audit-tier failure counts toward the three-strike rule (or otherwise leaves a durable trace via recordError) instead of silently falling through.
- [ ] Unit tests cover: failure → strike/log; empty → no-candidate behavior unchanged; success path unchanged.
- [ ] packages/herdr/README.md failure-path logging section updated to reflect the fixed behavior.

## Key Files

- packages/herdr/src/index.ts:356-391 (getNextAuditCandidate)
- packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts:523, 555-566 (dispatch + strike handling)
- packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts (tests)

# Downtime claim failure discarded — dispatch proceeds and is recorded as success

**discovered-from:** WL-0MSKUG2WW0058A7W (audit gap AC3, follow-up 2 of 3)

## Problem

The downtime worker's pre-dispatch claim is best-effort with the result discarded. The `claimItem` dep (packages/herdr/src/index.ts:393-396) calls `claimWorkItem` (packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts:599-610 — never throws; returns `{ success, error }`) and ignores the result. On a claim failure (wl error, lock contention, timeout):

- The failure is silent — no log entry, no strike, no stderr message (only `claimItemForAgentCommand`, index.ts:318-323, logs claim failures; the downtime path does not).
- `dispatchDowntimeWork` proceeds anyway: it spawns the pane and awaits `recordDispatchAudit`, which records the dispatch as a SUCCESS (downtime-worker.ts:525-527 / :537-539 / :551-553).
- The claim is the documented cross-pane serialization mechanism (README "No lock file"): the item is set to `in_progress` so a second pane's `wl next` cannot select it. A failed claim leaves the item selectable, so two panes can dispatch the same item.

## User story

"As an operator, when the downtime worker fails to claim the item it is about to dispatch, I want that failure to be observable and the dispatch outcome to reflect it, so a claim failure cannot silently produce duplicate sessions or a false success record."

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A claim failure leaves a durable trace (log entry, error record, or outcome reason) instead of being silently discarded.
- [ ] The dispatch outcome reflects the claim failure: either the dispatch aborts with a `claim-failed` outcome or the success record is not written when the claim failed (design decision: fail-closed vs proceed-but-mark — record the choice in the item).
- [ ] Unit tests cover: claim failure → observable outcome; claim success → current behavior unchanged.
- [ ] packages/herdr/README.md failure-path logging section updated.

## Key Files

- packages/herdr/src/index.ts:393-396 (claimItem dep — inaccurate comment "failures are returned and logged")
- packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts:599-610 (claimWorkItem)
- packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts:525-527, 537-539, 551-553 (claim → spawn → record)
- packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts (tests)

# Downtime pane spawn failure invisible — dispatch still logged as success

**discovered-from:** WL-0MSKUG2WW0058A7W (audit gap AC3, follow-up 3 of 3)

## Problem

A send-to-pi.sh spawn failure is invisible to the downtime worker, and the dispatch is still recorded as a success. `spawnDowntimePane` (packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts:662-671) spawns detached with `stdio: 'ignore'` and `unref()`s the child — there is no `error` listener and no `exit` handler:

- A spawn-level failure (ENOENT/EACCES on send-to-pi.sh) emits an async `error` event on the child. With no listener this can crash the plugin process (Node "Unhandled 'error' event"); even when handled, the dispatch continues.
- A script-level failure (send-to-pi.sh exits non-zero, e.g. tmux pane creation fails) is invisible because stdio is ignored and the child is unref'd — the parent never observes the exit.
- `dispatchDowntimeWork` awaits `spawnAgentPane` (which returns immediately — the spawn is fire-and-forget) then `recordDispatchAudit` (downtime-worker.ts:582-600) writes the dispatch log entry and the `herdr-downtime` item comment as a SUCCESS, even though no pane was ever opened.

The dispatch log therefore conflates "dispatch attempted" with "agent pane actually opened".

## User story

"As an operator, when the downtime worker cannot open the agent pane, I want that failure to be observable (handled error, exit-status trace, or a non-success outcome) so the dispatch log does not claim success for a pane that never appeared."

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A spawn `error` event is handled (no unhandled-exception crash of the plugin process).
- [ ] A spawn failure or non-zero script exit is observable: an error/exit trace is recorded or the dispatch outcome is not `success` (design decision: attach exit/error handlers and distinguish "attempted" from "opened" in recordDispatchAudit — record the choice in the item).
- [ ] Unit tests cover: spawn error → handled + observable; non-zero exit → observable; success path unchanged.
- [ ] packages/herdr/README.md failure-path logging section updated.

## Key Files

data.description:
# Follow-up work item — stale doc comment in worklist.ts (discovered during audit of WL-0MSKCRX730052IIW)

## Headline

The `fetchItemsForView` doc comment in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` (lines ~2190-2194) still documents the pre-fix contract: stage-filtered views show "EVERY open root item in that stage (\`wl list --status open --stage <stage> --root-only\`)" and "Items with status blocked, in-progress, or completed are excluded". This is now inaccurate for the `in_review` stage since WL-0MSKCRX730052IIW introduced `STAGE_STATUS` (fetcher.ts) with `in_review: completed,in-progress,open`.

## Problem Statement

The audit of WL-0MSKCRX730052IIW (audit_runner, Ready to close: No) marked AC6 (docs) as **partial** solely because of this stale comment: the README and fetcher.ts comments were updated, but the `fetchItemsForView` doc comment in worklist.ts was missed. All other ACs (1-5) are met; this comment is the only remaining gap before the parent can close.

discovered-from: WL-0MSKCRX730052IIW

## Expected behaviour

The comment accurately describes the per-stage status rule: stage-filtered views show every root item in the selected stage matching the stage's status rule — `open`-status items for most stages, and `completed`/`in-progress`/`open` for the `in_review` stage (via `STAGE_STATUS` in fetcher.ts). It must not claim an unconditional status=open-only contract.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The `fetchItemsForView` doc comment in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` reflects the per-stage status rule (in_review fetches `completed`/`in-progress`/`open` via `STAGE_STATUS`; other stages `status=open` only), removing the "EVERY open root item" and "blocked/in-progress/completed excluded" wording that is now inaccurate for in_review.
2. No behavioural code change — comment-only edit; herdr test suite still passes (worklist.test.ts stage-filter tests green).
3. No contradiction with existing docs: README.md and fetcher.ts comments remain consistent with the updated comment.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — `fetchItemsForView` doc comment (lines ~2190-2194)

## Notes

- Work item is a child of WL-0MSKCRX730052IIW; the parent remains at open/plan_complete with audit verdict Ready to close: No until this comment is fixed and the parent is re-audited.

data.author: OpenCode
data.comment:
Fixed textarea viewport/scrolling issue when using Ctrl+Enter

Problem: When pressing Ctrl+Enter to add a new line, the first line would disappear and only reappear when typing a character.

Root cause: The textarea was setting the new value before the dialog had expanded, causing rendering issues with the viewport.

Solution in commit cdf5991:
- Update layout and expand dialog BEFORE setting the new value
- Improved scroll calculation to properly keep cursor line visible
- Added viewport handling when box height changes
- Force internal cursor update to refresh the display

The textarea now properly displays all content when adding new lines.

data.author: OpenCode
data.comment:
FOUND THE ROOT CAUSE! Fixed textarea scroll issue in commit abe7e24

Problem: When pressing Ctrl+Enter to add lines, the first line would disappear.

Root Cause: The textarea has scrollable=true and maintains internal scroll state. When adding a newline:
1. The cursor moves to line 2
2. The dialog expands to fit 2 lines
3. But the textarea's scroll position wasn't being reset
4. If scroll was > 0, line 1 would be scrolled off the top

Solution: Explicitly set scroll to 0 whenever totalLines <= visibleLines. This ensures all content is visible from the top when it fits in the viewport.

The fix was simple - we were only setting scroll when content EXCEEDED the visible area, but never resetting it to 0 when content should be fully visible.

data.author: OpenCode
data.comment:
SUCCESS! Fixed the Ctrl+Enter textarea rendering issue in commit ae5b9e2

The root cause was finally identified:
1. Ctrl+Enter sends a 'linefeed' keypress event (not 'C-enter')
2. Blessed's textarea handles this internally and inserts the newline
3. Our .key(['C-enter']) handler never ran because blessed processed it first
4. We were resizing AFTER the newline was inserted, causing scroll issues

The solution:
- Intercept the 'linefeed' keypress event BEFORE blessed processes it
- Read the current line count
- Calculate the future line count (current + 1)
- Resize the dialog preemptively to the correct height
- Let blessed insert the newline naturally
- Scroll to bottom after insertion completes

Now when pressing Ctrl+Enter:
- The box expands smoothly
- All content remains visible
- The cursor stays visible on the new line
- No content scrolls off screen unexpectedly

This was a complex debugging journey that involved understanding blessed's internal event handling!

data.author: @OpenCode
data.comment:
Audit: Enumerated all event listener usages (\.on/\.once) under src/ and noted recommended cleanup actions. Summary:

- Files requiring explicit cleanup (transient UI widgets, child processes, SSE): src/tui/opencode-client.ts, src/commands/tui.ts, src/tui/components/modals.ts, src/tui/components/dialogs.ts, src/tui/components/opencode-pane.ts, src/tui/components/overlays.ts, src/tui/components/list.ts, src/tui/components/detail.ts, src/tui/components/help-menu.ts, src/tui/components/toast.ts, src/tui/update-dialog-navigation.ts, src/tui/update-dialog-submit.ts

- Files where handlers are expected to be long-lived or global (no action required unless future refactor): src/cli.ts (process SIG handlers), src/index.ts, src/sync.ts (child process usage should still be audited in context).

- Recommendations (per-file):
  * Remove/deregister listeners on destroy for transient blessed widgets (use removeAllListeners or remove specific handlers) — applicable to all files creating widgets: components/* and commands/tui.ts.
  * Child process handlers (stdout/stderr/error/close) should be registered once and removed in stop/cleanup; ensure proc.kill() is preceded by removing listeners and nulling refs.
  * SSE/HTTP request listeners must be removed/aborted on stream finish/error to avoid late payload processing (opencode-client.ts).
  * Add unit tests that create/destroy widgets and start/stop child processes repeatedly to assert listener counts do not grow and no duplicate handling occurs.

Full per-file line references and notes were recorded locally and are available on request. I will attach a detailed per-file list as the next comment if you want it posted to the work item.

- Post-move cursor follows the moved item (auto-expand parent, scroll to item)
- Footer shows source item title and ID for context
- Visual treatment uses both color (background/foreground) AND prefix markers
- No confirmation dialog; moves execute immediately
- Unit + integration tests required (mocked blessed)

✓ All existing tests pass

data.author: @AGENT
data.comment: Added failing regression test to reproduce single-machine overwrite: tests/sync.test.ts → 'local persistence race' → 'can overwrite a recent update if sync imports a stale snapshot'. The test now fails (expected status 'completed' but got 'open') when a stale snapshot is imported, matching observed behavior. Run: npm test -- --run tests/sync.test.ts

data.author: @AGENT
data.comment:
Plan to fix overwrite (single-machine, concurrent writers):

Root cause: multiple WorklogDatabase instances hold stale snapshots. Any write exports the instance snapshot to JSONL, so a stale instance can overwrite newer changes from another instance.

Recommended fix (Option 1): merge-on-export in WorklogDatabase.exportToJsonl.
- Before writing JSONL, load current JSONL from disk and merge with in-memory snapshot using mergeWorkItems/mergeComments (newer updatedAt wins; non-default beats default).
- Write merged result back to JSONL.
Why it works: prevents stale writers from overwriting newer fields; each write reconciles with latest on-disk state.

Alternatives:
- Import-before-write guard based on JSONL mtime (simpler but still racey).
- File lock around JSONL writes (robust but more complexity).

Plan:
1) Implement merge-on-export in WorklogDatabase.exportToJsonl.
2) Update failing regression test in tests/sync.test.ts to pass.
3) Run npm test -- --run tests/sync.test.ts.

Expected outcome: stale snapshot imports no longer revert recent updates.

    {
      "id": "WL-0MLRFRY731A5FI9I",
      "title": "Sync restores removed parent link, overwriting more recent unparent operation",
      "description": "## Summary

When a work item is unparented (e.g. using the 'm' key in the TUI to set parentId to null) and then `wl sync` is run, the parent link is restored to its previous value even though the removal of the parent is the more recent operation. This means local edits that clear a parent are silently reverted by sync.

## User Story

As a user, when I remove the parent of a work item and then sync, I expect the unparented state to be preserved because my local change is more recent than the previous parent assignment.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Pick a work item that currently has a parent (e.g. `wl show <id>` shows a non-null parentId).
2. Remove the parent: use the 'm' key in TUI or `wl update <id> --parent null` to set parentId to null.
3. Verify the parent is removed: `wl show <id>` should show parentId as null.
4. Run `wl sync`.
5. Check the item again: `wl show <id>`.

## Actual Behaviour

After sync, parentId is restored to the original parent value. The unparent operation is lost.

## Expected Behaviour

After sync, parentId should remain null because the local unparent operation is more recent than the previous parent assignment. Sync should respect the timestamp/ordering of operations and not revert newer local changes.

## Impact

- Data integrity: user intent (removing a parent) is silently overwritten.
- Trust: users cannot rely on sync to preserve their local edits.
- Workflow disruption: items re-appear under parents they were intentionally removed from, breaking planning and hierarchy management.

## Suggested Investigation

- Review the sync merge logic (likely in the JSONL merge/import path) to understand how parentId changes are reconciled.
- Check whether setting parentId to null generates a JSONL event with a timestamp, and whether the merge logic correctly compares timestamps for null vs non-null parentId values.
- A null parentId may be treated as \"missing\" rather than \"explicitly set to null\", causing the sync to treat the remote non-null value as authoritative.
- Check `src/persistent-store.ts` and the sync/merge helpers for how parentId is handled during import/refresh.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Setting parentId to null and running `wl sync` preserves the null parentId when the unparent operation is more recent than the last parent assignment.
2. The JSONL event log correctly records unparent operations with timestamps.
3. The sync merge logic treats an explicit null parentId as a valid value, not as a missing field.
4. A regression test verifies that unparent + sync does not restore the old parent.
5. Existing sync behaviour for re-parenting (changing from one parent to another) is not affected.",

      "id": "WL-0ML4CQ8QL03P215I",
      "title": "Standardize status/stage labels from config",
      "description": "# Intake Brief: Standardize Status/Stage Labels From Config

## Problem Statement
Status and stage labels (and their legal combinations) are currently hard-coded in the TUI, creating inconsistent formatting and a split source of truth across TUI and CLI. This work makes labels and compatibility config-driven so both TUI and CLI render and validate against one shared, repo-specific definition.

## Users
- Contributors and agents who update work items via TUI or CLI and need consistent labels and rules.

### Example user stories
- As a contributor, I want status/stage labels to be consistent and configurable so TUI/CLI use a single source of truth.

## Success Criteria
- Status and stage labels and compatibility rules are sourced from `.worklog/config.defaults.yaml`.
- TUI update dialog renders labels from config and validates status/stage compatibility using config rules.
- CLI `wl create` and `wl update` reject invalid status/stage combinations with a clear error listing valid options.
- CLI accepts kebab-case values that map to valid snake_case values, with a warning on conversion.
- No remaining hard-coded status/stage label or compatibility arrays in the TUI/CLI code path.

## Constraints
- No backward compatibility: remove hard-coded defaults; if config is missing required sections, fail with a clear error.
- Canonical values and labels use `snake_case`.
- Compatibility is defined in one direction in config (status -> allowed stages); derive the reverse mapping in code.
- If CLI inputs are kebab-case equivalents of valid values, accept with warning; otherwise reject with error.
- Doctor validation depends on this config work landing first.

## Existing State
- TUI uses hard-coded status/stage values and compatibility in `src/tui/status-stage-rules.ts` and validation helpers.
- Inventory exists in `docs/validation/status-stage-inventory.md` describing current rules and gaps.

## Desired Change
- Extend config schema to include status labels, stage labels, and status->stage compatibility in `.worklog/config.defaults.yaml`.
- Refactor TUI update dialog and validation helpers to read labels and compatibility from config.
- Refactor CLI create/update flows to validate status/stage compatibility from config, including kebab-case normalization with warnings.
- Remove hard-coded status/stage labels and compatibility arrays from TUI/CLI runtime path.

## Risks & Assumptions
- Risk: Existing work items may contain invalid status/stage values and will fail validation; remediation will be required.
- Risk: Missing config sections will cause immediate failure by design.
- Assumption: Config defaults will include the full, canonical status/stage values and compatibility mapping.
- Assumption: `snake_case` is the canonical value format for statuses and stages.

## Related Work
- Standardize status/stage labels from config (WL-0ML4CQ8QL03P215I)
- Validation rules inventory (WL-0ML4W3B5E1IAXJ1P)
- Doctor: validate status/stage values from config (WL-0MLE6WJUY0C5RRVX)
- wl doctor (WL-0MKRPG64S04PL1A6)
- `docs/validation/status-stage-inventory.md` — current rules and gaps
- `src/tui/status-stage-rules.ts` — current hard-coded values and compatibility

## Suggested Next Step
Proceed to review and approval of this intake draft, then run the five review passes (completeness, capture fidelity, related-work & traceability, risks & assumptions, polish & handoff) before updating the work item description.",

data.author: @opencode
data.comment: Fixed in commit 1f9d695. Root cause: editTextarea used blessed.list for buttons, which does not reliably emit select on mouse clicks, causing the modal Promise to never resolve. Replaced with blessed.box widgets (same pattern as confirmTextbox). Also simplified resetInputState by removing aggressive workarounds. All 327 tests pass, build clean.

data.author: @opencode
data.comment: Second fix in commit 76e2f17. Found the deeper root cause: blessed textarea with inputOnFocus=true sets screen.grabKeys=true when readInput() is called on focus. This blocks ALL screen-level key handlers. The previous fix (replacing blessed.list buttons with blessed.box) was necessary but not sufficient -- the textarea's readInput cycle was never properly ended during cleanup, leaving grabKeys permanently true. Now cleanup explicitly calls textarea.cancel() to end the readInput cycle before destroying widgets, plus grabKeys=false safety nets in all cleanup paths including forceCleanup().

data.author: gpt-5.2-codex
data.comment: Diagnosis: CLI delete uses DB deletion, but SQLite foreign_keys are off by default in better-sqlite3. TUI uses status=deleted (soft delete), while CLI hard delete left dependent rows (comments/dependency_edges) and could be rolled back/ignored by downstream merge. Fix: enable PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON on DB open so delete cascades apply consistently.

data.comment: Analysis: Resort complete. Updated 9 item(s). uses  which orders siblings by existing  (ascending), then , then uid=1000(rogardle) gid=1000(rogardle) groups=1000(rogardle),4(adm),24(cdrom),27(sudo),30(dip),46(plugdev),119(lxd),1001(docker), and traverses tree depth-first. It does NOT factor priority.  then reassigns sequential indexes based on that order, so priority differences are ignored. This explains low-priority items having smaller sortIndex values than higher-priority items. data.author: @opencode
data.comment: Corrected analysis: re-sort uses getAllOrderedByHierarchySortIndex which orders siblings by existing sortIndex ascending, then createdAt, then id, and traverses depth-first. This explains low-priority items having smaller sortIndex values than higher-priority items. data.author: opencode
data.comment:
Findings: 
- next filtering excludes status='deleted' in WorklogDatabase.findNextWorkItemFromItems, so a truly deleted item should not be selected.
- CLI delete (src/commands/delete.ts) calls db.delete which removes the row from SQLite (not soft-delete). TUI 'delete' uses db.update status='deleted'.
- WorklogDatabase.exportToJsonl merges DB items with disk JSONL (src/database.ts). If an item was deleted from DB, but still exists in disk JSONL, mergeWorkItems will keep the JSONL item (it is treated as a real item, not a tombstone).
- refreshFromJsonlIfNewer re-imports JSONL back into DB when JSONL mtime is newer. This can resurrect deleted items (the DB delete isn't represented as a deletion in JSONL), and then wl next can surface it.
Hypothesis: deletion via CLI (hard delete) + stale JSONL + refresh/merge can resurrect the item, causing wl next to return it. Fix likely needs a tombstone or deletion record in JSONL or merge logic to drop items absent from DB when DB has newer state (or set status='deleted' instead of hard delete).

data.author: OpenCode
data.comment:
Investigation (initial review):
- Current runtime sources:
  - SQLite DB: the runtime persistent store at `.worklog/worklog.db` managed by `SqlitePersistentStore` (`src/persistent-store.ts`) and accessed via `WorklogDatabase` (`src/database.ts`). This is where the application reads/writes during normal operation (the `WorklogDatabase` methods use it).
  - JSONL file: `.worklog/worklog-data.jsonl` (read/write via `src/jsonl.ts` functions `importFromJsonl` / `exportToJsonl`). `WorklogDatabase.refreshFromJsonlIfNewer()` refreshes from JSONL on start or when JSONL is newer and `WorklogDatabase.exportToJsonl()` exports to JSONL after updates.
  - In-memory objects: process-local in-memory structures (the Map-backed cache and in-process caches) hold runtime state derived from the DB.
  - Git sync layer: commands in `src/commands/sync.ts`, `src/commands/import.ts` and `src/commands/export.ts` interact with remote JSONL content and may overwrite local JSONL.

- Key code pointers where ambiguity or conflicts can arise:
  - `importFromJsonl` (`src/jsonl.ts`): imports JSONL into the DB (used by `WorklogDatabase.refreshFromJsonlIfNewer()` and import handlers), called around mutating workflows — this makes JSONL an implicit upstream source that can modify DB state mid-operation.
  - `exportToJsonl` (`WorklogDatabase.exportToJsonl` / `src/jsonl.ts`): writes JSONL after DB changes; it merges with disk via `importFromJsonl` and writes the file. Note: export currently does not update DB metadata about the export (e.g., `lastJsonlImportMtime`).
  - `importFromJsonlContent` / parsing logic (`src/jsonl.ts`): the parsing/writing logic; `getDefaultDataPath()` in `src/jsonl.ts` is used as the data path source.
  - Destructive import flow: clearing and replacing DB contents happens inside a transaction via `SqlitePersistentStore` methods when importing from JSONL — this is atomic at DB level but risky if triggered inadvertently.
  - `resolveWorklogDir()` (`src/worklog-paths.ts`): determines where `.worklog` lives; differences between worktrees / repo root can cause processes to point at different physical locations. (See earlier work item WL-0ML0IFVW00OCWY6F.)
  - Git sync (`src/sync.ts`) + git operations: remote fetch/merge may write JSONL which then becomes a trigger for local imports.

- Observed ambiguity / risk areas:
  1) Dual writable surfaces: both DB and `.worklog/worklog-data.jsonl` are being written by the process; other processes or git operations can also modify JSONL — no single canonical runtime owner guaranteed.
  2) Import/export races: `refreshFromJsonlIfNewer()` runs before many mutating ops; `exportToJsonl()` runs after mutating ops — in concurrent scenarios these can flip-flop and cause lost updates or merge conflicts.
  3) Metadata handshake missing on export: exports don't update DB metadata (e.g., `lastJsonlImportMtime`) so two processes can repeatedly re-import/export the same data.
  4) Atomicity of JSONL writes: `exportToJsonl()` currently writes directly to file; ensure atomic write (temp file + rename) to avoid corruption.
  5) Path ambiguity: `resolveWorklogDir()` behavior across worktrees must be consistent to avoid different processes using different `.worklog` dirs.

- Recommendations (options to remove ambiguity, preserve data integrity):
  Option A — DB-first single source (Recommended):
    - Designate the SQLite DB (e.g., `.worklog/worklog.db`) as the canonical runtime source of truth. All runtime mutating operations must write to the DB and treat JSONL as a secondary export/backup.
    - Changes:
      * Keep the DB (`SqlitePersistentStore`) as single-writer data store.
      * Centralize export logic: make exports to JSONL an explicit, serialized operation with a global mutex; write JSONL atomically (write temp + rename) and AFTER writing, update a DB metadata key such as `lastJsonlExportMtime` (or set `lastJsonlImportMtime` appropriately) so other processes know the export is local and should not re-import.
      * Remove or constrain `refreshFromJsonlIfNewer()` usage: do NOT call it before every mutating operation. Instead, only refresh on startup or when an explicit import/sync command runs, or when an external trigger (e.g., git post-checkout hook) indicates JSONL changed and the process should refresh.
      * Add file-locking or process-level mutex around export/import/sync operations to avoid concurrent merges.
    - Pros: strong runtime guarantees, SQLite already provides transactions and WAL for concurrency; easiest to test.
    - Cons: requires changing many call sites (remove frequent refresh calls) and coordinating multi-process sync via explicit hooks.

  Option B — JSONL-first single file at runtime:
    - Make JSONL the canonical runtime file; processes load JSONL into memory at start and write JSONL on every change using atomic writes and a file lock. DB becomes a cache only.
    - Pros: single file is easier to inspect and push via git; simple single-file sync semantics.
    - Cons: poor concurrency for multiple processes; losing SQLite benefits (transactions, WAL). Not recommended for multi-process environments.

  Option C — Merged multi-writer with strict merge protocol:
    - Keep both JSONL and DB but introduce explicit versioning and deterministic merge rules (e.g., per-field timestamps, per-item vector clock or Lamport counter). Extend the export with per-field last-writer-with-identity and write metadata.
    - Ensure `exportToJsonl()` writes atomically and also writes a sidecar metadata (exportedBy, exportedAt, exportRevision) and update DB with the same exportRevision so local process will not re-import. Add file locks for export/import window.
    - Pros: supports multi-writer scenarios with automated merging.
    - Cons: more complex; requires robust merge testing and careful conflict resolution semantics.

  Option D — Single-writer coordination via git/lock (operational):
    - Keep current model but enforce a single writer per repo (or branch) using an external coordination mechanism (git ref lock, advisory file lock in `.worklog`, or CI-based sync). Other processes operate read-only or queue write requests via the designated writer.
    - Pros: minimal code changes; operationally simple.
    - Cons: needs operational discipline and tooling; not resilient to writer failure unless failover planned.

- Minimum quick fixes (low-effort, high-impact):
  - Make `exportToJsonl()` perform atomic write (temp file + rename). Update DB metadata (e.g., `lastJsonlImportMtime`/`lastJsonlExportMtime`) after a successful export so refresh logic won't re-import immediately. (Files: `src/jsonl.ts`, `src/database.ts`, `src/persistent-store.ts`).
  - Serialize import/export/sync with a simple mutex (process-wide) to avoid concurrent merge windows. (Files: `src/database.ts`, `src/commands/sync.ts`).
  - Audit and harden `resolveWorklogDir()` tests and behavior to ensure all processes point to the intended `.worklog` directory. (File: `src/worklog-paths.ts`).

- Suggested next steps (subtasks to create):
  1) Implement atomic JSONL export + update DB metadata to avoid re-import loops (high).
  2) Replace implicit per-operation `refreshFromJsonlIfNewer()` calls with controlled refresh points (startup + explicit import/sync hooks) (high).
  3) Add process-level mutex around import/export/sync and test concurrent modifications (high).
  4) Add integration tests simulating two processes concurrently updating DB and JSONL (medium).
  5) Decide canonical strategy (DB-first vs merge) and implement the final design with documentation (high).

I will create the concrete subtasks and implement Option A (DB-first, recommended) unless you prefer a different approach.

When a work item is unparented (e.g. using the 'm' key in the TUI to set parentId to null) and then `wl sync` is run, the parent link is restored to its previous value even though the removal of the parent is the more recent operation. This means local edits that clear a parent are silently reverted by sync.

## User Story

As a user, when I remove the parent of a work item and then sync, I expect the unparented state to be preserved because my local change is more recent than the previous parent assignment.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Pick a work item that currently has a parent (e.g. `wl show <id>` shows a non-null parentId).
2. Remove the parent: use the 'm' key in TUI or `wl update <id> --parent null` to set parentId to null.
3. Verify the parent is removed: `wl show <id>` should show parentId as null.
4. Run `wl sync`.
5. Check the item again: `wl show <id>`.

## Actual Behaviour

After sync, parentId is restored to the original parent value. The unparent operation is lost.

## Expected Behaviour

After sync, parentId should remain null because the local unparent operation is more recent than the previous parent assignment. Sync should respect the timestamp/ordering of operations and not revert newer local changes.

## Impact

- Data integrity: user intent (removing a parent) is silently overwritten.
- Trust: users cannot rely on sync to preserve their local edits.
- Workflow disruption: items re-appear under parents they were intentionally removed from, breaking planning and hierarchy management.

## Suggested Investigation

- Review the sync merge logic (likely in the JSONL merge/import path) to understand how parentId changes are reconciled.
- Check whether setting parentId to null generates a JSONL event with a timestamp, and whether the merge logic correctly compares timestamps for null vs non-null parentId values.
- A null parentId may be treated as \"missing\" rather than \"explicitly set to null\", causing the sync to treat the remote non-null value as authoritative.
- Check `src/persistent-store.ts` and the sync/merge helpers for how parentId is handled during import/refresh.

4. A regression test verifies that unparent + sync does not restore the old parent.

## Backward Compatibility Analysis

### No Risk (Safe Changes)

1. **Extracting the normalization logic into a reusable utility** -- Pure refactor. The existing inline normalizer in `saveWorkItem` (lines 303-315 of `src/persistent-store.ts`) already produces the correct output. Extracting it into a function and reusing it in `saveComment` and `saveDependencyEdge` does not change behavior for any existing call path.

2. **Adding normalization to `saveComment` and `saveDependencyEdge`** -- All current callers already pass correctly-typed values (strings, numbers, null). Adding a normalization pass would be a no-op for valid inputs and only adds defensive safety. Existing stored data is unaffected since this only changes the write path.

3. **Boolean coercion (`needsProducerReview`)** -- Already handled at both layers. No change needed.

### Low Risk (Needs Care)

4. **Date object handling** -- The normalizer currently `JSON.stringify`s unexpected objects, which would turn a raw `Date` into a double-quoted ISO string. If the fix changes this to `v.toISOString()`, the stored format would differ from what the `JSON.stringify` fallback produces. However, no caller currently passes raw `Date` objects (they all use `new Date().toISOString()`), so this is theoretical only. The read layer (`rowToWorkItem` at line 636) treats date fields as opaque strings, so a format change in the stored value would be transparent to consumers.

5. **JSONL round-trip** -- The JSONL export (`jsonl.ts:63-118`) serializes `WorkItem` objects as-is via `stableStringify`. The JSONL import (`jsonl.ts:132-276`) re-hydrates with extensive backward-compatibility normalization. Since the JSONL layer works with the `WorkItem` TypeScript interface (which uses `boolean` for `needsProducerReview`, `string[]` for `tags`, etc.), and the SQLite layer handles the type conversions at the boundary, changes to SQLite binding normalization do **not** affect the JSONL format.

6. **`saveComment` uses `INSERT OR REPLACE`** (line 471) -- Unlike `saveWorkItem` which uses `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE`, `saveComment` does a full replace. The read path at `rowToComment` (line 697) already handles `JSON.parse` failures gracefully by falling back to `references: []`. No risk here.

### The One Real Concern

7. **`saveComment` uses `||` instead of `??` for `githubCommentUpdatedAt`** (line 484). If normalization is added and this expression is changed to `?? null`, the behavior would change for falsy-but-not-nullish values like `""` (empty string). Currently `"" || null` returns `null`, but `"" ?? null` returns `""`. This is a subtle semantic difference. Since `githubCommentUpdatedAt` is typed as `string | undefined`, an empty string would be a caller bug regardless, but this should be documented if changed.

### Conclusion

| Area | Risk | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Extracting normalizer to utility | None | Pure refactor |
| Adding normalizer to saveComment/saveDependencyEdge | None | No-op for existing callers |
| Changing Date handling in normalizer | Very low | No caller passes raw Dates today |
| JSONL round-trip format | None | JSONL layer operates on typed objects, not raw SQLite values |
| Read-path compatibility with old data | None | rowToWorkItem/rowToComment already handle all stored formats |
| `||` vs `??` in saveComment line 484 | Low | Only matters for empty string edge case |

**This work is safe to implement without backward compatibility issues**, provided:
- The normalization logic produces the same output as the current inline code for all types already handled
- The `||` vs `??` difference in `saveComment` is preserved or intentionally changed with awareness
- Unit tests verify round-trip consistency (write -> read -> write produces identical SQLite rows)

data.comment:
## Reproduction Confirmed

Successfully reproduced the bug in a fresh temp project (/tmp/tmp.kWpT8Qwkdy and /tmp/tmp.LI5X2QGSvM).

### Reproduction Steps
1. `mktemp -d && cd $_ && git init && git commit --allow-empty -m 'init'`
2. `wl init --project-name Test --prefix T --auto-export yes --auto-sync no --agents-template skip --json`
3. `wl init --project-name Test --prefix T --auto-export yes --auto-sync no --agents-template skip --stats-plugin-overwrite yes --json` (second run installs stats plugin)
4. `wl list --json 2>&1` -> stderr shows: `Failed to load plugin stats-plugin.mjs: Cannot find package 'chalk' imported from ...`

### Key Findings
- The error is emitted on EVERY `wl` command once the stats plugin is installed
- The error goes to stderr (not stdout), so JSON output is still valid
- The `stats` command itself is never registered (it fails silently)
- The TUI and other commands still work but with noisy stderr output
- First-time `wl init --json` does NOT install the stats plugin (code path at init.ts:1177+ skips it)
- Second+ `wl init --json` (re-init path at init.ts:902+) DOES install it

### Root Cause Confirmed
Node.js ESM module resolution resolves `chalk` relative to the plugin file location, not relative to the wl binary. Since the plugin is copied to `<project>/.worklog/plugins/stats-plugin.mjs` and the project has no `node_modules/chalk`, the import fails.

- Feature 3 depends on Feature 1
- Feature 4 depends on Feature 1
- Feature 5 depends on Features 1, 2, and 3

### Approach Selected
- Option C+D: Graceful fallback in stats plugin (ANSI escape codes) + plugin loader downgrades errors to warnings
- Stats plugin becomes fully self-contained with no external runtime imports
- Plugin loader emits single-line warnings for failed plugins (full details only with --verbose)
- First-init JSON path fixed for consistency

data.author: Ilya0527
data.comment:
Bumping timeouts will paper over the real signal here. The pattern — passes solo, fails under concurrent load, tsx startup as the suspected bottleneck — is almost certainly resource contention on the test runner pool, not slow code. Vitest defaults to `threads` with poolOptions roughly = CPU count; 5 files × multiple tsx subprocess spawns each = N tests fighting for the same CPU/IO while their 20s wall clocks keep ticking.

One diagnostic before you touch timeouts: run `npm test -- --reporter=verbose --poolOptions.threads.maxThreads=2` and see if the failures disappear. If they do, the tests aren't slow — they're starved. Bumping the timeout to 60s just hides the contention until someone adds the 563rd test.

Proposed fix shape: mark the tsx-spawning suites with `describe.concurrent` off and tag them `test.sequential`, OR move all subprocess-spawning tests into a dedicated project (`vitest.config.ts` → `test.projects`) that runs with `pool: 'forks'` and `singleFork: true`. The rest of the suite stays parallel. This is deterministic and doesn't hide future regressions behind a generous timeout.

One thing to verify while you're in there: are the tsx subprocesses inheriting the parent's `NODE_OPTIONS`? If `--enable-source-maps` or a loader is set, cold-start can balloon 3–5s per spawn. Strip the env for those children.

Skip the across-the-board `testTimeout: 60000` bump — it's the kind of change that makes CI green today and untraceable in three months.

data.comment: Fixed regression: dep-blocked in-progress items were being selected by wl next. The inProgressPool was incorrectly using preDepBlockerItems for in-progress items (should only be used for blocked items for blocker-surfacing). data.author: OpenCode
data.comment: Fixed hang: wl next was hanging indefinitely because hasActiveBlockers() called listDependencyEdgesFrom() for each of ~499 candidate items, and each call triggered refreshFromJsonlIfNewer() which acquires a file lock and potentially re-reads the entire JSONL. With 623 items and 857 comments, this caused the process to spin on file I/O. Fix: use store-direct access (this.store.getDependencyEdgesFrom / this.store.getWorkItem) in the filter loop, bypassing per-item refresh. Execution time: 136ms on the real worklog. All 834 tests pass. Commit: f50717e

data.comment:
Planning Complete.

## Approved Feature Plan (4 features)

### Sequencing: F1 → F2 → F3 → F4 (linear dependency chain)

1. **Remove lock from refreshFromJsonlIfNewer** (WL-0MM09W1K81PB9P0C) -- Remove the withFileLock() wrapper from the read path. Core behavioral change.
2. **Graceful fallback on JSONL parse errors** (WL-0MM09WH9M0A076CY) -- Add try-catch with debug logging so lockless reads fall back to cached SQLite data on transient errors.
3. **Concurrency test for lockless reads** (WL-0MM09WVWK12GTWPY) -- vitest test forking 5+ reader processes alongside a writer to validate zero lock errors under concurrency.
4. **Validate existing tests pass** (WL-0MM09X6SP0GIO002) -- Final regression check across the full test suite.

## Key Decisions

- Write lock (exportToJsonl) is kept as-is; only the read path is changed
- exportToJsonl in jsonl.ts already uses atomic write (temp + renameSync), so no write-path changes needed
- Parse error fallback uses debug-level logging (WL_DEBUG env var), silent otherwise
- Concurrency test uses child_process.fork() in vitest, not shell scripts
- No feature flag/env-var toggle; direct merge
- Stale reads are acceptable for all read-only commands

## Open Questions

None -- all requirements are clear from the PRD and interview responses.

Planning Complete. Decomposed into 5 child features:

1. Extract stage and type from labels (WL-0MM368DZC1E53ECZ) - Add stage/issueType/legacy-priority extraction to issueToWorkItemFields()
2. Fetch and cache issue event timelines (WL-0MM368S4W104Q5D4) - Add GitHub events API fetching with per-run caching
3. Event-driven label conflict resolution (WL-0MM3699KS10OP3M3) - Compare event timestamps to local updatedAt, apply newer values
4. Structured audit logging for import (WL-0MM369NX61U76OVY) - Emit fieldChanges in --json/--verbose output and sync log
5. Integration test for import resolution (WL-0MM36A3F60UO4E8X) - End-to-end test with mocked events

Dependency graph: F1 and F2 are independent (parallelizable). F3 depends on F1+F2. F4 depends on F3. F5 depends on F4.

Decisions confirmed during interview:
- stage and issueType extraction added (both were missing from import)
- Legacy priority mapping: P0->critical, P1->high, P2->medium, P3->low
- Events fetched only for issues with differing fields (minimizes API calls)
- Multi-label handling: defensive (pick most-recently-added label via events)
- Conflict resolution: label event timestamp vs local updatedAt (most-recent wins, local wins on tie)
- Audit output: structured fieldChanges array in JSON, human-readable lines in verbose
- In-memory per-run cache for events (no cross-run persistence)
- Scope: strictly import-side; no push changes or doc updates

data.author: OpenCode
data.comment:
## Fix committed and pushed (7c7b1d3)

**Root cause:** The worker script used `fs.writeFileSync(counterFile, String(counter))` which is not atomic. Under CI contention (likely overlayfs on GitHub Actions), a process could read a stale value before the previous write was fully visible -- a cross-process read-after-write visibility issue.

**CI diagnostics confirmed this:** final counter of 20 (expected 40) with per-worker finalCounter values [4, 10, 10, 20] -- lost increments from non-atomic writes, not worker crashes (all exit codes 0).

**Fix applied:** Replaced simple writeFileSync with atomic temp-file write + fsyncSync + renameSync + directory fsync in the worker script. No changes to src/file-lock.ts.

**Verification:**
- 50/50 local stress runs passed (zero failures, zero anomalies)
- All 1111 tests pass, no regressions
- TypeScript compiles cleanly

**Changes in commit 7c7b1d3:**
- tests/file-lock.test.ts: atomic write fix + enhanced per-worker diagnostics (callbackExecutions, iterLog, anomaly detection)
- scripts/stress-file-lock.sh: new local stress harness
- .gitignore: added stress-logs/

**PR:** https://github.com/rgardler-msft/Worklog/pull/775 -- pushed, awaiting CI.

**Child items closed:** WL-0MM5J7OC31PFBW60 (diagnostics), WL-0MM5J7V7415LGJ1H (stress harness), WL-0MM5J86RX13DGCP5 (root-cause fix), WL-0MM5J80T41MOMUDU (aggregation -- superseded by in-test diagnostics). Remaining: WL-0MM5J8E1717PXS51 (regression monitoring -- pending CI confirmation).

data.author: OpenCode
data.comment:
## CI confirmed the original fix was insufficient -- deeper root cause found and fixed (48a45f7)

**CI result from first push (7c7b1d3):** counter=32 (expected 40). Per-worker diagnostics: [10, 20, 32, 22] -- all workers ran 10 callbacks, but 8 increments were lost. Worker 4 (finalCounter=22) completed after worker 3 (finalCounter=32), proving the lock was not serializing access.

**True root cause:** TOCTOU race in `acquireFileLock` (src/file-lock.ts). When process A creates the lock file with `O_CREAT|O_EXCL`, there is a window between `openSync` and `writeSync+closeSync` where the file exists but is empty. If process B retries during this window:
1. B reads the empty file, `readLockInfo` returns null
2. B sees `fs.existsSync(lockPath)` is true, treats it as corrupted, deletes it
3. B re-creates the lock file with `O_EXCL` -- succeeds
4. Both A and B now believe they hold the lock -- mutual exclusion broken

**Fix applied (two parts):**
1. `fsyncSync` after `writeSync` in lock creation -- minimizes the empty-file window
2. Grace period on corrupted-lock cleanup -- only deletes unparseable lock files if mtime > max(2x retryDelay, 500ms), so half-written files from concurrent writers are not prematurely removed

**Verification:** 50/50 stress runs pass, 1111/1111 tests pass. Pushed as commit 48a45f7 to PR #775.

**Files changed:** src/file-lock.ts (lines 240-320: fsync in lock creation, grace-period logic in corrupted-lock cleanup)
