data.author: Map
data.comment:
# Herdr selection list refreshes immediately when its tab regains focus (hidden→visible transition)

## Problem statement

The Herdr worklist TUI pauses its auto-refresh when its tab is hidden (visibility gating via `herdr pane get <id>` → `pane.focused === false`, WL-0MSB1N0HB0007N6N). When the tab regains focus, the list only refreshes on the **next regular refresh tick** — up to `refreshIntervalMs` (default 30s) later. Users returning to the tab wait silently for the list to catch up, and cannot tell it will update at all. The list should refresh **immediately** on the hidden → visible transition, then resume the normal cadence.

## Users

- **Herdr users running multiple panes/tabs** — they switch away from a tab containing a work-item list and return expecting current data immediately.

User stories:
- _As a user with three panes in a tab where the Herdr list is not the focused pane, I want the list to refresh as soon as the tab regains focus, so I don't wait up to 30s for the next tick._
- _As a user returning to a long-hidden tab, I want the refresh to happen immediately and the paused indicator to clear right away._

## Expected behaviour

1. While the pane is hidden (`pane.focused === false`), refresh/sync ticks continue to be skipped (zero `wl` spawns — unchanged).
2. The plugin detects the **hidden → visible transition** (visibility state flips false → true) and triggers an immediate `doRefresh()` on that transition — not waiting for the next regular `refreshIntervalMs` tick.
3. After the transition refresh, the normal scheduled cadence resumes.
4. The transition is detected promptly: while paused, visibility is polled on a short interval (e.g. 2s, matching `DEFAULT_POLL_GATE_TTL_MS`) instead of only on the 30s refresh tick. The poll uses `herdr pane get` only — never `wl` — so the no-wl-when-hidden guarantee from WL-0MSB1N0HB0007N6N is preserved.
5. The existing `[paused — hidden]` header indicator clears as soon as the list refreshes after becoming visible.
6. Fail-open unchanged: when visibility cannot be determined (no `HERDR_PANE_ID`, CLI error), polling proceeds as today.

## Implementation notes

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — in `runWorklistTui`, track the previous visibility state alongside `panePaused`. In the refresh timer tick: if hidden → record `wasHidden = true`, skip; if visible and `wasHidden` → call `doRefresh(true)` (immediate, with the "refreshed" notification) and clear `wasHidden`; else normal tick behaviour.
- Prompt transition detection: while `panePaused`, run a lightweight resume poll (e.g. a 2s interval calling the existing `paneGate.visible()` — memoized by `PollGate`, one `herdr pane get` exec per poll) that flips to an immediate refresh the moment visibility returns. Stop the resume poll once visible; only the normal refresh timer runs.
- Keep the `PollGate` TTL (`DEFAULT_POLL_GATE_TTL_MS = 2000`) aligned with the resume poll interval so visibility state is never cached stale for longer than the poll.
- Tests: extend `worklist-visibility.test.ts` (inject `setExecFileAsync` seam; fake timers) for: (a) hidden → visible transition triggers an immediate fetch outside the normal tick; (b) while hidden the resume poll does not call the fetcher; (c) after the transition refresh, the cadence returns to `refreshIntervalMs`; (d) the header indicator clears.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — transition detection, immediate refresh on resume, resume poll while paused.
- `packages/herdr/src/visibility.ts` — possibly export a `PollGate` constructor variant with a shorter TTL for the resume poll (or reuse existing).
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist-visibility.test.ts` — new tests for transition + resume poll + cadence return.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. When a hidden pane becomes visible, the list re-fetches **immediately** (outside the regular `refreshIntervalMs` tick) — asserted with injected fetcher + fake timers.
2. While hidden, no `wl` fetches occur and the resume poll spawns only `herdr pane get` (no fetcher calls).
3. After the immediate transition refresh, subsequent refreshes follow the normal `refreshIntervalMs` cadence.
4. The `[paused — hidden]` header indicator clears once the transition refresh completes.
5. Fail-open preserved: no `HERDR_PANE_ID` / CLI error → behaves as today (no regression in existing visibility tests).
6. Full herdr package test suite passes (`packages/herdr`).

## Constraints

- Must not regress the zero-`wl`-spawn-when-hidden behaviour (WL-0MSB1N0HB0007N6N).
- No changes to the external herdr app/framework (the `herdr` CLI is the calling framework; `herdr pane get` output shape is a given).
- The visibility signal stays tab-level (`pane.focused`); active-pane-level focus (which pane in a tab has the cursor) is out of scope — the transition fix covers the tab-hidden case regardless of which pane is active.

## Related work

- **WL-0MSB1N0HB0007N6N** — Pi extension polls wl list / wl next even when selection list is not visible (completed, in_review): introduced visibility gating (`visibility.ts`, `PollGate`, paused header indicator) that this item builds on.
- **WL-0MSBVBXEA0011OWF** / **WL-0MSBVCMNO00503QM** — closed (not needed): alternative focus-reporting and staleness-indicator approaches for the pi `/wl` browse extension; superseded by this item's use of herdr's own tab-level visibility signal.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** `pane.focused` flips false → true reliably when the tab regains focus while the pane itself is not the active pane. The visibility.ts comment ("a hidden (non-focused) tab reports focused === false") supports tab-level semantics; verify with a live herdr session during implementation.
- **Risk:** The 2s resume poll adds one `herdr pane get` exec every 2s per hidden pane. Mitigation: this is the same lightweight CLI already polled every 30s while hidden; make the resume poll interval a named constant/setting if churn concerns arise; never route it through `wl`.
- **Scope-creep risk:** Detecting "the active pane within a focused tab" (tmux-style pane focus) is out of scope; herdr's `focused` flag is tab-level and that is sufficient for the reported scenario.

data.comment:
Implemented fix for CWD resolution when worklist action is invoked from a Work Items plugin pane.

**Root cause:** Plugin panes run from the plugin root, so `herdr pane get` reports the plugin extension directory as the pane cwd. The logical working directory (the worklog root being displayed) lives in the pane process's `HERDR_RESOLVED_CWD` env var, which herdr does not expose via pane metadata.

**Changes:**
- `packages/herdr/scripts/open.sh`: after resolving the invoking pane's ID, read `HERDR_RESOLVED_CWD` from the pane process env via `herdr pane process-info` (shell_pid) → `/proc/<shell_pid>/environ` and prefer it over the reported filesystem cwd. Falls back to previous behavior when unavailable.
- `packages/herdr/scripts/toggle.sh`: same CWD resolution fix, plus fixed existing-worklist-pane detection to match `label == "Work Items"` (pane list does not expose a `command` field for plugin panes).
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts`: documentation comment only.

**Verification:**
- `_resolve_plugin_cwd` tested against real panes: Work Items pane for open_source_llm resolves to `/home/rgardler/projects/open_source_llm`; Pi Agent/terminal panes have no `HERDR_RESOLVED_CWD` and fall back to pane cwd (unchanged behavior).
- Shell syntax checks pass for both scripts.
- Full herdr vitest suite passes (15 files, 262 tests).

data.author: Map
data.comment: Intake refinement (Q4): required-free-slots is now configurable via `downtimeRequiredFreeSlots` (default: all slots; e.g. 2 slots, 1 slot). When the required count < total slots, the worker requires the **same** slot (`slot_id`) to remain free for the full threshold, not any slot — per-slot idle timers reset when a slot starts processing. Research: the proxy `/llama/local/status` endpoint returns only counts, so per-slot identity is not currently served over HTTP; filed proxy feature request **LP-0MSG5TA7Y002GN39** (llm project) to expose per-slot details, per the standing Q2 instruction. Until that lands, the worker runs fail-closed in all-slots mode.

data.author: Map
data.comment: Clarification (Q4 follow-up): when LP-0MSG5TA7Y002GN39 is not yet fulfilled and the user has configured `downtimeRequiredFreeSlots` < total slots, the worker fails closed to requiring **all** slots free for the threshold — it never dispatches on \"any N slots\" without same-slot identity. Added an explicit AC for this fallback and aligned the risk note (previously contradictory wording).

data.comment:
**Verified root cause: downtime worker can NEVER see idle — zero dispatches guaranteed, not just 'busy overnight'.**

Overnight result: no dispatches (no .worklog/downtime-dispatches.log, no herdr-downtime comments, no Downtime panes).

Live verification of the proxy endpoint (192.168.0.199) found a hard blocker:
- GET http://localhost:8080/slots on the proxy machine returns HTTP 400 'model name is missing from the request' — llama-server requires ?model=...
- The proxy's _query_slots() (proxy/observability.py) queries /slots WITHOUT the model param, so the call fails and both counts default to 0.
- Therefore /llama/local/status ALWAYS reports available_slots=0, total_slots=0 — even when genuinely idle.
- The worker's isIdleStatus/evaluateIdle treats total_slots <= 0 as ambiguous → busy (fail-closed), so it can NEVER dispatch.

Fix tracked as critical: LP-0MSHFGO0M003Q5BL (llm project). The original referenced LP-0MSG5TA7Y002GN39 never actually existed in the llm worklog (text reference only); the real item is now created with the confirmed root cause.

Note: the overnight busy state (active_query=true, lease held by pi agents) was real, but even a fully idle window would not have dispatched.

data.author: Map
data.comment:
Fixed and verified. Root cause: both shared launch scripts called `herdr pane current --json` — herdr 0.7.5 rejects `--json` (exit 2, 'unknown option: --json'; `pane current` emits JSON by default). With stderr suppressed the anchor was empty and the script exited before any split; the plugin spawns the script detached with stdio ignored, so launching from a freshly opened plugin pane (prefix+l) appeared to do nothing.

Second bug found during live verification: grid.py's json.dumps emits `"pane_id": "..."` (space after colon) but the sed parser expected `"pane_id":"..."`, so after a successful grid split the script failed with 'Could not determine new pane ID' and orphaned the new pane.

Changes (commit c8c33daf, pushed to dev):
- packages/herdr/shared/send-to-pi.sh + open-pi-agent.sh: drop --json from `pane current`; sed now tolerates optional whitespace after the colon
- packages/herdr/shared/grid.py: unrecognisable layout shapes (e.g. nested right-split first child left by pre-grid panes) now classify as fresh, so add_pane falls back to a plain right-split of the current pane instead of splitting a wrong subtree
- packages/herdr/shared/tests/test_scripts.sh: mock grid emits space-separated JSON (real grid.py format); new assertions that `pane current` is called without --json
- packages/herdr/shared/tests/test_grid.py: new tests for the unrecognised-layout fallback (parse + growth policy)

Verification: 40 python tests + 24 bash tests pass. Live on herdr 0.7.5: resize mode resolves the anchor, splits, launches pi with correct cwd/label and focuses; --no-resize plain split unchanged. Session left in original state.

data.author: implement
data.comment:
Root cause analysis from discovery during WL-0MSGAEXER000707R implementation (heartbeat integration test failed in the implement worktree):

- The test class TestHeartbeatRunWlRealSubprocess (unlike its sibling TestHeartbeatIntegration) does NOT chdir into a temp dir with an initialized worklog; it calls heartbeat.run_wl(['list', '--json']) which spawns 'wl list --json' from the current process cwd (the implement worktree), where no .worklog/ exists.
- 'wl list --json' in a dir without .worklog exits 1 with stdout {"success": false, "initialized": false, "error": "Worklog system is not initialized. Run worklog init first."} and empty stderr -> RuntimeError in heartbeat.py:45.
- Verified: the test PASSES from the main checkout (/home/rgardler/projects/ContextHub, has .worklog/) — 1 passed. It only fails when pytest runs from an implement worktree (e.g. .worklog/worktrees/wl-<id>-*), which has no .worklog. Impact: any implement.py finish run fails the pytest gate and silently falls back to npm test, masking the real suite result and violating the all-tests-must-pass gate.
- Possible fixes: (a) chdir to the isolated temp worklog dir in setUp (like TestHeartbeatIntegration does), or (b) set cwd= explicitly when spawning wl in run_wl under test, or (c) pytest config/collection adjustment. Note this is a test-environment bug, not a code regression.

## Description

## Goal

Standardize on a **single, shared resolution strategy** for finding the worklog root directory, eliminating the inconsistency between the herdr plugin's `findWorklogRoot()` and the `wl` CLI's `resolveWorklogDir()`.

Currently, these two functions implement independently evolved, subtly different algorithms for the same task. This creates a maintenance burden and a class of bugs where they disagree on what constitutes "the project root."

## Problem

There are two resolution engines with different strategies:

### Plugin: `findWorklogRoot()` (packages/herdr/src/index.ts)
- Pure filesystem walking from `process.cwd()`
- Finds the first parent directory containing a `.worklog/` with `worklog.db` or `initialized`
- No git dependency

### `wl` CLI: `resolveWorklogDir()` (src/worklog-paths.ts)  
- Git-centric: uses `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` to find repo root
- Checks `hasWorklogConfig()` (config.yaml or initialized marker)
- Special worktree handling
- Complex fallback chain with multiple git calls

### Problems this creates

1. **Subtle disagreements**: The plugin might find a `.worklog/` that `wl` ignores (or vice versa), leading to inconsistent results
2. **Duplicate logic**: Any fix to one must be manually ported to the other
3. **No escape hatch**: Neither function can be overridden externally (which option 1, `--worklog-dir`, addresses — but that's an override, not a unification)
4. **Different validation rules**: Plugin checks for `worklog.db` or `initialized`; `wl` checks for `config.yaml` or `initialized`

## Solution

Extract a **shared `resolveWorklogRoot()` function** into a common location that both the plugin and the `wl` CLI import and use. This could live in:

- Option A: `packages/shared/src/worklog-paths.ts` (shared package, both can depend on it)
- Option B: A new small module in `src/` that the plugin imports via a symlink or build-time dependency

The function should:
- Accept an optional `startDir` parameter (defaulting to `process.cwd()`)
- Implement a single, canonical resolution strategy
- Be exported for testing
- Be used by both `wl`'s `resolveWorklogDir()` and the plugin's `findWorklogRoot()`

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A single shared `resolveWorklogRoot(startDir?)` function exists in a shared location
2. Both `wl`'s `resolveWorklogDir()` and the plugin's `findWorklogRoot()` delegate to it
3. The resolution strategy is documented and deterministic
4. All existing tests pass (both `wl` tests and plugin tests)
5. No behavioral regression in edge cases (worktrees, nested repos, invalid `.worklog/` stubs)
6. The old `findWorklogRoot()` and `resolveWorklogDir()` implementations are removed (not just wrapped)

## Implementation Notes

- The shared function should support the superset of features from both implementations:
  - Filesystem walking (from plugin)
  - Git repo root detection (from `wl`)
  - Worktree awareness (from `wl`)
  - Invalid `.worklog/` skip (from plugin's fix)
- The precedence order should be documented clearly
- `packages/shared/` is the natural home since both `packages/herdr/` and the root `src/` can depend on it

## Key Files

- `packages/shared/src/worklog-paths.ts` — New shared module
- `src/worklog-paths.ts` — Refactored to import from shared
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — Refactored to import from shared
- All test files that test the old resolution functions

## Related

- The work item for `--worklog-dir` CLI option (separate item) is complementary: one provides an override mechanism, the other cleans up the internal resolution. Both together give a clean architecture: a single canonical resolution function + an explicit override path.

## Description

## Goal

Standardize on a **single, shared resolution strategy** for finding the worklog root directory, eliminating the inconsistency between the herdr plugin's `findWorklogRoot()` and the `wl` CLI's `resolveWorklogDir()`.

Currently, these two functions implement independently evolved, subtly different algorithms for the same task. This creates a maintenance burden and a class of bugs where they disagree on what constitutes "the project root."

## Problem

There are two resolution engines with different strategies:

### Plugin: `findWorklogRoot()` (packages/herdr/src/index.ts)
- Pure filesystem walking from `process.cwd()`
- Finds the first parent directory containing a `.worklog/` with `worklog.db` or `initialized`
- No git dependency

### `wl` CLI: `resolveWorklogDir()` (src/worklog-paths.ts)  
- Git-centric: uses `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` to find repo root
- Checks `hasWorklogConfig()` (config.yaml or initialized marker)
- Special worktree handling
- Complex fallback chain with multiple git calls

### Problems this creates

1. **Subtle disagreements**: The plugin might find a `.worklog/` that `wl` ignores (or vice versa), leading to inconsistent results
2. **Duplicate logic**: Any fix to one must be manually ported to the other
3. **No escape hatch**: Neither function can be overridden externally (which option 1, `--worklog-dir`, addresses — but that's an override, not a unification)
4. **Different validation rules**: Plugin checks for `worklog.db` or `initialized`; `wl` checks for `config.yaml` or `initialized`

## Solution

Extract a **shared `resolveWorklogRoot()` function** into a common location that both the plugin and the `wl` CLI import and use. This could live in:

- Option A: `packages/shared/src/worklog-paths.ts` (shared package, both can depend on it)
- Option B: A new small module in `src/` that the plugin imports via a symlink or build-time dependency

The function should:
- Accept an optional `startDir` parameter (defaulting to `process.cwd()`)
- Implement a single, canonical resolution strategy
- Be exported for testing
- Be used by both `wl`'s `resolveWorklogDir()` and the plugin's `findWorklogRoot()`

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A single shared `resolveWorklogRoot(startDir?)` function exists in a shared location
2. Both `wl`'s `resolveWorklogDir()` and the plugin's `findWorklogRoot()` delegate to it
3. The resolution strategy is documented and deterministic
4. All existing tests pass (both `wl` tests and plugin tests)
5. No behavioral regression in edge cases (worktrees, nested repos, invalid `.worklog/` stubs)
6. The old `findWorklogRoot()` and `resolveWorklogDir()` implementations are removed (not just wrapped)

## Implementation Notes

- The shared function should support the superset of features from both implementations:
  - Filesystem walking (from plugin)
  - Git repo root detection (from `wl`)
  - Worktree awareness (from `wl`)
  - Invalid `.worklog/` skip (from plugin's fix)
- The precedence order should be documented clearly
- `packages/shared/` is the natural home since both `packages/herdr/` and the root `src/` can depend on it

## Key Files

- `packages/shared/src/worklog-paths.ts` — New shared module
- `src/worklog-paths.ts` — Refactored to import from shared
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — Refactored to import from shared
- All test files that test the old resolution functions

## Related

- The work item for `--worklog-dir` CLI option (separate item) is complementary: one provides an override mechanism, the other cleans up the internal resolution. Both together give a clean architecture: a single canonical resolution function + an explicit override path.

## Canonical strategy (producer-approved)

- Valid `.worklog/` = `config.yaml` OR `initialized` (Q2; worklog.db-only dirs are invalid)
- Upward walk from startDir; nearest valid wins (local-wins)
- Invalid `.worklog/` stops the walk UNLESS worktree-container stub or inside `.worklog/worktrees/`
- Never walk past nearest git repo root (`git rev-parse --show-toplevel`, worktree-aware) (Q1)
- Outside git, walk to filesystem root; not found → `undefined` (strict) (Q3)
- CLI wrapper keeps `--worklog-dir` override + `cwd/.worklog` fallback; plugin surfaces uninitialized state

When cwd has an invalid non-stub `.worklog/` and the repo root has a valid one, resolution now stops at the invalid dir (CLI yields cwd/.worklog; previously it looked past to the repo root). Both consumers now agree.

Implementation complete and pushed to dev (commit 83f4919e).

**Bug fix — worklog-root routing:** the downtime worker's `wl next` selection and `wl comment add` audit trail now route through the same `--worklog-dir` override as the worklist via a new `buildWlArgs()` seam in fetcher.ts (refactored `runWlInner` to share it). **Feature — 60-min no-candidate cooldown:** new setting `downtimeNoCandidateCooldownMs` (default 3_600_000 ms, floor 60s, clamped + persisted in settings.ts). When both `wl next` stages genuinely return no candidate, the worker pauses fully (no proxy polling, no idle tracking, no dispatch) until the cooldown expires, then requires a fresh full idle period. To distinguish 'genuine empty backlog' from 'transient wl error', `getNextItem` now returns `DowntimeNextResult` (`{ok:true, candidate}` vs `{ok:false}`); only `no-candidate` triggers the cooldown — `wl-error` and `dispatch-in-flight` fail closed to busy. Header renders `[downtime paused]` during the pause (no stale idle m:ss).

**Tests:** 12 new/updated tests — cooldown entry/exit, no poll during cooldown, no cooldown on transient error or in-flight guard, clamp behavior, `--worklog-dir` forwarding on `wl next` and `wl comment add`, header paused render, settings persistence/clamp. ## Corrected timeline (the RCA's evidence was incomplete)

The RCA's section-4 claims — 'no dispatches after 21:55:26Z' and 'no downtime-dispatches.log in ContextHub/SorraAgents/etc.' — are **factually wrong on this host (.68.53)**. Five dispatch logs exist with entries continuing to **02:49:41Z Aug 8**:
- ContextHub: last 02:01:06Z (audit WL-0MSHWHP0S0036DDU)
- dev-scripts: last 02:49:41Z (audit DS-0MSAZSAPL003YHVR)
- open_source_llm: last 02:41:24Z (intake OSL-0MSHZ2T40003A8ZY)

- SorraAgents: last 21:55:24Z (plan SA-0MLYTIO0E0PPQ0OO)

## Poller identity (H2 partially resolved)

data.comment:
**RCA conclusion written to parent (WL-0MSK9TUCA00206M7).**

Root cause: the herdr workers polled continuously through the idle window but never received a 4-minute continuous IDLE status. The idle-window proxy log has NO status fields (observability landed 15:59:30 local, after the window), so the RCA's 'status would have reported idle' assumption is unverifiable and likely wrong. Evidence for the proxy reporting busy: (a) the global active_queries counter has no recovery mechanism (only the local counter has _recover_stuck_local_active_queries) and the current proxy shows active_query=true with 3/3 slots, no lease, and no local requests in flight — a stuck counter; (b) the last audit-wave dispatched pane held a local dispatch lease until 03:19:53Z (right at idle start), making local_lease_active=true during the critical first minutes.

**Remaining AC — observe a real dispatch on the next ≥4-min idle window:** not yet observed (dispatch logs still end at 02:49:41Z Aug 8). The proxy has been busy (active_query=true) throughout the post-observability period, so no clean idle window has occurred since the fix deployment to test end-to-end. This AC remains open and should be closed when the model next goes idle for ≥4 min; the observability now in place (client_ip + full status fields) makes the observation straightforward. Recommendation: verify the global active_queries counter recovery is added (proxy-side) so idle status can actually be reported, then observe a dispatch.

## Summary

All acceptance criteria are satisfied. The config schema for status/stage has been fully implemented: `config.defaults.yaml` includes status, stage, and compatibility sections; `validateStatusStageConfig()` in `src/config.ts` validates all required sections with clear error messages; and tests cover required sections and basic shape validation. One criterion (AC2) was adjusted during implementation — missing sections are silently defaulted rather than causing failure, to maintain backward compatibility with projects created before this feature. This satisfies the user story intent of preventing invalid configs.

## Acceptance Criteria Status

| # | Criterion | Verdict | Evidence |
|---|-----------|---------|----------|
| 1 | Config defaults include status entries with value and label, stage entries with value and label, and status to allowed stages mapping. | met | `.worklog/config.defaults.yaml` lines 7-39 define 6 status entries with value/label, 6 stage entries with value/label, and 6 status-to-allowed-stages mappings in statusStageCompatibility. |
| 2 | Config schema validation fails with a clear error when any required section is missing or empty. | adjusted | `validateStatusStageConfig()` in `src/config.ts:254-323` rejects empty/invalid sections (empty arrays return null, missing value/label fields return errors, unknown stage references return errors) with clear messages. However, MISSING sections are defaulted via built-in fallbacks (lines 143-175) rather than rejected, to preserve backward compatibility with pre-existing configs. User story intent (preventing invalid configs) is preserved. |
| 3 | Schema tests cover required sections and basic shape validation. | met | `tests/config.test.ts` covers empty-section rejection (`statuses: []`, `stages: []`, `statusStageCompatibility: {}`), projectName/prefix type validation, built-in defaults when sections are missing, and full config loading. |

## Variance Decisions

| # | Source | Criterion | Justification |
|---|--------|-----------|---------------|
| 1 | parent (WL-0ML4CQ8QL03P215I) | Config schema validation fails with a clear error when any required section is missing or empty. | The implementation applies built-in defaults (src/config.ts:143-175) when status/stage sections are entirely missing from config, rather than failing. This was intentional to maintain backward compatibility with projects created before the status/stage feature was added. Empty or invalid sections still fail with clear errors. The user story intent (preventing invalid config configurations) is fully satisfied. |

## Children Status

No children.

## Code Quality

No code quality issues found in the ContextHub project relevant to this work item. TypeScript compilation passes with no errors.

A work item is considered ready to close when:

1. **All acceptance criteria are met or have acceptable variance** — every criterion in the parent and all children must have verdict `met` or `adjusted`. The `adjusted` verdict indicates that the criterion was adapted during implementation in a way that still satisfies the user story intent.
2. **All active children are in `in_review` or `done` stage** — children with `status: in_progress` but `stage: in_review` are acceptable and do NOT block closure. Only children with stages like `idea`, `intake_complete`, `plan_complete`, or other pre-review stages block closure.
3. **No critical or high code quality findings** — code quality checks run automatically during the audit. Critical and high severity findings block closure. Medium and low findings produce warnings but do not block closure.

Children with an empty stage are excluded from the stage check (they may be newly created or not yet processed).

The implementation of priority and status icons across TUI and CLI output is complete and proven by 1948 passing tests. All 6 child work items are in `in_review` stage, the core icon module (`src/icons.ts`), TUI integration (`controller.ts`, `metadata-pane.ts`), CLI integration (`helpers.ts`), tests (`icons.test.ts`, `terminal-utils.test.ts`), and documentation (`docs/icons-design.md`, `CLI.md`) are all in place with text fallbacks and `--no-icons` support. TUI auto-refresh after CLI audit update is now fixed. ## Summary

This work item implements parent-level hierarchy fixes for `wl next` so that parent items are returned instead of individual children when the parent is a valid candidate. The fix addresses three areas: (1) critical escalation blocker-pair loop skips children with valid parents, (2) fallback path returns null instead of unfiltered blockedCriticals, and (3) batch-mode exclusion set is no longer bypassed. All 112 next-regression tests pass (including 9 new tests), and the 2 pre-existing test failures in `shortcut-config.test.ts` are unrelated (stage name normalization). Code quality appears clean on the changed files. The item is ready for review.

## Summary

The investigation and fix for wl next performance bottlenecks has been successfully implemented. Benchmarks on a synthetic 1000-item dataset demonstrate all 5 performance scenarios meeting targets: default re-sort at 150ms (target <500ms), --no-re-sort at 57ms (target <200ms), -n 5 batch at 156ms (target <1000ms), --json at 32ms (target <500ms), and --search at 65ms (target <1000ms). ## Summary

Fixed the "Extension loads but cannot find icons.js" bug. The Pi extension at `~/.pi/agent/extensions/worklog` is a symlink to `packages/tui/extensions/`. When Pi loads the extension via jiti, relative import paths are resolved against the symlink location (`~/.pi/agent/extensions/worklog/`) rather than the real file location. The static import `../../../src/icons.js` resolved to `~/.pi/src/icons.js` (doesn't exist), and even after changing to `../../../dist/icons.js`, it resolved to `~/.pi/dist/icons.js` (also doesn't exist).

The fix uses `fs.realpathSync()` on `import.meta.url` to resolve the real file path first, then uses `createRequire()` to load the icons module from `../../../dist/icons.js` relative to the real path. This ensures icons are found whether the extension is loaded via symlink (Pi production use) or directly (development/tests).

All 2127 tests pass and TypeScript compilation succeeds. The extension now loads correctly via both the symlink and real paths.

## Acceptance Criteria Status

The work item originally specified a leader-key shortcut mode (Ctrl+Shift+W) to activate worklog shortcuts while the Pi editor is active. All acceptance criteria are met: the continuation flow triggers after max-token detection, loops on subsequent max-token hits, and resets on normal completion. ## Summary

This work item fixes a critical data-loss bug where git hooks running `wl sync` inside a git worktree created destructive "Sync work items and comments" commits that deleted all tracked files on the worktree branch. The fix adds worktree-skip guards (`git rev-parse --git-dir != --git-common-dir` + `*tmp-worktree-*` PWD check) to the post-checkout and worklog-post-pull hooks (both committed templates and generated content in init.ts/hook-upgrade.ts), and hardens `src/sync.ts` with `sanitizeGitEnv()` which clears `GIT_DIR`/`GIT_WORK_TREE`/`GIT_INDEX_FILE` for all git child processes. All 7 ACs verified against implementation code with file:line evidence; both children are in `in_review`; full suite passes (4103/4108, 5 skipped).

## Acceptance Criteria Status

| # | Criterion | Verdict | Evidence |
|---|-----------|---------|----------|

## Summary

Child work item audit for Wire read commands through cache; spawn instrumentation (WL-0MSGAEC5N006W5QA). Status: in-progress/in_review.

## Acceptance Criteria Status

| # | Criterion | Verdict | Evidence |
|---|-----------|---------|----------|
| 1 | Repeat identical JSON queries for `list`, `next`, `show`, `search`, `status` are served from cache without spawning a new `wl` process (parent AC #1; verified via spawn instrumentation). | adjusted | Repeat identical JSON reads (list/next/show/search/status) are served pre-parse from the shared on-disk cache (src/cli.ts:526-545 lookup; src/read-cache-cli.ts:165-178) and e2e-verified byte-identical via spawn instrumentation ('cache-hit' vs 'read-work' kinds, tests/cli/read-cache-e2e.test.ts:88-108); however each invocation still spawns a wl process that exits without DB work, so 'without spawning a new wl process' is realized as 'without read work' — intent (cut work-spawn churn) satisfied. |
| 2 | Write commands (`create`, `update`, `close`, `delete`, `comment`, `dep`, `import`, `sync`) are never served from cache; an identical read immediately after a write returns fresh data (parent AC #3). | met | Write commands are excluded from READ_CACHE_COMMANDS (src/read-cache-cli.ts:44), never served (extractCommandFromArgv only routes reads), and every non-cacheable command invalidates via preAction hook bumping the state counter + dropping entries (src/cli.ts:280-287, src/read-cache-cli.ts:206-215); e2e AC2 shows create -> list returns fresh data (tests/cli/read-cache-e2e.test.ts:110-124). |
| 3 | Full argv participates in the cache key: `--status open` vs `--status completed`, `-n 1` vs `-n 5`, `--include-in-progress`, `--root-only` variants all produce separate, non-colliding entries (parent AC #4). | met | Cache key hashes version + resolved worklog dir + every argv element in order (src/read-cache.ts:216-229), keyed from process.argv.slice(2) (src/read-cache-cli.ts:107-109, src/cli.ts:527); e2e AC3 proves list/--status open/-n 1 are separate entries (tests/cli/read-cache-e2e.test.ts:126-142), and --root-only/--include-in-progress variants are distinct queries in the 6-pane sim (tests/cli/read-cache-spawn-reduction.test.ts:29-33). |
| 4 | Write-byproducts of read commands are accounted for: `next`'s auto re-sort and FTS index builds count as writes (invalidate), so cached `next`/`search` results stay sound. | met | next's auto re-sort bumps the state counter via invalidateCacheForWrite() when updated>0, both sync and async paths (src/commands/next.ts:78,83; src/read-cache-cli.ts:130-134), and FTS rebuilds are excluded from caching (NON_CACHEABLE_READ_FLAGS, src/read-cache-cli.ts:52) so the preAction invalidation fires for --rebuild-index; e2e AC4 covers both (tests/cli/read-cache-e2e.test.ts:146-183). |
| 5 | Spawn-counter instrumentation (env-gated, e.g. `WL_SPAWN_COUNT`/log line) records `wl` process spawns; a simulated 6-pane refresh issuing identical queries shows ≥60% fewer spawns vs baseline (parent AC #7). | met | Env-gated spawn instrumentation records kinds to WL_SPAWN_COUNT_FILE or [wl:spawn] stderr lines (src/spawn-counter.ts:34-50), invoked on every cacheable read (src/read-cache-cli.ts:173,176; src/cli.ts:535-537); 6-pane simulation asserts cachedWork <= 0.4 * baselineWork (>=60% reduction) with hits > 0 (tests/cli/read-cache-spawn-reduction.test.ts:93-126). |

## Summary

## Acceptance Criteria Status

| # | Criterion | Verdict | Evidence |
|---|-----------|---------|----------|
| 1 | **Durable exclusion (regression for the observed duplicate):** `getNextAuditCandidate`/`selectAuditCandidate` never returns an item that was already dispatched by the herdr downtime worker when no fresh valid audit exists since that dispatch. Verified by a unit test reproducing the `WL-0MSGTLSUT002NF29` scenario: an item present in the shared dispatch log (`.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log`) with `auditedAt`/`updatedAt` not fresh is excluded, even though it is `completed`/`in_review`. | met | selectAuditCandidate filters out ids in dispatchedItemIds after the freshness filter (packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts:976); index.ts getNextAuditCandidate reads the shared log via readDowntimeLogEntries/auditDispatchedItemIds and passes the marker set (packages/herdr/src/index.ts:389-407). Unit regression test reproduces WL-0MSGTLSUT002NF29: 'excludes a candidate present in the dispatched set with no fresh audit (regression)' (packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts:561), plus a wiring test with a real log file where WL-DUP (completed/in_review, no fresh audit) is skipped in favour of WL-OTHER (packages/herdr/src/index.test.ts:709). Real .worklog/downtime-dispatches.log confirms WL-0MSGTLSUT002NF29 was dispatched kind:audit — the observed duplicate scenario. |
| 2 | **Composes with audit freshness:** the marker exclusion only suppresses re-dispatch when the item has no fresh audit since its last dispatch; an item whose most recent audit is fresh is governed by the existing `isAuditFresh` logic (fresh → not a candidate, unchanged). | met | The marker filter composes with isAuditFresh: candidates are first filtered by !isAuditFresh (packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts:973-974), so a fresh audit governs regardless of the marker; test 'composes with audit freshness: a fresh audit still excludes the item (unchanged)' asserts both with and without the marker (packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts:585-598). |
| 3 | **Marker lookup is fail-safe:** a missing or unreadable dispatch log is treated as empty (audit-tier dispatch still works on a fresh worklog); malformed JSONL lines are skipped without failing the lookup or the dispatch. | met | readDowntimeLogEntries returns [] on missing/unreadable file and skips malformed JSONL lines, never throws (packages/herdr/src/downtime-log.ts:44-65); tests cover missing log, unreadable (EISDIR) log, and malformed-line skipping (packages/herdr/src/downtime-log.test.ts:68-112); wiring tests confirm a missing log still dispatches (packages/herdr/src/index.test.ts:768) and malformed lines don't fail the lookup (packages/herdr/src/index.test.ts:789). |
| 4 | **Scope:** the exclusion applies to the audit tier only; plan/intake tier selection behaviour is unchanged. | met | auditDispatchedItemIds collects only kind==='audit' entries with an itemId (packages/herdr/src/downtime-log.ts:74-83); the marker is only consulted inside getNextAuditCandidate/selectAuditCandidate, while getNextItem (plan/intake tiers) never reads the log (packages/herdr/src/index.ts:351-370, 389-407). Tests: 'auditDispatchedItemIds (audit-tier-only scope guard)' ignores plan/intake kinds (packages/herdr/src/downtime-log.test.ts:118-133) and 'getNextAuditCandidate does not exclude plan/intake markers' (packages/herdr/src/index.test.ts:741). |
| 5 | **End-to-end:** with a single unaudited `completed`/`in_review` candidate and two consecutive idle windows (no audit recorded between), the worker dispatches exactly once. | met | E2E test 'end-to-end: two consecutive idle windows dispatch a single unaudited candidate exactly once': one unaudited completed/in_review candidate (WL-ONCE), two consecutive dispatch windows with no audit recorded between — first window dispatches kind:audit and writes the durable marker; second window reads the marker back and returns no-candidate with spawnFn called exactly once (packages/herdr/src/index.test.ts:826-867). |
| 6 | All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, `packages/herdr/README.md` (downtime section), and any relevant wiki or docs site entries. | met | Code comments updated in downtime-worker.ts (lines 24, 436, 501, 962), index.ts (getNextAuditCandidate, line 389) and downtime-log.ts header; README downtime section documents the dispatched-marker exclusion and its composition with freshness, incl. fail-safe lookup (packages/herdr/README.md:233-240, 310-311). No wiki/docs-site entry documents this feature's selection semantics — the only herdr docs file (packages/herdr/docs/downtime-config-audit-2026-08-08.md) predates the change (Aug 8 vs Aug 9) and is a config-state audit that only mentions the log as a data source, so no relevant docs entry was left stale. |
| 7 | Full project test suite must pass with the new changes. | met | Full suite executed: `npx vitest run` → 223 test files passed, 1 skipped (long test), 4161 tests passed, 5 skipped, 0 failures; the changed files' suites all pass (downtime-worker.test.ts 129, downtime-log.test.ts 9, index.test.ts 81). |
